title: Annal Ambedkar Business Champions Scheme
benefit_summary: 35% capital subsidy on eligible project cost (max Rs.1.5 crore) plus 6% interest subvention on loans, for SC/ST entrepreneurs starting or expanding businesses in Tamil Nadu.
caveats: 100% SC/ST-owned enterprise required; interest subvention capped to loan tenure up to 10 years, working-capital subvention up to 2 years.

title: Aponar Apon Ghar
benefit_summary: Home loan subsidy of Rs.2,50,000 for loans between Rs.5-40 lakh from listed banks in Assam, on a sliding scale (e.g. Rs.1,00,000 subsidy for Rs.5-10 lakh loans up to Rs.2,50,000 for Rs.30-40 lakh loans), for first-time home buyers.
caveats: Only for first house purchase; loan must not be NPA; loan sanctioned on/after 1 April 2019; relaunched 16 June 2026 for FY2026-27 disbursals.

title: Assam Arogya Nidhi Scheme
benefit_summary: Financial assistance up to Rs.3,00,000 for treatment of life-threatening diseases (heart, cancer, kidney, orthopedic, AIDS, etc.) or accident/disaster injuries, for BPL families or those with income under Rs.5 lakh/year.
caveats: CORRECTED: coverage raised to Rs.3 lakh (from Rs.2 lakh). Government employees/pensioners and their families are not eligible. PMJAY/AAA cardholders must use those schemes first.

title: Ashraya Adhar Scheme
benefit_summary: Loan of up to Rs.5,00,000 at 2% p.a. interest for repair, renovation, or reconstruction of houses owned by Scheduled Tribe members in Goa, disbursed in two installments (Rs.3,75,000 then Rs.1,25,000).
caveats: CLARIFIED: this is a loan scheme, not a cash grant. Age limit relaxed to 58 for government/PSU employees. Work must commence within 3 months of sanction; borrower must insure life and property.

title: Aushadhi Avam Sugandhit Fasal Shetra Vistar
benefit_summary: 20-50% subsidy (crop-dependent) to farmers for cultivating medicinal/aromatic crops (Amla, Ashvagandha, Tulasi, Sarpagandha, etc.), for 0.25 to 2.0 hectares of land.
caveats: CORRECTED: subsidy is 20-50% of cost depending on crop, not a flat amount. Grant payable only once per farmer; forest-rights-certificate holders also eligible.

title: Agriculture Academic Studies Scheme
benefit_summary: Monthly stipend of Rs.1,200 plus a book grant of Rs.1,200/year for Meghalaya-domicile students sponsored under State-quota seats for 4-year Agriculture/Horticulture degree courses.
caveats: Requires passing 10+2 Science (55% general/OBC, 45% SC/ST) with PCB+English, plus qualifying ICAR AIEEA entrance exam.

title: Atal Awasiya Vidyala Yojana
benefit_summary: Free residential education (school, accommodation, meals, medical, sports) for children (ages 6-16) of registered construction workers, orphans, and destitute children, currently in 18 districts of UP.
caveats: Parent must be registered with the labour welfare board for at least 1 year (365 days); maximum 2 children per registered worker.

title: Atal Asra Yojana
benefit_summary: Financial assistance of up to Rs.5,00,000 for new construction/reconstruction of a house, or up to Rs.3,00,000 for repairs, for Scheduled Tribe families in Goa.
caveats: CORRECTED: new-construction/reconstruction cap is Rs.5 lakh (not Rs.3 lakh as originally listed); repairs cap Rs.3 lakh (originally listed as the main benefit). Income eligibility cap raised from Rs.3 lakh to Rs.5 lakh/year in 2026.

title: Aaws Bhatta Sahayata Yojana
benefit_summary: Rent assistance for SC/ST college students who must live away from home: Rs.2,000/month in Bhopal, Indore, Jabalpur, Gwalior, Ujjain; Rs.1,250/month at district HQs; Rs.1,000/month at tehsil/block level.
caveats: CORRECTED: rate varies by location, not a flat Rs.2,000. Not eligible if staying in a government hostel; ineligible next year if exam is failed/postponed; family income must be within Rs.6 lakh/year (Post-Matric Scholarship limit).

title: Agri-Clinics And Agri-Business Centres Scheme
benefit_summary: Back-end composite subsidy of roughly 36-44% (category/region dependent) on project cost, plus free start-up training, for agriculture graduates/diploma holders setting up Agri-Clinics or Agri-Business Centres. Project cost ceiling Rs.20 lakh (individual, Rs.25 lakh for outstanding candidates) or up to Rs.100 lakh for group projects.
caveats: Loan repayment period 5-10 years with a 2-year grace period; NABARD channels the subsidy through banks.

title: Andaman & Nicobar Bed & Breakfast / Home Stay Establishment Scheme
benefit_summary: Official classification (Silver/Gold star) for homestay/B&B establishments letting 1-6 rooms where the owner resides on-site, valid for 3 years; classification fee Rs.1,000 (Silver) or Rs.2,000 (Gold).
caveats: CORRECTED: this is a tourism registration/licensing scheme, not a cash-benefit scheme. Applications now routed via the National Single Window System (NSWS). Reclassification application must be submitted 3 months before expiry.

title: Accidental Death Assistance Scheme- Gujarat Labour Welfare Board
benefit_summary: Rs.2,00,000 financial assistance to the family of a worker (Shramyogi) who dies in an accident during employment.
caveats: Employer must have regularly paid Labour Welfare Fund contributions; benefit applies from the day after joining the job; application must be filed within 2 years of death; natural/sickness deaths not covered.

title: Accidental Death Assistance Scheme (GBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.3,00,000 financial assistance to legal heirs of a construction worker who dies accidentally or is permanently disabled at a construction site.
caveats: Applies to both registered and unregistered construction workers with the Board.

title: Accidental Death Benefit Scheme (PBAOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.2,25,000 financial assistance (Direct Benefit Transfer, within 15 days) to nominees/dependents of a construction worker in Puducherry who dies in a workplace accident, in addition to Rs.2,00,000 via LIC insurance.
caveats: Deceased must have been registered with the Puducherry BOCW Board, aged 18-60, contributing regularly with no default over 1 continuous year; application must be filed within 2 months of death.

title: Assistance For Delivery / Miscarriage Of Pregnancy / Termination Of Pregnancy To Female Differently Abled Person
benefit_summary: Rs.1,000/month for delivery (total Rs.6,000 over 6 months) or a one-time Rs.3,000 for miscarriage/termination of pregnancy, for differently-abled women in Tamil Nadu.
caveats: Applicant must hold an identity card issued by the Tamil Nadu welfare board for the differently abled.

title: Agriculture Engineering (Mechanical) Scheme
benefit_summary: ~50-60% subsidy on hiring/purchase of farm machinery (power tillers, bulldozers, tractors, diesel water pumpsets) for bonafide farmers in Meghalaya.
caveats: Selection is first-come-first-served; minor source inconsistency on exact subsidy percentage (50-60%).

title: Allowance To Eunuchs Scheme
benefit_summary: Monthly financial assistance of Rs.3,000 to transgender/eunuch residents of Haryana aged 18 and above.
caveats: Must have resided in Haryana for 5+ years; requires Civil Surgeon certificate confirming status; case transfers to Old Age Allowance Scheme at age 60; applicant must not be involved in unlawful activity. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Rs.2,750 was the 01.04.2023-31.12.2023 rate; revised to Rs.3,000/month effective 01.01.2024 per socialjusticehry.gov.in.

title: Amar Fasal Amar Gola
benefit_summary: Subsidy of Rs.5,000-Rs.25,000 (varies by storage type: small storehouse, pucca storage, or onion storage) for small/marginal farmers to build their own storehouse (godown), credited to Kisan Credit Card-linked bank accounts.
caveats: CORRECTED: original description wrongly framed this as a seed/fertilizer input subsidy; it is actually a storage/godown infrastructure scheme. A separate companion scheme 'Amar Fasal Amar Gari' gives Rs.10,000 for a vending vehicle -- do not conflate. Pilot scheme initially covering only ~10,000 of 24 lakh eligible farmers.

title: Advocate Grant
benefit_summary: Grant of Rs.12,000/year for 3 consecutive years to OBC law graduates enrolled as advocates with the Bar Council of Kerala, to help them start legal practice.
caveats: Preference given to BPL candidates and those with lower family income; distinct from the separate 'Advocate Stipend Scheme' (Rs.3,000/month, different administering body). [Fix 2026-07-23] Occupation constraint (advocate/legal professional) removed from structured matching -- our FLOW has no "advocate" occupation option and this is a single narrow scheme; this is specifically for practicing advocates, not the general public.

title: AGR 2 (Farm Mechanization) Scheme Of Farmers Other Than SC/ST
benefit_summary: Subsidy for farm equipment purchase (power tillers, rice transplanters, tractors/implements): 50% of cost or Rs.45,000 (small/marginal/women farmers) or 40% or Rs.36,000 (other farmers), whichever is less; other implements have separate tiers.
caveats: Applies only in the 208 talukas where the central SMAM scheme is not implemented; equipment must be purchased from empanelled manufacturers/dealers; not for SC/ST farmers (see AGR 3/AGR 4 schemes).

title: AGR 3 (Farm Mechanization) Scheme For ST Farmers
benefit_summary: Subsidized seeds, fertilizer, and farm equipment (plant protection equipment, tarpaulin, pump sets, micronutrients, etc.) for Scheduled Tribe farmers in Tribal Area Sub Plan (TASP) talukas; power tiller subsidy of 50% of cost or Rs.45,000, whichever is less.
caveats: Applies only in 208 talukas where the central SMAM scheme is not implemented and in TASP-notified areas/districts.

title: AGR 4 (Farm Mechanization) Scheme For SC Farmers
benefit_summary: Subsidy for farm equipment purchase (power tillers, rice transplanters, tractors/implements) for Scheduled Caste farmers: 50% of cost or Rs.45,000 (small/marginal/women farmers) or 40% or Rs.36,000 (others), whichever is less.
caveats: Applies only in the 208 talukas where the central SMAM scheme is not implemented; equipment must be purchased from empanelled dealers.

title: AGR-50 Scheme-Assistance To Purchase Tractors
benefit_summary: Subsidy for tractor purchase: 25% of cost or Rs.45,000 (up to 40 PTO HP) / 25% or Rs.60,000 (40-60 PTO HP), whichever is less, for any Gujarat farmer.
caveats: Tractor must be an empanelled model purchased from an authorized dealer; no income or land cap stated.

title: Arundhati Gold Scheme
benefit_summary: One-time incentive of Rs.40,000 (~10g gold equivalent) deposited to the bride's account at marriage registration, to help economically weaker families gift gold to their daughter.
caveats: Bride must be 18+, groom 21+; marriage registered under Special Marriage Act 1954 on/after 1 Dec 2019; must apply same day as marriage registration; first marriage only; both must have passed HSLC (waived for Tea Tribe/Adivasi for 5 years); parental income must be below Rs.5 lakh/year; funds restricted to gold purchase only.

title: Akanksha Housing Scheme
benefit_summary: No-profit-no-loss, subsidized flats (Rs.2,200-3,100/sq.ft depending on category, tied to employee grade pay) for serving West Bengal state government employees, allotted via lottery at a New Town, Kolkata project.
caveats: Employees with their own department housing schemes (e.g. police 'Pratyasha') are excluded; requires Rs.25,000 application-money deposit via challan at Bank of Baroda; only one application per person allowed.

title: Airavata Scheme
benefit_summary: Subsidy of up to Rs.5,00,000 (50% of vehicle cost) to SC/ST youth in Karnataka to purchase a light motor vehicle (taxi/cab) for self-employment via aggregators like Ola/Uber, covering ~1,000 beneficiaries.
caveats: Requires valid driving license and cab badge; family income must not exceed Rs.5 lakh/year; ineligible if the applicant/family previously received a Corporation/Government subsidy exceeding Rs.1,00,000; selection by merit (age, education, driving experience).

title: Agriculture Information Unit Scheme
benefit_summary: Free distribution of agricultural information leaflets/booklets and sponsorship for farmers/self-help groups to attend trade fairs, expos, and exhibitions within and outside Meghalaya.
caveats: Selection is first-come-first-served; not a cash benefit.

title: Aswasakiranam
benefit_summary: Rs.600/month financial assistance to family caregivers of totally bedridden or severely mentally/physically disabled BPL patients (e.g. autism, cerebral palsy, blindness, bedridden cancer/elderly patients), in addition to any pension the patient receives.
caveats: CORRECTED: assistance is Rs.600/month, not higher figures sometimes assumed. Run by Kerala Social Security Mission; disbursed 10-11 months at once; requires BPL ration card/certificate and doctor-attested medical certificate.

title: Asangathit Karmakar Gambhir Bimari Chikitsa Sahayata Yojana
benefit_summary: Up to Rs.50,000 medical assistance (or actual treatment cost if lower) to unorganized workers for serious illness treatment (kidney, cancer, sickle cell anemia, heart disease, AIDS, paralysis).
caveats: Must be registered with the State Unorganized Workers Board for at least 90 days.

title: Asangathit Karmakaar Mrtyu Evan Divyaang Sahaayata Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.1,00,000 to the family on death of a registered unorganized worker, or Rs.50,000 for permanent disability.
caveats: Not payable for death due to suicide, substance abuse, or fighting/crime; only on the worker's own death (not a family member's); not applicable to those already benefiting from the Board's silicosis assistance scheme.

title: Asangathit Karmakar Prasuti Sahayata Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.20,000 delivery/maternity financial assistance for registered unorganized workers (male or female).
caveats: Recently raised from Rs.10,000 to Rs.20,000. Contract workers, female domestic workers, porters, and sanitation workers are not eligible. Pregnancy must be verified by a doctor, ANM, or Mitanin.

title: Asangathit Karmakaar Silai Machine Sahayata Yojana
benefit_summary: Free sewing machine (or equivalent value) provided annually to registered unorganized women workers (tailors, embroiderers, weavers) aged 18-50 in Chhattisgarh.
caveats: Not eligible if already received a sewing machine/equivalent under another state scheme, or benefited under the Chief Minister Cycle Assistance Scheme.

title: Asangathit Karmakar Samachar-Patr Hawker Cycle Sahayata Yojana
benefit_summary: One free bicycle provided to registered unorganized newspaper-delivery workers (hawkers) in Chhattisgarh.
caveats: Not eligible if already receiving benefits from a parallel scheme.

title: Artificial Limbs/Assistive Equipments Scheme
benefit_summary: Financial grant of up to Rs.15,000 per beneficiary (flat, raised from the earlier Rs.8,000/Rs.10,000 tiers effective FY2024-25) for artificial limbs/auxiliary equipment (tricycles, wheelchairs, hearing aids, braille kits, etc.) for persons with disabilities of any age in UP; the same Rs.15,000 maximum applies in one sanction for multi-disability cases needing more than one aid.
caveats: Family income must be within the BPL limit (Rs.46,080/year rural, Rs.56,460/year urban); not eligible if benefited from a similar govt scheme in the last 3 years (1 year for regular students); allocated first-come-first-served against available funds. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Grant raised to a flat Rs.15,000 (from Rs.8,000/10,000 tiers) effective FY2024-25, per uphwd.gov.in and The Statesman.

title: Super IAS 500 Scholarship Manipur
benefit_summary: Free/subsidized offline UPSC civil-services coaching for meritorious Manipur-resident IAS aspirants: top 200 scholarship-exam rankers get full scholarship, ranks 201-500 get 40-75% grants toward ALS Institute coaching. Total outlay Rs.2.8 crore.
caveats: Selection based on a scholarship entrance exam; must be permanent resident/domicile of Manipur.

title: Accident Medical Assistance Scheme (PBAOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.1,500/month (via DBT within 15 days) to a registered construction worker in Puducherry who suffers an accident/fracture, paid until fit to resume normal work.
caveats: Requires registration fee Rs.25 plus Rs.100/year subscription and Rs.300 triennial renewal fee; must not have defaulted contribution for over 1 continuous year; needs medical certificate from a prescribed doctor.

title: Alpsankhyak Merit-Cum-Means Chatravriti Yojana
benefit_summary: Maintenance allowance of Rs.1,000/month (hostellers) or Rs.500/month (non-hostellers) for 10 months, plus reimbursement of course fees up to Rs.20,000, for meritorious minority-community students in Madhya Pradesh.
caveats: CORRECTED: allowance varies by hostel status, not a flat Rs.1,000. Requires 50%+ marks in last qualifying exam and family income under Rs.2,50,000/year.

title: Award For Meritorious Students Of Meghalaya In The HSSLC Examination (Science Stream)
benefit_summary: One-time award of Rs.10,000 plus a certificate for tribal (Khasi, Jaintia, Garo, Koch, Hajong) students of Meghalaya scoring 60%+ in the HSSLC Science stream exam, selected district-wise (20 awardees in East Khasi Hills, 6 each in other 10 districts).
caveats: One-time award only; requires Scheduled Tribe certificate of Meghalaya.

title: Atma Nirbhar Bagwani Yojana
benefit_summary: Bank-linked credit subsidy for horticulture (arecanut, pineapple, avocado, dragon fruit, orange, banana, guava) and farm equipment (tractor, power tiller, brush cutter): 45% government subsidy, 45% bank finance, 10% farmer contribution. Loans up to Rs.1.6 lakh (individual) or Rs.10 lakh (SHG/FPO) are collateral-free.
caveats: Loans above Rs.1.6 lakh (individual) or Rs.10 lakh (SHG/FPO) require collateral security (land/property or guarantee).

title: The Andaman & Nicobar Islands Allowance to Destitute Women Scheme
benefit_summary: Rs.2,500/month financial assistance (via bank account) to poor, destitute women in Andaman & Nicobar Islands.
caveats: Household income must not exceed Rs.4,000/month (~Rs.48,000/year); must not already receive any other government assistance/pension; must report address/employment changes within 15 days or face recovery of paid allowance.

title: The Andaman & Nicobar Islands Disability Allowance Scheme
benefit_summary: Rs.2,500/month disability allowance (paid via bank account until death, or until employed) for unemployed persons in Andaman & Nicobar Islands with 40%+ disability, from age 1 month.
caveats: No income ceiling. Assistance stops if beneficiary gets employment. Disability certificate must be renewed every 5 years.

title: The Andaman & Nicobar Islands Old Age Assistance Scheme
benefit_summary: Rs.2,500/month for seniors aged 60-79, or Rs.3,000/month for those 80+, in Andaman & Nicobar Islands.
caveats: Household income must not exceed Rs.4,000/month; not eligible if receiving any other government pension/assistance (except IGNOAPS beneficiaries, who are covered under this scheme too).

title: Andaman & Nicobar Islands Scheme for Health Insurance
benefit_summary: Cashless medical treatment up to Rs.5,00,000 per patient per illness (indoor/outdoor), plus travel reimbursement for patient and one attendant, for BPL households, A&N government pensioners, or permanent residents with family income below Rs.3 lakh/year.
caveats: Only valid at empanelled hospitals with prior codal formalities completed at the ANISHI Nodal Cell; reimbursement denied if admitted at a non-empanelled hospital without approval.

title: Atma Nirbhar Krishi Yojana
benefit_summary: Collateral-free bank loans of up to Rs.1,60,000 for farmers in Arunachal Pradesh to invest in scientific land terracing, double cropping, farm mechanization, apiculture, and diversified fruit cultivation (apple, kiwi, orange, arecanut, walnut, persimmon).
caveats: Farmer must hold land for agricultural activities and meet participating banks' loan criteria; women farmers and SHG members are also eligible. Same subsidy structure as the companion Atma Nirbhar Bagwani Yojana.

title: Assam Orunodoi Scheme
benefit_summary: Rs.1,250/month (raised from Rs.830) direct benefit transfer to a woman member of poor households in Assam, covering essentials like pulses, sugar, medicines, fruits/vegetables.
caveats: CORRECTED: now Rs.1,250/month (raised from Rs.830); mixed reporting on a possible added Rs.250 LPG component from Jan 2026 (verify before using Rs.1,500 figure). Priority to widows, separated women, physically handicapped, unmarried women over 35. Family must live in a kutcha house with max 15 bigha land in villages (3 katha in small towns, 1.5 katha in Kamrup Metro); ex-PRI members' family income must be under Rs.2 lakh/year.

title: Award of Pre-matric Scholarship to Scheduled Caste Students Studying from VI to X Standard in Government Schools and Government recognised Private Schools
benefit_summary: Rs.150/month (Class VI-VIII) or Rs.250/month (Class IX-X) scholarship, paid 10 months/year, for SC students in Puducherry government/recognized private schools.
caveats: Parent/guardian annual income must not exceed Rs.24,000 (BPL limit); student must be native of Puducherry (by birth or 5+ years' residence) and must secure annual promotion to continue receiving it.

title: Advance for Purchase or Construction of House (GBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.50,000 advance sanctioned to a registered construction worker in Goa for outright purchase/construction of a house, recovered in installments fixed by the Board.
caveats: Requires 90 days of service in the year as a registered worker, 5 continuous years of Fund membership, and 15 years of remaining service before superannuation; applicant must declare neither they nor spouse/children already own a house (for new construction); completion certificate due within 6 months of withdrawal.

title: Assistance for Power Driven Chaff Cutter Scheme under Integrated Fodder Development Scheme (General Category)
benefit_summary: Subsidy of 75% of the purchase cost of a power-driven chaff cutter, or Rs.18,000, whichever is less, for General-category dairy farmers in Gujarat owning at least 5 animals.
caveats: A separate, non-power-driven chaff cutter scheme exists with a lower 50%/Rs.15,000 subsidy -- do not confuse the two. Must purchase from an empanelled vendor and submit the bill for subsidy claim.

title: Assistance for Power Driven Chaff Cutter Scheme under Scheduled Castes Sub Plan (SC Category)
benefit_summary: Subsidy of 75% of the purchase cost of a power-driven chaff cutter, or Rs.18,000, whichever is less, for Scheduled Caste dairy farmers in Gujarat owning at least 5 animals.
caveats: A separate, non-power-driven chaff cutter scheme exists with a lower 50%/Rs.15,000 subsidy -- do not confuse the two.

title: Assistance for Power Driven Chaff Cutter Scheme under Tribal Area Sub Plan (TASP- ST Category)
benefit_summary: Subsidy of 75% of the purchase cost of a power-driven chaff cutter, or Rs.18,000, whichever is less, for Scheduled Tribe dairy farmers in Gujarat owning at least 5 animals.
caveats: A separate, non-power-driven chaff cutter scheme exists with a lower 50%/Rs.15,000 subsidy -- do not confuse the two.

title: Arun Pig Development Scheme
benefit_summary: Piggery subsidy (75% government / 25% beneficiary contribution) providing piglets and support for sty construction to pig-rearing farmers/SHGs in Arunachal Pradesh; 5 selected entrepreneurs per district get 15 piglets each worth Rs.1.5 lakh (govt share).
caveats: Preference given to women and genuinely poor farmers; farmer must construct a suitable sty before piglets are handed over.

title: Alpasankhyak Post-Maitrik Chhaatravrtti Yojana
benefit_summary: Course fee reimbursement up to Rs.20,000/year plus a maintenance allowance (Rs.570/month hostellers, Rs.300/month non-hostellers for UG/PG; Rs.1,200/month hostellers, Rs.550/month non-hostellers for M.Phil/PhD), for 10 months/year, for minority-community post-matric students in Madhya Pradesh.
caveats: CORRECTED: fee component is reimbursement up to Rs.20,000, not a flat Rs.3,000. Requires 50%+ marks in last qualifying exam and family income under Rs.2,00,000/year.

title: Award of Post-Matric Scholarship to Scheduled Caste Students
benefit_summary: Fee reimbursement plus maintenance allowance (hostellers/day scholars) up to roughly Rs.13,500 total (varies by course and hostel status) for SC post-matric/post-secondary students in Puducherry.
caveats: Requires 5+ years' residence in Puducherry; family income must not exceed Rs.2,00,000/year; based on Ministry of Social Justice norms.

title: Award of Pre-matric Scholarship to the Students Whose Parents Are Engaged in Unclean Occupation
benefit_summary: Rs.1,850/year scholarship for SC students in Class 1-10 in Puducherry whose parent(s) work in an unclean occupation (scavenger, flayer, tanner), regardless of family income.
caveats: Provided irrespective of income; requires certificate of unclean occupation from the parent's employer.

title: Assistance For Purchase Of Spectacles By A Differently Abled Person
benefit_summary: Rs.500 reimbursement toward the cost of spectacles for differently-abled persons in Tamil Nadu.
caveats: Applicant must hold an identity card issued by the Tamil Nadu welfare board for the differently abled.

title: Atal Pension Yojana
benefit_summary: Contribution-based pension scheme guaranteeing a monthly pension of Rs.1,000-5,000 (subscriber's choice) after age 60 until death, with the same amount continuing to the spouse, and return of accumulated corpus to the nominee thereafter.
caveats: Not open to new enrollment for income-tax payers since October 2022 (subscribers who joined before then are grandfathered); contributions via auto-debit from savings account; voluntary exit before 60 forfeits government co-contribution (for pre-2016 joiners).

title: Arogya Lakshmi
benefit_summary: One full nutritious meal per day (rice, dal, vegetables, egg, 200ml milk) plus iron/folic acid tablets for pregnant and lactating women, and supplementary nutrition (Balamrutham/eggs) for children under 6, delivered through Anganwadi centres in Telangana.
caveats: In-kind (food/nutrition) benefit, not cash; delivery must occur at a designated healthcare facility or with a qualified provider.

title: Accident Relief Scheme
benefit_summary: Rs.20,000 to legal heirs of a BPL household when the primary breadwinner (male or female, engaged in one of 44 notified occupational categories) dies in an accident; Rs.5,000-15,000 relief for injury/impairment cases.
caveats: Application must be filed within 6 months of death.

title: Award to Scheduled Castes Students Who Secured Top Ranks at State and District Level in Standard X & XII (Sahuji Maharaj Assistance)
benefit_summary: Cash prizes for SC students topping Standard X/XII in Gujarat: state level Rs.51,000/41,000/31,000 for 1st/2nd/3rd rank; district level Rs.15,000/11,000/9,000. No income limit.
caveats: CORRECTED: rates raised per GR dated 07/04/2025 (previously state-level was Rs.41,000/21,000/11,000 for Std X and Rs.31,000/21,000/11,000 for Std XII; district level was Rs.6,000/5,000/4,000). List of winners is sourced directly from the Gujarat education board, no separate application needed.

title: Ashirwad
benefit_summary: One-time financial assistance of Rs.51,000 (hiked from Rs.21,000 in April 2021) to help economically disadvantaged families with a daughter's wedding expenses, for SC/Christian, Backward Class, EWS, widow's daughters, and SC widows/divorcees remarrying.
caveats: CORRECTED: benefit is Rs.51,000, not Rs.21,000 as originally listed. Limited to 2 daughters per family; family income must not exceed Rs.32,790/year; application must be made before or within 30 days of marriage.

title: Assistance Scheme For Construction Worker In Case Of General Or Accidental Death Or Injury
benefit_summary: CORRECTED - this is the 'normal' (non-accidental) death/injury tier: Rs.75,000 for normal death; Rs.20,000 for serious injury (5+ days hospitalization); Rs.5,000 for minor injury. A separate accidental-death tier under this same scheme pays Rs.5,00,000 (death), Rs.3,00,000 (total disability), Rs.1,00,000 (partial disability).
caveats: Not payable for death/injury from suicide, drug/substance use, or unlawful assault; application within 1 year of death or 6 months of injury/discharge.

title: Assistance Scheme for Handicraft Artisans
benefit_summary: One-time back-end grant for setting up handicraft micro-enterprises: 40% of Fixed Capital Investment up to Rs.2 lakh (general category), or 50% up to Rs.3 lakh (youth 18-45, women, SC/ST, disabled artisans), covering workshop, tools, equipment, and design support.
caveats: CORRECTED: assistance is tiered by percentage, not a flat Rs.2,000. Released in one installment; artisans who already received a subsidy under another scheme get only the remaining eligible balance. Total capped at Rs.7.5 lakh including working capital.

title: Assistance Scheme for Occupational Diseases (GBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Free medical treatment plus monthly assistance of Rs.1,500 (disability under 90%) or Rs.3,000 (disability 90-100%) for registered construction workers in Gujarat suffering from 1 of 15 occupational diseases or 23 serious injury types, up to a total of Rs.3,00,000.
caveats: Requires registration and e-Nirman Card; treatment only at State Government-approved hospitals.

title: Attendance Scholarship Scheme for Girl Students with Disabilities of Rural Areas
benefit_summary: Rs.2,500/year (up to 10th standard) or Rs.3,000/year (10+1 onward through higher education) attendance scholarship for rural girl students in Punjab with 40%+ disability.
caveats: Requires minimum 70% attendance; family monthly income must not exceed Rs.5,000 (~Rs.60,000/year); credited directly to student's bank account.

title: Antya Sanskar Sahay Yojana
benefit_summary: Financial assistance up to Rs.20,000 (or actual cost, whichever less) for funeral/religious ceremony expenses of a deceased Scheduled Tribe family member in Goa.
caveats: Claim must be made within 12 months of death; if applicant is not ST but deceased is, applicant must prove close relationship to the deceased. Family income cap Rs.3,00,000/year.

title: AICTE-SHORT TERM TRAINING PROGRAMME (STTP) (UT-J&K,LADAKH AND NER)
benefit_summary: Institutional grant of Rs.5,00,000 to AICTE-approved technical education institutions in J&K, Ladakh, and NER to conduct a 6-day residential faculty training programme; not a direct individual cash benefit.
caveats: Maximum 5 proposals per institute per year (max 3 approved); institution must submit utilization certificate within 1 month of program completion; approved programme must run within 6 months of fund release.

title: Assistance for Tools, Equipment, Shorting/Grading Equipment, PHM Equipment for Scheduled Tribes (HRT-3)
benefit_summary: Subsidy for horticulture tools/sorting-grading/post-harvest management equipment: 75% of cost or Rs.3,750 (individual ST farmer), or 90% of cost up to Rs.7,50,000 (farmer groups/cooperatives).
caveats: Equipment must be purchased from empanelled dealers; disability certificate accepted for PWD applicants; forest rights letter accepted where applicable.

title: Assistance for Tools, Equipment, Shorting/Grading Equipment, PHM Equipment for General Category (HRT-2)
benefit_summary: Subsidy for horticulture tools/sorting-grading/post-harvest management equipment: 75% of cost or Rs.3,750 (individual General-category farmer), or 90% of cost up to Rs.7,50,000 (farmer groups/cooperatives).
caveats: Equipment must be purchased from empanelled dealers.

title: Assistance for Tools, Equipment, Shorting/Grading Equipment, PHM Equipment for Scheduled Castes (HRT-4)
benefit_summary: Subsidy for horticulture tools/sorting-grading/post-harvest management equipment: 75% of cost or Rs.3,750 (individual SC farmer), or 90% of cost up to Rs.7,50,000 (farmer groups/cooperatives).
caveats: Equipment must be purchased from empanelled dealers.

title: Annai Teresa Ninaivu Marriage Assistance Scheme for Orphan Girls-I
benefit_summary: Rs.25,000 cash plus an 8g 22-carat gold coin (for the Thirumangalyam) as marriage assistance to orphan girls (non-graduates) in Tamil Nadu, aged 18+ at marriage.
caveats: No income ceiling. Application must be filed 40 days before marriage (or at least 1 day before in exceptional cases). A companion scheme (Scheme-II) offers Rs.50,000 + gold for graduate/diploma-holder orphan brides.

title: Annai Teresa Ninaivu Marriage Assistance Scheme for Orphan Girls-II
benefit_summary: Rs.50,000 cash plus an 8g 22-carat gold coin (for the Thirumangalyam) as marriage assistance to orphan girls holding a degree or diploma, in Tamil Nadu, aged 18+ at marriage.
caveats: No income ceiling. Application must be filed 40 days before marriage (or at least 1 day before in exceptional cases). Companion Scheme-I offers Rs.25,000 + gold for non-graduate orphan brides.

title: Acharya Vidyasagar Gau Samvardhan Yojana
benefit_summary: For native-cow shelters/owners (minimum 5 cows, 1+ acre land): margin money support of 25% of project cost up to Rs.1.5 lakh (general/OBC) or 33% up to Rs.2 lakh (SC/ST), plus interest reimbursement (govt covers 5%/year, max Rs.25,000/year, for 7 years) on a bank loan covering 75% of project cost (max project Rs.10 lakh).
caveats: CORRECTED: margin money is tiered by category (25%/33%), not a flat amount. Cow shelter/owner must register with the Gau Samvardhan Board; only indigenous (native-breed) cows qualify.

title: Award Of Stipend To VJNT And SBC Students Studying In ITI
benefit_summary: Monthly stipend of Rs.40-100 (for 10 months) for VJNT (Vimukta Jati/Nomadic Tribes) and SBC category students studying at an approved ITI in Maharashtra.
caveats: Rs.100/month applies only to students not already receiving a stipend from the Technical Education Department; family income must be within Rs.65,290/year; selection done by the ITI Principal.

title: Bal Ashrams
benefit_summary: Free residential care for orphan/destitute children in Jammu & Kashmir: schooling, boarding, lodging, bedding, clothing, recreational material, and medicines (in-kind institutional benefit, no cash amount).
caveats: Applied for by a guardian or social worker on the child's behalf through the District Social Welfare Officer; child must not already be receiving similar benefits elsewhere.

title: Border Areas Development Department
benefit_summary: Community infrastructure development funding (roads, health/education buildings, irrigation, sports facilities, drinking water) of roughly Rs.4-60 lakh per project, for villages/towns within 0-10km of the International Boundary in border districts across 16 states and 2 UTs.
caveats: CORRECTED: this is a community/infrastructure development scheme, not an individual cash benefit -- likely a mismatch for an individual-eligibility bot; flag to user that it does not apply to individual welfare applications.

title: Basic Agriculture Training Centre Scheme
benefit_summary: Free short-term agricultural vocational training plus a monthly stipend of Rs.500 and seed money of Rs.1,00,000 per participant, for educated unemployed rural youth (Class X passed) in Meghalaya who own/lease agricultural land.
caveats: Selection based on merit and land ownership/lease for farm-based activities (land document not mandatory for non-farm agri-business). [Audit fix 2026-07-23] TREYSEFA seed money raised from Rs.10,000 to Rs.1,00,000 in 2021; still Rs.1 lakh as of the June 2024 batch disbursement per Agriculture Post/India Education Diary.

title: Bed & Breakfast/Homestay Scheme- Punjab
benefit_summary: Lifetime registration/certification (Gold or Silver category) for homeowners in Punjab letting 1-6 rooms as a Bed & Breakfast or Homestay unit, providing Punjab Tourism branding, marketing support, and additional income opportunity -- not a cash grant.
caveats: Owner must reside on the property; requires a non-refundable application fee; Gold category requires the house to be under 20 years old with 25%+ open area.

title: Berojgari Bhatta Yojna
benefit_summary: Unemployment allowance of Rs.1,000-1,500/month for educated (10th pass+) unemployed youth aged 21-35 in Uttar Pradesh, with family income under Rs.3 lakh/year, until they secure a job.
caveats: 2026: requires renewal every 3 months and mandatory attendance at employment fairs; must register with the employment exchange.

title: Bio Control Laboratory and Pesticides Testing Laboratory Scheme
benefit_summary: Free distribution of bio-control agents (Trichoderma, Trichogramma) to bonafide farmers in Meghalaya for organic pest/plant-health management.
caveats: First-come-first-served, requires sufficient cultivable land.

title: Back Ended Interest Subsidy (BEIS)
benefit_summary: 5% back-ended interest subsidy on term loans for new/upgrading micro and small manufacturing enterprises in Tamil Nadu, for 5 years -- capped at Rs.20 lakh (CGTMSE-backed loans up to Rs.2 crore) or Rs.25 lakh (technology upgradation loans up to Rs.5 crore); max Rs.10 lakh per loan up to Rs.1 crore.
caveats: Interest subsidy reimbursed quarterly directly to the lending institution, not the borrower.

title: Bhausaheb Fundkar Falbag Lagvad Scheme
benefit_summary: DBT subsidy for planting 16 perennial fruit crops (mango, cashew, guava, sapota, pomegranate, coconut, etc.), varying by crop (roughly Rs.43,596/ha to Rs.2,02,090/ha), paid over 3 years (50:30:20 split); land limits 0.10-10.00 ha (Konkan) or 0.20-6.00 ha (rest of Maharashtra).
caveats: Requires 80% plant survival in year 1 and 90% in year 2 to receive later installments; drip irrigation separately 100% subsidized; requires Aadhaar-linked bank account and 7/12 + 8-A land certificates. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Removed incorrect caste_category=[sc,st] restriction. Official Maharashtra guideline confirms this is open to ALL farmers (General/SC/ST/women/disabled) with SC/ST/women/disabled given priority in fund allocation, not an eligibility gate. A general-category farmer was being wrongly told they don't qualify.

title: Boarding House Stipend Scheme (Tripura Govt.)
benefit_summary: Boarding house stipend of Rs.65/day/student (including LPG subsidy and Rs.1/day cleaning charge) for 322 days/year, for ST students in Class 1-12 in Tripura living in government/approved NGO hostels, whose home is beyond 3km from school.
caveats: Only applicable to students actually residing in a government-run or approved NGO-run hostel.

title: Bidya Lakshmi Loan
benefit_summary: Education loan of Rs.5-10 lakh at 4% interest (0.5% discount for women) for children of serving Assam state government employees admitted to professional/technical courses, covering fees, books, equipment, and study-abroad costs; loans above Rs.10 lakh available from SBI at market rate.
caveats: NOT a general-public scheme -- restricted to wards of currently serving Assam state government employees with 5+ years of residual pensionable service; parent must repay even if student doesn't get a job after the course; student must not have failed the last qualifying exam.

title: Bebe Nanki Laadli Beti Kalyan Scheme
benefit_summary: Total financial assistance of Rs.61,000-81,000 (staged via LIC) for a girl child born on/after 1 Jan 2011 in Punjab: Rs.2,100 at birth, at age 3 (post-immunization), at Class I admission, and at Class IX admission, Rs.31,000 at age 18 (Class XII pass), plus a monthly scholarship of Rs.100 (Class I-VI) or Rs.200 (Class VII-XII).
caveats: Family annual income must be below Rs.30,000 (proof via Blue Card); benefit stops permanently if the girl drops out of school; also covers abandoned girls in orphanages/Children's Homes.

title: Building And Other Construction Scholarship
benefit_summary: Scholarship of roughly Rs.2,000-40,000/year (Class 6 through professional courses), with an extra 20% for girls, for SC-category students pursuing ITI/Polytechnic/technical education in Odisha, now administered under the Nirman Shramik Kalyan Yojana education assistance component.
caveats: Living costs are not covered under this component.

title: Biju Pucca Ghar Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.1,20,000 (non-IAP districts) or Rs.1,30,000 (IAP/mining-affected districts) for constructing a Pucca house, released in 4 installments tied to construction progress, for EWS households living in kutcha houses in Odisha, preferentially sanctioned to the woman head of household.
caveats: RENAMED to Antyodaya Gruha Yojana, covering low-income kutcha-house households not covered by PMAY-Gramin. Applicant must not already own a pucca house; no contractor may be involved in construction.

title: Biju Patnaik Sports Award for Best Contribution to promotion of Sports and Games
benefit_summary: Cash award of Rs.1,00,000 (this category's rate, per the original scheme design) plus a statue, scroll of honour, and blazer, for individuals/organizations aged 45+ who substantially contributed to sports administration/support in Odisha for at least 7 years' residence.
caveats: RENAMED: the scheme was renamed 'Odisha Rajya Krida Samman' in July 2024 by the state government; the Lifetime Achievement category is confirmed at Rs.3,00,000, but this specific category's updated rate is not individually confirmed post-rename. Given once per lifetime; can be awarded posthumously.

title: Biju Patnaik Sports Award for Excellence in Coaching
benefit_summary: Cash award of Rs.1,00,000 (this category's original rate) plus a statue, scroll of honour, and blazer, for coaches in Odisha (7+ years' residence) who have produced sportspersons achieving national/international excellence.
caveats: RENAMED: the scheme was renamed 'Odisha Rajya Krida Samman' in July 2024; this category's updated rate is not individually confirmed post-rename (Lifetime Achievement category confirmed at Rs.3,00,000). Given once per lifetime; can be awarded posthumously.

title: Biju Patnaik Sports Award for Excellence in Sports Journalism
benefit_summary: Cash award of Rs.50,000 plus a statue, scroll of honour, and blazer, for accredited/freelance sports journalists in Odisha (7+ years' residence) recognized for significant sports journalism work.
caveats: RENAMED: the scheme was renamed 'Odisha Rajya Krida Samman' in July 2024; this category's updated rate is not individually confirmed post-rename. Given once per lifetime; can be awarded posthumously.

title: Biju Patnaik Sports Award for Lifetime Achievement in Promotion of Sports & Games
benefit_summary: Cash award of Rs.3,00,000 plus a statue, scroll of honour, and blazer, for retired sportspersons in Odisha (45+, 7+ years residence) who continued contributing to sports promotion after their active career and have not tested positive for banned substances.
caveats: RENAMED: the scheme was renamed Odisha Rajya Krida Samman in July 2024; this Lifetime Achievement category rate (Rs.3,00,000) is confirmed post-rename, unlike other categories. Given once per lifetime; can be awarded posthumously; not eligible if convicted of a criminal offence or found positive for performance-enhancing substances.

title: Biju Patnaik Sports Award for Outstanding Performance in Sports and Games for the Year
benefit_summary: Cash award of Rs.2,00,000 (this category's original rate) plus a statue, scroll of honour, and blazer, for Odisha sportspersons (7+ years' residence) with outstanding performance during the year.
caveats: RENAMED: the scheme was renamed 'Odisha Rajya Krida Samman' in July 2024; this category's updated rate is not individually confirmed post-rename. Not eligible if tested positive for banned substances; given once per lifetime; can be posthumous. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] The July 2024 rename to 'Odisha Rajya Krida Samman' was announced then REVERSED within 1-2 days after public backlash over dropping Biju Patnaik's name; CM Mohan Charan Majhi confirmed it would not proceed. The award remains officially named 'Biju Patnaik Sports Award' (confirmed via 2025-cycle award ceremony coverage and live myscheme.gov.in listing). Do not treat the rename as settled fact.

title: Bihar Rajya Fasal Sahayata Yojna
benefit_summary: Crop-loss compensation for Bihar farmers (own-land or tenant/sharecropper) for notified paddy/maize/soybean crops: Rs.7,500/hectare (irrigated) up to 2 hectares for up to 20% yield loss, or Rs.10,000/hectare for greater loss; higher slabs Rs.15,000-20,000/ha noted in some cases.
caveats: Applies only to notified crops in notified gram panchayats/blocks; requires land documents dated after 31-03-2022.

title: Banishree Scholarship
benefit_summary: Monthly scholarship for students with disabilities in Odisha, not covered by Central Government scholarships: Rs.400 (Class I-V), Rs.500 (VI-X), Rs.600 (+2/+3), Rs.700 (PG/technical/vocational); plus a reader's allowance (Rs.200/300/400 per month (primary/middle-high/higher-PG-technical)) for visually impaired students and Rs.200/month transport allowance for 75%+ orthopedic disability.
caveats: Family income must not exceed Rs.60,000/year (waived for BPL families); not available if already receiving a similar Central Government scholarship; continues regardless of pass/fail as long as regularly enrolled. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Per Odisha Gazette Resolution 394/SSEPD (11.01.2022): Reader's Allowance is Rs.200 (primary)/Rs.300 (middle-high)/Rs.400 (higher/PG/technical) per month, not capped at Rs.200; Transport Allowance for 75%+ orthopedic disability is Rs.200/month, not Rs.100.

title: Bihar Student Credit Card Scheme
benefit_summary: Education loan up to Rs.4,00,000 for Bihar students (12th pass, under 25) admitted to higher education/professional courses, with interest moving toward 0% for eligible categories in 2026 (previously 4%/1% concessional).
caveats: Not applicable if the student already holds a degree at the same level (exception for technical/managerial courses); if the student drops out, remaining loan is not disbursed.

title: Biju Swasthya Kalyan Yojana - Cashless Health Care In State Government Hospitals
benefit_summary: Cashless health coverage of Rs.5,00,000/year per family (additional Rs.5,00,000 for women members after exhausting the initial limit) at empanelled hospitals, for NFSA/SFSS card holders or those with income below Rs.50,000 (rural)/Rs.60,000 (urban) in Odisha.
caveats: RENAMED to Gopabandhu Jana Arogya Yojana (GJAY), merged/integrated with PM-JAY under a unified 'BSKY Nabin Card' from Dec 2024. No direct enrollment needed for NFSA/SFSS families; income certificate needed only for those without such cards.

title: Bank Tie-Up Scheme
benefit_summary: Bank loan with a capital subsidy of up to 50% (max Rs.10,000) for SC, BPL residents of Punjab, arranged via PSCLDFC.
caveats: Income limit is Rs.67,649/year (rural) or Rs.88,756/year (urban); applicant must not already be availing this scheme's benefits.

title: Bhagyalaxmi Scheme
benefit_summary: CORRECTED (2021+ model): Rs.3,000/year deposited into a Sukanya Samriddhi Account for 15 years (maturing at ~Rs.1,27,000), plus annual scholarships (Rs.300-1,000 up to 10th standard) and health insurance up to Rs.25,000/year, for up to 2 girl children per BPL family in Karnataka.
caveats: Girl must be born after 31 March 2006, registered within a year of birth, properly immunized, not engaged in child labor, and unmarried before 18; 2nd child registration requires a family planning certificate from parents.

title: Cash Award (MBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Annual cash prizes of Rs.1,000/750/500 (1st/2nd/3rd rank) to the top 3 male and top 3 female SSLC-scoring children of registered construction workers in each district of Meghalaya.
caveats: Parent must be an active, registered member of the Meghalaya BOCW Welfare Board.

title: Mahila Samriddhi Yojana
benefit_summary: Microfinance loan of up to Rs.1,25,000 (90% of a project cost up to Rs.1.4 lakh) at concessional interest (~4% p.a.) for women aged 18-55 from economically/socially backward classes, directly or via SHGs, repayable within 3.5 years including a 6-month moratorium.
caveats: Administered by NSFDC/NBCFDC via State Channelizing Agencies; family annual income must be below Rs.3 lakh.

title: Concessional Bus Travel Facility to Women above 60 years of age- Punjab
benefit_summary: 50% concession in bus fare on Punjab Roadways and PRTC buses for women aged 60+ residing in Punjab.
caveats: CORRECTED: this is a 50% fare concession, not free travel (a separate scheme provides free travel for all women). 2026 update replaces Aadhaar-linked passes with Digital Smart Cards.

title: Credit Card Scheme For Artisans And Weavers Of Handicrafts And Handloom Sector
benefit_summary: Collateral-free credit card with a maximum limit of Rs.2,00,000 (loan component Rs.1,80,000 + beneficiary contribution Rs.20,000) and 7% interest subvention over 5 years, for registered artisans and weavers in J&K.
caveats: Requires registration with the Handicrafts and Handloom Department, J&K; credit limit valid for 5 years subject to annual review.

title: Central Sector Scheme of National Fellowship for Providing Fellowship to Scheduled Caste Students to Pursue M.Phil. & PhD
benefit_summary: Fellowship of Rs.37,000/month (JRF, years 1-2) and Rs.42,000/month (SRF, years 3-5), plus contingency grant (Rs.10,000/year Humanities, Rs.12,000/year Sciences), for SC students pursuing M.Phil/PhD who qualify UGC-NET-JRF or UGC-CSIR-NET-JRF, at UGC-recognized institutions.
caveats: 2,000 fellowship slots/year (1,500 Humanities/Social Sciences, 500 Science), over and above normal reservation quota; granted up to 5 years max; cannot hold another fellowship/scholarship simultaneously.

title: Competitive Exam Coaching
benefit_summary: Free competitive-exam coaching (via Mankyi Lal Verma Tribal Research and Training Institute or Scheduled Area Project Officer) plus a hostel/relocation allowance up to Rs.40,000/year, expanded to 30,000 seats covering SC/ST/OBC/EBC/Minority/EWS students with family income up to Rs.8 lakh/year.
caveats: Originally restricted to ST students in 8 districts (Banswara, Chittorgarh, Dungarpur, Pali, Sirohi, Udaipur, Rajsamand, Pratapgarh); note says 'cec' may be a duplicate label for the broader Anuprati coaching scheme -- recommend cross-checking against related scheme records. Can be availed only once per student.

title: Construction of Fish Markets
benefit_summary: Subsidy for local bodies (Municipalities/Village Panchayats) in Goa to construct fish markets: 100% subsidy (up to Rs.5,00,000) if the body's annual income is under Rs.2,00,000, or 75% (up to Rs.5,00,000) otherwise. Not an individual benefit.
caveats: Applicant must be a local body (Municipality/Village Panchayat), not an individual.

title: Chief Minister Agriculture and Food Processing Scheme
benefit_summary: Credit-linked back-ended subsidy of 30% of project cost (max Rs.50 lakh) for setting up/upgrading agro and food processing units (including cold chain) in Maharashtra, disbursed in two installments after project completion and full commercial production.
caveats: One beneficiary per family, one-time only (expansion projects excepted); loan amount must be at least 1.5x the subsidy; not independently confirmed on a .gov.in page, only cross-corroborated -- treat as high-confidence but not certain.

title: Chief Minister Sustainable Agriculture Irrigation Scheme - Magel Tyala Shettale (Individual Farm Pond)
benefit_summary: Subsidy of Rs.14,433 to Rs.75,000 (depending on farm pond size) for individual farmers in Maharashtra to construct a farm pond for protective irrigation.
caveats: Minimum land holding 0.20 ha (Konkan region) or 0.40 ha (rest of Maharashtra); no advance payment -- construction must be pre-approved before starting; not eligible if already availed subsidy for a farm pond/community tank/bodi under any government scheme.

title: Capital Investment Subsidy (for New and Existing Industries) under MESIFAI
benefit_summary: Capital investment subsidy on land/building/plant/machinery for industrial units in Puducherry: 40% (max Rs.40 lakh) Micro/Small enterprises, 35% (max Rs.35 lakh) Medium/Large enterprises, 45% (max Rs.75 lakh) Women/SC/ST entrepreneurs.
caveats: Unit must provide at least 60% local (Puducherry) employment, maintained during the scheme period; unit must not dispose of fixed assets for 5 years from application/disbursement; SC/ST/women category units must be fully owned by that category.

title: Capital Investment Subsidy: 5% Additional Capital Investment Subsidy to Karaikal Region (MESIFAI)
benefit_summary: 5% additional capital investment incentive (on top of existing MESIFAI subsidy rates) for priority/thrust-area industrial units located in the Karaikal region of Puducherry: e.g. 30% (max Rs.30 lakh) for SC/ST/Women entrepreneurs, 25% (max Rs.25 lakh) for IT industries, 40% (max Rs.35 lakh) for Small/Micro Thrust Area enterprises.
caveats: Applicant must have an industrial unit specifically in Karaikal region; application must be filed within 1 year of production commencement (new units) or expansion completion (existing units).

title: Capital Investment Subsidy: IT/ITES Industries (MESIFAI)
benefit_summary: 20% subsidy on plant and machinery investment (max Rs.20,00,000) for new IT/ITES industrial units in Puducherry that started production on or after 6 November 2002.
caveats: Disbursed in a single installment; via bank if financed, or directly to entrepreneur if self-financed.

title: Capital Investment Subsidy: Physically Handicapped Persons/Ex-Servicemen (MESIFAI)
benefit_summary: 25% capital investment subsidy (max Rs.25,00,000) on land/building/plant/machinery for new micro and small manufacturing units in Puducherry started on/after 5 August 2009 by physically handicapped entrepreneurs (40%+ disability) or Ex-Servicemen.
caveats: Disbursed in a single installment where possible.

title: Capital Investment Subsidy: SC/ST/Women Entrepreneurs (MESIFAI)
benefit_summary: 25% capital investment subsidy on land/building/plant/machinery (max Rs.25,00,000) for SC/ST/Women entrepreneurs' small/micro manufacturing units in Puducherry started on/after 27 March 2002; SC/ST entrepreneurs get a higher cumulative max of Rs.50,00,000 for investments made on/after 24 August 2011.
caveats: Second-hand machinery eligible only if directly/agent-imported with proper documentation.

title: Capital Investment Subsidy: Thrust Area Industries (MESIFAI)
benefit_summary: Subsidy on plant and machinery investment for thrust-area industries in Puducherry (electronics, biotech, food/agro processing, leather/footwear, light engineering, textiles) started on/after 3 April 2003: 20% (max Rs.20,00,000) for large/medium enterprises, 35% (max Rs.30,00,000) for small/micro enterprises.
caveats: Disbursed in a single installment where possible; application must be filed within 1 year of production/expansion.

title: Chhatraon Ke Liye Protsahan Rashi
benefit_summary: Scholarship for girls in Rajasthan pursuing agricultural studies: Rs.15,000/year (Class 11-12), Rs.25,000/year (undergraduate agriculture/horticulture/dairy programs), Rs.25,000/year (M.Sc. Agriculture), Rs.40,000/year (PhD in Agriculture, up to 3 years).
caveats: CORRECTED: rates are tiered by education level, not a flat Rs.15,000. Only for girls studying agriculture-related subjects at government-recognized institutions.

title: Chief Minister's Shasakt Kisan Yojana
benefit_summary: Cash assistance of Rs.1,00,000/hectare for tea plantation or Rs.80,000/hectare for rubber plantation, plus seedlings, fencing material, tools, and cultivation inputs, for progressive farmers of any category in Arunachal Pradesh.
caveats: Land documents (LPC/allotment) must be certified by GB/HGB/PRI and countersigned by local district administration.

title: Chief Minister's Jeevan Jyoti Swaniyojan Yojana
benefit_summary: Institutional credit up to Rs.6,00,000 with a margin money subsidy of 50% of project cost (max Rs.40,000 individually, or Rs.1,60,000 for a 4-member Joint Liability Group) for self-employment ventures (agriculture, horticulture, fishery, handloom, poultry, handicrafts, small business, etc.) for educated unemployed youth aged 18-37 in Assam.
caveats: Minimum Class X education (relaxed to Class V for women in handloom/sericulture, Class VII for men in agriculture/animal husbandry); typically implemented via a minimum 4-member group; annual income must not exceed Rs.25,000.

title: Chief Minister's Yuva Kaushal Yojana
benefit_summary: Free high-end vocational training with a guaranteed minimum 70% job placement, a monthly stipend of Rs.3,000 (in-state) or Rs.300/day (out-of-state training, covering boarding/lodging/transport/fees), plus free uniforms/books, for Arunachal Pradesh youth (Class X pass minimum).
caveats: Stipend disbursed via DBT after verification.

title: Chief Minister Arogya Arunachal Yojana
benefit_summary: Cashless health insurance coverage up to Rs.5,00,000 per family per year (including pre-existing diseases, 3 days pre-hospitalization, 10 days post-hospitalization) for Arunachal Pradesh Scheduled Tribe (APST) members and state government employees/dependents.
caveats: Recently expanded to cover retired state government employees' families; non-APST residents of Changlang, Lohit, or Namsai districts also eligible with a Resident Certificate.

title: Cm Anuprati Coaching Scheme
benefit_summary: Free coaching, study material, and mentorship for competitive exams (IAS/RAS etc.) for disadvantaged students in Rajasthan, plus hostel/relocation allowance up to Rs 40,000/year.
caveats: Family income cap Rs 8 lakh/year (per verification note; Eligibility section in source was empty). Covers SC/ST/OBC/MBC/EWS/Minority categories. 30,000 seats available (expanded from 15,000).

title: Chief Minister's State Disability Pension Scheme - Sikkim
benefit_summary: Monthly pension of Rs 1,500 for persons with 40%+ disability from BPL households in Sikkim.
caveats: Mutually exclusive with IGNDPS (Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme) - applicant must not already receive that pension. Requires a PM Jan Dhan Yojana bank account.

title: CHIEF MINISTER EMPLOYMENT GENERATION PROGRAMME (CMEGP)
benefit_summary: Backend capital subsidy of 15-35% of project cost (up to Rs 20 lakh for service/business or Rs 50 lakh for manufacturing) for new self-employment ventures, via bank term loan.
caveats: Age relaxed by 5 years (to 50) for SC/ST/OBC/women/ex-servicemen/disabled applicants. Minimum 7th std pass required for projects up to Rs 10 lakh; 10th std pass for projects above Rs 25 lakh.

title: Chief Minister Ekal Nari Samman Pension Yojana
benefit_summary: Monthly pension for widowed, divorced, or abandoned women in Rajasthan without adequate income: Rs 1,000/month (age 18-75) and Rs 1,500/month (age 75+), per a 2023 revision.
caveats: 2023 revision replaced the original age-tiered amounts (Rs500/750/1000/1500 by age band) with a flat Rs1,000 (18-75) and Rs1,500 (75+).

title: Chief Minister's Free Cancer Chemotherapy Scheme
benefit_summary: Free chemotherapy medicines, consultation, and counseling for cancer patients who are Arunachal Pradesh state government employees/dependents; ceiling Rs 5 lakh/patient/year.
caveats: CORRECTED: ceiling is Rs 5 lakh/patient/year, not Rs 10 lakh as some sources show. MoU with Tata Memorial Hospital Mumbai; limited to 1000 patients/year.

title: Chief Minister's Girl Child Protection Scheme-I
benefit_summary: Rs 50,000 fixed deposit for one girl child of low-income Tamil Nadu families (income <=Rs72,000/yr), plus Rs1,800/year incentive from year 6; FD + interest paid at 18 if she appears for the 10th std board exam.
caveats: Only for families with exactly one girl child and no male child (no future male adoption allowed). One parent must be sterilized before age 40. Also open to Sri Lankan Tamil refugee-camp girls in TN. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Income ceiling raised from Rs.72,000 (2014 rate) to Rs.1,20,000/year per Dec 10, 2024 TN Social Welfare Dept circular; confirmed on tnsocialwelfare.tn.gov.in.

title: Chief Minister's Girl Child Protection Scheme-II
benefit_summary: Rs 25,000 fixed deposit each for two girl children of low-income Tamil Nadu families (income <=Rs72,000/yr), plus Rs1,800/year incentive from year 6; FD + interest paid at 18 if she appears for the 10th std board exam.
caveats: Only for families with exactly two girl children and no male child. One parent must be sterilized before age 40. Also open to Sri Lankan Tamil refugee-camp girls in TN. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Income ceiling raised from Rs.72,000 to Rs.1,20,000/year; confirmed on the same official page as Scheme-I (tnsocialwelfare.tn.gov.in).

title: Chief Minister Housing Assistance Programme
benefit_summary: Cost-sharing housing assistance in Meghalaya: EWS families get 3 bundles of aluminium roofing sheets; LIG families get a Rs 75,000 cash grant toward house construction (total house cost ~Rs2.3 lakh).
caveats: Beneficiary must not already own a house in Meghalaya (self/spouse/dependents) for the credit-linked subsidy component, nor have received a prior housing loan from govt/co-op. House cannot be sublet or sold after construction.

title: Chief Minister's Health Insurance Scheme - Nagaland
benefit_summary: Cashless family health insurance in Nagaland: Rs 5 lakh/family/year (general residents not already covered by AB PM-JAY) or Rs 20 lakh/family/year (state govt employees/pensioners under CMHIS-EP).
caveats: Two tiers: CMHIS(GEN) for general permanent/indigenous residents not covered under AB PM-JAY; CMHIS(EP) for state govt employees/pensioners. OPD and standalone diagnostics not covered.

title: Chief Minister's Krishi Rinn Yojana
benefit_summary: Zero-interest crop loans/KCC limits up to Rs 3 lakh for Arunachal Pradesh farmers: 4% state interest subvention plus an extra 3% rebate for timely repayment.
caveats: Requires a good repayment track record; benefit realized via bank/NABARD reimbursement, not a direct cash payout.

title: Chief Minister's Krishi Samuh Yojana
benefit_summary: Financial assistance to Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) in Arunachal Pradesh: Rs 4.75 lakh/FPO/year subsidy plus a Rs 10 lakh revolving fund per FPO for mobilization, training, registration, and office setup.
caveats: Benefit flows to the FPO/society, not directly to individual farmers; FPO must be a registered body with an active bank account 6+ months.

title: Chhattisgarh Mukhyamantri Kanya Vivah Yojana
benefit_summary: Marriage assistance for daughters of BPL families in Chhattisgarh: Rs 25,000 total (plus Rs5,000 makeup, Rs14,000 gifts, Rs1,000 bank draft to bride) or Rs5,000 for group marriages; also covers widows/orphans/destitute girls.
caveats: Max two girls per BPL family; scheme promotes group marriages to prevent dowry.

title: Chief Minister Ladli Behna Yojana
benefit_summary: Monthly cash transfer to eligible women in Madhya Pradesh: Rs 1,500/month (Rs18,000/year), per a 2023 revision (up from Rs1,250).
caveats: A proposed Rs3,000/month hike is a political promise NOT yet implemented as of July 2026 - do not report it. Excludes families with an income-tax payer or government pensioner.

title: Chief Minister's Overseas Scholarship Scheme for Minorities
benefit_summary: Up to Rs 20 lakh (or actual admission-letter cost, whichever lower) for postgraduate/PhD study abroad for Telangana minority-community students, paid in 2 installments, plus one-way economy airfare and visa costs.
caveats: One award per family, one per lifetime; must join university within 1 year of selection; restricted to USA/UK/Australia/Canada/Singapore/Germany/NZ/Japan/France/South Korea.

title: Chief Minister Specially Abled Samman Pension Scheme
benefit_summary: Monthly pension for persons with 40%+ disability in Rajasthan: Rs 750/month (below 55 women/58 men), Rs 1,000/month (55/58-74), Rs 1,250/month (75+), Rs 1,500/month for silicosis patients, and Rs 2,500/month (the highest tier) for leprosy-free/leprosy-cured persons.
caveats: Verification note only explicitly confirms the Rs750 and Rs1,000 tiers - the higher elderly/leprosy-free tiers are per original scheme text but unconfirmed by verification. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Fixed tier misattribution: Rs 1,500/month is the silicosis tier, not leprosy-free. The separate, higher Rs 2,500/month leprosy-free tier was missing entirely and has been added.

title: Chief Ministers Special Rural Development Fund (CMSRDF)
benefit_summary: Local-area development fund for rural/semi-rural Meghalaya: MLA/NGO-nominated infrastructure and wage-employment projects (roads, footbridges, community halls, ambulances etc.), not a direct individual cash benefit.
caveats: Not an individual welfare payment - beneficiaries are villages/SHGs via MLA/NGO nomination.

title: Chief Ministergi Shotharabasingi Tengbang
benefit_summary: Free travel with one escort (for intellectual disabilities) or 50% travel concession on Manipur State Transport (for other listed disabilities); the same umbrella scheme also includes MSSD loans, scholarships, and a Rs 2 lakh family insurance component per verification note.
caveats: Component amounts vary across the umbrella scheme's sub-benefits.

title: Chief Minister's UPSC Combined Civil Services Coaching Scheme
benefit_summary: Free UPSC Civil Services coaching (Rs70,000/student for General Studies + Rs30,000 for Optional papers) for APST candidates of Arunachal Pradesh, plus Rs2 lakh on clearing Prelims and Rs3 lakh on clearing Mains, and Rs2 lakh one-time for NDA/CDS/IFS/IES clearers.
caveats: Restricted to Arunachal Pradesh Scheduled Tribe (APST) candidates only; training cost capped at 25 students per batch.

title: Coconut Palm Insurance Scheme
benefit_summary: Insurance for coconut palms (minimum 5 nut-bearing palms) against natural perils: sum insured Rs900/palm (age 4-15yrs) or Rs1,750/palm (16-60yrs); farmer pays only 25% of the premium, the rest is subsidized by the Coconut Development Board (50%) and state government (25%).
caveats: Separate scheme from PMFBY (which excludes perennial coconut palms). Insurable age group is 4-60 years for dwarf/hybrid, 7-60 for tall varieties; partial insurance of a plantation is not allowed (minimum 5 palms in a contiguous area).

title: Capital Subsidy
benefit_summary: 25% capital subsidy on eligible plant & machinery for new MSME manufacturing enterprises in Tamil Nadu (cap Rs50 lakh under the 2021 Industrial Policy, per verification), plus additional 5-10% subsidy (cap Rs5-25 lakh) for women/SC/ST/disabled/transgender entrepreneurs, micro-enterprises, expansions, and clean-tech adoption.
caveats: CORRECTED: original scheme document cites a Rs150 lakh cap; verification confirms the current cap is Rs50 lakh under the 2021 Industrial Policy - use Rs50 lakh as the current figure.

title: Cancer Suraksha Scheme
benefit_summary: Free cancer treatment for BPL children under 18 (extendable one more year if mid-treatment) in Kerala; initial expenditure ceiling Rs 50,000/child, which can be exceeded with hospital-committee approval, making treatment effectively cashless.
caveats: Separate from, but complementary to, Karunya Arogya Suraksha Padhathi (broader Rs5 lakh/year cashless scheme).

title: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Post-Matric Scholarship for OBC Students for studying in India
benefit_summary: Maintenance allowance for OBC post-matric students: Rs5,000-20,000/year by course group (now under the PM-YASASVI umbrella since 2021-22); income ceiling per verification note is Rs2.5 lakh/year (original scheme text stated Rs1.5 lakh).
caveats: Scheme subsumed into PM-YASASVI umbrella from 2021-22. Restricted to a maximum of two boys per family (no restriction on girls).

title: Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Pre-matric Scholarship to Other Backward Classes (OBC) for Studies in India
benefit_summary: Consolidated scholarship for OBC pre-matric students (Class IX-X, govt school) of approx. Rs4,000/year, income ceiling Rs2.5 lakh (per verification note; scheme subsumed into PM-YASASVI umbrella).
caveats: Minimum 60% attendance required; cannot be combined with any other pre-matric scholarship; 30% of beneficiaries reserved for girls, 5% for students with disabilities.

title: Central Sector Scheme for Rehabilitation of Bonded Labourer
benefit_summary: Rehabilitation assistance for rescued bonded labourers: Rs1 lakh (adult male), Rs2 lakh (women/children/orphans/forced-labour victims), Rs3 lakh (extreme cases - transgender/trafficking/sexual-exploitation victims), partly via annuity scheme plus Direct Benefit Transfer.
caveats: [Fix 2026-07-23] Occupation constraint removed from structured matching -- this is specifically for rescued bonded labourers, a rescue-status our FLOW does not capture, not a general occupation category.

title: Central Sector Scheme Of Scholarship For College And University Students
benefit_summary: Merit scholarship for students in the top 20th percentile of their board in Class 12, pursuing regular degree courses: Rs.12,000/year (flat) (UG years 1-3), Rs20,000/year (year 4-5 or PG).
caveats: Cannot be combined with any other scholarship or fee-waiver scheme; renewal each year requires minimum 50% marks and 75% attendance. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] UG years 1-3 rate is a flat Rs.12,000/year (not a Rs.10,000-12,000 range), effective FY2024-25 -- the Rs.10,000 rate was superseded.

title: Contributory Social Security Scheme
benefit_summary: Contributory pension savings for J&K marginal workers: state contributes Rs300/quarter + beneficiary Rs200/quarter into a joint account for 5-10 years; matured amount is withdrawable or re-investable in a pension scheme, with insurance cover included.
caveats: Applicant or spouse must not already be a beneficiary of another similar existing scheme.

title: Cattle Shed Subsidy Scheme under Scheduled Castes Sub Plan (SC Category)
benefit_summary: Rs30,000 or 50% of cattle-shed construction cost (whichever is less) for Scheduled Caste beneficiaries in Gujarat owning at least 2 animals.
caveats: Requires land owned or leased (10+ years) by the beneficiary.

title: Coir Udyami Yojana
benefit_summary: 40% government subsidy on coir-unit project cost (cap Rs10 lakh, plus working capital up to 25% of cost); 55% bank credit, 5% beneficiary contribution.
caveats: Special focus on SC/ST and North-East region applicants per verification note. Open to individuals, SHGs, NGOs, co-operatives, and trusts.

title: Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) Internship Scheme
benefit_summary: Rs10,000/month stipend for a 1-2 month internship with the Central Vigilance Commission for graduate/postgraduate/research students, preferably in Law/IT/MBA/Social Sciences.
caveats: Internship is not a job and doesn't guarantee future employment; only about 3 interns selected per year.

title: Co-Working Space/ Incubators/ Accelerators Subsidy Scheme
benefit_summary: Reimbursement of 50% of seat cost at SPC-listed co-working spaces (cap Rs3,000/seat), incubators (cap Rs5,000/seat), or accelerators (cap Rs6,000/seat), up to 8 seats/startup, for Goa Startup Promotion Cell-certified startups.
caveats: Requires Aadhaar-linked bank account for digital payments to co-working providers.

title: 60% and above Disability Allowances
benefit_summary: Monthly disability pension in Tripura of Rs5,000 (raised from Rs2,000 around Aug 2025) for persons with 60%+ disability, age 10+, family income <=Rs1 lakh/year, no government employee in family.

title: Dr Ambedkar Central Sector Scheme of Interest Subsidy on Educational Loans for Overseas Studies for Other Backward Classes (OBCs) and Economically Bac
benefit_summary: Interest subsidy on education loans (up to Rs20 lakh) for OBC/EBC students pursuing Masters/MPhil/PhD abroad, covering the full interest during the moratorium period.
caveats: 50% of the outlay is earmarked for girl candidates. A separate, lower EBC-specific income ceiling of Rs2.5 lakh applies per verification note (the Rs8 lakh figure is the general/OBC ceiling).

title: Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam Shramik Pravidhik Shiksha Sahaayata Yojana
benefit_summary: Financial assistance for technical/professional education of children of registered UP shop/factory workers earning <=Rs15,000/month: Rs25,000 (degree), Rs15,000 (diploma), Rs10,000 (certificate courses).
caveats: Income figure is a monthly salary cap (Rs15,000/month), converted here to an annual equivalent.

title: Dhanvantari Arogya Rath Yojana (GBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Free onsite primary healthcare (checkups, common disease treatment, basic diagnostics, medicines) for registered Gujarat construction workers and their families, via a mobile Dhanvantari Arogya Rath van.

title: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission
benefit_summary: Flagship rural livelihoods mission organizing rural poor households (preferably women) into bank-linked Self Help Groups for financial inclusion, livelihood promotion, and skill training; FY26-27 allocation raised to Rs17,280 crore, targeting roughly 100 million rural women via the 'Lakhpati Didi' push.
caveats: Benefit is institutional/group-based (SHG formation, training, bank linkage) rather than a direct individual cash payout.

title: Death Benefit (GBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Flat Rs.50,000 death compensation (under insurance coverage) to a Goa construction worker's family, announced by CM Pramod Sawant on Labour Day (1 May 2026), replacing the earlier differentiated Rs.30,000 (natural)/Rs.1,00,000 (accidental) structure. A new Rs.25,000 one-time injury assistance benefit was introduced at the same time.
caveats: Figures possibly updated/expanded per a May 2026 CM Sawant Labour Day announcement, which also added a new Rs25,000 construction-injury assistance (not yet reflected in this record) - verify current tier structure locally. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Updated to lead with the current May 2026 announcement (Rs.50,000 flat + Rs.25,000 injury benefit) rather than presenting the superseded Rs.30,000/Rs.1,00,000 tiers as current, per goemkarponn.com and Prudent Media.

title: Death Benefit (A.B.O.C.W.W.B)
benefit_summary: Financial assistance to nominee/dependent of a registered Assam construction worker on death: Rs.50,000 for natural death, Rs.3,00,000 for accidental death, plus a separate Rs.5,000 funeral-expense assistance.
caveats: Resolved per the official Assam Commissionerate of Labour page: Rs.50,000 (natural)/Rs.3,00,000 (accidental) + Rs.5,000 funeral assistance are the correct current figures. The Rs.1,00,000/Rs.2,00,000 'verification note' alternative was unsupported and has been dropped -- it likely conflated this with the separate PMJJBY/PMSBY central insurance add-on. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Ambiguity resolved in favor of the original Rs.50,000/Rs.3,00,000 figures per direct fetch of labourcommissioner.assam.gov.in.

title: Double Bedroom Housing Scheme (2BHK Scheme)
benefit_summary: Free 560 sqft 2BHK house with land, no beneficiary contribution, for BPL families in Telangana (with rural/urban reservation for SC/ST/minorities). Superseded after Dec 2023 government change by 'Indiramma Illu', offering Rs5 lakh/house in 4 phases for landowners plus housing colonies for the landless.
caveats: Original 2BHK scheme replaced; unfinished 2BHK units are being completed and distributed under the new Indiramma Illu banner.

title: Disablement Benefit Scheme (PBAOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs75,000 Direct Benefit Transfer (within 1 month of application) for registered Puducherry construction workers who become disabled, based on a Disablement Certificate.

title: Dr. Baba Saheb Ambedkar Loan for Higher Study in Foreign Countries
benefit_summary: Rs15 lakh loan at 4% interest for Scheduled Caste students of Gujarat pursuing higher studies (PG/PhD/technical/professional courses) abroad; no income limit.
caveats: Maximum of two persons per family may benefit; loan repayment begins 6 months after course completion, to be repaid within 10 years.

title: Dayanand Bandodkar Scheme For Higher Education For Orphans
benefit_summary: Full fee waiver (tuition/library/lab/development fees plus hostel/food/transport charges) for students orphaned of both parents pursuing UG/PG degree courses in Goa.
caveats: Applicant must be born in Goa or a Goa resident of 15+ years, and have passed the qualifying exam from a Goa institution.

title: Dependent Children Pension Scheme - Punjab
benefit_summary: Rs1,500/month pension for children under 21 in Punjab who have lost one/both parents, or whose parents are physically/mentally incapacitated, family income <=Rs60,000/year.

title: Dr. Dharmambal Ammaiyar Ninaivu Widow Remarriage Assistance Scheme-I
benefit_summary: Rs25,000 (Rs15,000 via Electronic Clearing Service + Rs10,000 as a National Savings Certificate) plus an 8g 22-carat gold coin, for widow remarriage in Tamil Nadu (bride 20+, no education requirement).

title: Dr. Dharmambal Ammaiyar Ninaivu Widow Remarriage Assistance Scheme-II
benefit_summary: Rs.50,000 (Rs.30,000 ECS + Rs.20,000 NSC) plus an 8g 22-carat gold coin, for widow remarriage in Tamil Nadu, specifically for widows holding a degree/diploma (this is 'Scheme-II').
caveats: Distinguished from Scheme-I (non-graduate widows, Rs.25,000 = Rs.15,000 ECS + Rs.10,000 NSC, same gold coin) by requiring the widow to hold a degree/diploma. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Fixed reversed figures: Scheme-II (graduate/diploma widows) pays Rs.50,000, not Rs.25,000 -- Rs.25,000 is Scheme-I's amount. Confirmed via tnsocialwelfare.tn.gov.in.

title: Deen Dayal Disabled Rehabilitation Scheme
benefit_summary: Central grant-in-aid to registered voluntary organizations (NGOs) for disability rehabilitation services - early intervention, special education, vocational training, skill development - for persons with disabilities, via the NGO Darpan and e-Anudaan portals.
caveats: Funding flows to NGOs/organizations, not directly to individual persons with disabilities.

title: D. D. Kosambi Research Fellowship Scheme
benefit_summary: Research fellowship on Goa-related topics: Rs15,000/month (junior category, up to age 35, max 2 years), Rs20,000/month (senior/post-doctoral, max 2 years); up to Rs30,000/month for full-time researchers. One fellowship per category awarded per year.
caveats: Topics must be closely connected to Goan history/culture/society; awarded only once per scholar per category in their lifetime.

title: Dai Didi Mobile Clinic Scheme
benefit_summary: Free mobile healthcare (checkup, treatment, consultation, medicines) delivered door-to-door by all-female medical staff for women and girls in rural Chhattisgarh.
caveats: Beneficiaries do not need to apply anywhere - medical camps come via mobile units to villages.

title: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Bunkar Yojana
benefit_summary: 7% interest subvention on working-capital/short-term credit (confirmed up to Rs2 lakh) for women weavers in Arunachal Pradesh who own a working loom, individually or in groups.

title: Destitute/Deserted Wives Pension Scheme
benefit_summary: Rs1,000/month pension (Rs1,500/month if aged 80+) for legally divorced/deserted destitute women 30+ in Tamil Nadu with fixed assets <=Rs1 lakh, plus a free saree at Pongal/Deepavali and subsidized Anganwadi rice.

title: Distance Education Scholarship–Scholarship For Disabled Students Pursuing Degree, PG Courses
benefit_summary: Up to Rs10,000 scholarship covering registration/course/tuition/exam fees and study materials, for differently-abled Kerala students pursuing degree/PG courses via distance/open-university education.

title: Delhi Family Benefit Scheme
benefit_summary: One-time Rs20,000 payment to the family of a deceased primary breadwinner (aged 18-60 at death) in Delhi, household income <=Rs1 lakh/year, 5+ years Delhi residency.
caveats: Aadhaar is mandatory; requires a singly-operated bank account in NCT Delhi; typically applies to BPL households.

title: Denture Grant (Sainik Welfare)
