benefit_summary: Financial assistance for the purchase of dentures for registered ex-servicemen/widows of ex-servicemen in Puducherry: scheme text states Rs20,000, but verification confirms the current amount is Rs5,000.
caveats: Not eligible if covered under the Ex-Servicemen Contributory Health Scheme (ECHS).

title: Diwali Gift Benefit Scheme (PBAOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs2,000/year Diwali gift via Direct Benefit Transfer for construction workers registered 6+ months with the Puducherry Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board.

title: Pension To The Disabled Person
benefit_summary: Monthly pension for disabled residents of UT Chandigarh (3+ years residency): Rs1,000/month (40-70% disability), Rs2,000/month (>70% disability), family income <=Rs1.5 lakh/year.

title: Dulari Kanya
benefit_summary: Rs30,000 fixed deposit at institutional birth of a girl child (raised from Rs20,000), plus a new Rs20,000 DBT payment on Class XI admission - total Rs50,000 per girl child, max 2 per household, in Arunachal Pradesh.
caveats: Father/guardian must be Scheduled Tribe, domicile resident, or hold a household residential certificate of Arunachal Pradesh.

title: Direct Loans For Business Enterprise
benefit_summary: Business loans up to Rs20 lakh for religious minority (Muslim/Christian/Sikh/Buddhist/Jain) entrepreneurs in Karnataka: 4% interest if family income <Rs8 lakh, 6% if Rs8-15 lakh; secured against property mortgage.
caveats: Loan given to only one member of a family.

title: Direct Lending Scheme
benefit_summary: Subsidy of 50% of loan amount or Rs10,000 (whichever less), for BPL Scheduled Caste individuals or persons with disability in Punjab, age 18-55, for self-employment/business loans.
caveats: Eligible via SC category OR disability (not necessarily both). Family income not considered if the applicant is unemployed and starting their own business.

title: Disable Marriage Scheme (Divyang Lagna Sahay)
benefit_summary: Marriage assistance in Gujarat for disabled persons: Rs75,000 for a mixed couple (one disabled + one non-disabled, raised from Rs50,000 in June 2025), or Rs1,00,000 total (Rs50,000 each) when both spouses are disabled.
caveats: One-time benefit per couple; must apply within 2 years of marriage. Disability percentage threshold varies by condition type (40-100%). It is not fully confirmed whether the both-disabled tier has also risen. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Age eligibility is gender-specific per sje.gujarat.gov.in: bride must be 18+, groom must be 21+. min_age=18 (kept as the lower/bride threshold) understates the requirement for a male applicant aged 18-20, who is NOT actually eligible as groom -- flagging since our schema has no per-gender age field.

title: Dr. Muthulakshmi Reddy Ninaivu Inter-caste Marriage Assistance Scheme-I
benefit_summary: Rs25,000 financial assistance (Scheme-I tier) plus an 8g gold coin for inter-caste marriages in Tamil Nadu where one spouse is SC/ST and the other from a different community.
caveats: A higher Rs50,000 tier applies if the bride holds a degree/diploma, per verification note.

title: Dr. Muthulakshmi Reddy Ninaivu Inter-caste Marriage Assistance Scheme-II
benefit_summary: Rs50,000 financial assistance (tier II, requires the bride to hold a degree/diploma) plus an 8g gold coin, for marriages between Backward/Most Backward Class and Forward Community individuals in Tamil Nadu.

title: Dr. P. G. Solanki Scheme for Loan/Assistance to Medical Graduate Doctors of Scheduled Caste
benefit_summary: Rs25,000 subsidy plus up to Rs2.5 lakh loan at 4% interest for Scheduled Caste medical graduates (MBBS/BAMS/BHMS/BDS etc.) in Gujarat to start an independent practice.
caveats: Must start the clinic within 3 months of receiving assistance; repayment of Rs5,000/month for 12 months. Homeopathic doctors must practice pure homeopathy only. Not eligible if employed in a government hospital or private organization.

title: Disability Pension (MBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs150/month disability pension plus an ex-gratia payment of up to Rs5,000 (depending on disability %), for registered Meghalaya construction workers permanently disabled by paralysis/leprosy/TB/accidents.

title: Disabled Person Pension Scheme - Punjab
benefit_summary: Rs1,500/month pension for disabled persons in Punjab, family income <=Rs60,000/year.
caveats: Requires disability >50% (mentally disabled/retarded persons exempt from the percentage requirement). Family annual income limit Rs.60,000/year. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Corrected disability_percent_min from 40 to 50 per the official Punjab Dept of Social Security page (sswcd.punjab.gov.in), which explicitly states <50% disability is NOT eligible. The prior 40% figure traced to a single non-official aggregator that itself cited (and contradicted) the official 50% source.

title: Disability Pension - West Bengal
benefit_summary: Monthly disability pension in West Bengal for persons unable to work due to disability (deaf/dumb/blind/orthopedic/mentally challenged/permanently incapacitated); currently Rs1,000/month.
caveats: A rate increase (to Rs1,500 or Rs2,000, two competing proposals) has been announced after the May 2026 change of government but was NOT formally notified as of July 2026 - do not assume the new figure. Managed via the Jai Bangla portal since April 2020.

title: Divyang Pension Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.1,000/month pension (paid quarterly as Rs.3,000) for persons with disabilities in Uttar Pradesh.
caveats: A raise to Rs.1,500/month was announced/proposed as part of the UP 2026-27 state budget, but as of July 2026 the official UP pension portal (sspy.up.in) itself states the current disbursed amount remains Rs.1,000/month and explicitly describes Rs.1,500 as still 'expected,' not yet implemented. Do not present Rs.1,500 as the current benefit. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Reverted from 'already raised to Rs.1,500' (not yet true) back to the actually-disbursed Rs.1,000/month, with a caveat about the pending-but-unimplemented hike -- mirroring how the West Bengal disability pension (dpwb) record handles its own analogous pending-increase situation.

title: Diggy
benefit_summary: 75-85% subsidy (up to Rs3,40,000, corrected from Rs3,00,000) for farm pond/'diggi' construction with a minimum 4-lakh-litre capacity, for Rajasthan farmers with 0.5+ hectare irrigated land.
caveats: Mandatory drip/sprinkler installation on the diggi; construction can only start after Agriculture Department approval.

title: Distress Relief Fund For The Differently Abled (Medical Treatment)
benefit_summary: Rs5,000/person/year for medical treatment/surgery of disabled persons (including accident-disabled) in Kerala, from a corpus Distress Relief Fund.

title: Dr. Panjabrao Deshmukh Hostel Maintenance Allowance
benefit_summary: Hostel maintenance allowance for Maharashtra professional/technical course students: Rs3,000/year (Mumbai/Pune/Nagpur/Aurangabad) or Rs2,000/year (elsewhere), for families with income <Rs8 lakh/year.
caveats: Max 2 children per family per year; minimum 50% attendance in previous semester required. A separate, higher SC/ST-specific tier (Rs20,000-30,000) exists but does not apply to this general scheme.

title: Distress Relief Scheme
benefit_summary: Rs20,000 one-time assistance to BPL agriculture-dependent families in Tamil Nadu on the death of their primary breadwinner.

title: Dulari Scheme
benefit_summary: Milestone incentives for girl children in Andaman & Nicobar Islands: Rs8,000 (institutional birth) or Rs5,000 (home birth), Rs5,000 (Class VIII), Rs10,000 (Class X), Rs10,000 (Class XII), Rs5,000 (marriage at 21) or Rs10,000 (marriage after 25).
caveats: Benefits cease if the child marries before 21, drops out of school (education incentives only), or a false statement/certificate is provided.

title: Dr. Savitaben Ambedkar Inter Caste Marriage Assistance Scheme
benefit_summary: Financial assistance for inter-caste marriage (one spouse Scheduled Caste) in Gujarat: CORRECTED total is Rs50,000 (Rs25,000 cash + Rs25,000 savings certificates), per the official sje.gujarat.gov.in page (updated June 2026) - not Rs2,50,000 as the raw scheme text claims.
caveats: CORRECTED: total is half of what the raw scheme data states (same error pattern as a similar Maharashtra inter-caste marriage scheme). Marriage must be registered; apply within 2 years; no income limit.

title: Development of Strawberry Cultivation
benefit_summary: 100% assistance for strawberry runners/mulching/drip irrigation, plus a 50% subsidy for strawberry 'spokes', for bonafide Meghalaya farmers with 200+ sqm of owned/leased land.
caveats: Benefits allocated on a first-come-first-served basis.

title: Devnarayan Scooty Distribution And Incentive Scheme
benefit_summary: Free scooty (expanded to 4,240/year from 1,500) for extremely-backward-class (MBC) girl students scoring 50%+ in 12th grade, enrolled in Rajasthan government colleges; non-priority-list students instead get Rs10,000/year (UG) or Rs20,000/year (PG) cash incentive.
caveats: Some recent cycles reportedly shifting to a Rs70,000 cash transfer instead of a physical scooty - verify current cycle before advising students.

title: Dattopant Thengadi Mratak Shramik Aarthik Sahayata Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs1,00,000 financial assistance to the spouse/dependent of a registered UP factory worker who dies in service (salary <=Rs15,000/month).
caveats: Must apply within 1 year of the worker's death.

title: Destitute Widow Pension Scheme
benefit_summary: Rs1,000/month pension (Rs1,500/month if aged 80+) for destitute widows 18+ in Tamil Nadu with fixed assets <=Rs1 lakh, plus a free saree at Pongal/Deepavali and subsidized Anganwadi rice.

title: Dr. YSR Aarogyasri Health Insurance Scheme
benefit_summary: Cashless family health insurance for Andhra Pradesh rice-card holders and income-eligible families (<=Rs5 lakh/year): up to Rs.25 lakh/family/year (Rs.2.5 lakh insurer-funded + Rs.22.5 lakh via the Dr NTR Vaidya Seva Trust) following the AP Cabinet's September 2025 Universal Health Insurance Policy approval; APL families remain capped at Rs.5 lakh. Scheme renamed 'Dr NTR Vaidya Seva' after the July 2024 change of government.
caveats: 2025 reporting shows hospital payment dues (~Rs2,500 crore) and a suspension risk at 380 hospitals - verify claim status locally; cashless service is not always guaranteed currently. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] For this record's targeted BPL/income-eligible population, cover rose from a flat Rs.5 lakh to up to Rs.25 lakh/family/year after the Sept 2025 Cabinet-approved revamp.

title: E-Medhabruti
benefit_summary: Merit scholarship for Odisha students (60%+ marks, family income <=Rs6 lakh): UG/Technical & Professional Rs20,000/year (one-time lump sum per verification note), PG Rs15,000/year over 2 years.

title: National Agriculture Market
benefit_summary: Pan-India electronic trading platform (1,656+ mandis integrated, 1.8 crore+ farmers registered, Rs4.82-4.84 lakh crore cumulative trade) enabling farmers to sell produce online for transparent price discovery and reduced transaction costs.
caveats: Not a cash-benefit scheme - it is a market-access platform for farmers/traders.

title: Educational Assistance (A.B.O.C.W.W.B)
benefit_summary: Annual education grant for children of registered Assam construction workers: Rs1,500 (Class 1-4) up to Rs20,000/year (Post Graduate); full expenses covered for IIT/Engineering/Medical admissions.

title: Educational Assistance To Children Of Prisoners (Pursuing Professional Course)
benefit_summary: Rs1,00,000/student (including annual and hostel fees) for children of prisoners serving life imprisonment or death sentence, pursuing professional degree courses in Kerala government/aided colleges, minimum 70% marks in +2.

title: Educational Assistance For Children Of Victims Of Crime
benefit_summary: Tiered annual education assistance for children of crime victims in Kerala: Rs3,000/year (class 1-5) up to Rs15,000/year (PG/MPhil), family income <=Rs1 lakh.

title: Educational Assistance to Children of Women Headed Families
benefit_summary: Tiered monthly education stipend for children of women-headed households in Kerala: Rs300/month (class 1-5) up to Rs1,000/month (degree and above); max 2 children per family.
caveats: HIV/AIDS-affected persons, socially discriminated persons, and war widows are eligible irrespective of BPL status.

title: Education Assistance/Ph.D Scheme (GBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Annual education assistance for up to 2 children of registered Gujarat construction workers: Rs1,800/year (class 1-5) up to Rs2,00,000 or 100% of fees (medical/dental), covering school through professional/PG courses.
caveats: Maximum age 30 for beneficiary child (no limit if the child has a disability); one attempt per class/standard - repeaters ineligible for that standard's aid.

title: Educational Award Scheme - Gujarat Labour Welfare Board
benefit_summary: Merit award for children of Gujarat Labour Welfare Fund-contributing workers: Rs2,500 (70%+ marks in 10th standard) or Rs5,000 (70%+ in 12th standard).

title: Economic Help To Sahariya Tribal Girl Students (Class 11 And 12)
benefit_summary: Rs350/month x 10 months = Rs3,500/year stipend for Sahariya tribal girl students (Class 11-12) in Baran district, Rajasthan, studying in government schools without hostel accommodation.
caveats: Parent/guardian must not be an income-tax payer; not available to students in government residential schools/ashram hostels. This is a small monthly stipend, not a lump sum.

title: Education Loan Scheme
benefit_summary: Education loan for Backward Class students via NBCFDC: 90% of course cost (cap Rs.15 lakh) for study in India, but only 85% of course cost (cap Rs.20 lakh) for study abroad -- not 90% for both -- at 4% (general) / 3.5% (girls) interest.
caveats: Verification note suggests the record may actually describe the Central Sector Interest Subsidy Scheme (Ministry of Education) instead - 100% interest subsidy on loans up to Rs10 lakh for EWS families (income <=Rs4.5 lakh), now on the PM-Vidyalaxmi/Jan Samarth portal. Confirm which scheme applies before advising a specific applicant. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] NBCFDC Education Loan Scheme covers 90% of course expenditure for study in India (cap Rs.15 lakh) but only 85% for study abroad (cap Rs.20 lakh) -- not 90% for both. If the benefit_summary text didn't auto-match for replacement, manually verify and correct it to reflect this 90%/85% split.

title: Entrepreneur Support Scheme
benefit_summary: Capital investment subsidy for MSMEs in Kerala: 15% (general, cap Rs30 lakh) or 25% (young 18-45/women/SC-ST/NRK, cap Rs40 lakh) of Fixed Capital Investment, plus an additional 10% (cap Rs10 lakh) for priority sectors, backward districts, or new technology; overall cap Rs40 lakh.
caveats: CORRECTED: this is a percentage-based subsidy on capital investment, not a flat Rs30,000 amount as raw data suggested.

title: Funeral Assistance (A.B.O.C.W.W.B)
benefit_summary: Rs5,000 funeral expense grant to the nominee/dependents of a deceased registered Assam construction worker.

title: Financial Assistance to Brackish Water Aquaculture Farms
benefit_summary: Subsidy for Goa brackish-water aquaculture farms (<=2 hectares, CAA-licensed): 25% for construction/renovation (cap Rs2 lakh/ha), 50% for equipment (cap Rs1 lakh/ha), 25% for feed (cap Rs30,000/crop/ha, 2 crops/year).

title: Funeral Assistance (CBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs5,000 funeral assistance to legal heirs of a deceased registered Chandigarh construction worker (6+ months of membership).
caveats: Application must be made within 3 months of the worker's death.

title: Financial Assistance for Construction/ Purchase of Wooden/ FRP Fishing Vessel (Canoe) for Fishermen
benefit_summary: 50% subsidy for wooden/FRP fishing canoe purchase or construction: cap Rs60,000 (general category) or Rs80,000 (SC/ST category), available once every 4 years, one craft per household.

title: Financial Assistance To Disabled For Self Employment
benefit_summary: Rs1,50,000 total (80% bank loan + up to Rs30,000 state subsidy) for self-employment/small business for disabled Maharashtra residents, age 18-50, income <Rs1 lakh/year.

title: Financial Assistance To Disabled Students Pursuing (10th, 11th, 12th Equivalent Exams)
benefit_summary: Tiered fee assistance for disabled Kerala students (40%+ disability) pursuing SSLC/+1/+2-equivalent courses under the State Literacy Mission: Rs1,750-1,950 course fee plus exam/registration/admission fee components depending on class.
caveats: Open to both APL and BPL category students.

title: Financial Assistance To Fishermen For Purchase of Fisheries Requisites (Gill Net/ River Gill Net with Accessories)
benefit_summary: 50% subsidy for gill net/river gill net with accessories: cap Rs30,000 (general) or Rs40,000 (SC/ST), for Goa traditional fishermen who own a registered canoe.

title: Financial Assistance to Fresh Water Aquaculture Farms
benefit_summary: Subsidy for Goa freshwater fish/prawn farming: 25% for construction (cap Rs2 lakh/ha, max 2 ha), 50% for equipment (cap Rs60,000/ha/year), 25% for feed (cap Rs50,000/ha/year, max 2 ha).
caveats: Requires 15 years of Goa residency.

title: Financial Assistance To Inter-Caste Married Couples (Except SC/ST Category)
benefit_summary: Rs30,000 one-time financial assistance for legally married inter-caste couples (excluding SC/ST category) in Kerala, combined family income <=Rs1 lakh, applied for 1-2 years post-marriage.
caveats: Funds must be used for business, land purchase, or house construction; Local Self Government Institutions monitor utilization via a signed agreement.

title: Financial Assistance To Purchase Singel Net / Small Rampon Net & Its Accessories
benefit_summary: 50% subsidy (cap Rs50,000) every 5 years for purchase of a single net/small rampon net and accessories, for OBC (Kharvi community) traditional fishermen in Goa who do not own a registered canoe/trawler.
caveats: Only one member per household family can avail this benefit.

title: Financial Assistance for Registered Fishermen Society
benefit_summary: Rs50,000 grant-in-aid to registered Goa fisheries co-operative societies/associations with 25+ members.
caveats: Benefit flows to the registered society, not directly to individual fishermen.

title: Rs 5 Lakh Insurance Cover To Farmers
benefit_summary: Rs5 lakh life insurance cover (any cause of death) for Telangana farmers aged 18-60, premium fully paid by the state government via LIC, payout within 10 days of death.
caveats: Functionally the same scheme as 'Rythu Bima' - no separate rebrand beyond that commonly used name. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Corrected max_age from 60 to 59 -- Rythu Bima eligibility is 18-59; farmers who turn 60 are no longer eligible for fresh enrollment, per myscheme.gov.in and a Telangana High Court judgment quoting the scheme rule.

title: Financial Assistance on the Natural Death of Differently Abled Person
benefit_summary: Rs15,000 financial assistance to the legal heir on the natural death of a registered disabled person (member of the TN Welfare Board for the Differently-Abled).

title: Financial Assistance to Purchase/Construct New Fishing Craft less than 26 feet for Fishing in Inland Waters of Goa
benefit_summary: 50% subsidy (cap Rs30,000, or 60%/cap Rs36,000 for SC/ST/women) on a unit cost of Rs60,000, for a new fishing craft under 26 feet for inland waters in Goa, renewable every 7 years.

title: Financial Assistance for Marriage (GBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs4,000 one-time marriage assistance for registered Goa construction workers (3+ years continuous Board membership), covering own or a child's marriage.

title: Financial Assistance On Marriage Of Children (HBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs21,000 (son's marriage) or Rs50,000 (daughter's marriage) for children of registered Haryana construction workers (1+ year of membership); covers marriage of up to 2 children, extendable to 3 daughters.

title: Financial Assistance to Mussel Culture and Oyster Farming in Goa
benefit_summary: 50% subsidy for mussel culture/oyster farming units in Goa: cap Rs25,000/unit (estuarine waters, max 2 units) or Rs40,000/unit (open sea, max 2 units).
caveats: Requires 15 years of Goa residency and completion of a training programme on mussel/oyster farming.

title: Funeral Assistance Scheme (PBAOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs7,000 funeral assistance (via DBT within 7 days) to the nominee/dependent of a deceased registered Puducherry construction worker.
caveats: Must apply within 2 months of the worker's death.

title: Financial Assistance To Self-Employment For Trained Disabled Persons
benefit_summary: Rs1,000 financial assistance for purchase of tool kits/equipment for vocationally-trained disabled persons in Maharashtra to start their own small business.

title: Funeral Assistance Scheme (GBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs10,000 financial assistance to the legal heirs of a deceased registered Gujarat construction worker.

title: Financial Assistance for Purchase of Fuel (Petrol) to the Fishermen for Operation of Out Board Motors
benefit_summary: Rs30/litre petrol subsidy for outboard motors (<=10HP), capped at 1,000 litres/year (general) or 1,100 litres/year (SC/ST), for registered Goa fishermen.

title: Financial Aid For Providing Hostel Facility To Transgender Students
benefit_summary: Rs4,000/month hostel rent assistance for transgender students pursuing courses at Kerala institutions.
caveats: Students must submit a new application each academic year.

title: Financial Assistance for the Purchase of Lifejackets and Lifebuoys for Fishermen
benefit_summary: 75% subsidy for lifejackets (cap Rs1,000 each) and lifebuoys (cap Rs1,500 each) for Goa fishermen; quantity varies by vessel type (canoe/trawler).

title: Financial Assistance Under The National Fund For Persons With Disabilities
benefit_summary: Central support fund for persons with disabilities: (1) grants up to Rs20 lakh (national)/Rs15 lakh (regional) to organizations running exhibitions/workshops showcasing PwD-made products; (2) travel/support for PwDs (40%+ disability) who have excelled in sports/arts/culture to compete nationally or internationally; (3) mobility-equipment reimbursement up to Rs1 lakh.
caveats: Multi-component scheme with different eligibility per component; income ceiling is Rs3 lakh for national events, Rs6 lakh for international events.

title: Financial Assistance to Take up Value Addition to Seafood
benefit_summary: 50% subsidy for seafood value-addition units in Goa: cap Rs5 lakh (construction/renovation) and Rs2 lakh (equipment) per unit.
caveats: Preference given to self-help groups, women entrepreneurs, and trained youth. Requires 15 years of Goa residency.

title: Financial Assistance for Setting up Crab Culture Unit
benefit_summary: Subsidy for Goa crab farming: 25% of unit cost (cap Rs1.5 lakh/ha, max 2 ha) plus 50% for seed/feed (cap Rs75,000/ha, max 2 ha).
caveats: Requires completion of a crab-farming training programme and 15 years of Goa residency.

title: Financial Assistance for setting up of Ornamental Fish Unit in Goa
benefit_summary: 50% subsidy for ornamental fish farming in Goa: cap Rs1.5 lakh (breeding or rearing unit alone) or Rs2.5 lakh (combined unit).
caveats: Requires training, own/leased land, adequate water facilities, and 15 years of Goa residency.

title: Floriculture Development Scheme
benefit_summary: 50% subsidy on quality flower planting material plus a free low-cost polyhouse (minimum 100 sqm), for bonafide Meghalaya farmers taking up floriculture.

title: Financial Assistance To Visually Impaired Advocates
benefit_summary: Rs3,500 one-time grant (books/legal suits) plus Rs5,000/month reader's allowance for 10 years, for visually impaired practicing advocates in Kerala with family income <=Rs1 lakh.

title: Funeral Benefit (MBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs1,000 funeral benefit to nominee/dependents of a deceased registered Meghalaya construction worker.

title: Festival Gift Coupons (Sainik Welfare)
benefit_summary: Festival gift coupons worth Rs 4,000 per year for non-pensioner ex-servicemen registered with Dept of Sainik Welfare Puducherry, aged 60+ (no age bar for widows of ex-servicemen).
caveats: Coupons collected in person on intimation from DSW, normally between November and January.

title: Free Coaching Scheme for SC and OBC Students
benefit_summary: Free coaching for competitive exams (UPSC/SSC/banking/engineering/medical entrance etc.) for SC/OBC students, with stipend of Rs 3,000/month (local) or Rs 6,000/month (outstation) for up to 12 months, plus Rs 15,000 incentive for interview coaching after clearing the mains stage of Civil Services exams.
caveats: Usable a maximum of twice per student; SC:OBC selection ratio roughly 70:30; applicant must not already be availing benefits of another coaching scheme.

title: Free Motorized Tricycle Scheme for Persons with Disabilities
benefit_summary: Free motorized tricycle for persons with disabilities; grant covers actual price up to a cap of Rs 25,000 (any excess cost borne by the beneficiary).
caveats: One-time benefit per beneficiary; not eligible if previously given a motorized tricycle by Government of India/Local Bodies/MLA Fund/MPLADS or other government-funded source.

title: Fodder Minikits under Integrated Fodder Development Scheme (General Category)
benefit_summary: In-kind provision of a fodder seed minikit (3 Kg, 7 Kg, or 10 Kg) of improved fodder varieties to farmers; no cash component.

title: Farm Pond (Khet Talai) Nirman Karyakram
benefit_summary: Subsidy for constructing farm ponds for irrigation. SC/ST/marginal/small farmers: up to Rs 73,500 (kaccha/raw pond) or Rs 1,35,000 (plastic-lined). General category farmers: up to Rs 63,000 (kaccha) or Rs 1,20,000 (plastic-lined).
caveats: Applicant must hold minimum 0.5 hectares of cultivable land at one place in their name. Note: this scheme record overlaps with another farm-pond scheme entry in the source database covering the same program by category/lining tier — may be a duplicate.

title: Family Pension (MBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Family pension to the surviving spouse of a deceased Meghalaya Building & Other Construction Workers Welfare Board pensioner: 50% of the deceased's pension amount, or Rs 100/month, whichever is higher.
caveats: Surviving spouse must not be receiving any pension or salary from Government/Semi-Government/Private Organization.

title: Financial Assistance To Dependent Children Of Widows And Destitute Women
benefit_summary: Rs 1,000/month per child (up to 2 children per family) for dependent children (under 18) of widows/destitute women, or of a legal guardian if both parents have died, to help meet maintenance and education costs.
caveats: Applicant (widow/destitute woman/guardian) must be a Chandigarh resident for more than 3 years; child must not already receive a family pension from State/Central Govt; children placed in institutional (govt/NGO) care are not eligible.

title: Financial Incentives To Mothers Who Deliver A Girl Child (Mamta)
benefit_summary: One-time financial incentive of Rs 10,000 to mothers who deliver a live girl child (up to 2 deliveries) in a registered medical institution.
caveats: Applicant must be a Goa resident for at least 3 years (or married to a Goa resident); application must be made within 45 days of delivery. Those who already received the earlier Rs 5,000 first installment are eligible only for the balance Rs 5,000.

title: Fodder Minikits under Schedule Castes Sub Plan (SC Category)
benefit_summary: In-kind provision of a fodder seed minikit (3 Kg, 7 Kg, or 10 Kg) of improved fodder varieties to Scheduled Caste farmers; no cash component.

title: Fodder Minikits under Tribal Area Sub Plan (TASP) Scheme (ST Category)
benefit_summary: In-kind provision of a fodder seed minikit (3 Kg, 7 Kg, or 10 Kg) of improved fodder varieties to Scheduled Tribe farmers; no cash component.

title: Farmers Training Institute Scheme
benefit_summary: Specialised agricultural training and exposure/field-tour programmes for farmers, including sponsoring progressive/award-winning farmers for exposure trips within and outside the state.

title: Fitter Training to Hearing Impaired Persons
benefit_summary: Two-year Fitter trade training for hearing-impaired candidates at ITI Guindy (also now Ulundurpet and Nagercoil), with a stipend of about Rs 300/month.
caveats: Applicant must have passed 10th standard; stipend figure not independently re-confirmed in latest check.

title: Grant In Aid To Old Age Home
benefit_summary: Grants to registered NGOs running old-age homes to provide food, accommodation, and medical assistance to old/destitute/disabled persons — about Rs 900 per resident per month for nourishment. Men must be 60+ and women 55+ to be accommodated.
caveats: Beneficiary must be an Indian citizen and permanent resident of Maharashtra; benefit is paid to the NGO, not directly to the individual.

title: Grants In Aid To SC/ST Patients Suffering From Cancer And Other Malignant Diseases
benefit_summary: One-time fixed financial assistance of Rs 50,000 to SC/ST patients suffering from cancer or other malignant diseases.
caveats: Can be claimed only once per person; note flags this as a duplicate of another scheme entry (grants-in-aid-to-scst-patients) — recommend merging.

title: Grant of Financial Assistance to Differently Abled Person
benefit_summary: Monthly financial assistance to persons with disabilities: Rs 3,000/month (40-65% disability), Rs 3,500/month (66-85%), Rs 4,500/month (86-100%); age-based top-ups of Rs 3,700/month (age 60-79) and Rs 4,800/month (age 80+).
caveats: Applicant must be a native/resident of Puducherry for at least 5 years. Selection is periodical and depends on availability of funds. For Mentally Retarded applicants, IQ must be below 69 instead of the percentage test.

title: Ghar Ghar Aushodhi Yojana
benefit_summary: Distribution of medicinal plant saplings (Tulsi, Ashwagandha, Giloy, Kalmegh) to promote use of medicinal herbs — 24 saplings per family over 5 years. This is a plant-distribution scheme, not a free-medicine-delivery scheme.
caveats: Applicant must have a Rajasthan Jan Aadhaar card and adequate space to plant saplings. A separate, unrelated home-delivery-of-medicines scheme for seniors 70+ is planned for late 2025/2026 — do not conflate the two.

title: Gharaunda-Group Home for Adults Scheme
benefit_summary: Assured group-home residential care for adult persons with disabilities (Autism, Cerebral Palsy, Mental Retardation, or Multiple Disabilities) under the National Trust Act, 1999 — includes accommodation, medical care, and vocational activities.
caveats: Care is provided through registered organizations (ROs) empanelled with the National Trust, not as direct cash to individuals.

title: Go Green Scheme- Gujarat Labour Welfare Board
benefit_summary: Subsidy for labourers/industrial workers purchasing a battery-operated (lithium-ion) two-wheeler: 30% of purchase price or Rs 30,000, whichever is less, plus reimbursement of RTO registration and road tax.
caveats: Labourer must be regularly contributing to the Labour Welfare Fund; vehicle must be FAME-2 and GEDA empanelled with minimum 50km range on a single charge.

title: Go-Green Shramik Scheme (GBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: One-time subsidy for registered construction workers purchasing a battery-operated two-wheeler: 50% of the price or Rs 30,000, whichever is less, plus reimbursement of registration fee and road tax.
caveats: Requires at least 1 year of registration with GBOCWWB; worker must hold a two-wheeler driving license; vehicle cannot be sold for 3 years after purchase; available once per worker.

title: Go-Green Three Wheelers Scheme (GBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: One-time subsidy for registered construction workers who became disabled/incapacitated in a construction-site accident, to purchase a battery-operated three-wheeler (e-rickshaw): 50% of ex-showroom price or Rs 48,000, whichever is less, plus reimbursement of registration fee and road tax.
caveats: Worker must hold a valid tricycle license; benefit available once per registered disabled construction worker.

title: Gharelu Mahila Kamgar Cycle, Chhatari, Chappal/Joota Sahayta Yojana
benefit_summary: In-kind assistance (cycle, umbrella, slippers/shoes) for registered unorganized women workers, at a fixed CSIDC rate rather than a flat rupee amount.
caveats: Not eligible if already received a similar item under another parallel State Government scheme.

title: Ganga Kalyana Scheme
benefit_summary: Subsidized borewell/open-well irrigation (drilling + pump set installation) for small/marginal farmers from religious minority communities. Bore-well project allocation is up to Rs 3.75 lakh in Bengaluru Rural, Kolar, Chikkaballapur, Ramanagara and Tumakuru districts, and up to Rs 2.25 lakh in other districts (figures vary by district — verify current district-specific cap).
caveats: Applicant must belong to a State-notified Religious Minority Community and be a small/marginal farmer with 1 acre 20 gunte to 5 acres of dry land (minimum 1 acre in a few named low-land-availability districts).

title: Theka Shramik, Gharelu Mahila Kamgar Evan Hamal Shramik Prasuti Sahayta Yojana
benefit_summary: Maternity/paternity benefit for registered unorganized workers: women get Rs 4,200 in the 3rd month of pregnancy and Rs 2,800 in the 8th month; men get Rs 3,000 paternity assistance after the child's birth (total up to Rs 10,000 per family).
caveats: Benefit limited to two children per beneficiary.

title: Grant for Incubation Centers within Educational Institutes Scheme
benefit_summary: One-time capital-expense grant of up to Rs 10,00,000 (max 15 institutes/year) plus up to Rs 3,00,000/year operational-expense grant for 3 years, for educational institutes in Goa setting up or expanding an incubation centre.
caveats: Only institutes affiliated with a recognized public university are eligible; not considered an entitlement — SPC has sole discretion to accept/reject.

title: Grant to Meritorious Wards of ESM in Sports: National / International Level (Sainik Welfare)
benefit_summary: Cash grant to wards of Ex-Servicemen (or of widows of ESM) for sporting achievement: Rs 50,000 for international-level achievement, Rs 30,000 for national-level achievement.
caveats: Event must be organized by a government-approved/recognized body; application must be submitted offline within 3 months of the achievement.

title: Godhan Nyay Yojana
benefit_summary: Government purchases cow dung from cattle rearers at Rs 2/kg (expanded to include gaumutra purchase at Rs 4/litre), converted into organic vermicompost fertilizer sold to farmers at nominal rates.
caveats: Cow dung collector must have Aadhaar card, own bank account, ID card, mobile number, and must register their animals.

title: GITANJALI HOUSING SCHEME
benefit_summary: Housing construction subsidy for homeless/economically weaker section people in West Bengal, following an IAY-style pattern: Rs 70,000/unit (plain rural/urban areas) or Rs 75,000/unit (Hilly/Difficult/Sundarban areas), disbursed in 70%/30% installments.
caveats: Income ceiling of roughly Rs 6,000/month per household is reported but not confirmed on the official page; BPL-listed households get priority.

title: General Pre Matric Scholarship-Uttar Pradesh
benefit_summary: Pre-matric scholarship for General-category students (Class 9-10) whose parents work in occupations traditionally considered untouchable, up to about Rs 3,500/year (varies by class/hosteller status).
caveats: Cannot generally be combined with other scholarships (with some exceptions); all children of the same parents are eligible.

title: Gatidhara Scheme
benefit_summary: Subsidy for registered unemployed youth purchasing a commercial vehicle for self-employment in transport: 30% of ex-showroom price up to Rs 1,00,000 (up to Rs 1,50,000 for women applicants).
caveats: Applicant must be enrolled in the Employment Bank of the Labour Dept; age relaxation of 5 years for SC/ST and 3 years for OBC; only one member per family eligible.

title: Girl Students Health & Hygiene Scheme
benefit_summary: Rs 50/month per student via DBT (or equivalent sanitary napkin provision) for girl students in Classes VI-XII in government/government-aided schools, to support menstrual health and hygiene.

title: Government Service Home - Tamil Nadu
benefit_summary: Institutional care for widows, destitute/deserted women, adolescent girls, differently-abled women, and socially/economically backward women: free accommodation, food, education, vocational training, textbooks/uniforms and sanitary supplies.
caveats: Income ceiling not applicable for differently-abled applicants; women can stay with a male child up to 5th standard or a girl child up to 12th standard.

title: Guru Shishya Parampara
benefit_summary: Financial honorarium for preserving rare/vanishing classical or folk/tribal art forms via a mentor-disciple model: Guru gets Rs 7,500/month, Accompanist Rs 3,750/month, each of 4 Shishyas Rs 1,500/month, for one year.
caveats: This is a Central (Ministry of Culture, via Zonal Cultural Centres) scheme, not a Meghalaya state scheme, though Meghalaya artists participate. Guru must be 45-70 years old and Shishyas 15-25 years old.

title: Gopinath Munde Shetkari Apghat Suraksha Sanugrah Audhan Yojana
benefit_summary: Accident compensation for registered farmers (and one family member): Rs 2,00,000 for death; Rs 1,00,000 for loss of one limb/eye; Rs 2,00,000 for loss of two limbs/eyes or one limb and one eye.
caveats: Registration is evidenced by 7/12 land extract; benefit is independent of any other similar scheme; no extra documents beyond those in the Government Resolution are required.

title: Gopabandhu Sambadika Swasthya Bima Yojana
benefit_summary: Health insurance coverage of Rs 5,00,000 per family (journalist, spouse, and up to 3 dependent children under 25) for indoor/outdoor treatment.
caveats: Applicant must be an Odisha-based journalist working for a media house registered with the I&PR department, Odisha; coverage is in addition to any existing employer-provided insurance. Registration window extended to Sept 2025.

title: Gopabandhu Sikhya Sahayata Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs 20,000/year financial assistance for graduate/postgraduate students from underprivileged categories (HIV/AIDS-affected families, homeless, destitute, manual scavengers, particularly vulnerable tribal groups, released bonded labourers, single-mother families) studying in Odisha institutions.
caveats: Can be availed alongside other scholarships; limited to normal course duration. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Income ceiling raised from Rs.1,20,000 (the original 2019 GO ceiling) to Rs.2,50,000/year per a November 2023 DHE guideline, confirmed by current scholarship-portal listings.

title: Goa Value Added Tax-Based Subsidy on H.S.D. Oil Consumed by Fishing Vessels Scheme
benefit_summary: Full reimbursement of Value Added Tax paid on HSD (diesel) oil consumed by registered fishing vessels, subject to a statewide quota of 20,000 KL of oil per financial year.
caveats: Applicant must hold a valid Net Licence and Fishing Licence, must not be a Fisheries Department defaulter, and must procure oil from an approved outlet. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] As of June 2026, the Goa Fishing Boat Owners Association publicly stated this VAT-diesel subsidy 'has been discontinued in Goa' with prior-year dues unpaid, contrasting with Maharashtra/Karnataka's still-active fuel subsidies. Do not present as currently/reliably disbursed -- flag this to users as uncertain/likely inactive pending restoration.

title: Government Working Women's Hostel
benefit_summary: Subsidized hostel accommodation (rent Rs 300/month in Chennai, Rs 200/month in other districts) plus food/electricity for working women, for up to 3 years.
caveats: Income ceiling is Rs 25,000/month in Chennai and Rs 15,000/month in other districts (higher figure used as the income field here per the Chennai cap; the lower-district cap applies outside Chennai).

title: Ganesh Shankar Vidyaarthi Shramik Puraskar Rashi Yojana
benefit_summary: Scholarship for children of workers (in registered factories, commercial establishments, or shops) who pass High School/Intermediate/Graduation/Post-Graduation exams: Rs 5,000 for 60-74.99% marks, Rs 7,500 for 75%+.
caveats: Worker's monthly salary (basic + DA) must not exceed Rs 15,000.

title: Goa Tribal's Employment Generation Programme Scheme
benefit_summary: Subsidized business loan scheme for unemployed tribal youth in Goa to start micro/small manufacturing, service, or trade enterprises: 40% subsidy on loan amount, project cost caps of Rs 25 lakh (manufacturing) or Rs 15 lakh (service/trade), plus compulsory entrepreneurship training.
caveats: Applicant must have passed Class 4 (relaxable), be a permanent Goa resident for 15+ years, and not be a loan defaulter; farming/tobacco activities are excluded.

title: Hamaal Hetu Joota, Huk Evan Mahila Hamaal Hetu Soopa Aur Tokari Sahaayata Yojana
benefit_summary: In-kind/financial assistance of about Rs 500 per beneficiary for shoes and lifting hooks (for male porters/Hamal) or soup and baskets (for female Hamal workers), at fixed CSIDC rates.
caveats: Not eligible if already benefited under another parallel State Government scheme.

title: Homes For Intellectually Impaired Persons
benefit_summary: Institutional shelter care (food, shelter, protection) for orphaned Mentally Deficient Children in need of care and protection, at 19 MDC homes across Maharashtra (14 aided, 5 non-aided) — no individual cash benefit.
caveats: Admission is via the district Child Welfare Committee under the Juvenile Justice Act.

title: Horticulture Mission for North Eastern Hill Scheme- Meghalaya
benefit_summary: Training, technology support, and input subsidies for horticulture farmers under the central MIDH umbrella (GoI 90%/State 10% funding) — improving productivity, marketing support, and drip irrigation.
caveats: Applicant must possess owned or leased land of at least 200 sq. m.

title: Health Check-up (A.B.O.C.W.W.B)
benefit_summary: Rs 5,000 once a year for an annual health check-up at any hospital, for registered construction workers with continuous Assam BOCWWB membership.

title: Haryana Divyang Pension Schemes
benefit_summary: Monthly disability pension of Rs 3,000 for persons with 60-100% disability (blindness, low vision, cured leprosy, hearing impairment, locomotor disability, mental retardation, or mental illness).
caveats: Applicant's own income must not exceed the minimum wage for unskilled labour as notified by the Labour Department; must be a Haryana domicile resident for the last 3 years.

title: Hearing Aid Grant (Sainik Welfare)
benefit_summary: Financial assistance of about Rs 1,000 (re-confirmed figure; the raw scheme benefit text stated Rs 8,000) toward the purchase of a hearing aid for registered ex-servicemen/widows of ex-servicemen.
caveats: Not eligible if a member of the Ex-Servicemen Contributory Health Scheme (ECHS).

title: Haritha Haram
benefit_summary: State-wide tree plantation programme (green cover increase, no individual cash benefit) — individuals, NGOs, schools, government departments and corporates can all participate in plantation drives.
caveats: Renamed to 'Vanamahotsavam' after the Dec 2023 government change; same tree-plantation concept, target reduced from 20.2 crore saplings (2024) to 18.02 crore (2025).

title: Hostel Assistance Scheme for Children of Migrant Construction Workers (GBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Free hostel accommodation (and meals) in primary school for children of migrant construction workers registered with GBOCWWB; no cash component.

title: HIMAYAT- Deen Dayal Upadhyaya-Grameen Kaushalya Yojana
benefit_summary: Free placement-linked skill training (3-12 months, residential/non-residential) for unemployed youth in J&K, with at least 70% placement assurance and one year post-placement tracking; no direct cash transfer.
caveats: Applicant must have passed Class 8; upper age limit is 35 generally but extended to 45 for women, PVTGs, PwDs, transgender persons and other special groups. 40,000 seats reserved for young women; 1,000 youth trained for overseas placement.

title: Mukhya Mantri Himachal Health Care Scheme (himcare)
benefit_summary: Cashless health insurance coverage up to Rs 5,00,000 per family per year at empanelled hospitals, for families not covered under Ayushman Bharat (BPL families, street vendors, MNREGA workers with 50+ days, seniors 70+, orphanage children, and other listed categories with differential premium rates).
caveats: Operates on a co-payment/premium basis with three beneficiary categories at different premium rates; enrolment is online or via Lok Mitra Kendra/CSC.

title: Hita-dhikaari Ke Samanye Athava Durghatana Me Mrityu Ya Ghayal Hone Ki Dasha Me Sahayata Yojana
benefit_summary: Accident/death compensation for registered construction workers: Rs 5,00,000 for accidental death; Rs 3,00,000 for permanent total disability; Rs 1,00,000 for permanent partial disability; up to Rs 20,000 for serious injury (5+ days hospitalization); up to Rs 5,000 for minor injury; Rs 75,000 for normal (non-accidental) death.
caveats: Worker must be depositing contributions regularly with the labour board; this is a different, higher-tier scheme from a separate normal-death-only scheme (asfcw) — do not conflate the two.

title: Home Loan Interest Subsidy Scheme- Gujarat Labour Welfare Board
benefit_summary: 3% interest subsidy on home loans for workers in Gujarat's organized sector purchasing their own house, on loans up to Rs 15 lakh.
caveats: Worker must have 1+ year continuous employment with Labour Welfare Fund contributions; house purchase price max Rs 30 lakh; loan tenure 15+ years; loans must be from a Nationalized/Scheduled Bank/NBFC; apply within 1 year of purchase.

title: Himachal Pradesh Maharishi Valmiki Sampoorn Swachata Puraskar (state Sanitation Reward Scheme)
benefit_summary: Cash prize awarded to Gram Panchayats (not individuals) for cleanliness/sanitation achievement: Rs 1,00,000 (block level), Rs 3,00,000 (district level), Rs 5,00,000 (division level), Rs 10,00,000 (state level).
caveats: Gram Panchayat must have achieved open-defecation-free status; previous winners at a level are barred from competing at that same level for 3 years.

title: Honorarium for Pradhan Samajpatis of Indigenous Tribal Community
benefit_summary: Monthly honorarium of Rs 5,000 (raised from an earlier Rs 2,000) for Pradhan Samajpatis (Chief Community Headmen) of indigenous tribal communities in Tripura.
caveats: Covers roughly 20 tribal heads statewide; an earlier restriction excluding govt employees/pensioners has reportedly been removed. [Fix 2026-07-23] Occupation constraint removed from structured matching -- this is specifically for Pradhan/Samajpati (indigenous tribal community headmen), a single-scheme role our FLOW does not capture.

title: H.P. Swaran Jayanti Middle Merit Scholarship Scheme For Govt. Schools
benefit_summary: Merit scholarship for Class 5 students (via state-level exam) continuing through Classes 6-8: Rs 4,000/month (Class 6), Rs 5,000/month (Class 7), Rs 6,000/month (Class 8), for 12 months each year; 100 scholarships/year distributed via SCERT Solan exam.
caveats: Requires minimum 75% attendance (waivable for verified medical reasons) and continuous study at a Himachal Pradesh government school without repeating a class.

title: Harvesting Tools Assistance for General Category (HRT-2)
benefit_summary: Financial assistance for harvesting/processing equipment: individual General-category farmers get 50% of cost or Rs 1,00,000 (whichever less); FPO/FPC/FIG/SHG/Cooperative Societies get 75% of cost or Rs 1,50,000 (whichever less). Unit cost of equipment must be up to Rs 2,00,000.
caveats: Assistance available once every 5 years; equipment must be ISO/BIS/ISI-certified and purchased from an authorized dealer.

title: Harvesting Tools Assistance for Scheduled Castes (HRT-4)
benefit_summary: Financial assistance for harvesting/processing equipment: individual SC farmers get 50% of cost or Rs 1,00,000 (whichever less); FPO/FPC/FIG/SHG/Cooperative Societies get 75% of cost or Rs 1,50,000 (whichever less). Unit cost of equipment must be up to Rs 2,00,000.
caveats: Assistance available once every 5 years; equipment must be ISO/BIS/ISI-certified and purchased from an authorized dealer.

title: Harvesting Tools Assistance for Scheduled Tribes (HRT-3)
benefit_summary: Financial assistance for harvesting/processing equipment: individual ST farmers get 50% of cost or Rs 1,00,000 (whichever less); FPO/FPC/FIG/SHG/Cooperative Societies get 75% of cost or Rs 1,50,000 (whichever less). Unit cost of equipment must be up to Rs 2,00,000.
caveats: Assistance available once every 5 years; equipment must be ISO/BIS/ISI-certified and purchased from an authorized dealer.

title: Housing Subsidy Scheme (GBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Housing subsidy of Rs 1,50,000 for registered construction workers, disbursed as Rs 30,000/year over 5 years, for those with a home loan up to Rs 15 lakh (10+ year tenure).
caveats: Requires at least 2 years of continuous board registration; worker must not own any house/property jointly with spouse (affidavit required); annual written proposal needed to continue receiving the remaining 4 years of assistance.

title: Integrated Child Development Services: Chandigarh
benefit_summary: Universal in-kind child-development services (supplementary nutrition, immunization, health check-ups, referral, pre-school education, nutrition/health education) for children 0-6 years, pregnant women, lactating mothers, and adolescent girls 14-18 in Chandigarh — no cash amount.
caveats: Delivered through ~450 Anganwadi Centres across 3 ICDS projects.

title: Immediate Assistance for Severe Injury in Road/Fire Accident (Sainik Welfare)
benefit_summary: One-time Rs.25,000 spot assistance for ex-servicemen/widows registered with the Dept of Sainik Welfare Puducherry who suffered a severe injury in a road/fire accident or other mishap including natural calamities.
caveats: Not eligible if a member of the Ex-Servicemen Contributory Health Scheme (ECHS). [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Reverted an incorrect prior 'Rs.5,000 re-confirmed' override back to Rs.25,000 -- the official Puducherry Sainik Welfare Dept page (sainik.py.gov.in/assistance-affd-fund) states Rs.25,000 verbatim; Rs.5,000 traced to an outdated third-party aggregator only.

title: Incentive For The Simple Marriage
benefit_summary: Rs.50,000 marriage incentive for SC couples in Karnataka married on or after 11-08-2015.
caveats: Only couples married on or after 11-08-2015 are eligible, and application must be made within 1 year of marriage. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Removed an incorrect 'corrected to Rs.2.5 lakh' claim -- the official myscheme.gov.in page states a flat Rs.50,000 with no alternate figure. Rs.2,50,000 belongs to Karnataka's separate Inter-Caste Marriage Assistance scheme and was a conflation error.

title: Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme - Sikkim
benefit_summary: Monthly disability pension of Rs 2,000 for persons with 80%+ disability from BPL households, aged 18+.
caveats: Applicant must not receive any salary/pension/family pension from Central/other State Governments; must hold a PM Jan Dhan Yojana bank account.

title: Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme
benefit_summary: Central portion of the disability pension under NSAP: Rs 300/month for persons aged 18-79 with 80%+ disability from BPL households; Rs 500/month for those aged 80+. (States commonly top this up separately.)
caveats: Dwarfism is also covered as a qualifying disability under this scheme.

title: Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme - Sikkim
benefit_summary: Monthly widow pension of Rs 2,000 for BPL widows aged 21+.
caveats: Pension ceases upon remarriage; applicant must not receive salary/pension from Central/other State Governments; requires PM Jan Dhan Yojana account.

title: Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme
benefit_summary: Central portion of the widow pension under NSAP: Rs 300/month for BPL widows aged 40-79; Rs 500/month for those aged 80+. (States commonly top this up separately.)

title: Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme-Madhya Pradesh
benefit_summary: Monthly widow pension of Rs 600 for BPL widows aged 40-79 in Madhya Pradesh, operating under the umbrella Samagra Samajik Suraksha Pension Yojana.

title: Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme - Sikkim
benefit_summary: Tiered monthly old-age pension for BPL residents of Sikkim: Rs 1,500/month (age 60-69), Rs 2,000/month (70-79), Rs 2,500/month (80+).
caveats: If both spouses qualify, only one gets the pension; requires annual 'Life Certificate' submission in November or payment stops; requires PM Jan Dhan Yojana account.

title: Indira Gandhi National Vridhavastha Pension Yojana
benefit_summary: Monthly old-age pension of Rs 600 for BPL residents of Madhya Pradesh aged 60+, under the Samagra Samajik Suraksha Pension Yojana umbrella.

title: Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme - Tamil Nadu
benefit_summary: Monthly pension of Rs 1,200 (raised from Rs 1,000 in Aug 2023; Rs 1,500/month if aged 80+) for destitute BPL widows 40+, plus a free saree during Pongal/Deepavali and subsidized rice at Anganwadi Centres (2kg or 4kg/month depending on nutritious-meal enrollment).

title: Indira Mahila Shakti Udyam Protsahan Yojana
benefit_summary: Business-loan subsidy scheme for women entrepreneurs and women's self-help groups in Rajasthan: individual women get bank loans of Rs 5 lakh-Rs 1 crore with 25% margin-money subsidy (capped at Rs 25 lakh subsidy); SHGs can get loans up to Rs 5 crore with 25% subsidy capped at Rs 1.25 crore. SC/ST/widowed/abandoned/disabled women get 30% margin money instead of 25%.
caveats: Self-help group (or cluster/federation) must be registered under a state government department or the Cooperative Act.

title: Incentive To Owners Of Artificial Insemination Born Female Calf Through Pure Breeding In Indigenous Cow
benefit_summary: Incentive of Rs 3,000 to owners of a female calf (under 11 months old) born via artificial insemination through pure breeding of indigenous cows (e.g. Gir, Kankrej), once per beneficiary per year for one calf.

title: Plant Protection including Integrated Pest Management Scheme
benefit_summary: Free distribution of bio-pesticides and other Integrated Pest Management tools to farmers, plus a 50% subsidy on the sale of sprayers and plant protection equipment.

title: Intellectual Property Rights (IPR) Reimbursement Scheme
benefit_summary: Reimbursement of up to 100% of IP-filing costs for Goa-certified startups registering national or international IP, capped at Rs 2,00,000 (national) or Rs 5,00,000 (international); limited to 200 startups per year.
caveats: IP must relate to a technology-based product/service; applicant must have already filed/been granted the IP and paid required fees digitally; reimbursement is a one-time payment per IP application.

title: Inter-state Border Areas Development Programme
benefit_summary: Community/infrastructure development programme (roads, socio-economic upliftment, border security, tourism) for villages within 0-10 km of the Meghalaya-Assam inter-state boundary — not an individual cash benefit.
caveats: Villages within 0-5 km of the boundary get first priority.

title: Integrated Social Security Scheme - Old Age Pension
benefit_summary: Monthly old-age pension via DBT for men 60+ or women 55+ who are BPL or have income under Rs 75,000/year: Rs 1,250/month for women aged 55-59, Rs 1,500/month for ages 60-79, Rs 2,000/month for ages 80+ (tiered structure effective 1 April 2025, up from a prior flat Rs 1,000).
caveats: Min age is 60 for men and 55 for women. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Updated from the stale flat-Rs.1,000 (with 80+-only Rs.1,500 top-up) structure to the tiered Rs.1,250/1,500/2,000 rates that took effect 1 April 2025 under a J&K govt order, confirmed by 5 independent J&K news sources.

title: Integrated Social Security Scheme - Pension For Transgender
benefit_summary: Monthly pension via DBT for transgender persons in J&K who are BPL or have income under Rs 75,000/year: Rs 1,250/month (below 60), Rs 1,500/month (60-79), Rs 2,000/month (80+) -- the same tiered structure applied to old-age/widow/disability pensions, effective 1 April 2025.
caveats: [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Updated from a stale flat Rs.1,000/month to the tiered Rs.1,250/1,500/2,000 structure that the same April 2025 J&K order explicitly extended to the transgender pension.

title: Integrated Social Security Scheme - Pension For Physically Challenged Persons
benefit_summary: Monthly pension of Rs 1,000 via DBT for persons aged 18-79 with 40%+ (severe/multiple) disability in J&K who are BPL or have income under Rs 75,000/year.

title: Interest Subsidy Reimbursement Scheme
benefit_summary: Interest-repayment grant for Goa-certified startups: top 3 promising startups get 30% of loan interest up to Rs 5,00,000/year for 2 years; other startups get 10% up to Rs 2,00,000/year for 2 years (up to 40 startups/year selected). Note also references a broader 1.5% of turnover/30% of interest structure with women-entrepreneur enhancement to 2%/35%, cap Rs 8 lakh.
caveats: This is in addition to any subsidy under Chief Minister Rojgar Yojana (CMRY); benefits are not an entitlement.

title: Interest Subsidy Scheme for Smaller Business Units
benefit_summary: Interest subsidy on working capital loans for smaller business units in Goa, up to Rs 5,00,000/year for 3 years (claimable once per fiscal year); note identifies this as effectively the same scheme as the Interest Subsidy Reimbursement Scheme (isrs) under a different label, with 1.5%/30% of interest, cap Rs 5 lakh/year (Rs 8 lakh for women entrepreneurs).
caveats: Applicant entity's bank accounts must be Aadhaar-linked; subject to budgetary allocation with no promissory estoppel if discontinued.

title: Incentive For The Sc Widow Remarriage
benefit_summary: Incentive of Rs 3,00,000 (reduced to Rs 2,50,000 if the simple-marriage incentive was already claimed) for SC widows who remarry.
caveats: Widow must belong to SC community (spouse can be of any community); no annual income limit; application must be made within 1 year of the (re)marriage.

title: Industrial Skill Development Allowance To The New Employees Employed In Industries In H.p
benefit_summary: Monthly Industrial Skill Development Allowance of Rs 1,000 for new employees/apprentices in Himachal Pradesh industries during on-the-job skill training, up to 24 months; Rs 1,500/month for those with 50%+ permanent disability.
caveats: Applicant must be registered with an Employment Exchange in Himachal Pradesh and currently unemployed/seeking employment; no minimum educational qualification required. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Added missing max_income=Rs.15,000/month gross salary cap -- mandatory per clauses 3(j) and 4(f) of the official 2018 HP scheme rules; previously encoded as null (no cap enforced).

title: Integrated Sheep Development Scheme
benefit_summary: Sheep/goat unit establishment support (100% Centrally Sponsored, via J&K Sheep Husbandry Dept): participatory-mode beneficiaries get 10 ewes/does free of cost; subsidy-mode beneficiaries get 50% subsidy for 20-200 ewe/doe units (ceiling Rs 1,00,000/unit, max Rs 8,00,000 for 8 units); shearing units get 50% subsidy (ceiling Rs 75,000/unit).
caveats: Beneficiary can be an individual, group, SHG, cooperative society, or FPO; effort made to cover 20% SC/ST and 10% women beneficiaries; must have basic infrastructure/grazing access.

title: Integrated Social Security Scheme - Women In Distress
benefit_summary: Monthly pension of Rs 1,000 via DBT for destitute widowed/divorced/deserted women aged 40-79 in J&K who are BPL or have income under Rs 75,000/year.

title: Integrated Technology Enabled Agriculture Management System Or iTEAMS
benefit_summary: Free telephonic agricultural advisory (Dial 1917), access to subject-matter specialists, and transport/logistics support for farmers' produce at Rs 2/km/quintal.

title: Indirect Tax Internship Scheme In Central Board Of Indirect Taxes And Customs (CBIC)
benefit_summary: Paid legal internship at CBIC: law student interns get a stipend of about Rs 10,000/month (raw source stated Rs 5,000) for 1-2 months, and law graduate interns get about Rs 20,000/month (raw source stated Rs 15,000) for up to 6 months; a Certificate of Internship is awarded on satisfactory completion of the minimum duration.
caveats: Only 10 law students and 10 law graduates selected per year; graduates must have completed their LLB within the last 2 years; internship is based in Delhi and is full-time (no other course/work allowed).

title: Jyotiba Phule Shramik Kanyadan Yojana
benefit_summary: Financial assistance of Rs 51,000 for the marriage of a registered worker's daughter, payable for up to 2 daughters.
caveats: Worker's monthly salary (basic + DA) must not exceed Rs 15,000 (Rs 24,000/month per updated note); girl must be 18+ at marriage; apply within a window of 3 months before to 1 year after the marriage date.

title: Jagananna Amma Vodi
benefit_summary: Annual financial assistance of Rs 15,000 (Rs 2,000 deducted for a school-development/hygiene fund, net Rs 13,000 to the beneficiary) to mothers/guardians for sending children (Class 1-12) to school, until the child passes Class 12.
caveats: Renamed to 'Thalliki Vandanam' after the 2024 government change. Income ceiling is Rs 10,000/month (rural) or Rs 12,000/month (urban); family must not own a four-wheeler, have monthly electricity use over 300 units, include a government employee/pensioner or income-tax payer, or own 1000+ sq ft of land in a municipal area; child attendance must be 75%+.

title: Jagananna Chedodu
benefit_summary: Rs 10,000/year for 5 years (Rs 50,000 total, in 5 installments) for tailors, washermen (Rajakas), and barbers (Nayee Brahmins) in Andhra Pradesh, to buy tools/equipment for their trade.
caveats: Family land holding must be under 10/25 acres (wet/dry land); no government employee/pensioner in family (sanitary workers exempted); no four-wheeler ownership; property under 1,500 sq ft in urban areas; no income-tax payer in family. [Fix 2026-07-23] Occupation mapped to the closest broad FLOW category (self-employed) -- this scheme is actually restricted to tailors, washermen (Rajakas), and barbers (Nayee Brahmins) specifically in Andhra Pradesh, a finer distinction our FLOW does not capture; confirm the specific trade before relying on this.

title: Janta Juth Accidental Insurance Scheme
benefit_summary: Farmer accident insurance (100% state-funded premium): Rs 4,00,000 for accidental death/permanent disability or loss of two eyes/limbs (raised from Rs 2,00,000 per FY2025-26 state budget); Rs 2,00,000 (50% assistance) for loss of one eye/limb (raised from Rs 1,00,000).
caveats: Beneficiary can be the farmer, their child, or spouse; suicide or natural death are not covered; application must be made within 150 days of the accident.

title: Jeevanam Self-Employment Scheme To Dependents Of Crime Victims
benefit_summary: One-time financial assistance of Rs 20,000 for a crime victim (seriously injured) or their dependent (spouse/unmarried son or daughter), for self-employment support.
caveats: Application must be made within 5 years of the crime; beneficiary must execute an agreement with the Dept of Social Justice on Rs 200 stamp paper.

title: Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram
benefit_summary: Free and cashless institutional delivery (including C-section) for pregnant women at government health facilities: free drugs, diagnostics, diet, blood, transport to/from and between facilities, and exemption from user charges; extends to free treatment for sick newborns/infants up to 1 year.

title: Jai Johar (Old Age Pension) Scheme
benefit_summary: Monthly old-age pension of Rs 1,000 (via Jai Bangla portal) for Scheduled Tribe residents of West Bengal aged 60+ who receive no other pension.
caveats: A rate increase to Rs 1,500 or Rs 2,000 has been proposed following the May 2026 change of government but is NOT yet formally notified as of July 2026 — do not assume the higher figure is in effect.

title: JANANI SURAKSHA YOJANA
benefit_summary: Cash assistance for institutional delivery in Mizoram: Rs 600 (Aizawl/Lunglei) or Rs 700 (elsewhere) for delivery at a public/accredited private facility, regardless of BPL/APL status; via DBT.
caveats: Applicant must be 19+ years old; benefit limited to up to two live births.

title: Jagananna Thodu
benefit_summary: Interest-free (0%, 'Sunna Vaddi') loan up to Rs 10,000 through banks for hawkers, street vendors, and traditional handicraft artisans (lacework, kalamkari, toy-making, pottery, etc.).
caveats: Income ceiling Rs 10,000/month (rural) or Rs 12,000/month (urban); family land under 3 acres wetland or 10 acres dry land; no shop larger than 5x5 sq ft.

title: Jagananna Vidya Kanuka
benefit_summary: In-kind school kit (3 uniform pairs, notebooks, textbooks, shoes, 2 pairs of socks, belt, school bag) for students in Class 1-10 at government/aided/residential/model schools and registered madrasas in Andhra Pradesh.
caveats: [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Renamed to 'Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan Vidyarthi Mitra' (SRKVM) in mid-2024 under the TDP-led NDA government, as part of the same de-branding initiative that renamed sibling schemes jav and jvvd (already correctly flagged in this database). The scheme itself (in-kind school kit) continues under the new name.

title: Jagananna Videshi Vidya Deevena
benefit_summary: Overseas study scholarship for PG/PhD/MBBS courses: 100% tuition fee for admission to top 100 ranked institutions; 50% of tuition fee or Rs 5,00,000 (whichever less) for institutions ranked 101-200; plus one-way economy air ticket and visa fee reimbursement.
caveats: Renamed to 'Ambedkar Overseas Vidya Nidhi' after the 2024 government change (Jagananna branding dropped 18 June 2024); only one candidate per family; requires 60%+ marks in qualifying exam; must join the institution within 6 months of selection.

title: Krushy Aranya Protsaha Yojane
benefit_summary: Subsidized tree seedlings plus a survival-based cash incentive to farmers: Rs 35/seedling (year 1), Rs 40/seedling (year 2), Rs 50/seedling (year 3) — Rs 125/seedling total over 3 years.
caveats: Registration must be completed before the rainy season (by end of May). Note flags this as a likely duplicate of another entry (kapy) for the same scheme — recommend merging.

title: Kali Bai Bheel Medhavi Chhatra Scooty Scheme
benefit_summary: Scooty (or, in limited cases, a cash-alternative of roughly Rs 40,000, some 2026 reports cite up to Rs 70,000) for meritorious girl students in Rajasthan who scored 65%+ (RBSE) or 75%+ (CBSE) in Class 12 and are pursuing an approved degree course.
caveats: No gap year allowed between Class 12 and degree admission; girls who already received a scooty based on Class 10 marks under an earlier scheme are only eligible for the cash alternative, not a second scooty.

title: Kunwar Bai Nu Mameru Yojana
benefit_summary: Financial assistance for the marriage of Scheduled Caste girls in Gujarat: Rs 12,000 for marriages after 1 April 2021, or Rs 10,000 for marriages before that date, for up to 2 daughters per family.
caveats: Girl must be 18+ and boy 21+ at marriage; application must be made within 2 years of marriage; not available for remarriage; benefit can be combined with the Sat Fera Samuh Lagna Yojana group-marriage scheme if conditions of both are met.

title: Karmaveer Padmashri Dadasaheb Gaikwad Birth Centenary And Prize Distribution
benefit_summary: Award for social-movement work against untouchability/for landless farm workers: Rs 21,000 to the individual awardee and Rs 30,000 to the organization awardee (corrected from a raw combined figure of Rs 51,000), plus memorabilia, shawl and coconut.
caveats: Applicant must have 15+ years of social service work (organizations need 10+ years); raw source's gender-based age threshold (male 50+/female 40+) is not confirmed on the current official listing.

title: Khiladi Protsahan Yojana
benefit_summary: Sports incentive (up to Rs 50,000 one-time, tiered by competition level) for registered construction workers or their family members who excel in district/divisional/state-level sports: District Rs 10,000 (selection) / Rs 5,000 (winner); Division Rs 25,000 / Rs 15,000; State Rs 25,000 / Rs 30,000.
caveats: Applicant/family must be registered with the MP Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board.

title: KCR Nutrition Kit
benefit_summary: Monthly nutrition kit (1kg nutritional mix powder, 1kg dates, 3 bottles iron syrup, 500g ghee, a cup) for pregnant women in Telangana from economically weaker sections, to reduce anemia and improve maternal/infant health.
caveats: Renamed to 'MCH Kit' (Mother and Child Health Nutrition Kit) after the Dec 2023 government change — same contents, KCR branding removed; some reports note procurement/supply lapses under the new branding.

title: Krishak Durghatna Kalyan Yojana
benefit_summary: Farmer accident compensation in UP: Rs 5,00,000 for accidental death or complete disability (loss of both hands/legs, or one hand and one foot); Rs 2,50,000 for partial disability; graded lower amounts (Rs 1-3 lakh) for lesser disability percentages (25-50%) or loss of an eye; no premium required.
caveats: Covers landless farmers who farm on lease/share as well as landowners; farmer suffering 60%+ disability is also covered; family members (parents, spouse, children, grandchildren) are covered after the farmer's death.

title: Kantedar Tarbandi Yojana
benefit_summary: Subsidy for barbed-wire fencing to protect crops from stray animals: small/marginal farmers get 60% of cost up to Rs 48,000; other farmers get 50% up to Rs 40,000; community applications (10+ farmers, 5+ hectares combined) get 70% up to Rs 56,000/farmer. Covers up to 400 meters of fencing per farmer.
caveats: Minimum land requirement is 1.5 hectares (0.5 hectares in Scheduled Tribe areas, recently reduced from 1.5 ha generally); priority given to SC (17.83%), ST (13.48%), and women farmers (30% participation target).

title: Kisan Kaleva Yojana
benefit_summary: Subsidized meal (8 chapatis, dal, vegetables, jaggery/buttermilk) at Rs 5/plate for farmers and their assistants (Hamal/Palledar/Tulara) selling produce at market (mandi) premises; total meal cost is Rs 40, with Rs 35 subsidized by the Market Committee.
caveats: Applicant must be a licensed member of the market premises.

title: Kalyana Lakshmi Pathakam
benefit_summary: One-time financial assistance of Rs 1,00,116 at marriage for unmarried SC/ST/BC/EBC girls in Telangana (18+); Rs 1,25,145 for disabled girls' parents regardless of caste. Available only once in a lifetime.
caveats: BC/EBC income limit is Rs 2,00,000/year (urban) or Rs 1,50,000/year (rural); marriage must be on or after 2 October 2014; FY2025-26 allocation has seen widely reported disbursement delays.

title: Kam Lagat Pyaaj Bhandaran Sanrachna
benefit_summary: Subsidy for building a low-cost onion storage structure (25 metric ton capacity): 50% of unit cost, capped at Rs 87,500.
caveats: Applicant must hold a minimum of 0.5 hectares of land and be cultivating onions.

title: Krushi Mahotsav
benefit_summary: Agricultural outreach event providing free scientific-farming guidance, soil health cards, subsidized input kits for small farmers, and sanction letters for other agricultural schemes — no direct cash from this scheme itself.

title: Krishak Bandhu Scheme
benefit_summary: Assured annual income support of Rs 10,000/acre/year (>=1 acre) or a minimum Rs 4,000/year (<1 acre), paid in two installments (Kharif and Rabi); plus a one-time death benefit of Rs 2,00,000 to legal heirs if a registered farmer/sharecropper aged 18-60 dies.
caveats: The 18-60 age band applies ONLY to the separate one-time Rs.2,00,000 death benefit paid to a deceased registered farmer's heirs -- NOT to the main annual cultivation assistance (Rs.10,000/acre or minimum Rs.4,000/year), which has no age restriction and depends solely on land ownership/tenancy documentation. Applicant must hold cultivable land with RoR/Patta/Forest Patta, or be a recorded Bhagchasi (sharecropper). [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Removed min_age=18/max_age=60 from the main record -- those fields described the death-benefit component only and would have wrongly excluded landholding farmers under 18 or over 60 from the actual annual income-support payment.

title: Kushal Shramik Sahay Yojana (GBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Full course-fee reimbursement for up to two children of registered Gujarat construction workers enrolled in Skill University-affiliated courses (paid annually for multi-year courses).
caveats: Age limit of 30 does not apply if the child has a disability; assistance limited to the first attempt in an academic year (no second aid for repeating the same class/standard).

title: Kanya Sumangala Yojana
benefit_summary: Total benefit of Rs 25,000 (raised from Rs 15,000 in 2024) paid across 6 DBT milestone installments: Rs 5,000 at birth, Rs 2,000 after full immunization, Rs 3,000 on Class 1 admission, Rs 3,000 on Class 6 admission, Rs 5,000 on Class 9 admission, and Rs 7,000 on passing Class 12 and taking admission in a 2+ year degree/diploma course.
caveats: Applicant family must be UP residents with a permanent residence certificate; benefit limited to a maximum of 2 girls per family (with special provisions for twins).

title: Kisan Samriddhi Yojana - Chhattisgarh
benefit_summary: Grant for tube-well boring and pump installation for irrigation: General category farmers get actual cost or Rs 10,000 (boring)/Rs 20,000 (pump), whichever less; SC/ST farmers get actual cost or Rs 18,000 (boring)/Rs 25,000 (pump), whichever less.
caveats: Not eligible if the farmer previously received a tube-well mining grant under this or any other department scheme; priority given to small/marginal farmers. Note clarifies this is a distinct scheme from the Krishak Unnati Yojana successor programs — do not conflate.

title: Khushi Scheme
benefit_summary: Free sanitary napkins for girl students in Classes 6-12 at government/government-aided schools in Odisha (about 17 lakh beneficiaries); rural women outside this group can get 6 pads for Rs 6.

title: Karkhandar Scheme For Development Of Craft Sector
benefit_summary: Skill-upgradation training stipend for craft-sector trainees in J&K: Rs 2,000/month per trainee for 6 months (via Aadhaar-linked bank account); trainer (Karkhandar) gets Rs 2,000/trainee/month plus a Rs 25,000 lump sum per training batch for logistics.
caveats: Applicant must be a pass-out/ex-trainee from a Handicrafts & Handloom Dept training centre; disbursement is via DBT only, with the trainer's honorarium paid only after skill assessment.

title: Kotwar Cycle Evam Torch Sahayata Yojana
benefit_summary: Financial assistance of Rs 3,000 (or CSIDC fixed rate, whichever lower) for a bicycle, plus Rs 750 for a torch, for registered unorganized workers.
caveats: Applicant must not have received a cycle/torch under this or another department scheme previously. [Fix 2026-07-23] Occupation constraint removed from structured matching (originally tagged "unorganized_worker", not a real FLOW-selectable value) -- this is for registered unorganized workers specifically.

title: Kerala Stressed MSMEs Revival & Rehabilitation Scheme
benefit_summary: One-time financial assistance up to Rs.5 lakh per unit for stressed/sick MSMEs in Kerala, covering margin money grant, interest subvention (6%/yr, max Rs.1 lakh), and restart expenses.
caveats: CORRECTED note: total assistance capped at Rs.5 lakh/unit, composed of working capital grant (up to Rs.2 lakh), interest subvention (up to Rs.1 lakh), plant/machinery (up to Rs.1.5 lakh), repair/maintenance (up to Rs.1 lakh), statutory dues (up to Rs.40,000). Unit must restart within 1 month and operate continuously for 5 years or assistance is recovered.

title: Kushal Yuva Program
benefit_summary: Free 240-hour soft-skills/English/computer literacy training for Bihar youth, plus a one-time Rs.1,000 self-help allowance for 75%+ attendance.
caveats: Age relaxation to 33 for SC/ST/PwD, 31 for OBC. Must have passed Class 10th. Applicant must not be employed/self-employed.

title: LIDCOM 50% Subsidy Scheme
benefit_summary: 50% subsidy (max Rs.10,000) on a loan up to Rs.50,000 for Charmakar (SC cobbler/leather-worker) community members in Maharashtra.

title: Labour Accident benefit Scheme- Gujarat Labour Welfare Board
benefit_summary: Financial assistance of Rs.25,000 for workplace-accident disability between 40-70%, or Rs.50,000 for disability exceeding 70%.
caveats: Organization/unit must have paid Labour Welfare Fund contributions regularly for the last year. Application must be made within 2 years of the accident. [Fix 2026-07-23] Occupation constraint removed from structured matching (originally tagged "labourer/industrial_worker", not real FLOW values) -- worker_board_registration_required=True already carries the real gate (Gujarat Labour Welfare Board registration).

title: Loan Assistance to Scheduled Castes Students for Commercial Pilot Training
benefit_summary: Loan of Rs.25 lakh at 4% interest for SC students in Gujarat to undergo Commercial Pilot License training, repayable over 10 years.
caveats: Must have passed Matriculation/HSC; training institute must be government-approved; candidate must serve in India for at least 5 years after training abroad.

title: Ladli Beti Scheme
benefit_summary: Government deposits Rs.1,000/month for 14 years (total ~Rs.1,68,000 principal) into a recurring/term deposit for a girl child, maturing at age 21 with maturity value around Rs.6.5 lakh.
caveats: Girl must be born on or after 01/04/2015. No partial withdrawals allowed. Family annual income must be below Rs.75,000.

title: LIDCOM Education Loan Scheme
benefit_summary: Education loan for postgraduate SC (Charmakar community) students: up to Rs.30 lakh for study in India, Rs.40 lakh abroad, at 6-7% (male) or 5.5-6.5% (female) interest.
caveats: CORRECTED note: raw data understated figures — actual is Rs.30L(India)/Rs.40L(abroad) at 6%/5.5% (India, male/female) or 7%/6.5% (abroad, male/female), not Rs.10L/Rs.20L at 4%/3.5% as originally listed. Repayment 10yr (up to Rs.10L) or 12yr (beyond). Household income cap Rs.3,00,000/year.

title: LIDCOM Gattai Stall Scheme
benefit_summary: 100% subsidy for erection of a tin stall (4'x5'x6.5') costing Rs.16,367 plus Rs.500 incidental charge, for roadside cobblers of the Charmakar community in Maharashtra.
caveats: Applicant must be identified as a Roadside Cobbler by the Gram Panchayat.

title: Khet Talai
benefit_summary: Subsidy for farm-pond (Khet Talai) construction: SC/ST/small/marginal farmers get 70% (max Rs.73,500, kaccha) or 90% (max Rs.1,35,000, plastic-lined); other farmers get 60% (max Rs.63,000) or 80% (max Rs.1,20,000).
caveats: CORRECTED note: two overlapping scheme IDs cover the same tiered farm-pond subsidy; recommend consolidating. Farmer needs minimum 0.3 hectare land (0.5 ha if joint holder). Subsidy only for ponds of min 400 cubic meter capacity.

title: Kanti Velugu
benefit_summary: Free universal eye screening for all Telangana citizens, with free spectacles, free cataract/glaucoma/retinopathy surgeries, and free medicines for common eye ailments.
