caveats: Not confirmed as an actively continued program under the Congress-led Telangana government (in power since Dec 2023) -- Telangana Today reported the government 'showing no signs of continuing' it, and it is absent from the state's official current initiatives list (telangana.gov.in/government-initiatives). Do not present as a confirmed active statewide benefit; advise users to confirm current status/camp schedules locally (PHC/district health office). [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Flagged as likely discontinued/uncertain rather than presenting as a confirmed active universal scheme, given a change of government and its absence from the current administration's initiatives list.

title: Livestock Health and Diseases Control
benefit_summary: Central scheme funding livestock vaccination (PPR, Classical Swine Fever), disease surveillance, mobile veterinary units, and subsidized generic veterinary medicine for farmers/livestock owners nationwide.
caveats: CORRECTED note: renamed/expanded Livestock Health and Disease Control Programme (LHDCP), Rs.3,880 crore Cabinet-approved outlay for FY2024-25/25-26, now includes a new 'Pashu Aushadhi' component for subsidized generic veterinary medicine via PM-Kisan Samriddhi Kendras. Livestock must be used for commercial purposes.

title: Lakshadweep Scholarship Scheme
benefit_summary: Monthly scholarship (Rs.200 to Rs.3,000 depending on course level) plus annual lump-sum grant (Rs.1,500-Rs.9,000) for Lakshadweep students from primary school through PhD.
caveats: Both parents and student must be born in Lakshadweep, or have one islander parent; scholars cannot hold other scholarships simultaneously. Family income ceiling Rs.2 lakh/year.

title: Laadli Laxmi Scheme
benefit_summary: Rs.1,00,000 financial assistance (fixed deposit) for a Goan girl child, payable at age 18 (unmarried) or between age 19-45 (married), aimed at improving the female sex ratio.
caveats: Applicant must be born in Goa or resident for 15 years (with 7 years continuous education in Goa), or meet parental residency of 15/25 years. Application must be submitted within one year of turning 18 or of marriage registration.

title: Ladli Laxmi Yojana
benefit_summary: Staggered benefit totalling ~Rs.1,43,000 for a Madhya Pradesh girl child: Rs.6,000/yr for 5 years into a fund, scholarships at Class 6/9/11/12 (Rs.2,000-6,000), Rs.25,000 on higher-education admission, and Rs.1,00,000 lump sum at age 21/Class 12/legal marriage.
caveats: Girl must be born on/after 1 Jan 2006, registered in local Anganwadi; parents must not be income taxpayers and generally must adopt family planning after 2nd child (exceptions for triplets, orphaned parent, rape victims, women prisoners).

title: Karma Veer Dadasaheb Gaikwad Sabalikaran & Swabhiman Yojana
benefit_summary: Grant of 2 acres irrigated or 4 acres non-irrigated land, now 100% government-subsidized (fully free), for landless BPL Scheduled Caste/Nav-Buddhist families in Maharashtra.
caveats: CORRECTED note: land grant changed to 100% free via GR dated 23 Dec 2025 — no longer 50% subsidy + 50% loan as previously. Priority given to deserted women/widows.

title: Kanya Vivah Sahayta Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.65,000 for a normal marriage, Rs.75,000 for an inter-caste marriage, Rs.85,000 per couple for mass/group marriages, plus a separate Rs.15,000 grant for event/arrangement costs -- for daughters (18+, groom 21+) of registered UP construction workers (365-day membership), capped at 2 daughters.
caveats: Worker must have completed 365 days of board membership. Daughter must be 18+, groom 21+. Benefit capped at 2 daughters per worker. Application within 1 year of marriage (15 days before for mass marriage). [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Updated to the November 5, 2025 UP BOCW Welfare Board revision (Rs.65k/75k/85k/15k), which remained in effect through at least June 2026 -- the old Rs.55k/61k/65k/5k figures were stale.

title: LIDCOM Margin Money Loan Scheme
benefit_summary: For loans of Rs.50,001-Rs.5,00,000, Corporation pays 20% of project cost as seed capital at 4% interest (max Rs.10,000 subsidy); beneficiary contributes 5%; bank covers remaining 75%. Repayable in 36-60 monthly installments.

title: Laptop Purchase Assistance Scheme- Gujarat Labour Welfare Board
benefit_summary: 50% of laptop cost or Rs.25,000 (whichever is less) for children of registered Gujarat labourers who scored 70%+ in Class 12 and are admitted to a professional/design course, laptop price capped at Rs.50,000.
caveats: Parent worker must have contributed to Labour Welfare Fund for at least 1 year. Student must not have taken admission abroad. Application within 6 months of laptop purchase in the same year as board exam.

title: Lokprasar Prakalpo Scheme
benefit_summary: Rs.1,000/month pension for enlisted folk/tribal artists aged 60+ in West Bengal; artists under 60 get Rs.1,000/month retainer fee plus Rs.1,000/day performance fee when engaged at government events.
caveats: Applicant must be recognized by the Folk & Tribal Cultural Centre as belonging to a folk-art lineage/tribal cultural team.

title: Leprosy Pension Scheme
benefit_summary: Rs.3,000/month pension for persons disabled due to leprosy (any percentage) in Uttar Pradesh, below poverty line.
caveats: Income limit is Rs.56,460/yr urban and Rs.46,080/yr rural — used higher (urban) figure as the applicable ceiling. Not eligible if already receiving another pension scheme.

title: Lakshya Scheme
benefit_summary: Rs.1,00,000 for Tripura candidates clearing UPSC Civil Services Prelims (for coaching/travel until Mains), plus additional Rs.20,000 on clearing Mains and being called for interview.
caveats: Can receive assistance only twice regardless of attempts. Family income must not exceed Rs.10 lakh/year.

title: Ladli Social Security Allowance Scheme
benefit_summary: Rs.3,000/month per family for Haryana families with only daughters (no sons), paid to a parent aged 45-60, for 15 years from the date either parent turns 45.
caveats: After age 60 the benefit converts to the Old Age Samman Allowance Scheme. Family gross annual income must not exceed Rs.2,00,000. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Rs.2,750/month was the 01.04.2023 rate; revised to Rs.3,000/month effective 1 January 2024 per socialjusticehry.gov.in.

title: Labor Tool Assistance Scheme
benefit_summary: Free tool kit (or fixed cash equivalent) for registered construction workers in Chhattisgarh, one trade per worker.
caveats: Also known as Mukhyamantri Shramik Auzar Sahayata Yojana, started 01.10.2010.

title: Loans for Tools (MBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: A loan of Rs.5,000 (one-time) for purchase of tools by registered Meghalaya construction workers, recovered in up to 60 monthly installments.
caveats: CORRECTED note: this is a loan, not a grant. Requires 3 years of fund membership with regular contributions. Cannot resell tools purchased; no second grant allowed. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Fixed backwards age field: this is a MINIMUM age of 55 (no maximum), not a max_age of 55. The MBOCWWB's own page phrase 'completed 55 years' denotes a floor, consistent with standard Indian government usage (confirmed by the same page's Pension Plan scheme using identical phrasing for its own 60-year minimum).

title: Medical Assistance (ANBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Medical assistance for registered A&N construction workers and dependents: Rs.200/day for first 5 days of hospitalization, Rs.100/day thereafter (max Rs.5,000); Rs.1,00,000 if referred to mainland for treatment; Rs.1,000 for emergency treatment in A&N (once/year); Rs.600/day (max Rs.15,000) for referral from outer islands to Port Blair.
caveats: Requires medical certificate and referral letter from competent authority for higher-value claims.

title: Mukhyamantri Arogya Artham Yojana
benefit_summary: Cashless health insurance cover up to Rs.10 lakh per family per year for lower-income Gujarat families, covering hospitalization, surgery, cancer/kidney/cardiac treatment, and transportation.
caveats: MERGED note: this scheme has merged with Mukhyamantri Amrutum Yojana into unified PMJAY-MA (launched 17 Oct 2024) combined with central Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY — recommend showing one entry for both maay and ma slugs. Applicant must not have existing health insurance; covers up to 5 members (7 for larger families). [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Coverage doubled from Rs.5 lakh to Rs.10 lakh per family per year since the July 2023 Gujarat govt revamp, reinforced by the Oct 2024 unified PMJAY-MA card rollout; Rs.10 lakh remains current per Dec 2025 reporting.

title: LIDCOM Training Scheme
benefit_summary: Free in-kind training for Charmakar community students in Maharashtra: footwear design (via FDDI Amethi), UPSC/MPSC exam coaching, and a Smartness Quotient Booster program.
caveats: No stipend or cash — training is in-kind only.

title: Ladies Vocational Centres
benefit_summary: 11-month vocational training (tailoring, leather-work, embroidery, stenography, carpentry, weaving) for women/girls in J&K, with a Rs.100/month stipend.
caveats: Age 14-40 with Middle pass for craft trades; age 16-25 with 10+2 pass for stenography.

title: Medical Assistance (GBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.400/day for the first 5 days of hospitalization plus Rs.40/day thereafter (max Rs.2,000), for registered Goa construction workers hospitalized due to accident or disease.
caveats: Requires 90 days of registered service in the year. Unregistered workers/dependents can qualify with a certificate from the builder or area inspector.

title: Marriage Assistance Scheme (PBAOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.7,000 marriage assistance (DBT) for a registered Puducherry construction worker's children (up to 2 children), or for the worker's own marriage if female.
caveats: Applicant must not have defaulted on Board fund contributions for over a continuous year. Apply within 6 months of marriage.

title: Mukhyamantri Amrutum Yojana Scheme
benefit_summary: Cashless medical/surgical care (cardiovascular, neurosurgery, burns, cancer, renal, neonatal) for BPL families in Gujarat through an empanelled hospital network; MA Vatsalya extension covers families up to Rs.4 lakh income (Rs.6 lakh for senior citizens) including ASHA workers and Class-3/4 govt employees.
caveats: MERGED note: this scheme has merged with Mukhyamantri Arogya Artham Yojana into unified PMJAY-MA (launched 17 Oct 2024) — same scheme as 'maay' slug, recommend a single combined bot entry. [Fix 2026-07-23] Occupation constraint removed -- the originally-tagged asha_worker/govt_employee combo did not match this scheme's actual BPL-family healthcare purpose (max_income already gates it) and looked like an extraction error.

title: Marriage Assistance (A.B.O.C.W.W.B)
benefit_summary: Rs.25,000 marriage assistance for a registered Assam construction worker's children (up to 2 children), or for the worker's own marriage if female.
caveats: Requires 5 years of continuous Board membership.

title: Marriage Assistance To Differently Abled Women (Parinayam-II)
benefit_summary: One-time marriage assistance of Rs.30,000 for differently-abled Kerala women aged 18+.
caveats: Family income must not exceed Rs.1,00,000/year. Second marriage after dissolution is also eligible.

title: Marriage Assistance To Daughters Of Differently Abled Parents (Parinayam-I)
benefit_summary: One-time marriage assistance of Rs.30,000 for daughters (up to two per family) of differently-abled parents in Kerala.
caveats: Second daughter's marriage assistance only claimable 3 years after the first grant. Family income must not exceed Rs.1,00,000/year.

title: Marriage Assistance To Daughters Of Prisoners
benefit_summary: Marriage assistance of up to Rs.30,000 per person for daughters of Kerala BPL families where a parent is imprisoned for more than 2 years (max 2 daughters/family).
caveats: Application must be submitted after 6 months but within 1 year of marriage. Grant not payable again if remarried after the assisted marriage dissolves.

title: Maintenance Allowance for Leprosy Affected Persons
benefit_summary: Rs.2,000/month financial assistance for leprosy-affected persons with 40%+ deformity in Tamil Nadu.
caveats: Beneficiary must not receive any other Tamil Nadu pension benefit. Note: one district page shows a stale Rs.1,500 figure; weight of evidence favors Rs.2,000.

title: Maintenance Allowance for Persons Affected with Muscular Dystrophy
benefit_summary: Rs.2,000/month financial assistance for persons affected by muscular dystrophy with 40%+ disability in Tamil Nadu.
caveats: Note: one district page shows a stale Rs.1,500 figure; weight of evidence favors Rs.2,000.

title: Mukhyamantri Asangathit Karmakar Ijjat Monthly Season Ticket Card Yojana
benefit_summary: Monthly train/bus season ticket (commute pass) for unorganized workers in Chhattisgarh commuting up to 150km for daily travel.
caveats: Not eligible if already receiving a similar benefit from another state scheme. Started 19 June 2017 (not 30.06.2023). [Fix 2026-07-23] Occupation constraint removed from structured matching (originally "unorganized_worker", not a real FLOW value) -- worker_board_registration_required=True already carries the real gate. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Reverted an incorrect prior 'correction' that changed 150km to 50km -- the live myScheme.gov.in page confirms 150km is correct; the 'fix' had introduced the error, and the start-date claim (30.06.2023) was also wrong (actual: 19 June 2017).

title: Mukhyamantri Aarthik Kalyan Yojana
benefit_summary: Low-cost loan/equipment assistance for new BPL SC entrepreneurs in Madhya Pradesh, project cost up to Rs.50,000 with margin money subsidy of 50% of project cost (max Rs.15,000).
caveats: CORRECTED note: margin money subsidy is 50% of project cost capped at Rs.15,000, not a flat Rs.50,000. Not eligible if already availing another govt entrepreneur/self-employment scheme; usable only once.

title: Marriage Assistance For Legally Married Transgender Couples
benefit_summary: One-time marriage assistance of Rs.30,000 for legally married transgender couples (post Sex Reassignment Surgery) in Kerala.
caveats: Application must be made 6 months to 1 year after marriage. Not eligible for a second marriage after divorce if already availed.

title: Mamata Scheme
benefit_summary: Conditional cash transfer of Rs.10,000 (in two installments: Rs.6,000+Rs.4,000) to pregnant/lactating women in Odisha for their first two live births.
caveats: CORRECTED note: amount doubled in Feb 2024 to Rs.10,000 total, up from Rs.5,000. Not eligible for those already receiving maternity benefit as govt/PSU employees or spouses of such employees. Distinct from (not merged with) Subhadra Yojana.

title: Medical Assistance (MBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.200/day for first 5 hospitalized days plus Rs.20/day thereafter (min Rs.1,000 total), for registered Meghalaya construction workers hospitalized 5+ days; up to Rs.5,000 ex-gratia for accident-caused disability.

title: Mukhyamantri Avivahita Pension Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.600/month pension for unmarried women aged 50+ in Madhya Pradesh.
caveats: Applicant must not be an income taxpayer, government employee/officer, or honorary govt/non-govt office worker. Operates under the umbrella Samagra Samajik Suraksha Pension Yojana (SSSPY).

title: Marriage Assistance to Normal Persons Marrying Speech and Hearing Impaired Persons
benefit_summary: Rs.25,000 marriage assistance (Rs.12,500 NSC + Rs.12,500 cheque) for a non-disabled person marrying a speech/hearing-impaired person in Tamil Nadu, increased to Rs.50,000 if either spouse holds a degree/diploma, plus an 8g gold coin.
caveats: Both spouses must be above 18 years.

title: Marriage Assistance to Normal Persons Marrying Visually Impaired Persons
benefit_summary: Rs.25,000 marriage assistance (Rs.12,500 NSC + Rs.12,500 cheque) for a non-disabled person marrying a visually-impaired person in Tamil Nadu, increased to Rs.50,000 if either spouse holds a degree/diploma, plus an 8g gold coin.
caveats: Both spouses must be above 18 years.

title: Marriage Assistance to Normal Persons Marrying Orthopedically Differently Abled Persons
benefit_summary: Rs.25,000 marriage assistance (Rs.12,500 NSC + Rs.12,500 cheque) for a non-disabled person marrying an orthopedically differently-abled person in Tamil Nadu, increased to Rs.50,000 if either spouse holds a degree/diploma, plus an 8g gold coin.
caveats: Both spouses must be above 18 years.

title: Maintenance Allowance to Severely Affected Persons
benefit_summary: Rs.2,000/month financial assistance for locomotor-disabled persons in Tamil Nadu with disability exceeding 75% who cannot be rehabilitated through other schemes.

title: Maternity Assistance Scheme- Gujarat Labour Welfare Board
benefit_summary: Rs.10,000 financial assistance to female workers or wives of workers in Gujarat's organized sector during maternity, for one delivery only.
caveats: Worker must have contributed to Labour Welfare Fund continuously for 1 year; application within 1 year of delivery. [Fix 2026-07-23] Occupation constraint removed from structured matching (originally "labourer/industrial_worker") -- worker_board_registration_required=True already carries the real gate.

title: Mukhyamantri Aadharbhut Shiksha Prashikshan Sahayata Yojana
benefit_summary: Free coaching assistance for admission to Class 6th and 9th (e.g. Sainik School/Navodaya/KV/RTE seats) for the first two children of registered Chhattisgarh construction workers.
caveats: No fixed cash amount; in-kind coaching benefit. Requires 1 year regular Board membership.

title: Maternity Assistance Scheme (PBAOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.5,000 maternity assistance (via DBT within 15 days) for pregnant registered Puducherry construction worker or the pregnant spouse of a male beneficiary; available twice.
caveats: Applicant must not have defaulted on fund contributions for over a continuous year.

title: Marriage Assistance to Differently Abled Persons Marrying Differently Abled Persons
benefit_summary: Rs.25,000 marriage assistance (Rs.12,500 NSC + Rs.12,500 cheque) for a couple where both partners are differently-abled in Tamil Nadu, increased to Rs.50,000 if either spouse holds a degree/diploma, plus an 8g gold coin.
caveats: Both bride and groom must fall under one of the 21 RPwD Act 2016 disability categories and be above 18 years.

title: Maintenance Allowance to Intellectually Disabled Persons
benefit_summary: Rs.2,000/month financial assistance for intellectually disabled persons in Tamil Nadu with 40%+ disability.

title: Financial Assistance for the Marriage of Daughters of Widows/Destitute Women belonging to the Scheduled Caste
benefit_summary: Rs.20,000 financial grant for the marriage of daughters of SC widows/destitute women in Chandigarh, for up to two daughters per family.
caveats: Bride's mother must be SC; family monthly income must not exceed Rs.2,000 (verified by Tehsildar) — i.e. Rs.24,000/year; applicant must have resided in Chandigarh 3+ years; only for first marriage of each daughter.

title: Marriage Assistance Scheme- Gujarat Labour Welfare Board
benefit_summary: Rs.11,000 financial assistance to female workers in Gujarat's organized sector after their own marriage.
caveats: Requires 1 year Labour Welfare Fund contribution and 1 year gap between employment date and marriage date; application within 1 year of marriage. [Fix 2026-07-23] Occupation constraint removed from structured matching (originally "labourer/industrial_worker") -- worker_board_registration_required=True already carries the real gate.

title: Maternity Assistance Scheme (GBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.6,000 to the wife of a registered Gujarat construction worker (first 2 deliveries); a registered female construction worker herself gets Rs.17,500 pre-delivery plus Rs.20,000 post-delivery (total Rs.37,500), also covering miscarriage.
caveats: CORRECTED note: full breakdown confirmed as Rs.17,500 pre-delivery + Rs.20,000 post-delivery = Rs.37,500 for the registered female worker. Application must be made within 6-12 months of delivery/conception depending on stage.

title: Maternity Benefit (GBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.2,000 maternity benefit for registered Goa construction workers, available for up to two pregnancies.
caveats: Requires 90 days of registered service in the year.

title: Mai Bhago Vidya Scheme
benefit_summary: Free bicycle for BPL girl students in Classes 9-12 at government schools in Punjab, to reduce dropout due to distance from school.
caveats: CORRECTED note: provides free bicycles, not scooties as raw data suggested — no evidence found of an upgrade.

title: Maternity Benefit (ANBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.20,000 maternity benefit for a registered A&N female construction worker (1+ year membership); Rs.10,000 for a registered male worker's non-registered wife aged 19+.

title: Mukhyamantree Baal Aasheervaad Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.5,000-8,000/month for after-care (internship/vocational training/higher-education) for children leaving childcare institutions until age 24, plus Rs.4,000/month sponsorship for orphans under 18 living with relatives/guardians.
caveats: After-care requires 5 years' continuous residency in childcare institution (waived for orphans/abandoned children). Sponsorship guardian must not be eligible under Mukhyamantri Covid-19 Bal Seva Yojana.

title: Mukhyamantri Bhagyalaxmi Bond Scheme (GBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.25,000 bond for the first girl child (up to age 1) of a registered Gujarat construction worker, maturing when the girl turns 18.
caveats: Application must be made within 12 months of birth. Limited to one girl child per worker.

title: Madhu Babu Pension Yojana
benefit_summary: Pension for Odisha's elderly (60+), widows, leprosy patients, disabled persons (5+ yrs), and AIDS-affected persons: originally Rs.500/month (age 60-79) or Rs.700/month (80+), now boosted under new state government branding to Rs.3,000/month general or Rs.3,500/month for 80+ / 80%+ disability.
caveats: CORRECTED note: benefit amount massively increased under new government branding — Rs.3,000/Rs.3,500 replacing the earlier Rs.500-700 figures. Not eligible if receiving any other pension. Family income must not exceed Rs.24,000/year (for non-AIDS categories).

title: Maternity Benefit Scheme (HBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.36,000 (Rs.30,000 motherhood + Rs.6,000 nutrition) financial assistance for registered Haryana women construction workers after childbirth, for up to two children (expandable to 3 daughters).
caveats: Requires 1 year of regular Board membership. Not eligible if husband is availing paternity benefit elsewhere. Apply within 1 year of delivery with birth certificate.

title: Maternity Benefit (CBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.5,100 financial assistance to the spouse of a registered Chandigarh construction worker after childbirth, for up to two children.
caveats: Not payable if covered under ESIC. Requires 6 months prior Board membership and application within 3 months of delivery.

title: Mukhyamantri Bayan Jyoti Yojana
benefit_summary: Free lighting kit worth Rs.17,500 (20W tube light, 35W fan, inverter/battery, interest-free loan up to Rs.5,000) for weavers/ancillary workers in Odisha to enable late-hours weaving work.
caveats: At least 50% of family income must come from weaving. Only one beneficiary per family. Cannot resell unit within 3 years of purchase.

title: Maternity Benefit (MBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.1,000 maternity benefit for registered Meghalaya women construction workers, available up to twice.
caveats: Distinct from the Meghalaya marriage-assistance benefit under the same board.

title: Mukhyamantri Covid-19 Bal Seva Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.5,000/month pension until age 18 plus free education and ration for children orphaned when a parent/guardian died of COVID-19 (deaths between 1 March 2020 and 30 June 2021), plus fee assistance ranging up to Rs.1,50,000/year for higher/technical/medical education.
caveats: Closed cohort — only for children orphaned specifically during the COVID-19 period; scheme is winding down (no new enrollments expected) but existing beneficiaries remain covered. Not eligible if deceased parent was a government pensioner or family qualifies under Chief Minister Covid-19 Yodha Kalyan Yojana.

title: Merit Cum Means Based Scholarship For Students Belonging To The Minority Communities
benefit_summary: Rs.20,000/year course fee (subject to actuals) plus Rs.1,000/month (hosteller) or Rs.500/month (day scholar) maintenance allowance for minority-community (Muslim/Sikh/Christian/Buddhist/Parsi/Jain) students in technical/professional UG/PG courses, or full course fee reimbursement at listed institutes.
caveats: Requires minimum 50% marks in previous qualifying exam. Family income must not exceed Rs.2.5 lakh/year. ~60,000 scholarships distributed annually.

title: Madhyamik Drop-out Coaching
benefit_summary: 7-month special coaching for ST students who failed the Madhyamik (Class 10) exam in Tripura, with a Rs.65/day stipend for hostellers.
caveats: Preference given to students from interior Tribal Areas / BPL families.

title: Mukhyamantri Chiranjeevi Swasthya Beema Yojana
benefit_summary: Cashless health insurance cover up to Rs.25,00,000/family/year for Rajasthan residents; free for NFSA/SECC-2011-eligible families, small/marginal farmers, and contract govt workers, or Rs.850/family/year premium (50% subsidized) for other families.
caveats: RENAMED note: scheme renamed to 'Mukhyamantri Ayushman Arogya Yojana (MAAY)' after Dec 2023 government change, effective Feb 2024; coverage amount unchanged. Recommend confirming current branding before publishing.

title: Matritva, Shishu Evam Baalika Madad Yojana
benefit_summary: Maternity and child benefits for registered UP construction workers: Rs.6,000 lump sum for male workers, ~Rs.1,500/month for 3 months maternity allowance for female workers, Rs.20,000 for a son's birth, Rs.25,000 for a daughter's birth (Rs.25,000 FD for 1st/2nd/adopted daughter, Rs.50,000 FD for a disabled daughter, maturing if unmarried at 18).
caveats: CORRECTED note: raw data's flat Rs.6,000 figure was incomplete — full structure includes differentiated amounts by gender of child and worker sex as above. Only first two deliveries covered; not eligible if already receiving a similar government scheme.

title: Modular Functional Artificial Limbs
benefit_summary: Free distribution of modular functional artificial limbs for orthopedically differently-abled students, employed, or self-employed persons in Tamil Nadu.

title: Marriage Grant for One Daughter (Sainik Welfare)
benefit_summary: One-time Rs.10,000 marriage grant for one daughter (18+) of a Puducherry-registered ex-serviceman or widow of an ex-serviceman, PBOR category, no income ceiling.
caveats: Application must be sent within 3 months of marriage; benefit usable once. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Resolved a self-acknowledged discrepancy: corrected from Rs.25,000 to Rs.10,000 per the official Puducherry Sainik Welfare Dept benefits list. The Rs.25,000 figure belongs to a separate, unrelated Women & Child Development scheme (GMAWD) that was mistakenly carried into this record.

title: Monthly Grant To Old Crafts Persons (Pension) Component of the Development of Handicrafts Scheme
benefit_summary: Rs.5,000/month pension for artisans aged 60+ in Puducherry who have practiced their craft for at least 5 years; surviving spouse gets Rs.2,500/month after the artisan's death.
caveats: Requires 5 years of Puducherry residency and craft practice. Subject to annual renewal. Not eligible if receiving similar assistance elsewhere. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Corrected significant understatement: Rs.5,000/Rs.2,500 (not Rs.2,000/Rs.1,000), and income ceiling Rs.75,000/year (not Rs.40,000), per dic.py.gov.in.

title: Manav Garima Yojana
benefit_summary: Free tool kit (worth ~Rs.4,000-5,000 depending on trade) across 28 trades (tailoring, carpentry, plumbing, beauty parlor, vending, etc.) for Scheduled Caste individuals in Gujarat seeking self-employment.
caveats: CORRECTED note: toolkit value confirmed at Rs.4,000 (up to Rs.5,000 for some trades), previously left blank in raw data. No income limit for Most Backward Caste among SC. One benefit per family.

title: Mukhyamantri Janakalyan (Sambal 2.0) Yojana (Asangathit Karmakaar Manda)
benefit_summary: Social security bundle for unorganized workers in Madhya Pradesh: Rs.5,000 funeral grant, Rs.4,00,000 accidental death, Rs.2,00,000 general death, Rs.2,00,000 permanent disability, Rs.1,00,000 partial disability, plus free 200 units electricity/month, ~Rs.16,000 maternity benefit, and free education.
caveats: CORRECTED note: benefits are a bundle, not a flat Rs.5,000 as raw data suggested. Not eligible if applicant/spouse has other social security cover (PF/ESI/Gratuity), owns more than 1 hectare of irrigated agricultural land, is a government employee, or is an income taxpayer. [Fix 2026-07-23] Occupation constraint removed from structured matching (originally "unorganized_worker", not a real FLOW value) -- this is specifically for registered unorganized workers in Madhya Pradesh.

title: Mukhyamantri Konya Atmonirbhor Yojana
benefit_summary: A free Scooty (in-kind) for meritorious top-ranking girl students in the 1st semester of General Degree Colleges in Tripura, for commuting to college.
caveats: CORRECTED note: not a cash scheme — in-kind Scooty only for top rankers (100 TBSE + 40 CBSE toppers), effective 2023-24. Income ceiling Rs.8 lakh/year. Parents/guardians must be Tripura natives or 10+ years continuous residents.

title: Mumkin - Livelihood Generation Scheme
benefit_summary: Subsidy up to Rs.80,000 (or 10% of on-road vehicle price, whichever lower) plus a matching subsidy from the vehicle manufacturer, for unemployed J&K youth to purchase a small commercial vehicle for self-employment in transport.
caveats: Applicant must hold a commercial driving license and must not have received any other government self-employment subsidy. Usable only once.

title: Matrimonial Incentives
benefit_summary: Marriage incentive for a Maharashtra couple where one or both partners have 40%+ disability (valid UDID/disability certificate): Rs.1,50,000 if one partner is disabled and marries a non-disabled person, Rs.2,50,000 if both partners are disabled (per a Government Resolution dated 18 December 2025).
caveats: This scheme (run by the Persons with Disabilities Welfare Department) has NO caste requirement -- it was previously conflated with a separate SJSA inter-caste marriage incentive (Rs.50,000 state + Rs.2,50,000 Ambedkar Foundation, requiring one partner SC/ST/VJ/NT/SBC, no disability requirement), which is a distinct scheme. Administered by the District Disability Empowerment Officer; apply within one year of marriage registration. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Fixed record conflating two distinct schemes -- this one (Matrimonial Incentives, disability-based, no caste requirement) had incorrectly inherited the caste-gated inter-caste marriage scheme's amount and eligibility logic. Updated to the correct Dec 2025 disability-based figures.

title: Mukhya mantri Krishak Udyami Yojana
benefit_summary: Business loan of Rs.50,000-Rs.10,00,000+ for sons/daughters of farmers in Madhya Pradesh to start a business, with capital subsidy of 15% (general, max Rs.12,00,000) or 20-30% (BPL/SC/ST/OBC/women/disabled, max Rs.1,00,000-3,00,000 depending on project size), plus interest subsidy (5% general, 6% women) for up to 7 years.
caveats: Applicant's parents must not own agricultural land. Minimum 10th class education required. Applicant must not be an income taxpayer.

title: Mukhyamantri Kanya Vivah Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.5,000 marriage grant for BPL/low-income Bihar family daughters (18+) marrying a groom 21+, plus an additional Rs.2,000 if the marriage is registered (Rs.7,000 total).
caveats: Family annual income must not exceed Rs.60,000. Requires a self-attested declaration of non-payment of dowry.

title: Mukhyamantri Kanya Vivaah / Nikaah Yojana
benefit_summary: Financial assistance (approx Rs.49,000-55,000 total, varying by source: household setup, smartphone, marriage reimbursement) directly to the bride's account for needy girls/widows/abandoned women marrying via a mass/group marriage program in Madhya Pradesh, plus Rs.6,000 per couple to the organizing body.
caveats: CORRECTED note: no income restriction, but marriage must occur via an organized mass marriage program — single/individual marriages are not eligible. Note: this scheme (mkvymp) likely duplicates another MP scheme entry (vsylwb) covering the same underlying program (est. 2006, Nikah component added 2012) — recommend deduplicating.

title: Mukhyamantri Kanyadaan Yojana
benefit_summary: Marriage financial assistance for Rajasthan BPL/ST/minority/disabled brides: Rs.31,000-41,000 typically, up to Rs.41,000 for 10th-pass brides and Rs.51,000 for 12th-pass brides.
caveats: Applicant/parents must not be income taxpayers; also covers Palanhar Yojana beneficiaries. Amount tiered by education level of the bride.

title: Matru Jyothi - Financial Assistance For PwD Mothers
benefit_summary: Rs.2,000/month financial assistance for differently-abled mothers in Kerala until their child turns 2 years old, for nurturing and basic amenities.
caveats: Disability percentage threshold varies by type (50-100% depending on disability category, per RPwD Act 2016). Family income must not exceed Rs.1,00,000/year.

title: Mahatma Jyotirao Phule Jan Arogya Yojana
benefit_summary: Cashless health insurance covering hospitalization for 996 medical/surgical procedures across 34 specialties, now up to Rs.5 lakh/family/year (Rs.1.5 lakh base, Rs.2.5 lakh for renal transplants under older cap), available universally across Maharashtra since July 2024.
caveats: Effective 1 July 2024, integrated with Ayushman Bharat-PMJAY and extended to cover ALL families in Maharashtra with no income limit, no ration-card requirement, and no occupation restriction (~2.72 crore families / ~12.5 crore people). The old structured tiers (max_income Rs.1 lakh, AAY/BPL ration cards, farmer/construction/journalist occupation) describe the scheme's PRE-2023/2024 restrictive eligibility, since superseded. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Removed the stale restrictive structured fields (max_income/ration_card_types/occupation) that contradicted this record's own 'universal coverage' benefit_summary -- a matching bot using those fields as hard filters would have wrongly rejected otherwise-eligible Maharashtra residents.

title: Mahatma Jyotiba Phule Mandi shramik kalyaan yojana
benefit_summary: Benefit bundle for licensed Rajasthan mandi (market) workers: 45 days' wage maternity support, 15 days' wage paternity leave, Rs.75,000 marriage assistance (licensed woman or 2 daughters), merit scholarships (Rs.2,000-6,000), Rs.25,000 natural-death benefit, Rs.50,000 accidental-death benefit, Rs.2,000 maternity assistance, and Rs.500/year education scholarship for children in Class 1-8.
caveats: CORRECTED note: raw data's flat Rs.50,000 figure was only the accidental-death benefit — natural death is Rs.25,000, and there are multiple other benefit tiers as listed above. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Marriage assistance increased from Rs.50,000 to Rs.75,000 per daughter under the Rajasthan FY2025-26 budget (announced ~Feb 27, 2025), still capped at 2 daughters.

title: Mahatma Jyothiba Phule Overseas Vidya Nidhi for BC and EBC Students
benefit_summary: Up to Rs.20 lakh grant (paid in two Rs.10 lakh installments) for fees/living expenses for BC/EBC Telangana students pursuing postgraduate studies at accredited universities in USA, UK, Australia, Canada, Singapore, Germany, New Zealand, Japan, France, or South Korea, plus optional Rs.10 lakh education loan and visa/flight reimbursement.
caveats: CORRECTED note: amount increased to Rs.20 lakh from an earlier Rs.1 lakh figure in older snapshots. Only 1 child per family eligible; awarded once per lifetime; family income cap Rs.5 lakh/year; only 300 students sanctioned/year.

title: Mukhyamantri Jankalyan (Shiksha Protsahan Yojna)
benefit_summary: Full tuition/admission fee coverage for higher education (graduate, engineering up to Rs.1.5 lakh/year, medical via NEET, polytechnic/ITI/diploma courses) for children of unorganized workers registered with the Madhya Pradesh Labour Department.
caveats: Applicant's parent must be a registered unorganized worker. Mess charges and caution money are not covered. May duplicate/overlap with the 'sppy' scheme in the source database — recommend distinguishing or merging listings.

title: Mukhyamantri Kisaan Kalyaan Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.6,000/year (three installments of Rs.2,000) state top-up for Madhya Pradesh farmers, added on top of the central PM-Kisan Rs.6,000/year, totaling Rs.12,000/year via DBT.
caveats: Farmer must be registered under PM Kisan Samman Nidhi Yojana and own cultivable land. Excludes constitutional post-holders, legislators, government employees/pensioners (pension >=Rs.10,000/month), income-tax payers, and licensed professionals (doctors/engineers/lawyers/CAs/architects). [Audit fix 2026-07-23] MP state top-up increased from Rs.4,000/year (2 installments) to Rs.6,000/year (3 installments) since FY2023-24, bringing the combined total with central PM-Kisan to Rs.12,000/year, not Rs.10,000/year.

title: Mukhyamantri Kisan Sahay Yojana
benefit_summary: Financial assistance for Gujarat farmers whose crops are damaged by natural calamities (drought/flood/earthquake): Rs.20,000/hectare (33-60% crop loss) or Rs.25,000/hectare (60%+ loss), capped at 4 hectares (max Rs.1,00,000/farmer).
caveats: No premium required. Farmer must have availed an agricultural loan and have the crop loss certified by the Revenue Department; land must be surveyed with a record of rights.

title: Mukhya Mantri Kanyadaan Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.40,000 marriage financial assistance for daughters of BPL families, widows, and destitute women in Himachal Pradesh.
caveats: Covers unmarried daughters of BPL families (the primary beneficiary group), widows, destitute/orphan women, and divorced/deserted women -- NOT restricted to widows. Family annual income must be below Rs.35,000. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Removed the incorrect marital_status=['widowed']-only restriction, which would have wrongly excluded unmarried BPL daughters (the scheme's main beneficiary group) and divorced/deserted women -- our schema has no clean way to encode this broad multi-category eligibility, so the constraint has been dropped rather than mis-gated.

title: Mukhyamantri Mahalaxmi Kit Yojana
benefit_summary: Free nutritional/postpartum care kit (dry fruits, blankets, sanitary items) for new mothers and a baby-care kit for their first two daughters, in Uttarakhand.
caveats: Duplicate note: this is the same scheme as 'mmy' (Mukhyamantri Mahalaxmi Yojana) in the source database — should be merged, not shown as two separate schemes.

title: Mukhiya Mantri Protsahan Yojna
benefit_summary: One-time Rs.75,000 incentive/award for Himachal Pradesh students admitted to IIT, AIIMS, IIM (PG Diploma), ISM Dhanbad, or IISc Bangalore.

title: Mukhya Mantri Sahara Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.3,000/month financial assistance for economically weaker Himachal Pradesh patients with Parkinson's disease, cancer, paralysis, muscular dystrophy, hemophilia, thalassemia, or chronic renal failure; Rs.1,500/month for HIV/AIDS patients.
caveats: Not eligible if already receiving another government pension scheme. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Added missing max_income=Rs.4,00,000/year -- a hard, independent eligibility gate for this scheme regardless of qualifying disease status; was previously null (no cap enforced).

title: Mukhyamantri Mahalaxmi Yojana
benefit_summary: In-kind Mahalakshmi Kit (dry fruits, clothing, sanitary items for the mother; baby clothes/blanket/vaccination card for the newborn girl) for pregnant/postpartum women and their first two daughters in Uttarakhand.
caveats: Family income must not exceed Rs.6,000/month (Rs.72,000/year). Not for families of income-tax-paying government employees. Distinct from ngy scheme (a separate cash-milestone scheme).

title: Mukhyamantri Noni Babu Medhavi Shiksha Sahayata Yojana
benefit_summary: Merit-based education assistance for the first two children of registered Chhattisgarh construction workers, ranging Rs.5,000-12,500 (Class 10-12 through vocational/professional courses, higher for female students), up to Rs.1,00,000 for state-level top-10 rankers, full academic fees for undergrad/postgrad admission, and Rs.50,00,000/session for study abroad.
caveats: Requires 75%+ marks for most tiers; registration must be done 90 days in advance. Student must reimburse fees if they discontinue studies. Not eligible if receiving assistance for studying abroad from another source.

title: Mukhyamantri Nirmaan Majadur Kaushal vikaas evan Parivaar Sashaktikaran Yojana
benefit_summary: Free skill-upgradation training and trade certification for registered Chhattisgarh construction workers, plus training for their family members, with an unskilled-wage stipend during training.
caveats: Not eligible if simultaneously receiving another state government benefit for the same purpose. Available once per 3 years for dependents.

title: Mukhyamantri Nirmaan Majadur suraksha upakaran sahaayata yojana
benefit_summary: Reimbursement for safety equipment (helmet, footwear, gloves, safety jacket, mask) up to Rs.1,500 for registered Chhattisgarh construction workers.
caveats: Applicant can apply only after 90 days of registration; worker purchases equipment first and is reimbursed on submitting invoice.

title: Mukhyamantri Nirman Shramik Awas Sahayata Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.1,00,000 lump sum housing assistance for registered Chhattisgarh construction workers to construct or purchase a house, disbursed as subsidy for loan interest payments.
caveats: CORRECTED note: benefit is Rs.1,00,000, not the Rs.50,000 stated in raw data. Requires 3+ years continuous registration; only one beneficiary per household; worker/family must not already own a residence in Chhattisgarh; land area capped at 500 sq ft urban / 1000 sq ft rural.

title: Mukhyamantri Matrupushti Uphar
benefit_summary: Rs.500 per antenatal checkup via DBT for pregnant women in Tripura, up to 4 times (max Rs.2,000), plus in-kind nutrition kits.

title: Mukhyamantri Mahila Utkarsh Yojana
benefit_summary: Interest-free, collateral-free loan up to Rs.1 lakh (repayable over 5 years, no processing fee) plus a 6%/year subsidy on timely repayment, for Gujarat women entrepreneurs starting/expanding a business, with training and skill-development support.
caveats: Applicant must have passed at least 8th standard. Note: some sources cite an income cap (Rs.1.2 lakh rural/Rs.1.5 lakh urban) not present in the raw data — worth confirming against the GWEDC portal.

title: Mukhya Mantri Vivah Shagun Yojna
benefit_summary: Tiered marriage assistance (Shagun) in Haryana: Rs.71,000 for SC/BPL widows' daughters, Rs.51,000 for widow/divorced/orphan daughters or mass marriages or Divyangjan, Rs.31,000 for other BPL/sportswomen — paid partly before marriage and partly on registration.
caveats: Applicant must not own more than 2.5 acres of land. Family income cap Rs.1,80,000/year (except sportswomen category, no income limit). Apply before marriage date; late applications up to 3 months accepted via escalating authority.

title: Mukhyamantri Medhavi Vidhyarti Yojana
benefit_summary: 100% fee coverage at government colleges, or up to Rs.1.5 lakh/year at private colleges, for meritorious Madhya Pradesh students (70%+ MP Board or 85%+ CBSE/ICSE in Class 12) admitted via JEE Mains/NEET/CLAT to engineering, medical, or law courses.
caveats: Family income must be below Rs.6 lakh/year. Mess fees and caution money are excluded. Disbursed via Aadhaar-linked DBT.

title: Mukhyamantri Nirmaan Shramik Dirghayu Sahayata Yojana
benefit_summary: Medical/accident reimbursement bundle for registered Chhattisgarh construction workers: up to Rs.20,000 for accidental medical treatment, Rs.1,000 for glasses, Rs.5,000 for dentures, Rs.6,000 for hearing aid, wage reimbursement for 15+ day hospitalization, and up to Rs.20,000 for serious illness (3 years' registration required for the illness benefit).
caveats: CORRECTED note: not a flat Rs.20,000 payout — it is a schedule of separate reimbursement tiers as listed above.

title: Mukhyamantri Nirmaan Shramik Pension Sahayata
benefit_summary: Rs.1,500/month pension for Chhattisgarh construction workers aged 60+, registered for 10+ years; surviving spouse gets Rs.700/month family pension after the beneficiary's death.
caveats: Not eligible if already availing the Chief Minister Syan Sahayata Yojana or another parallel scheme. Must submit an annual survival certificate in March. Apply within 6 months of turning 59 years 3 months to 60 years. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Widow/family pension corrected from Rs.750/month to Rs.700/month per the official myscheme.gov.in scheme page; Rs.750 was an unsupported figure that spread across secondary aggregators only.

title: Mukhyamantri Noni Sashaktikaran Sahayata Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.20,000 financial benefit for the first two unmarried daughters (aged 18-21, 10th pass) of registered Chhattisgarh construction workers.
caveats: Parent must be registered for at least 1 year and worked 90 days in the preceding year. Not eligible if the daughter already received Minimata Kanya Vivah Yojana / Rajmata Vijayaraje Kanya Vivah Assistance.

title: Mai Ramabai Ambedakar Saat Phera Samuh Lagna Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.12,000 per couple (paid to the bride) for participating in a group/mass marriage in Gujarat, plus Rs.3,000/couple to the organizing institution (capped at Rs.75,000/event).
caveats: Girl must be 18+, groom 21+; not applicable for remarriage. Application must be made within 2 years of marriage with marriage registration certificate.

title: Mukhyamantri Rajya Bridhhabasta Pension Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.1,000/month old-age pension via DBT for Jharkhand residents aged 60+.
caveats: Not eligible if applicant/spouse is a retired/current government or PSU employee/pensioner, an income taxpayer, or already receiving another social-security pension.

title: Maintenance Of Pregnant Desi/Indigenous Cow/Buffalo Ration Scheme For BPL Families Belonging To Scheduled Caste Category
benefit_summary: 50% subsidized balanced cattle ration (3kg/day) for pregnant desi/indigenous cows or buffaloes, for up to 2 animals for 3 months (last trimester), for SC BPL families in Himachal Pradesh — estimated to raise farmer income by ~Rs.18,000/year via increased milk yield.
caveats: Distinct from a similar general-BPL, cow-only variant scheme (not a true duplicate).

title: Modular Reflective Folding Sticks (Smartcane)
benefit_summary: Free distribution of modular reflective folding sticks (smartcanes) for visually impaired persons in Tamil Nadu.

title: Mukhyamantri Rajshri Yojana
benefit_summary: Staggered financial benefit totalling Rs.50,000 per girl child born in Rajasthan on/after 1 June 2016: Rs.2,500 at birth, Rs.2,500 after 1-year vaccination, Rs.4,000 at Class 1 admission, Rs.5,000 at Class 6, Rs.11,000 at Class 10, Rs.25,000 at Class 12.
caveats: CORRECTED note: total across all 6 installments is Rs.50,000, not just the Rs.2,500 birth installment as raw data implied. Must be born in a JSY-registered medical institution; limited to 2 girls per family.

title: Manabik Scheme
benefit_summary: Rs.1,000/month pension via DBT for disabled persons (40%+, certified unfit for physical work) in West Bengal.
caveats: IN FLUX note: a rate increase (to Rs.1,500 or Rs.2,000) has been announced but not formally notified as of July 2026 — do not treat as confirmed. CORRECTED note: disability threshold is 40%+ per a 2020 notification, not 50%+ as raw data said. Requires 10+ years West Bengal residency. Unified under the Jai Bangla portal since April 2020. Note: income figure interpreted as Rs.1,00,000/month per Eligibility text, i.e. Rs.12,00,000/year — unusually high, flagging as ambiguous.

title: Mukhyamantri Sports Development Scheme - Retired Person
benefit_summary: Rs.30,000/month fixed remuneration (contractual employment) for retired sportspersons in Tripura serving as Senior Physical Instructors (gymnastics, swimming).
caveats: Contract period max 6 months, renewable/curtailable; total engagement capped at 5 years or age 64, whichever is earlier. [Fix 2026-07-23] Occupation constraint removed from structured matching -- this is specifically for retired sportspersons, an occupation category our FLOW does not capture.

title: Mandahasam Scheme To Provide Artificial Dentures To Senior Citizens
benefit_summary: Free artificial dentures (full-set replacement) for BPL senior citizens (60+) in Kerala who have completely lost their teeth, provided via listed dental colleges/treatment centers.
caveats: CORRECTED note: this is free in-kind dental treatment, not a fixed Rs.5,000 cash grant. Not available for partial tooth replacement — only full replacement. Priority given to the oldest applicants.

title: Masala Shetra Vistar Yojana
benefit_summary: Subsidy for spice-crop expansion in Madhya Pradesh: 50% of seed cost (max Rs.10,000/hectare general, Rs.14,000/hectare SC/ST) for seed spices, or 50% of planting material cost (max Rs.50,000/hectare) for turmeric/ginger/garlic.
caveats: CORRECTED note: raw data's flat Rs.10,000/hectare figure applies only to seed spices (general category) — SC/ST get Rs.14,000/hectare, and rhizome crops (turmeric/ginger/garlic) get up to Rs.50,000/hectare. Farmer must not currently be growing spices; grant is one-time, for 0.25-2 hectares.

title: Mukhyamantri Samajik Sahayata Prakalpa - Unorganized Workers
benefit_summary: Rs.2,000/month pension via DBT for unorganized-sector workers (home-based/self-employed/wage workers) in Tripura, generally aged 55+ (23-59 for female domestic workers/'Greha Sahayika').
caveats: Family income must not exceed Rs.1,00,000/year. Benefit stops on remarriage of a widow, a family member getting a government job, or income exceeding the cap. School-age children (6-14) in the household must be enrolled in school.

title: Mukhyamantri Samajik Sahayata Prakalpa - Vulnerable Women
benefit_summary: Rs.2,000/month pension via DBT for vulnerable women in Tripura — widows, deserted women, or unmarried women (45+) — aged 18-59.
caveats: Family income must not exceed Rs.1,00,000/year. Benefit stops on remarriage or if a family member gets a government job. School-age children (6-14) must be enrolled in school.

title: Mukhyamantri Shramik Siyaan Sahayata Yojana
benefit_summary: One-time lump sum of Rs.20,000 for Chhattisgarh construction workers aged 59-60 nearing automatic termination of Board membership at 60.
caveats: Requires at least 3 years of registered Board membership. Distinct from mnsdsy (a separate medical/accident reimbursement scheme).

title: Mukhyamantri Samajik Sahayata Prakalpa - Old and Infirm
benefit_summary: Monthly pension of Rs.2,000 transferred directly to bank account for poor elderly (60+) or infirm (cancer/AIDS/leprosy affected) residents of Tripura.
caveats: Stopped immediately on death, widow remarriage, a family member getting a government job, or if family income exceeds Rs.1,00,000. Children aged 6-14 in the family must be enrolled in a recognized school.

title: Mukhyamantri Samajik Sahayata Prakalpa - Persons with Disabilities
benefit_summary: Monthly pension of Rs.2,000 transferred directly to bank account for persons with disabilities (blindness, hearing/locomotor/intellectual disability, autism, cerebral palsy, etc.) resident in Tripura.
caveats: Verification note indicates 60%+ disability is required for this scheme though not stated in the eligibility text itself. Stopped immediately on death, widow remarriage, a family member getting a government job, or family income exceeding Rs.1,00,000. Children aged 6-14 in family must be enrolled in a recognized school.

title: Modified Special Wheel Chairs for Persons Affected with Cerebral Palsy
benefit_summary: Free distribution of modified/customized special wheelchairs to persons affected with cerebral palsy.
caveats: Verification note says the age-12+ criterion was not independently confirmed.

title: Mangalya Scheme For Widow Remarriage
benefit_summary: One-time financial assistance of Rs.25,000 to eligible widows and legally divorced women (aged 18-50) in Kerala upon remarriage.

title: Mukhya mantri Swarojgar Yojana
benefit_summary: Under Mukhyamantri Udyam Kranti Yojana (MUKY), the scheme MMSY was merged into via a Nov 2021 gazette notification: collateral-free loan of Rs.1,00,000 to Rs.50,00,000 (service-sector loans capped lower at up to Rs.25 lakh per some sources) with a flat 3% p.a. interest subsidy for up to 7 years, plus a CGTMSE credit-guarantee-fee subsidy.
caveats: MMSY (along with Mukhyamantri Yuva Udyami Yojana and Mukhyamantri Krishak Udyami Yojana) was merged into Mukhyamantri Udyam Kranti Yojana (MUKY) via a gazette notification dated 29 Nov 2021 -- this record now reflects MUKY's current terms. Applicant age 18-40, minimum 12th pass (not 5th class), family income cap Rs.12 lakh/year. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Corrected a record that (even after an internal 'correction') still described defunct standalone-MMSY terms nearly 5 years out of date. Updated to MUKY's actual current terms: age 18-40, 12th pass minimum, Rs.12 lakh income cap, Rs.1L-50L loan at flat 3% p.a. subsidy.

title: Mukhyamantri Tirth Yatra Yojana - Delhi
benefit_summary: Free pilgrimage travel (train/bus, food, accommodation, paramedical staff) for senior citizens (60+) resident in Delhi, with one attendant (21+) allowed per traveller/couple.
caveats: Applicant/spouse must not be a Central/State government or autonomous body employee and must not have availed the scheme before. Needs a certificate from local MLA confirming residence in the constituency. Capped at 1,100 residents per assembly constituency per year (77,000 total/year). Apply via e-district portal; scheme resumed after a pause and was expanded to include Ram Mandir Ayodhya/Dwarkadhish routes.

title: Meghalaya Tourism Development & Investment Promotion
benefit_summary: Capital subsidy of 30% of project cost for entrepreneurs building tourism homestays (max project cost Rs.16 lakh) or resorts (max project cost Rs.100 lakh) in Meghalaya.
caveats: CORRECTED per verification note: this is an entrepreneur/business capital subsidy, not an individual welfare benefit, and may be the wrong category for an individual-eligibility bot. Entrepreneur must own the land/property; project must be completed within 12-18 months; must follow government Minimum Wage policy.

title: Mukhyamantri Teerth Darshan Yojana
benefit_summary: One-time free pilgrimage (rail/bus travel, meals, accommodation) to a chosen pilgrimage site outside Madhya Pradesh, for senior citizens: men 60+, women 58+, with no age limit for citizens with 60%+ disability.
caveats: Applicant must not be an income taxpayer and must not have availed the scheme before; must be medically fit and free of specified infectious/serious diseases (certificate required). Groups capped at 25 people. Single pilgrims above 65 or 60%+ disabled citizens may bring a caretaker/helper.

title: Mukhyamantri Vriksharopan Protsahan Yojana
benefit_summary: Incentive of Rs.10,000 per acre per year for up to 3 years to Chhattisgarh farmers/forest-rights holders who plant trees instead of paddy on their land (also available to Gram Panchayats and Joint Forest Management Committees for commercial plantations on revenue land).
caveats: Applicant must have cultivated and sold paddy to the government in Kharif 2020, or hold forest rights over the land being planted.

title: Mukhyamantri Vridhjan Pension Yojna
benefit_summary: Monthly old-age pension via DBT for Bihar residents aged 60+: as per verification note, hiked to a flat Rs.1,100/month for all eligible seniors effective July 2025 (previously Rs.400 for age 60-79 and Rs.500 for 80+, as originally stated in scheme text).
caveats: MAJOR CHANGE per verification note: pension hiked from Rs.400(60-79)/Rs.500(80+) to flat Rs.1,100/month for all eligible seniors, effective July 2025 - use the corrected amount. Applicant must not be a retired government employee and must not be receiving any other government/family/social security pension.

title: Mahadevi Verma Shramik Pustak Kraya Dhan Yojana
benefit_summary: One-time lump sum of Rs.7,500 for postgraduate students to help buy books, for daughters of registered construction/labour workers in Uttar Pradesh.
caveats: Worker's monthly salary (basic + DA) must not exceed Rs.15,000; worker must have completed at least 6 months of continuous service at a registered establishment/factory. Benefit limited to two daughters per worker. If both parents are workers, only one can claim. A woman worker herself is also eligible. Eligible worker category is specifically employees registered under the Shops and Establishments Act 1962 or the Factories Act 1948 (shop/commercial establishment or factory workers) -- a distinct registration category from Building & Other Construction Workers (BOCW) board registration. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Corrected occupation tag from ['construction_worker','daily_wage'] to ['private_job'] (closest existing broad category) -- this scheme is for Shops/Establishments Act or Factories Act registered workers specifically, not construction/BOCW workers, per multiple independent sources.

title: Mukhyamantri Vriddhjan Samman Pension Yojana
benefit_summary: Monthly old-age pension of Rs.1,000 for Rajasthan residents: women 55+, men 58+, with a couple's annual income under Rs.48,000 (income condition waived for BPL/Antyodaya/Aastha card holders and certain Sahariya/Kathauri/Khairwa caste members).
caveats: Verification note flags this scheme has likely been effectively merged into the consolidated RAJSSP pension scheme, with the amount possibly folded into current age-tiered rates rather than a standalone flat Rs.1,000 - treat the exact current amount with caution. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Rajasthan's RAJSSP old-age pension baseline has been hiked in stages to Rs.1,450/month (Budget 2026-27) via Rs.1,150 (2024) -> Rs.1,250 (2025) -> Rs.1,300 (Jan 2026) -> Rs.1,450 (2026-27); the flat Rs.1,000 figure was stale.

title: Mukhyamantri Vishesh Yogyajan Sammaan Pension Yojana
benefit_summary: Monthly disability pension for Rajasthan residents with 40%+ disability (or dwarfism, eunuchism, cured leprosy/silicosis), family income under Rs.60,000/year: baseline Rs.1,450/month (current RAJSSP rate as of Budget 2026-27, up from a Rs.1,000/1,250 base), with historically higher special tiers for leprosy-free (Rs.2,500) and silicosis (Rs.1,500) patients whose current status after the baseline hike is not independently confirmed.
caveats: Verification note indicates this scheme has been folded into the CMSASPS tiered structure (Rs.750-1,000/month, age-tiered) - the standalone amounts above may no longer be current. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Updated baseline from Rs.1,000/1,250 toward the current RAJSSP-wide Rs.1,450 rate (per multiple sources including govtschemes.in's RAJSSP overview), while flagging that the special leprosy-free/silicosis tiers' post-hike status is less certain -- no primary Rajasthan government order could be directly retrieved to confirm those specific tiers moved in lockstep.

title: Mukhyamantri Work Form Home-Job Work Yojana
benefit_summary: Connects women in Rajasthan with work-from-home job opportunities (typing, documentation, stitching, data entry, programming, etc.) and gives a Rs.3,000 training incentive per trainee once a private unit issues a work-from-home offer letter paying over Rs.5,000.
caveats: Preference given to widowed, abandoned, divorced, disabled women and victims of violence. Confirmed still active under the same name as of the verification note, unchanged under the new state government.

title: Mukhyamantri Yuva Swavalamban Yojana
benefit_summary: Scholarship for Gujarat students pursuing diploma/degree/medical courses: tuition fee grant up to Rs.2,00,000/year (MBBS/BDS), Rs.50,000/year (engineering/professional), Rs.25,000/year (general degrees like BA/BSc/BCom), Rs.10,000/year (diploma), plus a hostel grant of Rs.1,200/month and a one-time book/equipment grant.
caveats: Requires 80th percentile or higher in Class 10/12 board exam (or 65% in diploma for diploma-to-degree students) from a recognized Gujarat institution; parental income must not exceed Rs.6,00,000/year (income certificate valid for 3 years). CORRECTED per verification note: open to ALL categories of students, not just non-reserved categories as the raw benefits text implied.

title: Mukhyamantri Yuva Swarojgar Yojana
benefit_summary: Bank loan for self-employment for Chhattisgarh youth: up to Rs.25 lakh for manufacturing, Rs.10 lakh for services, Rs.2 lakh for business, with a margin money grant (10-25% of project cost, max Rs.1,00,000+) and interest subsidy (5% general / 8% for SC/ST/OBC/minority/women/disabled/ex-servicemen/Naxal-affected).
caveats: Max age relaxed by 5 years for SC/ST/OBC/women/PWD/Naxal-affected family members/retired soldiers. Applicant must have passed at least 8th class, not be a loan defaulter, and family income must not exceed Rs.3,00,000/year. Only one person per family may apply; prior beneficiaries of PMRY/PMEGP or similar schemes are not eligible.

title: Mukhyamantri Yuba Yogajog Yojana In Tripura
benefit_summary: One-time grant of Rs.5,000 for final-year undergraduate students at government colleges in Tripura to purchase a smartphone.
caveats: Only for students studying in a college located within Tripura and in the final year of the course; benefit can be availed once in a lifetime; applicant must buy the smartphone in their own name.

title: Swanirbhar Naari
benefit_summary: Support for indigenous handloom weavers in Assam: direct procurement of hand-woven items without middlemen (better remuneration/online payments), skill training, certifications, and market access via showrooms and e-marketing.
caveats: Weaver must own at least one handloom in their household, have a bank account with Core Banking Solution (CBS), and ideally hold a yarn passbook from the Directorate of Handloom & Textiles, Assam. Registration requires physical field verification and is mapped to Aadhaar. Verification note confirms this is a procurement/support scheme, not a cash-transfer scheme.

title: Namo Shetkari Mahasanman Nidhi Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.6,000/year paid in three equal installments of Rs.2,000 via DBT to cultivable-landholding farmer families in Maharashtra, on top of the central PM-KISAN Rs.6,000/year, for a combined Rs.12,000/year.
caveats: Only farmer families (husband, wife, minor children) who held cultivable land as of 01.02.2019 and are eligible for PM-KISAN qualify. Benefit is credited only to Aadhaar-linked bank accounts; amounts credited to ineligible beneficiaries are recovered as per PM-KISAN SOP. Confirmed current as of the 8th installment paid March 2026.

title: National Awards For Empowerment Of Persons With Disabilities: National Awards For Institutions Engaged In Empowering Persons With Disabilities: Divyan
benefit_summary: Annual national award (certificate and shield) presented by the President/Vice-President of India on 3 December (International Day of Persons with Disabilities) to organizations/employers that are outstanding employers of persons with disabilities, with travel, boarding and lodging covered for awardees and one escort.
caveats: This is an institutional/organizational award (government bodies, PSUs, private/NGO employers), not a benefit for individual citizens - eligibility is based on the employing organization's disability-employment practices (e.g. at least 10% disabled staff), not on any individual applicant's personal characteristics. 2026 nomination window is 15 May-31 Jul 2026 via awards.gov.in.

title: National Awards For Empowerment Of Persons With Disabilities: National Awards For Institutions Engaged In Empowering Persons With Disabilities: Sugamy
benefit_summary: Annual national award (certificate and shield) presented by the President/Vice-President of India on 3 December (International Day of Persons with Disabilities), with travel, boarding and lodging covered for awardees and one escort.
caveats: This is an institutional/organizational award category, not a benefit for individual citizens - eligibility is based on the nominated organization's track record (e.g. placement rates, accessibility retrofits, years of service), not on any individual applicant's personal characteristics.

title: Nationwide Artificial Insemination Programme
benefit_summary: Free/subsidized artificial insemination (AI) services for cattle, buffalo, goats and sheep to improve livestock fertility, breed quality and milk/meat production for livestock owners in Madhya Pradesh.
caveats: Verification note flags this is actually a nationwide/central scheme run under the Rashtriya Gokul Mission (continuing through 2025-26 with Rs.2,400 crore allocation), mistagged as Madhya Pradesh-specific in source data - eligibility may not require MP residency in practice. Eligibility text also unusually excludes applicants belonging to Scheduled Castes/Tribes, and requires valid livestock registration, needed infrastructure/skills, and no prior criminal record.

title: National Action Plan for Skill Development of Persons with Disabilities
benefit_summary: Free vocational/skill training (short and long-term) for persons with disabilities across India, delivered through a nationwide network of skill training partners (government, VRCs, private institutes, NGOs), including mentorship for self-employment.
caveats: Applicant must be an Indian citizen with 40%+ disability (as per RPwD Act 2016), aged 15-59 at course start, enrolled in an NCVET-approved course, and must not have taken another NAP-SDP-sponsored course in the preceding year. Confirmed active under the SIPDA umbrella scheme; SOP revised 1 Jan 2024.

title: National Awards For Outstanding Services In The Field Of Prevention Of Alcoholism And Substance (Drug) Abuse: Best Integrated Rehabilitation Centre Fo
benefit_summary: Biennial national award (citation, memento and cash award of Rs.2,00,000) for outstanding institutions or individuals working in prevention of alcoholism/substance abuse and rehabilitation, presented by the President/PM of India on 26 June (International Day against Drug Abuse and Illicit Trafficking), with travel/boarding covered.
caveats: Nominations must come from an authorized nominating body (ministries, state governments, resource centres, apex chambers, past awardees, etc.) - self-nomination is not accepted. A past awardee (individual or organization) is ineligible for the next three award cycles.

title: National Awards For Outstanding Services In The Field Of Prevention Of Alcoholism And Substance (Drug) Abuse: Best Research Or Innovation
benefit_summary: Biennial national award (citation, memento and cash award of Rs.5,00,000) for outstanding institutions or individuals working in prevention of alcoholism/substance abuse and rehabilitation, presented by the President/PM of India on 26 June (International Day against Drug Abuse and Illicit Trafficking), with travel/boarding covered.
caveats: Nominations must come from an authorized nominating body (ministries, state governments, resource centres, apex chambers, past awardees, etc.) - self-nomination is not accepted. A past awardee (individual or organization) is ineligible for the next three award cycles.

title: National Family Benefit Scheme - Sikkim
benefit_summary: One-time lump-sum grant of Rs.30,000 (Rs.20,000 central share + Rs.10,000 state share) to a BPL household in Sikkim upon the death of the family's primary breadwinner.
caveats: Benefit goes to the household (spouse, minor children, unmarried daughters, dependent parents) of the deceased. Applicant must have a bank account under Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana. A homemaker woman in the family is also considered a 'breadwinner' for this scheme.

title: National Family Benefit Scheme - Uttar Pradesh
benefit_summary: One-time compensation of Rs.30,000 (raised from Rs.20,000 in 2013) to a BPL family in Uttar Pradesh after the death of the family's sole/lead earner (aged 18-60).
caveats: Income threshold varies by area: Rs.56,450/year for urban families, Rs.46,080/year for rural families - use the higher urban figure as the general threshold. Application is online only; no offline mode available.

title: Natural Death Benefit Scheme (PBAOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Financial assistance of Rs.70,000 (via DBT, within 1 month of application) to the nominee/dependent of a deceased registered construction worker in Puducherry, in addition to a separate Rs.70,000 LIC payout.
caveats: Deceased worker must have been registered with the Puducherry Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board, aged 18-60 (not having completed 60 in the preceding 12 months) at time of death, and must have contributed regularly without a default of more than one continuous year. Applications are accepted offline only.

title: National Merit Cum Means Scholarship
benefit_summary: Scholarship of Rs.12,000/year (Rs.1,000/month) for students studying in classes IX to XII at government/government-aided/local body schools.
caveats: Requires minimum 55% marks (relaxable by 5% for SC/ST) in Class VII exam plus a Scholastic Aptitude Test. Verification note indicates this is likely the same as the central National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme (nmmss), not a distinct Mizoram-specific scheme - may be a duplicate/mistagged record.

title: National Means-Cum-Merit Scholarship Scheme
benefit_summary: Scholarship of Rs.12,000/year (Rs.1,000/month) for 1,00,000 meritorious students each year, from Class IX through Class XII, paid via DBT to the student's bank account.
caveats: Parental income from all sources must not exceed Rs.3,50,000/year. Requires 55% marks (relaxable 5% for SC/ST) in Class VII exam, and passing state-level Mental Ability Test (MAT) and Scholastic Aptitude Test (SAT) with 40% aggregate. Only for students in government/government-aided/local body schools. Approved for continuation through 2025-26 (15th Finance Commission cycle).

title: Nikshay Poshan Yojana
benefit_summary: Financial/nutritional support incentive of Rs.1,000/month (corrected from the outdated Rs.500 figure) paid via DBT to every notified tuberculosis (TB) patient for the duration of anti-TB treatment.
caveats: CORRECTED per verification note: amount is Rs.1,000/month per notified TB patient, not Rs.500 as originally listed - that figure is outdated. Patient must be registered/notified on the NIKSHAY portal on or after 1 April 2018 (or already under treatment).

title: National Fellowship For OBC Students
benefit_summary: Fellowship for OBC students pursuing M.Phil./Ph.D.: JRF Rs.37,000/month for first 2 years, SRF Rs.42,000/month thereafter (rates revised Jan 2023), 1,000 slots per year, plus annual contingency allowance.
caveats: Applicant must have qualified UGC NET-JRF (Humanities/Social Sciences) or UGC-CSIR NET-JRF (Science). These 1,000 slots are over and above the normal OBC reservation quota for UGC Fellowships. Verification note flags this as a PhD/M.Phil fellowship of low relevance to typical welfare-eligibility queries. IMPORTANT: New candidate selections have been effectively frozen since the June 2024 cycle -- NBCFDC has not obtained Ministry clearance to finalize selection lists for three consecutive cycles (June 2024, Dec 2024, June 2025), citing insufficient scheme funds per an RTI response (July 2025). Previously-selected scholars continue receiving stipends (~2-month delay), but a new applicant should NOT expect imminent selection as of the most recent available reporting (through Nov 2025). [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Added a caveat flagging that new selections are frozen, so the bot doesn't imply a prospective applicant will imminently receive this fellowship.

title: Non-Governmental Aided Organization (Special Schools And Vocational Training Centre) For Disabled
benefit_summary: Free special education (ages 6-18) and vocational training (18+) for persons with disabilities (40%+) in Maharashtra, including free food, shelter and education for those in residential institutions.
caveats: Verification note clarifies there is no direct cash benefit to individuals - this is a grant-in-aid (salary/operating grants) to NGOs running the special schools; the individual child receives free education/training/residential care, not cash.

title: Nai Hetu Avashyak Upkaran Sahayata Yojana
benefit_summary: Free barber kit (scissors, straight razor, comb, hair-cutting cape, water spray bottle, shaving brush) for registered barbers who are unorganized workers in Chhattisgarh.
caveats: Applicant must be registered as an Unorganized Worker with the State Social Security Board, aged 18-60, and must not be receiving any other parallel state government scheme.

title: New Generation Innovation Network
benefit_summary: Grants to technical institutions in Tripura to set up innovation/incubation centres (Rs.10 lakh one-time setup + Rs.5 lakh/year operations), enabling student teams to get project funding (up to Rs.1 lakh per project, max 5 projects/year per institute) to develop start-up ideas.
caveats: This is an institutional grant to eligible technical institutes (based on infrastructure/faculty/quality criteria), not a direct individual cash benefit - individual students/teams benefit indirectly through project funding routed via the host institute. Confirmed under Tripura Start-Up Policy 2024.

title: Nanda Gaura Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.11,000 paid at birth of a girl child and Rs.51,000 on passing Class 12 (total Rs.62,000), for permanent resident families of Uttarakhand, paid into a joint bank account with the mother (or father/guardian).
caveats: Limited to two living girl children per family. Birth must occur in a government/private hospital or ANM centre (institutional delivery certificate mandatory); first-phase application must be made within 6 months of birth. Family annual income capped at Rs.72,000 (Rs.6,000/month). Second-phase (Class 12) applications must be submitted by 30 November each year. Bank account must be Aadhaar-linked.

title: NIJASHAREE HOUSING SCHEME
benefit_summary: Allotment of a flat (1BHK for LIG, 2BHK for MIG) via lottery on an ownership basis, plus a credit-linked subsidy of about Rs.1.80 lakh (LIG) or Rs.3.60 lakh (MIG), for Lower/Middle Income Group families in West Bengal.
caveats: Monthly family income must be Rs.15,000 or less (LIG) or Rs.30,000 or less (MIG) - annual figure used here (Rs.30,000 x 12 = Rs.3,60,000) is the higher/more inclusive MIG threshold; flag notes the income limit varies by category. Beneficiary/family must not already own a pucca house/flat in the state. Applicant must reside in the same district as the project; one flat per family; cannot reapply if already allotted a flat elsewhere in the district. Selection via transparent lottery.

title: New Entrepreneur-cum-enterprise Development Scheme
benefit_summary: Capital subsidy of up to 25% of project cost (max Rs.75 lakh) plus 3% interest subvention for first-generation entrepreneurs in Tamil Nadu, aged 21-35 (up to 45 for women/BC/MBC/SC/ST/ex-servicemen/transgender/differently-abled), with an additional 10% capital subsidy for SC/ST or differently-abled promoted enterprises.
caveats: Applicant must be a Tamil Nadu resident for at least 3 years, a first-generation entrepreneur with minimum 12th std/diploma/ITI qualification, and not a defaulter to any commercial bank or TIIC. Not eligible if already availed assistance under PMRY/REGP/PMEGP/UYEGP/TAHDCO or any SHG group loan. No income ceiling for the applicant.

title: NAMO E-Tablet Scheme
benefit_summary: Subsidized tablet (7-inch, 4G, preloaded with textbooks/e-books/video lectures) for first-year college/university/polytechnic students in Gujarat, market value Rs.8,000-12,000, available for a student contribution of Rs.1,000.
caveats: Applicant must have passed 12th standard from a recognized Gujarat institution and be in the first year of college/polytechnic. Targets about 3 lakh students per year.

title: Nari Niketans
benefit_summary: Free residential shelter (food, bedding, clothing) and free education for school-going girls, for deserted/destitute women or widows with no means of livelihood in Jammu & Kashmir, across 7 Nari Niketan homes (total capacity 280).
caveats: No cash transfer - this is a non-cash institutional shelter scheme, fully state-funded. Male children accompanying mothers are transferred to Bal Ashrams after age 8. Resident stays until rehabilitated, married, or covered under an employment/self-employment scheme. Apply via the District Social Welfare Officer.

title: National Pension Scheme For Traders And Self Employed Persons
benefit_summary: Voluntary contributory pension of Rs.3,000/month after age 60 for small traders/shopkeepers/self-employed persons, with matching government contribution during working years (Rs.55-200/month based on entry age); spouse gets 50% family pension on death.
caveats: Business annual turnover must not exceed Rs.1.5 crore. Applicant must not be enrolled in EPFO/NPS/ESIC. Exiting before 10 years returns only own contribution with savings-bank interest; after 10 years but before 60, own contribution plus actual accumulated interest is returned.

title: Nirman Shramik Auzaar Toolkit Sahayata Yojana
benefit_summary: Reimbursement of the actual cost of purchasing work tools/toolkit, or Rs.2,000, whichever is less, for registered construction workers.
caveats: Applicant must be a registered construction worker for at least 3 years and must attach the purchase bill with the application. Note: the source Details paragraph text appears to reference Jharkhand rather than Rajasthan (likely a data/copy inconsistency), though the eligibility criteria and state_guess indicate this is a Rajasthan scheme.

title: Nirmaan Shramik ke Bachchon Hetu Utkrasht Khel Protsaahan Yojana
benefit_summary: Sports incentive for children of registered construction workers in Chhattisgarh who excel in recognized sports: Rs.1,000 (district level), Rs.2,000 (divisional level), Rs.5,000 (state level), Rs.50,000 (national level).
caveats: Child's sporting excellence must be recognized by the Sports Department. Benefit amount is tiered by achievement level, not a flat Rs.1,000 - use the appropriate tier.

title: Nirman Shramikon Ke Bacchon Hetu Nishulk Ganvesh Evam Pustak Copy Hetu Sahaayata Raashi Yojana
benefit_summary: Lump-sum assistance for school uniform and books/copies for children of registered construction workers in Chhattisgarh: Rs.1,000 for classes 1-8, Rs.2,000 for classes 9-12.
caveats: Applicant (parent) must be a registered construction worker under the Chhattisgarh BOCW Welfare Board; child must be enrolled in classes 1-12 at a recognized school in Chhattisgarh. Benefit amount is tiered by class range.

title: Nirman Shramiko Ko Videsh Mai Rojgar Hetu Visa Per Hone Wale Vyay Ka Punarbharan Yojana
benefit_summary: Reimbursement of visa expenses (up to Rs.5,000, one-time only) for registered construction workers in Rajasthan seeking construction-related employment abroad.
caveats: Worker must be registered with the welfare board and continuously depositing contributions, must obtain Protector of Emigrants (POE) permission, use a POE-registered recruiting agency, and hold a valid passport (6+ months validity) and visa.
