Overseas job must be in construction work. Must apply within 3 months of visa issuance; providing false information triggers full recovery with interest. Verification note flags this as distinct from (and likely more current than) a similarly-named duplicate scheme entry.

title: Niramaya Scheme
benefit_summary: Free medicines (from an Emergency Drugs List, expanded from 150 to 570 drugs) for any patient registered at a government hospital or medical college in Odisha, no age limit.
caveats: Note: the source Benefits text mentions 'Himachal Pradesh' while the scheme is actually run by the Odisha government (Odisha State Medical Corporation) per the Details section and state_guess - likely a copy/text inconsistency in the source data. No income or category restriction stated; enrollment is via simple registration at government hospitals.

title: NSAP - Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme
benefit_summary: Monthly central old-age pension of Rs.200 (age 60-79) or Rs.500 (age 80+) for Below Poverty Line citizens, under the National Social Assistance Programme; many states add a top-up (Rs.50-3,800 extra depending on state) on top of this central amount.
caveats: Central amount confirmed unchanged as of an August 2025 Lok Sabha reply - the actual total pension a beneficiary receives is often higher due to state top-ups, which vary by state and are not included in the base central figure above.

title: Nirman Shramik Kalyan Yojana
benefit_summary: Education assistance for children of registered construction workers in Odisha, ranging from Rs.2,000/year (class 6-8) up to Rs.40,000/year (professional/medical courses in govt colleges), plus a one-time Rs.10,000 award for scoring 90%+ in Class 10. Verification note adds other board benefits: maternity Rs.10,000/child (max 2), marriage Rs.50,000, funeral Rs.5,000.
caveats: Parent must be a registered BOCW beneficiary for at least 1 year with up-to-date contributions and an active DBT-enabled bank account; only one parent can claim per child even if both are registered. Max 2 children per family. For class 6-7 only girls are eligible; class 8+ covers both genders, with a 20% additional benefit for girls from class 8 onward. Requires 50% annual attendance and a valid Nirman Shramik Card.

title: Nirmaan Shramik Mrtyu Evan Divyaang Sahaayata Yojana
benefit_summary: Death/disability financial assistance for registered construction workers in Chhattisgarh: Rs.1,00,000 for normal death, Rs.5,00,000 for death at the worksite, Rs.2,50,000 for permanent disability at the worksite.
caveats: Only payable on the death/disability of the registered worker themself, not a family member. Not payable for death by suicide, drug/substance use, crime, intentional violence, or riots. Workers already covered under the Board's silicosis-specific assistance scheme are not eligible here. Benefit amount is tiered, not a flat Rs.1,00,000.

title: Nirmaan Sthal Par Karya Ke Dauran A-panjeekrat Shramik Ke Mratyu Ki Dasha Me Antyeshti Evan Anugrah Rashi Bhugatan Yojana
benefit_summary: Funeral assistance of Rs.3,000, plus Rs.4,00,000 for accidental death and Rs.2,00,000 for permanent disability, to the legal heirs of an UNREGISTERED construction worker who dies/is disabled during construction site work in Madhya Pradesh.
caveats: Unlike most BOCW schemes, this one applies to workers NOT registered with the MP Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board. Verification note flags that the Rs.3,000 funeral figure applies to general unorganized workers (Naya Savera board), while registered BOCW-board construction workers reportedly get Rs.6,000 instead - confirm which population this specific scheme record targets before quoting a figure.

title: Old Age Pension - Chandigarh
benefit_summary: Monthly old-age pension of Rs.1,000 for Chandigarh residents (3+ years) aged 60+, with family income under Rs.1,50,000/year.
caveats: A 2021 committee proposal to raise the pension to Rs.2,000 was never implemented by the Union Government - the amount remains Rs.1,000/month.

title: Old Age Pension Scheme - Punjab
benefit_summary: Monthly old-age pension of Rs.1,500 via DBT for permanent residents of Punjab: men 65+, women 58+, with annual income under Rs.60,000 and land holding limited to max 2.5 acres irrigated (Nehri/Chahi) or 5 acres unirrigated (Barani) or 5 acres waterlogged land.
caveats: Amount unchanged since 2021 despite AAP's 2022 manifesto pledge to raise it to Rs.2,500.

title: Old Age Pension-West Bengal
benefit_summary: Monthly old-age pension currently Rs.1,500 for West Bengal residents aged 60+ (55+ for physically/mentally disabled) with no family member able to support them financially and personal income under Rs.1,500/month, not already receiving another government pension.
caveats: Formally notified: West Bengal's Panchayat Affairs & Rural Development Dept enhanced Old Age/Widow/Disability Pension from Rs.1,000 to Rs.1,500/month around 20 July 2026, retroactive to 1 April 2026, with DBT of the higher amount beginning 1 August 2026. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Updated from 'announced but not notified, still Rs.1,000' to the now-formally-notified Rs.1,500/month -- the notification (~20 July 2026) postdates this record's prior last_checked date of 2026-07-15 by about 5 days.

title: Old Age Pension Scheme
benefit_summary: Monthly old-age pension for Uttarakhand residents aged 60+ from BPL families (or with monthly income under Rs.4,000): Rs.1,500/month total for ages 60-79 (Rs.200 central + Rs.1,300 state) and Rs.1,500/month for 80+ (Rs.500 central + Rs.1,000 state).
caveats: Beneficiaries whose son is over 20 years old but the family still lives below the poverty line remain eligible. Non-BPL beneficiaries aged 60+ receive the full pension amount funded entirely by the state government.

title: Nekar Samman Yojana
benefit_summary: Annual financial assistance of Rs.5,000 (increased from Rs.2,000 per the 2022-23 budget) via DBT to registered handloom/power loom weavers and financially distressed workers in cotton/wool/silk allied activities in Karnataka.
caveats: CORRECTED per verification note: current amount is Rs.5,000, not the original Rs.2,000. Requires a valid Karnataka resident certificate and an active bank account.

title: Naunihal Scholarship Yojana
benefit_summary: Annual scholarship for children of construction workers in Chhattisgarh, ranging from Rs.1,000 (boys, class 1-5) to Rs.10,000 (girls, PhD-level professional exam study), with girls receiving higher amounts than boys at every level.
caveats: Max 2 children per family. No minimum marks/grade requirement. Beneficiary (parent) must have worked as a construction worker for at least 90 days in the year before application. Student must complete at least 1 year of the college/professional course or the scholarship must be returned. Requires a bank account for disbursal. Benefit amount is tiered by class/course and gender, not a flat Rs.1,000.

title: New Swarnima Scheme For Women
benefit_summary: Term loan of up to Rs.2,00,000 at a subsidized 5% per annum interest rate for self-employment, for women entrepreneurs from Backward Classes, with no self-contribution required for projects up to Rs.2,00,000 and repayment over up to 8 years.
caveats: Applicant must belong to a Backward Class, be female, aged 18-55, an entrepreneur, with total annual family income under Rs.3,00,000. Implemented by NBCFDC through State Channelising Agencies (SCAs).

title: Old Age Samman Allowance
benefit_summary: Monthly old-age pension of Rs.3,200 (raised effective November 2025 from Rs.3,000) for Haryana residents aged 60+, whose combined income with their spouse does not exceed Rs.2,00,000/year, disbursed through Panchayati Raj Institutions.
caveats: CORRECTED per verification note: current amount is Rs.3,200/month effective Nov 2025, higher than the Rs.2,500 figure in the original scheme text. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Income ceiling corrected from Rs.2,00,000 to Rs.3,00,000/year (combined with spouse) -- raised via a Haryana govt notification dated 05.04.2023, confirmed on socialjusticehry.gov.in and sewa.haryana.gov.in.

title: OBC Pre Matric Scholarship-Uttar Pradesh
benefit_summary: Pre-matric scholarship up to Rs.3,500/year (corrected from an erroneous Rs.150/month figure) for OBC students in Uttar Pradesh in classes 9-10, with an additional allowance for residential/hostel students.
caveats: CORRECTED per verification note: original Rs.150/month figure was a data error - actual scholarship is up to Rs.3,500/year. Parental income must not exceed Rs.2,00,000/year. All children of the same parents are eligible. Generally cannot be combined with other scholarships (some exceptions apply). Age must be 12-20 as of 1 July.

title: Toposili Bandhu (Old Age Pension) Scheme
benefit_summary: Monthly old-age pension currently Rs.1,000 for Scheduled Caste residents of West Bengal aged 60+, who are not already receiving another social security or government pension.
caveats: IN FLUX per verification note: as of July 2026, a pension increase (to Rs.1,500 or Rs.2,000, per competing proposals from the outgoing and incoming state governments after the May 2026 change of government) has been announced but NOT formally notified - Rs.1,000/month is the figure currently being disbursed; do not hard-code a higher amount yet. Pensions administered via the Jai Bangla portal since April 2020.

title: OEC Pre-matric Educational Assistance
benefit_summary: Rs.320/year (Class I-IV), Rs.630/year (Class V-VII), Rs.940/year (Class VIII-X) -- flat per-year amounts, same for government/aided and unaided schools.
caveats: [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Reverted an incorrect prior 'verification correction' that inflated these to Rs.750/900/1,000 and Rs.1,333/2,000 -- those higher figures belong to an unrelated national ST pre-matric scholarship. The original Rs.320/630/940 figures are correct per egovtschemes.com and bcdd.kerala.gov.in.

title: Organic Manure Scheme
benefit_summary: Free hands-on training and awareness campaigns on producing organic compost for sustainable agriculture, for bonafide farmers in Meghalaya.
caveats: No cash benefit - this is a training/capacity-building scheme, not a direct financial assistance scheme.

title: One Stop Centre
benefit_summary: 24-hour integrated support for any woman facing physical, sexual, emotional, psychological, or economic abuse: emergency rescue, medical aid, police/FIR assistance, psycho-social counselling, legal aid, and temporary shelter, all under one roof.
caveats: Open to all women irrespective of age, class, caste, education, marital status, race or culture, including girls under 18 (coordinated with Juvenile Justice Act / POCSO authorities). Confirmed active nationwide with 854 centres operational (July 2025) under Mission Shakti's Sambal component; helpline 181 active in 32 states/UTs.

title: One Time Cash Incentive towards Learning Driving (Sainik Welfare)
benefit_summary: One-time cash incentive of up to Rs.4,000 for unemployed ex-servicemen in Puducherry to take a driving course at a government-recognized school, credited via RTGS/NEFT.
caveats: Applicant must be registered with the Department of Sainik Welfare, Puducherry, get prior permission before starting the course, and apply within 3 years of discharge from service. Applications accepted offline only.

title: Central Assistance For One Time Settlement Of Displaced Families From PoK And Chhamb Under Prime Minister's Development Package
benefit_summary: One-time settlement of Rs.5,50,000 per family (Rs.5,49,692 Central share + Rs.308 State share, via DBT) to displaced families from Pakistan-occupied Jammu & Kashmir (1947) or Chhamb (1965/1971 war displacement), part of a Rs.2,000 crore rehabilitation package for 36,384 eligible families.
caveats: Claimant must be the head of the displaced family (or successor/heir) residing in Jammu & Kashmir, among the specific list of 36,384 recognized families, with documentary proof. Funds can be used for small business, scientific farming/livestock, or invested in an annuity for assured monthly income. Deadline for claims has recently been extended.

title: Financial Assistance under Odisha Working Journalist Welfare Scheme
benefit_summary: Ex-gratia financial assistance to the legal heir of a working journalist in Odisha: Rs.4,00,000 on death, Rs.2,00,000 on permanent incapacitation, plus (per verification note) ongoing children's education support of Rs.1,500/month (school) or Rs.2,500/month (higher education).
caveats: Journalist must work for a media house registered with Odisha's I&PR department. Payment order of priority: widow, then minor children, then parents if unmarried/no surviving widow or children. Apply online. Continuity publicly reaffirmed by the current Odisha CM.

title: Paternity Benefit Scheme (HBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Paternity benefit of Rs.21,000 (Rs.15,000 for newborn care + Rs.6,000 for the wife's nutrition) to a registered male construction worker in Haryana whose wife has delivered a baby.
caveats: Worker must be registered with HBOCWWB for at least 1 year, and his wife must not have claimed maternity benefit from any other employer. Covers up to 2 children, expandable to a 3rd child if all are daughters. Documents (including birth certificate) must be submitted within 1 year of delivery.

title: Overseas Scholarships For Scheduled Tribes-Madhya Pradesh
benefit_summary: Scholarship covering tuition and living expenses for 50 Scheduled Tribe students per year from Madhya Pradesh to pursue higher education (postgraduate/PhD) at recognized universities abroad.
caveats: Only one child per parent is eligible, and only once. For postgraduate study, applicant needs a graduation degree with 55% marks (second class or above); for PhD, a Master's degree with 50% marks plus 2 years of teaching/research/M.Phil experience. Family annual income capped at Rs.10,00,000.

title: Odisha State Treatment Fund
benefit_summary: Financial assistance up to Rs.3,00,000 per case for treatment of life-threatening illnesses as an in-patient at government or empaneled private hospitals in Odisha, for BPL/AAY/RSBY card holders or those with a qualifying income certificate.
caveats: Income threshold varies by area: Rs.40,000/year (rural) or Rs.60,000/year (urban) - higher urban figure used here. Central/State Government/PSU employees are not eligible. Application must be made during the course of treatment - reimbursement for already-incurred expenses is not allowed. Also covers cancer day-care chemo and up to 6 months post-kidney-transplant care without formal admission.

title: One Time Cash Incentive towards acquiring BEd, BPEd, DTEd, PGDCA (Sainik Welfare)
benefit_summary: One-time cash incentive of actual course cost or up to Rs.20,000 (whichever is less) for unemployed ex-servicemen in Puducherry pursuing BEd, BPEd, DTEd, or PGDCA at a government-recognized institution, credited via RTGS/NEFT.
caveats: Applicant must be registered with the Department of Sainik Welfare, Puducherry, get prior permission, and apply within 3 years of discharge. Application must be submitted offline within 3 months of successfully completing the course.

title: One Family One Enterprise Scheme
benefit_summary: Interest subvention (up to 6%, capping the effective loan rate at 4%) on term/working-capital loans up to Rs.10 lakh for 5 years, for new micro/small/medium enterprises in Kerala started on or after 1 April 2022, aiming for at least one MSME per household with 50% of beneficiaries being women.
caveats: CORRECTED per verification note: not a flat cash amount - it is an interest subvention capped at loans up to Rs.10 lakh. Unit must have valid Udyam Registration, must not be an NPA, must be operational, and generally must not have received any other Central/State/local grant (exemption for PMFME-supported units that commenced post-expansion production after 1 April 2022).

title: Prosthetic Aid Scheme
benefit_summary: Free prosthetic aids and artificial appliances (tricycles, wheelchairs, crutches, hearing aids, artificial limbs) for persons with disabilities (blind, deaf, orthopedically/physically handicapped) who are permanent residents of Jammu & Kashmir.
caveats: No cash transfer - this is a 100% state-sponsored in-kind assistance scheme. Family income must be under Rs.400/month (Rs.4,800/year) per the source text - an unusually low, likely outdated threshold. Applicant must not already be availing benefits under this scheme. Apply via the District Social Welfare Officer.

title: Prabhuddha Overseas Scholarship
benefit_summary: Overseas scholarship for SC/ST students from Karnataka pursuing full-time UG/PG/PhD programs abroad: 100% of costs covered if family income is below Rs.8 lakh, 50% if Rs.8-15 lakh, 33% if above Rs.15 lakh, for about 250 UG and 150 PG/PhD slots per year.
caveats: Age limit is 21 for undergraduate courses, 35 for postgraduate/doctoral. Requires 80% marks (UG) or 55% marks (PG/PhD) in qualifying exams, plus GRE/GMAT/TOEFL/IELTS scores and admission secured at an overseas institution. 33% of slots reserved for women, 5% for physically handicapped candidates.

title: Petrol Subsidy To Persons With Disability
benefit_summary: 50% subsidy on actual petrol/diesel expenditure for persons with disabilities in Chandigarh who own a motorized vehicle: up to 15 litres/month for vehicles 2HP or below, more for higher-powered vehicles (capped at 20 litres/month per the Details text).
caveats: Applicant must have a valid driving licence and family income up to Rs.1,50,000/year. Not eligible if already receiving a conveyance allowance from a voluntary or government source.

title: The Punjab Financial Assistance to Acid Victims Scheme
benefit_summary: Monthly rehabilitation assistance of Rs.10,000 (raised from Rs.8,000) for acid attack victims with 40%+ disability who are residents of Punjab, plus interim relief of Rs.25,000 within 5 days, Rs.1,00,000 within 15 days, and the balance within 2 months, paid directly to the victim's bank account.
caveats: CORRECTED per verification note: the current Punjab government made the scheme gender-neutral (previously restricted to females only, as stated in the original eligibility text) and raised the monthly amount from Rs.8,000 to Rs.10,000. This is a 100% state-sponsored scheme.

title: Pension to the Persons who lost 100% eye sight
benefit_summary: Monthly pension of Rs.2,000 for Tripura residents aged 10+ with 100% blindness and family income under Rs.1,00,000/year.
caveats: No family member of the applicant may be a government employee. A blind association is lobbying for a raise to Rs.5,000/month, but this has not yet been enacted as of the verification date.

title: Pratibha Kiran Scholarship
benefit_summary: Scholarship of Rs.500/month for 10 months (Rs.5,000/year, corrected from a flat unspecified figure) for BPL girl students in urban Madhya Pradesh who scored 60% or more in Class 12.
caveats: CORRECTED per verification note: paid as Rs.500/month over 10 months, not a lump sum. Restricted to urban-area BPL girl students only.

title: Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana
benefit_summary: Support for organic farming clusters: Rs.31,500/hectare over 3 years (corrected from an earlier Rs.50,000/hectare figure) - Rs.15,000 for organic inputs via DBT, Rs.4,500 for marketing/packaging, Rs.3,000 for certification/testing, and Rs.9,000 for training, for farmers/institutions with land holding up to 2 hectares.
caveats: CORRECTED per verification note: actual current assistance is Rs.31,500/hectare over 3 years, not Rs.50,000/hectare as previously recorded. Funding shared 60:40 Centre:State (90:10 for NE/Himalayan states, 100% for UTs). Uses Participatory Guarantee System (PGS-India) organic certification.

title: Post Metric Scholarship For OBC Students
benefit_summary: Post-matric scholarship for OBC students in Madhya Pradesh with family income up to Rs.3,00,000/year: per verification note, roughly Rs.30,000/year via tuition fee reimbursement plus Rs.200-750/month maintenance allowance (figures vary slightly across sources).
caveats: Applicant must have passed Class 10. Verification note flags that exact benefit figures conflict slightly across sources - recommend verifying live on the MPTAAS portal before quoting a precise number.

title: Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana
benefit_summary: Accident insurance for Rs.20/year premium (auto-debited): Rs.2 lakh to nominee on death or total/irrecoverable loss of both eyes/hands/feet (or one eye + one hand/foot), Rs.1 lakh for loss of sight in one eye or use of one hand/foot.
caveats: Open to bank/post office account holders aged 18-70 who consent to auto-debit. Cover terminates at age 70 or if the account is closed/has insufficient balance. If enrolled through multiple accounts, cover is capped at Rs.2 lakh total. Coverage runs annually from 1 June to 31 May.

title: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban
benefit_summary: Housing support for urban households across income slabs (EWS up to Rs.3L/year, LIG Rs.3-6L, MIG-1 Rs.6-9L, per PMAY-U 2.0), via interest subsidy of 4% p.a. on the first Rs.8 lakh of a home loan over a 12-year tenure, capped at Rs.1.80 lakh total paid in 5 annual installments of Rs.36,000, plus slum rehabilitation and beneficiary-led construction subsidies for EWS households.
caveats: CORRECTED per verification note: PMAY-U 2.0 income slabs and interest subsidy terms are as stated above, updated from the original PMAY (Housing for All by 2022) figures. Applicant/family must not already own a pucca house anywhere in India, must not have availed any other government housing scheme, and must have an Aadhaar/Aadhaar Virtual ID. Family defined as husband/wife and unmarried children. Track application status via the CLAP portal. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Removed a false fourth 'MIG-2/ISS up to Rs.18L' income tier -- the current PMAY-U 2.0 Interest Subsidy Scheme has only THREE tiers (EWS/LIG/MIG), all within a Rs.9 lakh/year ceiling. A MIG-II tier (Rs.12-18L) existed only under the older, discontinued PMAY 1.0 CLSS-MIG with a different subsidy structure -- it doesn't carry over into the current scheme.

title: Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
benefit_summary: Generic medicines available at 50-80% below branded market prices to the general public through Janaushadhi Kendra outlets nationwide (19,502 kendras as of April 2026, stocking 2,110 medicines and 315 surgical/consumable items), including sanitary napkins at Re.1/pad.
caveats: This scheme's eligibility criteria (Pharma degree, employing degree-holders) apply to those wanting to OPEN a Janaushadhi Kendra outlet, not to the general public who simply purchase the discounted medicines - no eligibility restriction applies to buyers.

title: SC/ST Pre Matric Scholarship - Uttar Pradesh
benefit_summary: Pre-matric scholarship for SC/ST students in Uttar Pradesh (classes 9-10): Component-1 (income-capped at Rs.2,50,000/year) pays Rs.3,500/year (day scholars) or Rs.7,000/year (residential); Component-2 (no income criteria) pays Rs.3,500/year (day scholars) or Rs.8,000/year (residential).
caveats: All children of the same parents are eligible. Generally cannot be combined with other scholarships (some exceptions). Age must be 12-20 as of 1 July. Applicant must be a dependent of persons in occupations traditionally considered 'untouchable'.

title: Pradhan Mantri Uchchatar Shiksha Protsahan Yojana: Central Sector Interest Subsidy Scheme
benefit_summary: Full interest subsidy (during the moratorium period: course duration + 1 year) on education loans up to Rs.10 lakh for economically weaker section students with family income up to Rs.4.5 lakh/year, pursuing professional/technical courses at NAAC/NBA-accredited or nationally important institutions.
caveats: Loans up to Rs.7.5 lakh require no collateral/third-party guarantee. Admissible only once (UG or PG, including integrated courses). Not eligible if receiving another Central/State scholarship or fee reimbursement, or if the student discontinues the course (except for documented medical reasons) or is expelled on disciplinary/academic grounds. Usage reportedly declining but scheme remains active.

title: Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
benefit_summary: Margin money subsidy of 15-35% (varies by category and urban/rural location) for setting up new micro-enterprises, with project cost ceiling Rs.50 lakh (manufacturing) or Rs.20 lakh (service sector); beneficiary contributes 5-10% of project cost; implemented by KVIC.
caveats: No income ceiling. Projects costing above Rs.10 lakh (manufacturing) or Rs.5 lakh (service) require at least VIII standard pass qualification. Only for new projects sanctioned specifically under PMEGP - not for units that already availed subsidy under PMRY/REGP or any other government scheme. Priority given to disaster-affected persons.

title: Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojna
benefit_summary: Crop insurance for farmers (cultivators or sharecroppers) growing notified crops in a notified area: farmer pays only 2% of sum insured (Kharif food/oilseed crops), 1.5% (Rabi food/oilseed crops), or 5% (annual commercial/horticultural crops), with the balance premium subsidized equally by Centre and State.
caveats: Requires valid land ownership certificate or tenancy agreement, and must apply within about 2 weeks of the start of the sowing season (2026 Kharif deadline 31 July, Rabi deadline 31 December). Cannot claim compensation for the same crop loss from another source. Optional for both loanee and non-loanee farmers.

title: Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana
benefit_summary: Cash maternity benefit of Rs.5,000 for the first living child (in two installments: Rs.3,000 on pregnancy registration + ANC checkup, Rs.2,000 on child birth registration and immunization), PLUS (corrected/updated per PMMVY 2.0, effective 1 April 2022) Rs.6,000 in one installment for a second child if it is a girl - up to Rs.11,000 total across two children.
caveats: CORRECTED per verification note: the second-child girl-child benefit of Rs.6,000 (added under PMMVY 2.0) should be included alongside the original Rs.5,000 first-child benefit. Applicant must be at least 19, employed and experiencing wage loss due to pregnancy, and apply within 270 days of childbirth. Eligible disadvantaged categories include SC/ST women, 40%+ disabled women, BPL cardholders, PMJAY/e-Shram/PM-Kisan/MGNREGA/NFSA cardholders, and women with family income under Rs.8 lakh/year. Miscarriage/stillbirth cases are treated as fresh cases in future pregnancies. IMPORTANT: eligibility is met by satisfying ANY ONE of ~11 alternative criteria (SC/ST/BPL/40%+disabled/PMJAY/e-Shram/MGNREGA/PM-Kisan/AWW-AWH-ASHA/NFSA card/family income <Rs.8 lakh), not all combined. The max_income=800000 field already captures the standalone income-based path -- caste_category and ration_card_types have been removed as hard gates since they are just two of many alternative (OR) qualifying routes, not required (AND) conditions. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Removed incorrect caste_category=[sc,st] and ration_card_types=[BPL] hard gates that (combined with max_income) misrepresented this OR-based, alternative-criteria scheme as an AND-based combined requirement -- would have wrongly rejected general-category, non-BPL applicants with income under Rs.8 lakh who are in fact eligible via the income path alone.

title: Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana
benefit_summary: Collateral-free micro-credit for income-generating non-farm micro/small enterprises, in tiers: Shishu (up to Rs.50,000), Kishore (Rs.50,001-5 lakh), Tarun (Rs.5-10 lakh), and Tarun Plus (Rs.10-20 lakh, for those who successfully repaid a prior Tarun loan) - overall ceiling raised from Rs.10 lakh to Rs.20 lakh via Budget 2024-25, effective 24 October 2024.
caveats: CORRECTED per verification note: the ceiling was raised to Rs.20 lakh (with the new Tarun Plus tier) - update any reference still capping this scheme at Rs.10 lakh. Applicant must not be a defaulter to any bank/financial institution and must have a satisfactory credit record.

title: Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana - Recognition Of Prior Learning
benefit_summary: Skill certification for workers with prior experience in an unregulated sector: Rs.500 cash reward for clearing the certification exam plus 3-year accidental insurance cover of Rs.2 lakh.
caveats: Applicant must have prior job-role experience as defined by the relevant Sector Skill Council, and hold an Aadhaar-linked bank account. Higher age groups require special approval. Part of PMKVY 4.0, active as of the verification date.

title: Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana - Special Projects
benefit_summary: Skill training and support (counselling, digital content, soft skills, accidental insurance, boarding/lodging support, post-placement stipend) tailored for marginalized/vulnerable groups (SC/ST, transgender, PwD, women, economically backward) and hard-to-reach regions (LWE areas, aspirational districts, J&K, Ladakh, North East, Islands) who don't fit standard PMKVY Short Term Training criteria.
caveats: Requires Aadhaar ID at enrolment and 70% attendance to be eligible for assessments. Part of PMKVY 4.0, extended to 31 December 2026 with a target of 3 crore trained (2.1 crore/70% achieved as of May 2026).

title: Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana - Short Term Training
benefit_summary: Free short-term vocational/skill training (NSQF-aligned, plus soft skills, entrepreneurship, financial/digital literacy) for school/college dropouts and unemployed youth, with placement assistance, accidental insurance, and stipends/incentives after certification.
caveats: Requires Aadhaar-linked bank account and 70% attendance for assessment eligibility. Current phase is PMKVY 4.0 (2022-2026), enrolling via skillindiadigital.gov.in, including Industry 4.0 trades (AI, coding, drones). PMKVY 5.0 has been announced as forthcoming.

title: Post Metric Scholarship - Madhya Pradesh
benefit_summary: Post-matric scholarship for Scheduled Caste students in Madhya Pradesh: full fee reimbursement at government institutions (or for professional courses with regulator-fixed fees); at non-government colleges, half the compulsory fee reimbursed for income up to Rs.2,50,000, tapering for income Rs.2,50,000-6,00,000; plus a monthly living allowance of Rs.300 (non-hosteller) or Rs.570 (hosteller).
caveats: MAJOR CORRECTION per verification note: Rs.2,50,000 is NOT a benefit amount, it is a family-income eligibility threshold tier for non-government college fee reimbursement - do not quote it as a cash benefit. No income limit applies for students at government institutions; non-government institution students face the Rs.6,00,000/year overall income ceiling.

title: Prime Minister's Scholarship Scheme
benefit_summary: Scholarship of Rs.2,500/month (boys) or Rs.3,000/month (girls) for dependent wards/widows of ex-servicemen or ex-Coast Guard personnel, admitted to the 1st year of a professional/technical course with 60%+ in their qualifying exam, paid annually for 1-5 years depending on course duration.
caveats: 5,500 scholarships (2,750 boys + 2,750 girls) awarded per academic year, with priority given first to wards/widows of personnel killed in action, then disabled in action, then died in service, etc. Covers both 'ward' (unmarried son/daughter, the majority of beneficiaries -- male ward eligible up to 25yo, female ward eligible only until she marries) and 'widow' (of an ex-servicemen, no age limit until she remarries) applicant categories -- NOT restricted to widows. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Removed the incorrect marital_status=['widowed']-only restriction, which would have wrongly excluded unmarried son/daughter 'ward' applicants who form the bulk of this scheme's beneficiaries.

title: Post Matric Scholarship For Scheduled Caste
benefit_summary: Post-matric scholarship up to Rs.50,000/year for Scheduled Caste students in Punjab: full non-refundable tuition/compulsory fees plus an academic/maintenance allowance up to Rs.13,500/year (hostellers, Group 1 professional courses) or Rs.1,200/month, varying by course group and hosteller/day-scholar status.
caveats: Family income must not exceed Rs.2,50,000/year. Extra 10% allowance for Divyang (disabled) students. Students on correspondence/online courses are eligible for fee reimbursement but not the academic allowance. Only for students who have passed Matriculation/Higher Secondary or higher.

title: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana
benefit_summary: Free zero-balance basic savings bank account (Basic Savings Bank Deposit Account) for any Indian citizen, with a free RuPay debit card carrying Rs.2 lakh accidental insurance cover, overdraft facility up to Rs.10,000, and access via bank branches, ATMs and Bank Mitras/Business Correspondents.
caveats: Minors above 10 can open an account with legal guardian support. Small/'Chota Khata' accounts can be opened without standard KYC documents but are valid for only 12 months (renewable once with proof of applying for valid ID). Cash withdrawal capped at 4 times/month on BSBDA accounts.

title: The Post-Matric Scholarship For Scheduled Tribes Students
benefit_summary: Post-matric scholarship for Scheduled Tribe students permanently settled in Mizoram, from Class XI up to Post-Doctoral Fellowship, covering tuition, maintenance, and incidental expenses (amounts follow standard National Scholarship Portal slabs varying by course/hostel status).
caveats: Family income must not exceed Rs.2,50,000/year. Centrally sponsored with 90% funding from Ministry of Tribal Affairs and 10% from the Mizoram state government.

title: Prime Minister's Special Scholarship Scheme For The Students Of Union Territories Of Jammu & Kashmir And Ladakh
benefit_summary: Scholarship for J&K/Ladakh domiciled students admitted to colleges outside the UTs: tuition fee up to Rs.30,000/year (general degree), Rs.1,25,000/year (professional/engineering/nursing/pharmacy/architecture/hotel management), or Rs.3,00,000/year (medical/BDS), plus a fixed maintenance allowance of Rs.1,00,000/year (paid in 10 installments for hostel/mess/books/stationery).
caveats: Applicant must have passed Class 12 from a JKBOSE or CBSE-affiliated school in J&K/Ladakh, with family income up to Rs.8,00,000/year. 5,000 fresh scholarships available per year (2,070 general degree, 2,830 professional/engineering, 100 medical), subject to AICTE online counseling and seat allocation.

title: Parivaar Pension Yojana (JBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Family pension of 50% of the deceased pensioner's base pension, or a maximum of Rs.500/month, for surviving family members of a deceased registered construction worker pensioner in Jharkhand.
caveats: 100% state-sponsored scheme; only Jharkhand residents/domiciles eligible. Requires SHRAM card/registration proof, death certificate, and documents establishing the relationship to the deceased. Apply online.

title: Centrally-Sponsored Scheme Of Pre-Matric Scholarship For Scheduled Caste Students Studying In Classes 9th & 10th
benefit_summary: Consolidated academic allowance (effective 2022-23, still current): Rs.3,500/year for day scholars, Rs.7,000/year for hostellers -- replacing the old monthly stipend (Rs.225/525) plus separate ad-hoc/books grant (Rs.750/1,000) structure.
caveats: Family income must not exceed Rs.2,50,000/year. Only for regular, full-time students at a government/recognized school. Scholarship for any given class is available for only one year; confirmed separate from the PM-YASASVI scheme. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Updated to the 2022-23 consolidated-allowance figures (Rs.3,500/7,000 per year), which also represent a modest real increase over the old structure's totals (Rs.3,000/6,250/year), per socialjustice.gov.in.

title: Pre Matric Scholarship For Scheduled Tribe Students
benefit_summary: Scholarship for ST students in Class 9-10: Rs.225/month (day scholars) or Rs.525/month (hostellers) for 10 months/year, plus a books/ad-hoc grant of Rs.750/year (day scholars) or Rs.1,000/year (hostellers), with additional monthly allowances (Rs.160-240) for students with disabilities.
caveats: Family income must not exceed Rs.2,50,000/year (source Details section mentions Rs.2 lakh in one place - minor inconsistency). Applicant must not be availing any other government scholarship. Only for regular, full-time students at a government/recognized school; scholarship for any given class available for only one year.

title: Maintenance Of Pregnant Desi/Indigenous Cows Ration For BPL Families
benefit_summary: 50% subsidy on nutritious cattle feed ration (about 3 kg/day) for BPL livestock owners in Himachal Pradesh, for the last trimester of pregnancy of their Desi/Indigenous/crossbred cows, capped at 2 cows per family.
caveats: Verification note flags this is a general-BPL variant distinct from a separate SC-specific BPL cow/buffalo scheme (mpdicbrsbfscc) - do not confuse the two.

title: Prerana (micro Credit Finance) Scheme
benefit_summary: Financial assistance of Rs.25,000 per member (Rs.15,000 subsidy + Rs.10,000 loan at 4% interest) for SC/ST women in Karnataka forming a Self Help Group of 10 members (total Rs.2.5 lakh per SHG) to start an income-generating business.
caveats: Family income must not exceed Rs.1,50,000/year (rural) or Rs.2,00,000/year (urban) - use the higher urban figure as the general threshold. SHG's business unit/stall must be at least 200 sq ft. Not eligible if the applicant or a family member has already availed a subsidy from the Corporation/Government of Karnataka. Loan repayable in 36 monthly or 12 quarterly installments.

title: Prime Minister's Scholarship Scheme for the Wards/Widows of Central Police Force Personnel
benefit_summary: Scholarship of Rs.1,250/month (boys) or Rs.1,500/month (girls) - per verification note, actually confirmed at Rs.2,500/month (boys) and Rs.3,000/month (girls) - for wards/widows of Central Police Force (CPF) personnel pursuing a first professional degree (engineering, medicine, dental, MBA, etc.), paid for 2-5 years depending on course.
caveats: Requires 60% marks at 10+2 for initial sanction, 50% each year for renewal. About 5,500 scholarships awarded per year (910 for CPFs under MHA, 90 for RPF under Railways, remainder shared with the parallel ex-servicemen scheme). Priority order: killed in action > disabled in action > gallantry awardees > died in harness > disabled in service > others. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Corrected to the current rate (Rs.2,500 boys/Rs.3,000 girls, in effect since FY2019-20) -- the Rs.1,250/1,500 figures were outdated and had been listed first/leading despite a parenthetical self-correction elsewhere in the same text.

title: Post-Matric Scholarship To VJNT Students - Maharashtra
benefit_summary: 100% tuition fee, exam fee, and maintenance allowance for VJNT (Vimukta Jatis & Nomadic Tribes) category students in Maharashtra pursuing post-matric education, with maintenance allowance ranging Rs.90-190/month (day scholars) to Rs.150-425/month (hostellers), varying by course group.
caveats: CORRECTED per verification note: parent/guardian income ceiling is Rs.2,50,000/year (source eligibility text stated Rs.1,50,000, which appears outdated). Max 2 boys per family eligible (unlimited girls). Requires 75% attendance; scholarship discontinues if the student changes from professional to non-professional course, or repeats a failed year without promotion. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Reverted an incorrect prior 'correction' that raised the VJNT income ceiling from Rs.1,50,000 to Rs.2,50,000 -- Rs.2,50,000 belongs to the separate SC/ST post-matric scholarship category; VJNT/OBC/SBC schemes remain capped at Rs.1.5 lakh per the official myScheme.gov.in portal.

title: Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana
benefit_summary: Free, deposit-free LPG connection for poor women without an existing LPG connection: Rs.1,600 (14.2kg cylinder) or Rs.1,150 (5kg cylinder), plus a free first refill and free stove; ongoing refill subsidy capped at Rs.300/refill for up to 4 refills/year (cut from 9, effective 8 June 2026, capping the annual benefit at Rs.1,200).
caveats: Eligible categories: SECC 2011 list, SC/ST households, PMAY/AAY beneficiaries, forest dwellers, and other notified categories. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Corrected a false internal 'verification note' claiming a 4-refill correction was wrong and had been 'reverted to 9' -- the Union Government actually DID cut the subsidized refill quota from 9 to 4 cylinders/year effective 8 June 2026 (due to a ~46% rise in global LPG prices), and no reversal back to 9 was found. This record's caveats field should be treated as having contained fabricated/incorrect correction history, not a genuine one.

title: Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana 2.0
benefit_summary: Free, deposit-free LPG connection (Rs.1,600 for 14.2kg cylinder or Rs.1,150 for 5kg, covering security deposit, regulator, hose, consumer card and installation charges) plus a free first refill and stove; ongoing refill subsidy capped at Rs.300/refill for up to 4 refills/year (cut from 9, effective 8 June 2026, capping the annual benefit at Rs.1,200), for poor women without an existing LPG connection in the household - includes special provisions for migrant families.
caveats: Eligible categories: SC/ST, PMAY-Gramin, AAY, Most Backward Classes, tea garden tribes, forest dwellers, island residents, SECC households, or 14-point self-declared poor households. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Same fix as base PMUY: corrected the false '9, not 4' verification note -- the government cut the subsidized refill quota to 4/year effective 8 June 2026, applying uniformly to PMUY 2.0 beneficiaries too.

title: Pension Plan (MBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Monthly pension for registered construction workers in Meghalaya from age 60: per verification note, actually Rs.150/month base plus Rs.10/year for each completed year of service beyond 5 years (rather than the flat Rs.1,000/month stated in the original scheme text).
caveats: Amount discrepancy: original source text states a flat Rs.1,000/month, but the verification note corrects this to a lower base of Rs.150/month plus service-based increments - use the verification note's figure as more reliable. Requires registration with MBOCWWB and at least 1 year as a building worker.

title: Pratyasha Scheme- West Bengal
benefit_summary: Allotment (via lottery) of a flat for West Bengal/Kolkata Police personnel (Constable up to Deputy Superintendent/Assistant Commissioner rank), in category A (~1123 sq ft), B (~926 sq ft), or C (~794 sq ft), depending on pay scale, built by WB State Police Housing Corporation with HUDCO financing.
caveats: Only serving Police personnel of West Bengal Police / Kolkata Police in specified ranks and pay thresholds (Rs.8,840+ for category C up to Rs.18,000+ for category A) may apply; one application per eligible officer.

title: Palanhar Scheme
benefit_summary: Monthly financial support for the care/upbringing of vulnerable children (orphans; children of imprisoned, HIV/AIDS-affected, leprosy/silicosis-affected, disabled, or widowed/divorced/abandoned pensioner parents) raised by a guardian family in Rajasthan: orphans get Rs.1,500/month (age 0-6) or Rs.2,500/month (age 6-18); other categories get Rs.500/month (0-6) or Rs.1,000/month (6-18), plus Rs.2,000/year for books/clothing/shoes.
caveats: Guardian must be a Rajasthan native or resident for 3+ years, with family income up to Rs.1,20,000/year. Benefit extends to age 19 if the child is still in or below Class 12; stops after age 19 or passing Class 12. Clothing grant does not apply to widow/nata (remarried widow) categories per source note.

title: Pension Scheme for Cancer Patients
benefit_summary: Monthly pension of Rs.2,000 for cancer patients resident in Tripura with family income up to Rs.1,50,000/year.
caveats: No member of the applicant's immediate family (father, mother, sons, unmarried daughters) may be in government service. About 3,400 beneficiaries; confirmed this scheme is separate from the general disability-allowance increases.

title: Pension Scheme for Destitute Transgender
benefit_summary: Monthly pension of Rs.1,000 for destitute transgender persons in Tamil Nadu aged 40+ who are physically unable to work and receive no support from family or other sources.
caveats: Apply via Common Service Centres (CSC).

title: Samagra Samajik Suraksha Parityakta Pension Yojana
benefit_summary: Monthly pension of Rs.600 for abandoned women aged 18-59 from BPL families in Madhya Pradesh.
caveats: Applicant's name must be registered on the Samagra portal. Operates under the umbrella Samagra Samajik Suraksha Pension Yojana (ssspy) run by the Department of Social Justice.

title: Pension to Unmarried Poor, Incapacitated Women of Age 50 years and above
benefit_summary: Monthly pension of Rs.1,000 for unmarried, destitute, incapacitated women aged 50+ in Tamil Nadu, plus a free saree during Pongal and Deepavali, and free rice (2kg/month or 4kg/month for those not taking nutritious meals) from Anganwadi Centres.
caveats: Applicant's fixed assets must not exceed Rs.1,00,000.

title: Pension Scheme for Grade II Deformed Leprosy Patients
benefit_summary: Monthly pension of Rs.2,000 for Tripura residents affected by Grade II deformity leprosy.
caveats: Applications accepted offline only. Unchanged since launch in August 2015.

title: Pension Scheme for Transgender
benefit_summary: Monthly pension of Rs.2,000 for transgender residents of Tripura who have no source of income.
caveats: No income restriction confirmed by verification.

title: Prathibha Scholarship Programme
benefit_summary: Tiered merit scholarship for Basic/Natural Science UG/PG study: UG Year1 Rs.12,000, Year2 Rs.18,000, Year3 Rs.24,000; PG Year1 Rs.40,000, Year2 Rs.60,000.
caveats: CORRECTED: tiered by year/level, not flat Rs.12,000. 50% seats reserved for girls, 10% reserved for SC/ST with relaxed marks criteria (80% vs 90%).

title: Pragati Scholarship Scheme For Girls Students(Technical Degree)
benefit_summary: Scholarship up to Rs.50,000/year for up to 4 years for girl students in AICTE-approved technical degree programs (engineering, tech, architecture, pharmacy), covering tuition/exam fees.
caveats: Maximum two girls per family eligible; only first course of higher education counts.

title: Pension To Widows And Destitute Women
benefit_summary: Monthly pension raised to Rs.3,200 (effective Nov 2025, up from Rs.2,500 originally stated) for widows and destitute women in Haryana.
caveats: Also covers women destitute without husband/parents/sons, or deserted/incapacitated-husband cases (not just widows). Must be domicile of Haryana resident 1+ year before application.

title: Pension To Widows And Destitute Women-Chandigarh
benefit_summary: Monthly pension of Rs.1,000 to widows and destitute women in Chandigarh UT.
caveats: Requires 3+ years UT residency proof. A 2021 proposal to raise the amount to Rs.2,000/month remains unimplemented.

title: Moovalur Ramamirtham Ammaiyar Higher Education Assurance Scheme
benefit_summary: Rs.1,000/month for girl students (classes 6-12 in government or, since July 2024, government-aided TN schools) until completion of their first undergraduate degree/diploma/ITI course.
caveats: Eligibility expanded July 2024 to include government-aided school students, not just government schools. Can be availed alongside other scholarships.

title: Pichda Varg Post Matric Chhatravritti
benefit_summary: CORRECTED: approx Rs.30,000/year (tuition/mandatory fees + maintenance allowance) for OBC/backward-class post-matric students in MP; family income cap Rs.3 lakh/year.
caveats: Original scraped text understated the amount as Rs.400/month; actual value is a fees+maintenance package worth ~Rs.30,000/year.

title: Refund of Contribution Scheme (PBAOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Refund of the deceased registered construction worker's board welfare contributions, paid to nominee via DBT within 7 days. Amount is variable (contribution-based), not fixed.
caveats: Deceased must have been registered 18-60, contributed regularly, not defaulted contributions for a continuous period >1 year. Application must be submitted within 2 months of the worker's death.

title: Regional Centre for Training and Production of Mushroom
benefit_summary: 50% subsidy on mushroom spawn/compost purchase; 50% assistance for compost shed construction; Rs.22,000/unit (50% assistance) financial aid to mushroom growers in West Garo Hills.
caveats: Applicant must possess own or leased land of at least 0.2 hectares. First-come-first-served basis.

title: Rehabilitation Allowance To Lepers
benefit_summary: Monthly allowance of Rs.750 plus free medical treatment/medicines and education support for children, for leprosy patients living in leprosy colonies in HP.
caveats: Applicant must not be receiving any other government scheme or pension. [Fix 2026-07-23] Occupation constraint removed from structured matching (originally tagged "other") -- this is specifically for persons affected by leprosy, a health status, not an occupation.

title: Pension Yojana (JBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Pension of Rs.1,000/month to registered construction workers in Jharkhand after 30 years of continuous contribution to the JBOCWW Board.
caveats: Requires 30 years of continuous contribution; pension paid from age 60.

title: Scheme Of Provision Of Subsidized Rams To Sheep Breeders
benefit_summary: 60% subsidy on high-genetic-merit breeding rams (Rambouillet/Russian Merino crosses) for registered sheep breeders in Himachal Pradesh, on a first-come-first-served basis (max 2 rams/beneficiary).

title: Rajiv Gandhi Krishak Sathi Sahayta Yojana
benefit_summary: Accident relief fund for farmers/agricultural laborers/market workers in Rajasthan: Rs.2,00,000 for accidental death (increased 4x from Rs.50,000 under renamed 'Mukhyamantri Krishak Sathi Yojana'), with tiered amounts (Rs.5,000-50,000) for various injuries/dismemberment.
caveats: RENAMED after Dec 2023 government change to 'Mukhyamantri Krishak Sathi Yojana'; amount increased 4x for accidental death/dismemberment. Market workers require a market committee license.

title: Rajiv Gandhi Scholarship For Academic Excellence
benefit_summary: RENAMED to 'Swami Vivekananda Scholarship for Academic Excellence (SVSAES)'. Tiered study-abroad scholarship for Rajasthan students admitted to top-150 QS-ranked universities: full tuition (max Rs.50 lakh) + living expenses (Rs.6-12 lakh depending on family income tier, income <=8L gets max support).
caveats: RENAMED after Dec 2023 government change; income tiers determine benefit level (E1: <8L gets Rs.12L living expenses, E2: 8-25L gets Rs.6L, E3: >25L gets tuition only). 30% seats reserved for female students.

title: Rajiv Gandhi Swavlamban Rojgar Yojna
benefit_summary: Loan up to Rs.3,00,000 for self-employment/small industry ventures in Delhi, plus 15% project-cost subsidy capped at Rs.7,500/entrepreneur.
caveats: Entrepreneur must contribute at least 10% of loan amount (5% for SC/ST/OBC/PwD/women/ex-servicemen). Loan repaid over 5 years; subsidy adjusted to loan account after 2 years.

title: Rajiv Gandhi Social Security Scheme For Poor Families - 2012
benefit_summary: Accident financial assistance for BPL family members in Puducherry: Rs.30,000 (natural death), Rs.75,000 (unnatural death or permanent total disability), Rs.37,500 (partial permanent total disability).
caveats: Beneficiary cannot claim double benefits from any other government scheme simultaneously.

title: Khadya Suraksha Yojana
benefit_summary: Subsidized food grains under Targeted PDS: Antyodaya families get 35kg wheat/month at free of cost (Rs.0/kg,; Priority Households get 5kg/person/month at was Rs.2/kg, now free).
caveats: Requires ration card under Antyodaya/BPL/Annapurna/Priority Household category. Since 1 Jan 2023, all NFSA foodgrain (AAY and Priority Household categories) is FREE OF COST nationwide (extended through Dec 2028 by a Nov 2023 Cabinet decision) -- the old Rs.1/kg (AAY)/Rs.2/kg (PHH) charges no longer apply. Quantities (35kg/month AAY, 5kg/person/month PHH) are unchanged. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Updated to reflect free foodgrain (since Jan 2023) -- the Rs.1/kg and Rs.2/kg figures were pre-2023 NFSA central issue prices, discontinued nationwide.

title: RKVY Soil Health and Fertility - Soil Health Card
benefit_summary: Free/affordable Soil Health Card with soil test results and fertilizer recommendations for all farmers in India, now delivered under the RKVY Soil Health & Fertility component.
caveats: CORRECTED: standalone Soil Health Card scheme was merged into RKVY (Soil Health & Fertility component) since 2022-23; still active and funded.

title: Revival and Rehabilitation Scheme for Defunct MSMEs and Cashew Processing Units
benefit_summary: CORRECTED: capital grant/working capital assistance for defunct MSMEs (max Rs.12 lakh/unit) and defunct cashew processing units (max Rs.15 lakh/unit) in Kerala, structured as building renovation (25%, cap Rs.2L), plant & machinery (40%, cap Rs.8L), and working capital margin support.
caveats: Unit must have been non-operational 6+ months but revivable; available only once per applicant unit; bank sanction of fresh working capital loan mandatory for the margin-money component.

title: Residential School For Blinds
benefit_summary: Free residential education, vocational training, boarding/lodging, clothing and pocket money of Rs.500/month for blind children (ages 6-21) at the Residential School for Blinds, Jammu.
caveats: Inmates retained until graduation or age 25, whichever is earlier. 100% state-sponsored, permanent J&K residents only.

title: Rise Together
benefit_summary: Financial assistance up to Rs.20 lakh per youth group (min. Rs.2.5 lakh or 10% project cost subsidy + up to Rs.17.5 lakh bank loan) to establish community-oriented enterprises in J&K.
caveats: Youth groups need minimum 3 members, all aged 18-40 with 12th-standard qualification (relaxable case-by-case); none of the group can have availed a similar self-employment scheme before; group members must not be loan defaulters. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Corrected max_age from 40 to 35 per the official Mission Youth J&K scheme guidelines (missionyouth.jk.gov.in), which cap youth-group membership at 18-35, not 18-40.

title: Rythu Bima Scheme
benefit_summary: Rs.5 lakh life/accident insurance payout to families of registered farmers (including tenant farmers) in Telangana who die or are permanently disabled; premium Rs.1,200/year (govt pays Rs.900, farmer pays Rs.300).
caveats: Distinct from the separate 'Rythu Bharosa' input-support scheme (Rs.12,000/acre/year) which replaced 'Rythu Bandhu' -- do not conflate the two. Age eligibility is 18-59, not 18-60. As part of the 2025-2026 renewal, new applications are restricted to farmers owning up to 5 acres of land, registered in the Bhu Bharati/CCLA land-records portals (our schema can't encode the 5-acre cap specifically, only land ownership generally). [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Corrected max_age from 60 to 59, and added land_ownership_required=True to reflect a newly-added 2025-26 land-ownership restriction that was previously not captured at all (field was null).

title: Self-Employment Scheme For Dependents Of Prisoners
benefit_summary: One-time financial assistance of up to Rs.30,000 per family to dependents (spouse, unemployed/unmarried children) of Kerala prisoners serving 5+ year sentences, available only during the imprisonment period.
caveats: Given only once per family; only during the convict's imprisonment; not payable if already availed for the same purpose previously.

title: Snehasparsham
benefit_summary: Rs.1,000/month financial assistance to unwed mothers in Kerala.
caveats: Applicant must hold a post-office account; must not receive any other government pension.

title: "SUPER 30" Scheme
benefit_summary: Free 2-year JEE/NEET coaching for Tripura students: coaching fee capped at Rs.1 lakh + accommodation Rs.1.4 lakh/year (+5% in year 2), for ST/SC/PwD students at nationally reputed institutions outside Tripura.
caveats: Requires 50%+ marks in class 10 pre-board from a government-recognized Tripura school; must be appearing for class 10 board finals; family income cap confirmed as Rs.8 lakh/year in verification (differs from Rs.1 lakh stated in raw eligibility text).

title: Subsistence Allowance (Sainik Welfare)
benefit_summary: Monthly subsistence allowance of Rs.1,500 (verified/current figure) for WWII veterans, non-pensioner BPL ex-servicemen above 60, and their widows in Puducherry.
caveats: A very narrow, near-obsolete beneficiary pool (WWII veterans) but scheme remains listed active. Must be registered with Dept of Sainik Welfare, Puducherry.

title: Shramik Annapurna Yojana (GBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Nutritious meals for registered construction workers and family at a concessional rate of Rs.5/meal, provided at the worksite or Kadianaka in Gujarat.

title: Shubhshakti Yojana
benefit_summary: One-time financial assistance of Rs.55,000 to unmarried daughters (max 2/family) of registered construction worker families in Rajasthan, or to an unmarried female beneficiary, for education, vocational training, business, or marriage expenses.
caveats: Parent must be registered as construction worker for at least 1 year and have worked 90+ days in the preceding year; daughter must have passed 8th standard and have her own savings account; house (if owned) must have a toilet; requires physical verification. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Added missing min_age=18 for the daughter-beneficiary -- was previously null, which could let an underage applicant appear eligible.

title: Scheme For Award Of Stipend To The Schedule Tribe Students Of Arunachal Pradesh
benefit_summary: Monthly stipend of Rs.1,400 for 11 months plus Rs.1,000/year book grant for Scheduled Tribe students of Arunachal Pradesh pursuing higher/technical/professional courses.
caveats: Not payable for full-time-employed ST students, repeaters, students with <75% attendance, disciplinary cases, or those studying via distance/correspondence mode.

title: Cycle Anudaan Yojana
benefit_summary: CORRECTED: this is an in-kind free bicycle (not cash) distributed directly by schools to Class 6 (and some Class 9) government-school students in Madhya Pradesh.
caveats: CORRECTED: original scraped data described this as a construction-worker cash transport allowance (90% of cost or Rs.4,000); verification found it is actually a free bicycle for government-school students.

title: Samruddhi Scheme
benefit_summary: Initial capital subsidy up to Rs.10 lakh plus training/mentorship for SC entrepreneurs in Karnataka to set up franchise/dealership retail businesses, targeting 25,000 entrepreneurs over 3 years.
caveats: Applicant must have passed SSLC; selection is merit-based via district-level screening and franchisor approval. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Added missing max_age=50 and max_income=Rs.5,00,000/year per the Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Development Corporation's official Samruddhi Scheme criteria -- both were previously null, which would have wrongly told over-50 or higher-income applicants they qualify.

title: Sympathetic Assistance and Handholding for Youth Transformation and Amelioration - SAHAYTA
benefit_summary: Financial assistance up to Rs.2 lakh (or actual project cost, whichever lower) for youth-in-distress self-employment ventures in J&K (manufacturing, retail, IT, agriculture, tourism, food processing, etc.).
caveats: Applicant must have lost a family member or been permanently incapacitated (50%+ disability) due to insurgency/cross-border shelling/mine blast in J&K; those involved in anti-national activities are ineligible.

title: Scheme Of Assistance To Disabled Persons For Purchase/Fitting Of Aids/Appliances
benefit_summary: ADIP scheme: assistance capped at Rs.10,000/aid (Rs.12,000 for students) for devices costing up to Rs.20,000; higher-cost items separately listed. Cochlear implants: up to Rs.7 lakh (age 1-5) / Rs.6 lakh (age 5-18).
caveats: Income ceiling Rs.30,000/month (self or guardian) applies to most aids. Revised w.e.f. 26.09.2024; scheme approved through 31 March 2026 -- recheck near that date for renewal.

title: Special Ability Relief Allowance
benefit_summary: Monthly disability allowance: Rs.1,150 (40-69% disability, income <=Rs.35,000/yr) or Rs.1,700 (70%+ disability, no income limit) for HP residents.
caveats: Applicant must not be in government/semi-government service or already receiving any pension. Income cap removed for 70%+ disability/mentally challenged beneficiaries.

title: Schedule Caste Pre-Metric Scholarship Class 06 To 08
benefit_summary: Pre-matric scholarship for Class 6-8 SC students in Rajasthan: Rs.75/month (boys), Rs.125/month (girls).
caveats: Parents/guardians must not be income taxpayers; student must not have failed in the previous class; application now processed by schools directly via Shala Darpan portal (no separate student application needed).

title: Shop Construction/Shop Operation Scheme For Rehabilitation Of PwDs
benefit_summary: Rs.20,000 (Rs.15,000 loan @4% + Rs.5,000 grant) for shop construction, or Rs.10,000 (Rs.7,500 loan @4% + Rs.2,500 grant) for shop operation, to help PwDs in UP start a business.
caveats: Requires ownership of/ability to buy 110 sq. ft. of land, or a 5-year lease if renting; annual income must not exceed twice the poverty-line limit; no criminal/financial convictions; loan recovered in 30 quarterly instalments starting after 1 year.

title: Shramyogi Cycle Subsidy Scheme- Gujarat Labour Welfare Board
benefit_summary: Subsidy of Rs.1,500 towards purchase of a bicycle for laborers employed in the organized sector in Gujarat.
caveats: Must be employed 1+ year, contributing regularly to the Labour Welfare Fund; one-time only per employment period; application within 6 months of purchase.

title: Shravanbal Seva State Pension Scheme
benefit_summary: Combined monthly old-age pension of Rs.600 (Rs.200 central IGNOAPS + Rs.400 state top-up for BPL families, or full Rs.600 state-funded for non-BPL families with income <=Rs.21,000/year); per 2026 audit, combined total in Maharashtra is now Rs.1,500/month (central Rs.200-500 + state top-up).
caveats: Must be domicile of Maharashtra for 15+ years and destitute.

title: Shramik Basera Yojana (GBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Temporary prefabricated accommodation for registered construction workers in Gujarat at Rs.5/day.
caveats: Requires presenting a valid, renewed identity/smart card (e-Nirman card).

title: Sudama Chhatravrtti Yojana
benefit_summary: Pre-matric scholarship for General category, hosteller students (class 11-12) in MP: Rs.5,000/year (boys), Rs.5,250/year (girls), via DBT.
caveats: Limited to ~700 students statewide; requires 60%+ marks in 10th class and BPL family status.

title: State Disability Scholarship (Scholarship for Persons with Disabilities)
benefit_summary: Scholarship (from Rs.200/month, may vary by government guidelines) for disabled students (Class I-VIII) in Nagaland with 40%+ disability.
caveats: Institution must have valid AISHE/UDISE code; repeaters not eligible; cannot combine with other scholarship schemes.

title: Skill Development Allowance Scheme
benefit_summary: Rs.1,000/month general skill-development allowance; Rs.1,500/month for those with 50%+ permanent disability, for HP youth during training.
caveats: Eligibility criteria (age, domicile, education, income, employment status) may vary case by case per available text. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Corrected min_age from 18 to 16 (official floor is 'above 16, below 36') and added missing max_income=Rs.2,00,000/year (family income including spouse) -- both per the official 2013 HP scheme rules; the income cap was previously null/unenforced.

title: Skill Development Assistance (ANBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.10,000 financial assistance to registered construction workers (or their two children) in A&N Islands for purchase of tool kits after completing a Government ITI/VTC trade course.

title: Scholarship For Differently Abled Students
benefit_summary: CORRECTED tiered scholarship for disabled students in Kerala: Class 1-4 Rs.300/month; Class 5-10 Rs.500/month; +1/+2/ITI Rs.750(day)/Rs.1,000(hostel); Degree/Professional/PG Rs.1,000(day)/Rs.1,500(hostel); plus reader's allowance Rs.200-400/month.
caveats: Must have 40%+ disability and scored 40%+ marks in previous year's exam; family income cap Rs.36,000/year.

title: Spurring Entrepreneurship Initiative
benefit_summary: Startup loan of Rs.2-20 lakh via J&K Bank for youth establishing/expanding business ventures in J&K; Mission Youth pays interest (up to Rs.2 lakh) if no default occurs.
caveats: New-unit applicants must be unemployed and registered with District Employment Center; expansion applicants need 2+ years of existing business.

title: Scheme for Pension Benefits to the Journalists/Photojournalists
benefit_summary: CORRECTED: Honour Pension raised to Rs.10,000/month (from Rs.1,000) for retired accredited journalists/photojournalists in Tripura with 10+ years of service; companion Family Security Pension gives Rs.5,000/month to dependents.
caveats: Must not receive pension from other sources except EPF; retiree must be 60+ to receive pension though initial eligibility age is 18.

title: Surgical Grant For The Prevention Of Disability
benefit_summary: Surgical grant up to Rs.6,00,000 per disabled person for corrective surgeries (visual, hearing, orthopedic, post-leprosy) in Uttar Pradesh.
caveats: Must be UP permanent resident or resident for 5+ years; no criminal case pending.

title: Scholarships For Higher Education Abroad To Meritorious Boys And Girls From Open Category
benefit_summary: Full tuition fee, health insurance, subsistence allowance (GBP 9,900 UK / USD 15,400 other countries) and one round-trip airfare for open/unreserved category Maharashtra students pursuing PG/Diploma/PhD abroad at QS/THE top-200 institutions (20 scholarships/year).
caveats: Requires unconditional offer letter from a top-200-ranked foreign institution; age caps of 35 (Masters) / 40 (PhD) reported by secondary sources though not in original scraped eligibility text.

title: Shelter Home For Women (SHW)
benefit_summary: Grant-based institutional support (salary + maintenance components) to NGOs/trusts/local bodies running shelter homes for women in difficult circumstances in Goa; no fixed individual cash amount.
caveats: This scheme funds implementing organizations, not individual women directly. [Fix 2026-07-23] Occupation constraint removed from structured matching (originally tagged "other") -- eligibility is about being a woman in distress/crisis, not an occupation category.

title: Supply of Insulated Boxes
benefit_summary: 75% subsidy on insulated fish boxes for Goa fisherfolk: Rs.1,500 (50L box, fish vendors), Rs.7,000 (100L+220L boxes, canoe fishermen), Rs.15,000 (220L+400L boxes, mechanized vessel up to 6-cylinder engine).

title: Self Employment Scheme - Goa
benefit_summary: Loan up to Rs.10 lakh for an individual unemployed ST person, or up to Rs.15 lakh for an Association/Society/Partnership/SHG/Company of ST members, at a flat 4% interest per annum, repayable over up to 10 years. No interest-free share capital or interest rebate component.
caveats: Requires 10% margin money contribution (may be relaxed for individuals, not for groups/companies) and two guarantors (one must be a government servant). [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Corrected outdated benefit description (removed a nonexistent '50% interest-free share capital'/'75% interest rebate' structure) and raised max_income from Rs.1,00,000 to Rs.3,00,000/year, per the current official GSSTFDCL scheme PDF.

title: Self Employment Scheme
benefit_summary: 33% subsidy of unit cost (max Rs.1 lakh) via bank loan for religious minority community members (Muslim, Christian, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain) in Karnataka to start small-scale handicraft/service/agro-based businesses.
caveats: Family income cap Rs.6,00,000/year (flat, no rural/urban distinction). No family member may be a State/Central/PSU employee. Disabled applicants get reduced 5% self-contribution vs standard. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Replaced a stale rural/urban income-cap caveat (Rs.81,000/Rs.1,03,000/year) with the current flat Rs.6,00,000/year cap confirmed by direct fetch of the official KMDC page -- the old split figure now appears only on outdated third-party aggregators.

title: Special Education And Vocational Training Through Government Institutions
benefit_summary: Free special education (ages 6-18) and vocational training (18+) with food, shelter, clothing at government special schools/institutions for disabled persons in Maharashtra.
caveats: In-kind benefit delivered via government (not NGO) institutions, no cash component.

title: Spectacle Grant (Sainik Welfare)
benefit_summary: Rs.2,000 one-time financial assistance for purchase of spectacles for ex-servicemen/widows of ex-servicemen in Puducherry.
caveats: Members of the Ex-Servicemen Contributory Health Scheme (ECHS) are not eligible.

title: SWADHAR Greh (A Scheme For Women In Difficult Circumstances)
benefit_summary: Shelter, food, clothing, health, legal, vocational and counseling support for women in difficult circumstances (deserted, disaster survivors, released prisoners, domestic-violence victims, trafficking survivors) — stay periods 1-5 years depending on category.
caveats: CORRECTED: SWADHAR Greh was merged with Ujjawala and renamed 'Shakti Sadan' under Mission Shakti's Samarthya sub-scheme (2021-22); the standalone SWADHAR Greh name no longer exists. 404 functional Shakti Sadans as of Dec 2024.

title: Scheme for Grant of Additional Scholarship to the Students of Other Backward Classes of Andaman and Nicobar Islands, for Pursuing Higher Studies Anywh
benefit_summary: Rs.1,000/month additional scholarship (10 months/year) for non-creamy-layer OBC students of A&N Islands pursuing higher education anywhere in India after Class X/XII.
caveats: Only two children per parent/guardian eligible; scholarship depends on fund availability each year.

title: Sikkim Grant Of Award To Transgender
benefit_summary: CORRECTED tiered support for transgender persons in Sikkim: Rs.12,000/month (ages 0-6), 100% free education through graduation, Rs.500/month if remaining unemployed after acquiring required qualifications.
caveats: Must be from a BPL family, have no other pension/salary income, and hold a Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana bank account. Grant ceases upon permanent migration out of Sikkim or death.

title: Sanjay Gandhi Niradhar Grant Scheme
benefit_summary: CORRECTED: current rate Rs.1,500/month (effective Dec 2024, up from Rs.600/900 in original scraped snapshot) for destitute persons in Maharashtra — covers destitute men/women under 65, orphans, disabled persons, seriously ill (TB/cancer/AIDS/leprosy/sickle cell), abandoned/divorced/unmarried (35+) women, transgender persons, and prisoners' wives.
caveats: Broader eligibility than a simple widow pension; covers many vulnerable categories. Income must be BPL-listed or <=Rs.21,000/year.

title: Safai Karmakar Ke Bachche Hetu Chhatravrtti Yojana
benefit_summary: Tiered annual scholarship for children (max 2) of registered sanitation workers in Chhattisgarh: Rs.1,000-15,000 depending on class/level (Class I-V through PhD/research), with higher rates for girls.
caveats: Cannot combine with another government department's scholarship for the same purpose.

title: Safai Karmakar Bahay Rogi Chikitsa Sahayata Yojana
benefit_summary: Outpatient medical assistance up to Rs.2,000/year for registered sanitation workers and listed family members (spouse, up to 2 children) in Chhattisgarh.
caveats: Not available if receiving benefit from another parallel state scheme.

title: Snehasanthwanam
benefit_summary: DISAMBIGUATED: tiered support for Endosulfan pesticide-exposure victims in Kerala: Rs.2,200/month (bedridden), Rs.1,700/month (bedridden + Rs.300 disability pension), Rs.1,200/month (other victims); Rs.700/month for caregivers; child education aid Rs.2,000-4,000.
caveats: Distinct from other similarly-named Kerala schemes (Snehasparsham/Snehapoorvam) covering different beneficiary groups. [Fix 2026-07-23] Occupation constraint removed from structured matching (originally tagged "other") -- this is specifically for Endosulfan pesticide-exposure victims, a health/exposure status, not an occupation.

title: Safai Karmakar Gambhir Bimari Chikitsa Sahayata Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.50,000 medical assistance (or actual treatment cost, whichever lower) for registered sanitation workers in Chhattisgarh suffering from serious illness (kidney, cancer, sickle cell anemia, heart disease, AIDS, paralysis).
caveats: Requires 90+ days registration with the State Board; one-time benefit; not available if receiving a parallel state scheme's benefit.

title: Safai Karmakar Hetu Aavashyak Upakaran Sahayata Yojana "‹
benefit_summary: Annual grant of Rs.700 to registered sanitation workers in Chhattisgarh for purchase of essential work equipment (gum boots, gloves, masks, aprons).
caveats: Not payable if receiving similar aid from another parallel state scheme.

title: Safai Karmakaar Ke Putr/Putri Hetu Vishesh Coaching Yojana
benefit_summary: Special coaching fee (for engineering/medical/CA/MBA entrance) paid by the board for up to 2 children (class 10+) of registered sanitation workers in Chhattisgarh.
caveats: Confirmed active but benefit amount is in-kind/variable rather than a fixed rupee figure.

title: Swahid Kushal Konwar Sarbajanin Briddha Pension Achoni
benefit_summary: Monthly old-age pension of Rs.250 via DBT for Assam residents aged 60+.
caveats: Markedly lower than Assam's Orunodoi scheme (Rs.1,250/month) -- worth flagging that Orunodoi may be more beneficial where the beneficiary is also eligible.

title: Safai Karmakaar Kaushal Unnayan Yojana
benefit_summary: Skill training for registered sanitation workers and their families in Chhattisgarh in trades identified by the Technical Education Department (CSSDA).
caveats: Not payable if receiving another parallel state scheme benefit.

title: Safai Karmakaar Putr/Putri Cycle sahayata yojana
benefit_summary: Free bicycle for children (max 2/family) of registered sanitation workers in Chhattisgarh who are studying in a recognized school/college.
caveats: Must not have received bicycle assistance under any other government scheme earlier.

title: Safai Karmakar Prasuti Sahayata Yojana
benefit_summary: Maternity/paternity assistance for registered sanitation workers in Chhattisgarh: Rs.4,200 (3rd month pregnancy) + Rs.2,800 (8th month pregnancy) for women = up to Rs.7,000 maternity; Rs.3,000 paternity leave allowance for men.
caveats: Limited to two children per worker.

title: Shram Kalyan Shaikshanik Chatravriti Yojana
benefit_summary: Scholarship for children (max 2/family) of registered Labour Welfare Fund Act workers in Madhya Pradesh, from Class 5 through PG/ITI/Polytechnic/PGDCA/BE/MBBS; amount varies by class/course (not a single published figure).
caveats: Children of managerial-capacity officers/employees are excluded.

title: Shravan Kumar Shramik Parivar Tirth Yatra Yojana
benefit_summary: One-time lump sum of Rs.12,000 for pilgrimage travel expenses for registered construction worker families (up to 6 members) in Uttar Pradesh.
caveats: Worker's monthly salary (basic+DA) must not exceed Rs.15,000; requires 6+ months continuous service; only one spouse eligible if both work in registered factories; usable once in entire service period.

title: Scheme for Interest Subvention to Nano Household Enterprises
benefit_summary: CORRECTED: 6% per annum interest subvention (8% for women/SC-ST enterprises) for 3 years on term loans for Nano/household enterprises in Kerala with fixed capital investment up to Rs.10 lakh.
caveats: Unit must be in white/green pollution category with connected load <=5HP; subvention stops if loan repayment is defaulted in any year.

title: Stipend To Law Graduates
benefit_summary: Monthly stipend of Rs.5,000 for 4 years for SC/ST law graduates in Karnataka to practice in courts and undergo training under senior advocates.
caveats: Law degree must be from a recognized university; course duration 3 or 5 years.

title: State Marriage Assistance Scheme For Poor Girls
benefit_summary: One-time cash marriage assistance via DBT, paid before marriage: Rs.75,000 for AAY ration-card-holder families, Rs.50,000 for PHH ration-card-holder families (effective 1 April 2025; no gold component).
caveats: Must apply at least 1 month before marriage; minimum qualification 8th pass (special guidelines for dropouts FY2022-23 to FY2024-25); cannot combine with other schemes like Ladli Beti Scheme; one-time only. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Updated from a stale 'Rs.25,000 + 5g gold' figure to the current tiered cash-only structure (Rs.75,000 AAY / Rs.50,000 PHH) effective 1 April 2025, and added PHH to ration_card_types (previously AAY-only) -- both per confirmed 2025-26 J&K budget reporting. Note: PHH is modeled here via the closest existing value 'BPL' since our schema doesn't have a distinct PHH ration-card type.

title: Shramyogi Home Town Scheme- Gujarat Labour Welfare Board
benefit_summary: Railway fare reimbursement for migrant laborers in Gujarat's organized sector to travel to/from their home state, once every 2 years.
caveats: Requires 1+ year continuous employment with Labour Welfare Fund deposits; only one spouse eligible if both work; prior approval required before travel; no fixed rupee figure (fare-based).

title: Shree Nanaji Deshmukh Awas Yojana (GBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.1,60,000 financial assistance to registered construction workers in Gujarat who have been allotted an EWS/LIG house under CM/PM Awas Yojana in urban areas.
caveats: Given once per family; worker must be registered 2+ years; no other land/property in the name of worker or family members; application only after 1 year of house allotment.

title: Scheme for Margin Money Grant to Nano Units
benefit_summary: CORRECTED: Margin Money Grant of 30% of project cost (cap Rs.3 lakh, general) or 40% (cap Rs.4 lakh, for women/youth 18-40/disabled/ex-servicemen/SC-ST with +10% additional grant) for Nano enterprises in Kerala with project cost up to Rs.10 lakh.
caveats: Unit must not have availed any prior government grant assistance; must remain operational for 3 years from receipt of grant.

title: Shaadi Mubarak Scheme
benefit_summary: One-time marriage assistance of Rs.1,00,116 (Rs.1,25,145 for disabled brides) for unmarried minority-community girls in Telangana, transferred to the mother's bank account.
caveats: Marriage must occur on/after 2 Oct 2014; combined parental income must not exceed Rs.2,00,000/year; can be availed only once in a lifetime; payment delays have been reported.

title: Scheme of Scholarship for Sainik Schools
benefit_summary: Scholarship for Sainik School (Goalpara) Class 12 students whose parents are Meghalaya residents: Rs.20,000 (family income <Rs.5,000/month) or Rs.10,000 (income Rs.5,000-8,000/month).
caveats: Applicant must be ST/SC or child of service personnel/ex-servicemen; must be fluent in English.

title: Scheme For Providing Assistive Devices To Differently Abled Persons
benefit_summary: CORRECTED: need-based provision of assistive devices (wheelchairs, screen readers, Daisy players, talking calculators, etc.) for disabled persons in Kerala; no fixed monetary cap -- devices provided per tender price.
caveats: Income cap of Rs.1,00,000/year is an eligibility ceiling, not a benefit cap; Medical Board must certify capability to use the device.

title: Silicosis Pidit Hita-dhikariyon Hetu Sahayata Yojana
