benefit_summary: Rs.1,00,000 assistance for workers diagnosed with silicosis, plus Rs.3,00,000 death benefit, for registered stone-mine construction workers in Rajasthan.
caveats: Silicosis must be certified by the Pneumoconiosis Medical Board; cannot claim from both this scheme and the Rajasthan Environment and Health Care Fund simultaneously.

title: State Post-metric Scholarship For Disabled
benefit_summary: Post-metric maintenance allowance for disabled students in Maharashtra, tiered by course group: Rs.230-1,200/month depending on hosteller/day-scholar status and course level (Medical/Engineering/Agri/Vet/PG highest); HSC rates separately raised to Rs.800-1,000/month per an April 2026 Cabinet decision.
caveats: Must have passed class 10 and not failed the last qualifying exam; includes reader allowance for blind students.

title: Shiksha Protsaahan Puraskaar yojana
benefit_summary: CORRECTED tiered scholarship for children (max 2) of Madhya Pradesh Shram Kalyan Mandal registered workers: Rs.10,000 (General Grad/Law/PG), Rs.15,000 (Engineering), Rs.25,000 (MBBS/BDS), Rs.12,500 (Pharmacy), Rs.11,500 (ME/MTech).
caveats: Requires 70%+ marks in qualifying exam (60%+ for MBBS students); parent must be an enrolled industrial/institutional worker under the Labour Welfare Fund.

title: Scheme for Plantation Development (New planting & Replanting) under Medium Term Framework Plan (MTFP) in Traditional Areas (Kerala and Tamil Nadu), No
benefit_summary: CORRECTED: per-hectare rubber-planting subsidy up to Rs.25,000/ha (general) or Rs.40,000/ha (SC category) for Kerala/Tamil Nadu traditional rubber-growing areas, plus Rs.10/plant (up to 500 plants/ha) for planting material.
caveats: This is a Rubber Board (Ministry of Commerce, Govt of India) scheme, not a Kerala state department scheme, despite state_guess. Grower must hold absolute possession of the land (max 2 ha eligible, subsidy limited to 1 ha); paddy-field land is ineligible.

title: Scheme of Pension for Eminent Sports Persons
benefit_summary: Monthly pension for veteran sportspersons who represented India: Rs.1,000/month (Olympics/World Cup/Davis Cup/Test cricket) or Rs.600/month (Commonwealth/Asian Games) for Punjab domiciled athletes.
caveats: Payable from age 40; also payable alongside any Government of India sports pension. [Fix 2026-07-23] Occupation constraint removed from structured matching -- this is specifically for eminent/retired sportspersons, an occupation category our FLOW does not capture.

title: Satyvadi Raja Harishchandra Marnotar Sahay Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.5,000 funeral expense assistance for Scheduled Caste families in Gujarat upon the death of a family member.
caveats: Must apply within 6 months of death with death registration certificate; only one person per family can claim per death. Income ceiling per the official Gujarat SJE page: Rs.6,00,000/year overall (the same page also separately lists Rs.47,000/year rural / Rs.68,000/year urban -- an internal inconsistency in the source itself; we use the higher, more inclusive Rs.6,00,000 figure so eligible lower-income and mid-income applicants aren't wrongly turned away). [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Added missing max_income (was null) -- the official Gujarat source lists an income eligibility condition (either Rs.6,00,000 flat or a Rs.47,000/68,000 rural/urban split on the same page); used the higher, more inclusive figure given the source's own internal inconsistency.

title: Self Employment Scheme For Rehabilitation Of Manual Scavengers
benefit_summary: CORRECTED (revised w.e.f. 1.4.2021): one-time cash assistance of Rs.40,000 plus upfront capital subsidy up to Rs.5 lakh and concessional loans (up to Rs.15 lakh project cost) for identified manual scavengers and dependents to pursue alternative self-employment; skill training stipend Rs.3,000/month for up to 2 years; health insurance cover Rs.5 lakh under AB-PMJAY.
caveats: Applicant must be identified/surveyed as a manual scavenger with an MS-ID. Manual scavenging is NOT eradicated in India (still illegal but persists) -- do not present this as a solved/banned issue. [Fix 2026-07-23] Occupation constraint removed from structured matching -- this is specifically for rehabilitated manual scavengers, a status our FLOW does not capture. IMPORTANT: SRMS has been discontinued as a standalone scheme -- its components (health insurance, skill training, capital subsidy) were subsumed into NAMASTE (National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem), launched July 2023, jointly run by the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment and Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs. A citizen applying today would be routed through NAMASTE, not a freestanding SRMS application. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Flagged SRMS as superseded/subsumed into NAMASTE rather than presenting it as a currently active standalone scheme with its own live benefit track.

title: State Rice Mission Scheme
benefit_summary: 50% subsidy on quality paddy seeds, organic/bio-fertilizers, bio-pesticides, and 50% subsidy on power tillers/SRI tools for farmers in Meghalaya.

title: Silpi Pension Scheme - Assam
benefit_summary: CORRECTED tiered support for artists in Assam: Rs.8,000/month individual Artist Pension (raised), Rs.4,000/month Family Pension (for families of deceased/indigent artists), plus Rs.50,000 one-time Barxik Silpi Sanman and Rs.50,000 one-time family financial assistance.
caveats: Applicant must have recognition proof certificate for contributions in Music, Dance, Fine Arts, Puppetry, Theatre or Films.

title: Savitribai Phule Scholarship For V.J.N.T And S.B.C Girls Students Studying In 8th To 10 Std
benefit_summary: Rs.100/month (Rs.1,000 for 10 months) scholarship for VJNT/SBC girl students in Class 8-10 in Maharashtra.
caveats: No income limit and no minimum marks requirement.

title: Savitribai Phule Scholarship For V.J.N.T. And S.B.C. Girl Students Studying In 5th To 7th Standard
benefit_summary: Rs.60/month (Rs.600 for 10 months) scholarship for VJNT/SBC girl students in Class 5-7 in Maharashtra government-recognized schools.

title: Super 5000
benefit_summary: CORRECTED: one-time award of Rs.25,000 (not a recurring scholarship) for the top 5,000 statewide scorers in Class 10/12 board exams who are children of unorganized-sector/construction workers and study in an MP government school.
caveats: Construction-worker parent's age must be 18-60; restricted to Madhya Pradesh Board of Secondary Education results only.

title: State Pre-metric Scholarship For Disabled
benefit_summary: CORRECTED: pre-metric scholarship for disabled students in Maharashtra revised (Apr 2026 Cabinet decision) to Rs.500/month flat for Nursery-Class 8 (from Rs.100-150 tiered), and Rs.800/month hosteller / Rs.600/month day-scholar for Class 9-10 (from Rs.200/month); adds reader allowance Rs.150/month and study-tour allowance up to Rs.1,500/year.
caveats: Formal Government Resolution not yet located for the 2026 revision -- based on news coverage only; recommend confirming once the GR is indexed.

title: Shramik Parivahan Yojana (GBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Concessional bus pass for registered construction workers in Gujarat to commute from Kadianaka to worksite; worker pays 20% of pass cost, board covers 80%.

title: Samarth-Respite Care Scheme
benefit_summary: Respite care / group home facility (with vocational activities, medical care, therapeutic support) for orphaned/abandoned persons with Autism, Cerebral Palsy, Mental Retardation, or Multiple Disabilities, prioritizing BPL/LIG and destitute families, under the National Trust Act 1999.
caveats: Provides family respite time as well as institutional care for the person with disability.

title: Scholarship To Son And Daughter Of Differently Abled Persons
benefit_summary: Scholarship for children (son/daughter) of differently-abled parents in Tamil Nadu, from having passed Class 10 / studying Class 11 onward through postgraduate/professional/ITI/polytechnic courses: Rs.1,000 (10th pass, 11th std) rising to Rs.1,500 (12th), Rs.1,500-1,750 (UG), Rs.2,000-3,000 (PG), Rs.2,000-4,000 (professional degree), Rs.4,000-6,000 (professional PG), Rs.1,000-1,200 (ITI/Polytechnic) -- higher figures include hostel.
caveats: Parent must hold an identity card issued by the TN welfare board for the Differently Abled. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Corrected: this scholarship covers Class 11 onward (student must have passed Class 10), NOT Class 1 -- the original benefit_summary's 'Class 1 through PG' framing and tier amounts had been mixed up with a different, similarly-named scheme for disabled students themselves.

title: Scholarships to Students with Disabilities Scheme
benefit_summary: Monthly scholarship for students with disabilities in Punjab: Rs.200/month (Class 1-8), Rs.300/month (Class 9 onwards).
caveats: Requires 40%+ marks in previous annual exam; family monthly income cap Rs.5,000 (Rs.60,000/year).

title: Scholarship Scheme For Disabled Students To Study Abroad For Higher Education
benefit_summary: Scholarship for higher education abroad (PG/PhD) for 12 disabled students/year (2 each orthopedic/hearing/visual) from Madhya Pradesh; benefit amount not published.
caveats: Requires 60%+ marks in relevant postgraduate/research exam plus 2 years' teaching/research/professional experience or M.Phil for PhD-level applicants; registration on Sparsh portal required; one child per family, once only.

title: Sant Ravidaas Shiksha Protsaahan Yojana
benefit_summary: Tiered educational incentive for children of registered construction workers in UP: Rs.2,000 (Class 1-5) up to Rs.1,00,000 (research), including full fee reimbursement for MBBS/IIM/IIT/NIT/NIFT/Law courses, plus bicycle subsidy and merit bonuses (Rs.5,000 boys/Rs.8,000 girls for 70%+ marks in class 10/12).
caveats: Worker must be registered with the Board for 1+ year (365 days); child's age must fall within class-appropriate ranges (e.g., Class 1-2: age 6-8).

title: Sneha Sparsha
benefit_summary: Financial assistance for specialized pediatric treatment (Bone Marrow Transplant up to Rs.10 lakh, Cochlear Implant up to Rs.5.35 lakh BPL/Rs.3 lakh APL, Liver Transplant up to Rs.16 lakh BPL/Rs.10 lakh APL, Kidney Transplant up to Rs.3 lakh+) for children under 12 with serious ailments in Assam.
caveats: Priority given to BPL families; distinct from the separate Swanirbhar Naari scheme.

title: Swabhimaan Scheme
benefit_summary: Monthly take-home ration (7.5kg nutritious supplementary food kit) for pregnant women, lactating mothers, and adolescent girls (11-14 years) in Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu, to combat malnutrition and anemia.
caveats: Builds on the ICDS supplementary nutrition component; distinct from Poshan 2.0/Mission Saksham Anganwadi.

title: Snehapoorvam Scheme
benefit_summary: DISAMBIGUATED tiered educational assistance for orphaned/single-parent children in Kerala: Rs.300/month (below age 5, Class 1-5), Rs.500 (Class 6-10), Rs.750 (Class 11-12), Rs.1,000 (degree/professional).
caveats: For APL category, income cap is Rs.20,000/year (rural) or Rs.22,375/year (urban); BPL children have no income cap. Child must have lost one or both parents.

title: Shikshashree Scheme
benefit_summary: Annual financial assistance for SC day-scholar students (Class V-VIII) in West Bengal: Rs.750/year (Class V-VII), Rs.800/year (Class VIII).
caveats: Cannot combine with another scholarship/stipend for the same period; requires a nationalized bank account with core banking facility; renewed annually subject to good conduct/attendance.

title: Scheme for Small Business Owners of Scheduled Castes to Buy a Place of Business/Shop
benefit_summary: Loan up to Rs.10 lakh at 4% interest (government covers interest above 4% for 3 years) plus Rs.15,000 subsidy, for Scheduled Caste individuals in Gujarat to buy a shop/business premises in urban areas.
caveats: No income limit; priority to educated unemployed, unemployed mill workers, and technically qualified/self-employed persons; subsidy paid after 3 months of shop opening; shop mortgaged to government until loan repaid.

title: Subsidy Scheme For Establishment Of 100 Broiler Birds' Farm For Schedule Caste
benefit_summary: 75% subsidy (max Rs.27,000, cash to bank account) for establishing a 100-broiler-bird poultry farm for Scheduled Caste beneficiaries in Gujarat.
caveats: Requires prior poultry-keeping training and own/2-year-leased land; unit must be maintained for 2 years; priority to women/BPL applicants.

title: Subsidy Scheme On Establishment Of - 25 Kadaknath/R.I.R. Birds Unit To Scheduled Tribes
benefit_summary: 75% subsidy (max Rs.4,500, in the form of 25 Kadaknath/R.I.R. birds and poultry feed) for Scheduled Tribe beneficiaries in Gujarat to establish a poultry unit.
caveats: Requires prior poultry-keeping training; unit must be maintained for 2 years; priority to women/BPL applicants.

title: Subsidy Scheme On Establishment Of 25 R.I.R. Birds' Unit For Scheduled Caste
benefit_summary: 75% subsidy (max Rs.4,500, in the form of 25 R.I.R. birds and poultry feed) for Scheduled Caste beneficiaries in Gujarat to establish a poultry unit.
caveats: One member per family eligible; requires prior poultry-keeping training; unit must be maintained for 2 years; priority to women/BPL applicants.

title: Subsidy Scheme On Establishment Of 25 R.I.R. Birds' Unit For Weaker Section
benefit_summary: 75% subsidy (max Rs.4,500, in the form of 25 R.I.R. birds and poultry feed) for economically weaker section beneficiaries in Gujarat to establish a poultry unit.
caveats: Requires prior poultry-keeping training; unit must be maintained for 2 years; priority to women/BPL applicants.

title: Subsidy Scheme On Establishment Of 40 R.I.R. Birds Unit For Divyang People
benefit_summary: 90% subsidy (max Rs.7,200, in the form of 40 R.I.R. birds and poultry feed) for Divyang (disabled) beneficiaries in Gujarat to establish a poultry unit.
caveats: Requires prior poultry-keeping training; unit must be maintained for 2 years; priority to women/BPL applicants.

title: Shreshtam Scheme For Ensuring Participation Of PwDs In Arts & Sports
benefit_summary: Up to Rs.10,000 support for disabled persons in Kerala who have shown talent in arts/sports at state/national championships, for specialized training at recognized academies (10 beneficiaries/district).

title: Snehayanam Scheme For Mothers Of Persons With Special Needs
benefit_summary: Free electric auto-rickshaw (in-kind, no cash) for widowed/divorced/abandoned BPL mothers of persons with disabilities (National Trust Act categories) in Kerala, to provide a livelihood (2 beneficiaries/district initially).
caveats: Beneficiary must hold a valid 3-wheeler license; must bear tax/insurance costs; vehicle registered solely in beneficiary's name and cannot be transferred/sold. Also covers women abandoned by their husband (a third eligible category alongside widowed/divorced per the official Kerala Social Justice Dept page) -- our marital_status field has no 'abandoned' option, so this may be missed; an abandoned-but-still-legally-married woman may need to self-report as 'married' in the bot and would be incorrectly excluded. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Flagged a schema gap: eligibility also covers 'abandoned by husband' women, a category our FLOW's marital_status options (single/married/widowed/divorced) can't represent.

title: Stipend Scheme For Poultry Farming Training For Divyang People
benefit_summary: One-time stipend up to Rs.2,000 (Rs.300/day x 6 days + Rs.200 transport) for 6-day poultry farming training, paid via DBT; poultry training certificate awarded on completion.
caveats: Females and BPL beneficiaries given priority. Requires income proof certificate.

title: Stipend Scheme For Poultry Farming Training For Schedule Caste
benefit_summary: One-time stipend up to Rs.2,000 (Rs.300/day x 6 days + Rs.200 transport) for 6-day poultry farming training, paid via DBT; certificate awarded on completion.
caveats: Females and BPL beneficiaries given priority. Requires income proof and caste certificate.

title: Scheme For Subsidy On Interest For Establishment Of 1 To 20 Milch Animal Farm
benefit_summary: Interest subsidy up to 12% (max) on bank loan for purchasing 1-20 dairy animals (cow/buffalo), for 5 years, paid via DBT to loan account (no direct cash).
caveats: Only one family member can be beneficiary. Loan must be from nationalized bank/RBI-approved institution in the current financial year. Land must be owned by family member/beneficiary.

title: Scheme For Subsidy On Interest For Establishment Of 1 To 20 Milch Animal Farm For Scheduled Caste
benefit_summary: Interest subsidy up to 12% (max) on bank loan for purchasing 1-20 dairy animals, for 5 years, for small/poor SC farmers, paid via DBT to loan account.
caveats: Only one family member can be beneficiary. Loan must be from nationalized bank/RBI-approved institution in the current financial year.

title: Scheme For Subsidy On Interest For Establishment Of 1 To 20 Milch Animal Farm For Scheduled Tribe
benefit_summary: Interest subsidy up to 12% (max) on bank loan for purchasing 1-20 dairy animals, for 5 years, for small/poor ST farmers, paid via DBT to loan account.
caveats: Only one family member can be beneficiary.

title: Stipend Scheme For Poultry Farming Training For Weaker Section
benefit_summary: One-time stipend up to Rs.2,000 (Rs.300/day x 6 days + Rs.200 transport) for 6-day poultry farming training for economically weaker section adults, paid via DBT.
caveats: Females and BPL beneficiaries given priority. Requires income proof.

title: Swasraya Scheme For Parents/Mothers Of Physically Handicapped/Mentally Retarded Persons
benefit_summary: One-time financial assistance of Rs.35,000 for self-employment, for BPL mothers/caregivers (single, widowed, divorced, abandoned, or close female relatives) of children with 70%+ disability/mental retardation.
caveats: Applicant's child (not applicant) must have 70%+ disability/mental retardation. Priority to mothers of bedridden severely disabled patients.

title: Silicosis (Bimari) Se Pidit Shramiko Ke Liye Aarthik Evam Punarvas Sahayata Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.3,00,000 financial assistance for workers diagnosed with silicosis disease; Rs.1,00,000 lump sum to family plus remainder as fixed deposit with monthly interest if worker dies.
caveats: Must be registered with Chhattisgarh Unorganized Workers State Social Security Board (or unable to prove organized-sector work/ineligible for BOCW Board). Silicosis must be confirmed by competent doctors. [Fix 2026-07-23] Occupation constraint removed from structured matching (originally "unorganized_worker") -- this is specifically for workers diagnosed with silicosis, a health condition, not an occupation.

title: Shrama Shakthi Scheme
benefit_summary: Loan of Rs.50,000 at 4% interest (36 installments) for religious minority community entrepreneurs, with artisan/technical skill training; up to 50% back-end subsidy if 50% repaid within 36 months.
caveats: Restricted to State Religious Minority Community members. Applicant/family must not have used another KMDCL scheme (except Arivu) in last 5 years. Duplicate entries noted for this scheme - recommend merging.

title: Sant Surdas Scheme
benefit_summary: Monthly financial assistance of Rs.1,000 via DBT for disabled children aged 0-17 with 80%+ disability from BPL families.
caveats: Per the FY2025-26 Gujarat state budget, extended from 80%+ disability to 60%+ disability, and the earlier 0-17 age cap and BPL card requirement were both removed -- now open to disabled persons of any age with 60%+ disability regardless of BPL status. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Updated per the FY2025-26 budget revision: disability threshold lowered from 80% to 60%, and the age cap (0-17) and BPL requirement were both removed.

title: Sainik School Sujanpur Tihra Scholarship Scheme
benefit_summary: Scholarship of Rs.18,000/year plus Dietary Money Rs.10/day (295 days) and Clothing Allowance Rs.1,500/year (1st year)/Rs.750/year (subsequent), for HP resident students at Sainik School Sujanpur Tihra (Class VI-XII).
caveats: Scholarship suspended if student fails a class; discontinued if receiving financial assistance from any other source.

title: Samagra Samajik Suraksha Vridhavastha Pension Yojana
benefit_summary: Monthly pension of Rs.600 for destitute elderly (60+) unable to support themselves, registered on Samagra portal.
caveats: Parent/umbrella scheme for the Rs.600/month Samagra pension family.

title: Saphalam Scheme For Transgender Students Pursuing Professional Courses
benefit_summary: Financial assistance up to Rs.1,00,000/year for transgender students pursuing professional degree/diploma courses on merit seats (MBBS, BVSc, BSc Agriculture, and other government-college professional courses).
caveats: Only merit-seat admissions qualify, not management/NRI quota. Annual cap applies.

title: Samagr Samajik Suraksha Pension Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.600/month pension for one of several destitute categories: elderly 60+, widows 18+, unmarried women 50+ (non-income-taxpayer), abandoned BPL women 18-59, or disabled persons 6-18 with 40%+ disability.
caveats: Umbrella scheme covering multiple sub-categories (old-age, widow, unmarried, deserted-women, disabled) each with distinct age/condition criteria - see specific sub-scheme for precise eligibility.

title: Stipend Scheme For Scheduled Tribes - Poultry Training Stipend
benefit_summary: One-time stipend up to Rs.2,000 (Rs.300/day x 6 days + Rs.200 transport) for 6-day poultry farming training for Scheduled Tribe adults, paid via DBT.
caveats: Females and BPL beneficiaries given priority. Requires income proof and caste certificate.

title: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana
benefit_summary: Small savings account for girl child (opened before age 10): min deposit Rs.250/yr, max Rs.1,50,000/yr, ~8.2% interest (Q2 FY2026-27), matures after 21 years or on marriage after age 18; tax-exempt under Sec 80C.
caveats: Max 2 accounts per family (exceptions for twins/triplets). No premature withdrawal except up to 50% after girl turns 18.

title: Saur Sujala Yojana
benefit_summary: Subsidized solar irrigation pump (03 HP/05 HP) installation; beneficiary contribution ranges Rs.7,000-10,000 (SC/ST) to Rs.18,000-20,000 (general), plus a per-watt processing fee.
caveats: Beneficiary must own agricultural land and a water source (borewell/well/river) in their own name. Contribution amount varies by caste category.

title: Shauchalaya Sahayata Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.12,000 grant for toilet construction, paid in two installments of Rs.6,000 (before and after construction/use), for registered construction workers without a home toilet.
caveats: Must be registered with UP BOCW Welfare Board, regularly depositing contributions, and not have received similar benefit elsewhere. Bank account must be in a CBS branch of a nationalized bank.

title: Soil Testing Laboratory
benefit_summary: Free soil testing service for farmers plus issuance of a Soil Health Card (SHC).
caveats: Selection is first-come-first-served among bonafide farmers with sufficient cultivable land.

title: Seed Testing Laboratory Scheme
benefit_summary: Free seed testing service and training for farmers to ensure seed viability/purity.
caveats: Selection is first-come-first-served among bonafide farmers with sufficient cultivable land.

title: Schedule Tribe Pre-Metric Scholarship Class 06 To 08
benefit_summary: Pre-matric scholarship for ST students in classes 6-8: Rs.75/month (boys), Rs.125/month (girls).
caveats: Parents/guardians must not be income-tax payers. Student must not receive any other scholarship/allowance, and must not have failed the previous class. Applications now handled via Shala Darpan portal by schools.

title: Supply of Tri-Cycles (CBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: In-kind provision of a tri-cycle (once in a lifetime) to disabled registered construction workers and their disabled dependents.
caveats: Requires 6 months' membership with the Board and regular contribution to the Punjab Labour Welfare Fund before eligibility.

title: Scholarship For Transgender Students
benefit_summary: Tiered monthly scholarship for transgender students (10 months/year): Rs.1,000 (classes 7-10), Rs.1,500 (+1/+2), Rs.2,000 (Diploma/Degree/PG/Professional courses).
caveats: No income limit. Must be studying in State Govt/aided/self-financing institution from class 7 onward.

title: State Talent Search Examination in Mathematics and Science for Tribal Students of Meghalaya at the Close of Upper Primary Stage (Class VIII)
benefit_summary: Rs.600/month incentive award for 12 months over 2 years (Class IX-X), totaling Rs.14,400, for tribal students who score well in a Class VIII Maths/Science talent exam.
caveats: Restricted to Khasi, Jaintia, Garo, Koch and Hajong tribal communities of Meghalaya; requires 50+ aggregate marks in Class VII Maths/Science.

title: Surakshit Matritva Aashwasan Yojana
benefit_summary: Zero-expense delivery/C-section, 4 antenatal check-ups, transport to/from health facility, and newborn care visits for pregnant women and newborns (0-6 months) at public health facilities.
caveats: Zero-tolerance policy for denial of service; covers all categories (APL and BPL) with no income restriction. Complements JSSK.

title: Sikkim Unmarried Women Pension Scheme
benefit_summary: Monthly pension of Rs.2,000 for unmarried BPL women aged 45-59 with no source of income.
caveats: Must not be covered by any other state/central pension scheme.

title: Shri Vajpayee Bankable Yojana
benefit_summary: Bank loan up to Rs.25 lakh/sector (raised from Rs.8 lakh) with subsidy of 25-40% (rural) or 20-30% (urban) depending on category, now capped at Rs.3,75,000 (General category) or Rs.5,00,000 (SC/ST/Divyang/Women/Ex-servicemen) -- raised from the old Rs.1,25,000 cap, effective FY2025-26 under Gujarat's Cottage and Village Industries Policy 2024.
caveats: Requires min. 4th standard pass plus relevant training/experience, or hereditary craftsperson status. No income criteria. SC/ST/ex-servicemen/women/40%+ disabled get higher subsidy rates. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Updated loan/subsidy caps to the FY2025-26 revision (GRs dated May-June 2025): max loan Rs.25 lakh (from Rs.8 lakh), max subsidy Rs.3.75 lakh General / Rs.5 lakh SC-ST-Divyang (from Rs.1.25 lakh).

title: Swami Vivekananda Merit-cum-Means Scholarship
benefit_summary: Monthly scholarship tiers by course: UG Arts/Commerce Rs.1,000, UG Science Rs.1,500, PG Arts/Commerce Rs.2,000, PG Science Rs.2,500, plus Engineering/Medical/Nursing/Pharmacy (UG&PG) Rs.5,000/month.
caveats: Minimum 60% marks in Madhyamik (secondary) exam required for most tiers. Kanyashree recipients pursuing PG exempt from income proof.

title: Swami Vivekananda Utkrisht Chhatravriti Yojna
benefit_summary: Scholarship of Rs.18,000/year for 2 successive years after matric, for top-2000 merit rankers (general category) enrolled in Class 11 or professional/technical courses.
caveats: Restricted to general category students who passed Class 10 and rank in the top 2000 statewide.

title: Su-Swastha Yojna - Sikkim
benefit_summary: Cashless health insurance (up to Rs.10 lakh base + Rs.10 lakh critical care cover/year/family) for Sikkim government employees and up to 5 dependents, across 400+ empaneled hospitals; maternity cover up to Rs.50,000.
caveats: Restricted to regular Sikkim government employees (or central/other-state govt employees on deputation to Sikkim) and their dependents - not open to the general public.

title: Subsidy Scheme For Purchase Of Taxi / Goods Vehicle / Passenger Autorickshaw
benefit_summary: Subsidy of 33-75% of vehicle value (up to Rs.2.5-4 lakh depending on category) to purchase a taxi/goods vehicle/auto-rickshaw, for religious minority community members with a valid driving license.
caveats: SC/ST beneficiaries get a higher subsidy tier (75% or up to Rs.4 lakh) vs. general minority beneficiaries (50% or up to Rs.3 lakh). Open to all religious minorities, not Muslims-only, despite some viral claims. Also known as Swavalambi Sarathi.

title: Travel Concession To The Differently Abled Persons In State Owned Transport Corporation Buses
benefit_summary: Free bus travel up to 100km (visually impaired, no condition), free travel with escort (intellectually disabled, or children to early-intervention centers), and free travel up to 100km for school/work/hospital (speech/hearing/locomotor disabled); 75% concession on other statewide travel.
caveats: No income ceiling for any of these concessions.

title: Top Class Education For Students With Disabilities
benefit_summary: Full tuition fee (cap Rs.1.9-2 lakh/yr private institutions), living expenses Rs.3,000/month (hostellers)/Rs.1,500 (day scholars), book allowance Rs.5,000/yr, one-time computer grant Rs.45,000, one-time aids/assistive-device grant Rs.30,000, special allowance up to Rs.2,000/month.
caveats: Only 300 scholarships/year nationally, 50% reserved for women. Applicant must not be the third sibling already availing this scholarship.

title: Scheme For Working Women Hostel
benefit_summary: Subsidized hostel accommodation (branded 'Sakhi Niwas') for working women/trainees, with day-care for children; rent capped at 15%/10%/7.5% of salary for single/double/dormitory rooms.
caveats: Income ceiling Rs.50,000/month (metro) or Rs.35,000/month (other areas) - use the higher metro figure as general threshold. Max stay 3 years (extendable to 5). Married women whose husband/family lives elsewhere also qualify.

title: Shagun Yojana
benefit_summary: One-time marriage grant of Rs.31,000 for parents/guardians (or the woman herself) for the marriage of BPL/SC/ST/OBC daughters, or destitute/widow women's own (re)marriage.
caveats: Bride must be 18+, groom 21+. Grant disbursed up to 2 months before or within 6 months after the marriage date.

title: Technical Education Scholarship Scheme For Degree Level
benefit_summary: Monthly scholarship for PG/Degree Engineering/Technology/Architecture students: Rs.300 (general), Rs.500 (SC/ST, 100% coverage).
caveats: 175 scholarships available. Min. 60% marks required (waived for SC/ST students).

title: Technical Education Scholarship Scheme For Diploma Level
benefit_summary: Monthly scholarship of Rs.200 for Diploma-level Engineering/Technology/Architectural Assistantship students, for all categories.
caveats: 75 scholarships available. 100% scholarships reserved for SC, ST, and girl students.

title: Technical Education Scholarship Scheme for ITI Level
benefit_summary: Monthly scholarship for ITI trainees in Himachal Pradesh, open to all categories: Rs.250/month for SC/ST/OBC trainees, Rs.100/month for General category trainees.
caveats: Scholarship reduced correspondingly if trainee receives a stipend from elsewhere. Requires 80%+ attendance. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Removed incorrect caste_category=[sc,st,obc] restriction -- this scheme is open to ALL categories, just at a lower Rs.100/month rate for General-category trainees (vs Rs.250 for SC/ST/OBC). Was wrongly excluding General-category ITI trainees entirely.

title: Tripura Health Insuarance Scheme For Poor
benefit_summary: Family-floater health cover up to Rs.1.15 lakh/year (max 5 members) plus up to Rs.10,000 transport reimbursement, cashless at empaneled hospitals.
caveats: Family members must be listed on the Tripura family ration card.

title: Thayi Bhagya Scheme(comprehensive Maternal Healthcare)
benefit_summary: Free institutional delivery services (normal, complicated, caesarean, forceps) at registered private/government hospitals for BPL pregnant women, cashless from admission to discharge.
caveats: Geographically limited to 7 backward districts (Gulbarga, Bidar, Raichur, Koppal, Bijapur, Bagalkot, Chamarajanagar) - NOT available statewide. Benefit limited to first two deliveries. Eligibility is BPL ration card OR Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe category (separate, alternative qualifying paths, not a combined requirement) -- our schema can't express this OR condition, so the BPL hard-gate has been removed to avoid wrongly excluding SC/ST women without a BPL card. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Removed the ration_card_types=[BPL] hard gate since eligibility is actually BPL OR SC/ST (an alternative, not combined, requirement our AND-only matching engine can't represent) -- was wrongly excluding SC/ST pregnant women without a BPL card.

title: Total Health Check-up Scheme (GBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Preventive health check-up (routine/pathology/radiology/cardiology) for registered construction workers, up to Rs.1,950/beneficiary paid directly to the empaneled hospital (no cash to worker).
caveats: Must be registered with Gujarat Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board (e-Nirman Card).

title: Theka Shramik, Hamaal Shramik Evan Gharelu Mahila Kamgar Gambhir Bimaari Chikitsa Sahayata Yojana
benefit_summary: Medical aid of Rs.50,000 for serious illness (kidney disease, cancer, sickle cell anemia, heart disease, AIDS, paralysis) for registered contract/porter workers and female domestic workers.
caveats: Must be registered with State Social Security Board at least 90 days in advance. Benefit available only once; ineligible if already benefiting from a parallel state scheme.

title: Thatched House Repair Grant for Re-thatching & Repairs (Sainik Welfare)
benefit_summary: Grant of actual repair cost or up to Rs.40,000 for re-thatching/repair of a thatched house, every three years, for Ex-servicemen/widows/dependents.
caveats: Must be registered with Department of Sainik Welfare, Puducherry, and receiving Subsistence Allowance.

title: Tripura Journalist Health Insurance Scheme
benefit_summary: Health insurance coverage up to Rs.3,00,000 for accredited working journalists; government pays ~80%, journalist pays ~20%.
caveats: Must be accredited by state government or PIB, and not already covered under Ayushman Bharat or any other government health insurance.

title: Tool Kit Grant for Traditional Handicrafts Experts
benefit_summary: Training cost + stipend + tool kit grant together capped at Rs.25,000 (training/stipend portion itself capped at Rs.5,000) for modernizing traditional occupation equipment.
caveats: Preference given to those with more than two girl children, differently-abled persons, and 10+ years of experience. Grant must not be used as working capital.

title: Zero Ticket Bus Travel Scheme for Women
benefit_summary: Free bus travel on Tamil Nadu government buses for women, no fare up to 30 kilometers.
caveats: No formal application needed - request a zero-value ticket from the conductor. Recently informally rebranded from 'Magalir Vidiyal Payanam' to 'Magalir Payanam' (no official GO yet as of July 2026).

title: Allowance for 100% Blind
benefit_summary: Monthly pension of Rs.2,000 for 100% blind persons aged 10 and above.
caveats: Family annual income must be within Rs.1,00,000.

title: The Meghalaya Victim Compensation Scheme, 2022
benefit_summary: Tiered victim compensation ranging from Rs.1,00,000 to Rs.10,00,000 depending on crime type (murder, rape, gang-rape, permanent disability, etc.) and victim's age.
caveats: Must report the crime to police/magistrate and cooperate through trial. Perpetrators/dependents excluded. Applied for via District Legal Services Authority within 2 months.

title: Perunthalaivar Kamarajar Breakfast Scheme (formerly Chief Minister Breakfast Scheme)
benefit_summary: Free daily breakfast (13 rotating menu items) for students in Classes 1-5 at Tamil Nadu government schools, Monday-Friday.
caveats: No application needed - automatically provided at school. Expansion to classes 6-8 announced for 17 Sept 2026 but NOT yet active as of July 2026. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Renamed to 'Perunthalaivar Kamarajar Breakfast Scheme' via G.O. (Ms) No. 20 dated 15 July 2026 -- underlying benefit (free daily breakfast, Classes 1-5) unchanged; retained the old name in the title for searchability.

title: Teelu Rauteli Special Pension Scheme
benefit_summary: Monthly financial assistance of Rs.1,200 for physically disabled (20-40%) women/men engaged in agriculture or agriculture-related business in Uttarakhand.
caveats: Not a widow/vulnerable-women scheme - specifically for disabled farmers of either gender.

title: Thalolam Scheme
benefit_summary: Initial financial assistance of Rs.50,000 (per child, per illness) for free treatment of children under 18 from BPL families suffering chronic/fatal diseases (kidney, cardiovascular, cerebral palsy, thalassemia, etc.) at listed hospitals.
caveats: Rs.50,000 is an initial ceiling only - a hospital committee can approve additional expenditure above it. No separate application needed; assessed by hospital-based counselors.

title: Theka Shramik, Gharelu Mahila Kamgar Evan Hamaal Shramik Ke Bachcho Hetu Chhaatravrtti Yojana
benefit_summary: Annual scholarship (tiered Rs.500-Rs.5,000 by class/course, higher for girls) for up to 2 children of a registered Chhattisgarh sanitation/contract worker.
caveats: Parent must be a registered sanitation worker. Student must study continuously for at least 1 year or repay the scholarship; cannot receive two government scholarships simultaneously.

title: Theka Shramik Evan Hamaal Shramik Baahy Rogi Chikitsa Sahaayata Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.2,000 outpatient medical treatment assistance for registered contract/porter workers.
caveats: Ineligible if already benefiting from a parallel state scheme. [Fix 2026-07-23] Occupation constraint removed from structured matching -- this is specifically for contract/casual (Theka) workers, an occupation category our FLOW does not capture at this granularity.

title: Tripura Scheme For Incentive To Girl Child
benefit_summary: Rs.300/month incentive per girl child (max 2 per BPL family) paid to the mother, from birth (born on/after 1 June 2009) until the girl turns 15.
caveats: Paid preferably to the mother's bank/post office account.

title: Unemployment Allowance to Differently Abled Persons
benefit_summary: Monthly unemployment allowance for disabled job-seekers: Rs.600 (SSLC or below), Rs.750 (Higher Secondary), Rs.1,000 (Degree and above).
caveats: Must be registered live with the employment exchange for more than 1 year.

title: Unemployment Allowance to Disabled Persons
benefit_summary: Monthly unemployment allowance of Rs.500 for handicapped persons.
caveats: Requires 2+ years' registration in the Special Employment Exchange and 3+ years' UT Chandigarh residency immediately before application.

title: Uttarakhand Dwarf Pension Scheme
benefit_summary: Monthly financial assistance of Rs.1,200 for persons under 4 feet in height (dwarfism).
caveats: No income limit.

title: Unemployment Allowance
benefit_summary: Monthly unemployment allowance of Rs.2,500 for educated unemployed youth registered 2+ years with an Employment/Self-Employment Guidance Center, 12th pass minimum.
caveats: Only one family member can receive the allowance even if multiple qualify. Disqualified if any family member holds a government job above Class-IV/Group-D.

title: Unemployment Assistance Scheme - Tamil Nadu
benefit_summary: Monthly unemployment assistance tiered by qualification: Rs.200 (SSLC fail) to Rs.600 (Graduate) for general candidates; Rs.600-1,000 for differently-abled candidates (no age/income limit for this group).
caveats: General candidates: registered 5+ years with Employment Exchange, age cap 40 (45 for SC/ST). Differently-abled: registered 1+ year, no age or income limit. A higher-amount replacement scheme has been announced but not yet launched as of mid-2026.

title: Tejaswini-the Radiant
benefit_summary: Interest-free Mudra loan up to Rs.5 lakh for women's self-employment ventures, with Mission Youth subsidy of Rs.50,000 (or 10% of project cost) plus interest subsidy up to Rs.0.60 lakh.
caveats: Must be registered with Mission Youth J&K and District Employment & Counseling Center, min. 10th standard, not a loan defaulter. One-time benefit per woman. No family income criteria.

title: Uttar Pradesh Mukhyamantri Bal Seva Yojana (Genearal)
benefit_summary: Monthly financial assistance of Rs.2,500 for orphaned/destitute children under 18 (or 18-23 pursuing higher education after losing parents), max 2 children/family.
caveats: Income limit waived if both parents have died. COVID-orphan sub-category under the same umbrella gets Rs.4,000/month instead.

title: Uttar Pradesh Old Age Pension Scheme
benefit_summary: Monthly old-age pension, recently raised from Rs.1,000 to Rs.1,500.
caveats: Income limit Rs.46,080/year (rural) or Rs.56,460/year (urban) - urban figure used as general threshold.

title: Udyogini Scheme
benefit_summary: Business loan (Rs.1-3 lakh unit cost) with subsidy: 50% for SC/ST women (income<=Rs.2 lakh), 30% (max Rs.90,000) for general/special category women, plus EDP training.
caveats: No income limit for widowed or disabled women. Must not have defaulted on a prior loan.

title: Vikaas-Day Care Scheme For Person with Disability Children
benefit_summary: Day-care facility (min. 6 hrs/day) with vocational/interpersonal skill training and parental counseling for persons with Autism, Cerebral Palsy, Mental Retardation, or Multiple Disabilities.
caveats: Beneficiary must not be simultaneously enrolled under Samarth or Gharaunda scheme. Optional transport allowance available.

title: Vahli Dikri Yojana
benefit_summary: Staged financial assistance for up to two girl children born after 2 Aug 2019: Rs.4,000 (Class 1), Rs.6,000 (Class 9), Rs.1,00,000 (age 18, for higher education/marriage).
caveats: Income limit is Rs.2,00,000/year - a previous data error stated it as Rs.6,00,000 (3x too high).

title: Unemployed Youth Employment Generation Programme
benefit_summary: Subsidy up to 25% of project cost (max Rs.2.5 lakh) for setting up manufacturing (loan up to Rs.15 lakh)/service/trading (loan up to Rs.5 lakh) enterprises.
caveats: Age cap extends to 45 for SC/ST/MBC/BC/Minorities/Ex-servicemen/Differently-abled/Transgender applicants. Minimum 8th standard pass; EDP training mandatory; applicant contributes 10% (general) or 5% (special category) of project cost.

title: Vidyasiri-food And Accommodation Scholarship Scheme
benefit_summary: Monthly stipend of Rs.1,500 for 10 months (Rs.15,000/year) for food and accommodation, for backward-class post-matric students not in a government-funded hostel.
caveats: Family income limits vary by category (roughly Rs.1-2 lakh); Rs.2 lakh used as upper bound.

title: Vermicompost Ikai
benefit_summary: Subsidy of 50% of installation cost (max Rs.50,000) for a pucca vermicompost unit (30x8x2.5 ft), or max Rs.8,000 for a smaller HDPE vermi-bed unit.
caveats: Requires minimum 0.4 hectares of own land under horticultural crops plus available livestock/water.

title: Vidya Scheme
benefit_summary: Rs.10,000 fixed deposit for girl students entering Class VI, maturing when the student completes Class XII/turns 18; no premature withdrawal.
caveats: One-time benefit contingent on passing Class V and completing Class XII.

title: Vasantrao Naik Merit Awards To The Vjnt Students Who Came First In State Or First In Board Of 10th And 12th Standard Examination
benefit_summary: Merit award of Rs.1,00,000 (1st in state) or Rs.51,000 (1st in board) plus trophy/certificate, for VJNT-category students topping the 10th/12th board exams.
caveats: Restricted to VJNT (Vimukta Jati Nomadic Tribes) category students - this caste category is not one of the four standard tags (general/OBC/SC/ST).

title: Viswakarma Pension Scheme
benefit_summary: Monthly pension of Rs.1,100 for members of the traditional Viswakarma community (carpenters, goldsmiths, Moosari) aged 60+.

title: Vishist Coaching Scheme (GBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Reimbursement of registration fee and coaching/tuition fees for children of registered construction workers pursuing Chartered Accountancy or competitive government exams (GPSC/UPSC/etc).
caveats: Application must be made within 6 months of admission each academic year.

title: Vijayamritham Scheme - Cash Award For Meritorious Children With Disabilities
benefit_summary: One-time cash award of Rs.8,000 (Degree/equivalent, 10 students/district) or Rs.10,000 (PG/Professional, 5 students/district) plus certificate/memento, for meritorious disabled students (60%+ Arts/80%+ Science/60%+ PG marks).
caveats: Must have passed in the first attempt from a Kerala institution.

title: Vidyakiranam Scheme-Educational Assistance To Children Of Disabled Parents
benefit_summary: Tiered monthly scholarship (10 months/year) for children of disabled (40%+) BPL parents: Rs.300 (Std 1-5), Rs.500 (Std 6-10), Rs.750 (+1/+2/ITI), Rs.1,000 (Degree/PG).
caveats: Parent's disability (not applicant's) must be 40%+. Awarded once per class; 25 children/district.

title: Vidyajyothi Scheme- Financial Aid For Uniforms And Study Materials To PH Students
benefit_summary: Financial aid for study materials (Rs.1,000-3,000, by class) and uniforms (Rs.1,500, classes 9-12) for disabled (40%+) students from class 9 to Post-Graduation.
caveats: No income limit but BPL students given preference.

title: Vayomadhuram Scheme For Providing Glucometer To Senior Citizens
benefit_summary: Free glucometer for elderly (60+) BPL diabetic persons, 1,000 per district.
caveats: Requires doctor's certification of diabetes; priority to older applicants if oversubscribed.

title: Viranarayan Singh Shram Ann Yojana
benefit_summary: Subsidized hot meals (cooked rice, dal, vegetable/khichdi, pickle) at Rs.5 per meal for registered unorganized workers at food distribution centers.
caveats: No application needed - visit nearest food distribution center.

title: Vishesh Shiksha Sahaayata Yojana
benefit_summary: Special registration card enabling first two children of a deceased registered construction worker to access the Naunihal Scholarship, Meritorious Students Education Incentive, and Technical Education schemes (no fixed cash amount itself).
caveats: Worker must have died within 1 year of registration. Only first two eligible children qualify, and only if no other registered construction worker remains in the family.

title: Varnam Scheme For Transgender Students Pursuing Distance Education Courses
benefit_summary: Up to Rs.24,000/year for transgender students pursuing Degree/Diploma/PG via distance education, for 3 years (UG) or 2 years (PG).

title: Vivah Sahayata Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.30,000 financial assistance for the marriage of up to two children/female members of a registered construction worker's family.
caveats: Worker must have contributed continuously for 5 years. Bride must be 18+, groom 21+.

title: Vivah Sahayata Yojana - Madhya Pradesh
benefit_summary: Marriage assistance totaling approx. Rs.50,000-55,000: Rs.11,000 cash, Rs.38,000 worth of household goods, plus Rs.6,000 to mass-marriage organizers (if applicable).
caveats: Applicant's establishment must be covered under MP Labour Welfare Fund Act with regular contributions; worker must have 1+ year of employment there. Likely a duplicate of the mkvymp (Kanya Vivah/Nikah Yojana) scheme - recommend deduplicating.

title: Sabooj Sathi
benefit_summary: Free bicycle for students in classes 9-12 at government/government-aided schools who live 2km+ from school and don't already own a bicycle.
caveats: Requires 60%+ attendance in the last academic year. Purely in-kind benefit, no cash equivalent.

title: West Bengal Student Credit Card Scheme
benefit_summary: Education loan up to Rs.10,00,000 at 4% simple interest (after subvention) for secondary through postgraduate/professional studies, including competitive exam coaching.
caveats: No collateral beyond parent/guardian co-obligation. 15-year repayment including moratorium. Requires 10 years' WB residency (self-declared).

title: Sishu Sathi
benefit_summary: Free pediatric cardiac surgery (plus medicine, stay, and travel for child + 1 guardian) for children aged 0-18 with heart disease, at listed hospitals.
caveats: No income criteria; capacity ~3,000 children/year.

title: West Bengal Freeship Scheme
benefit_summary: Tuition fee waiver for merit-ranked undergraduate students in Engineering/Technology/Pharmacy/Architecture at self-financing private institutions.
caveats: Mutually exclusive with SVMCM and AICTE-TFW scholarships - cannot claim both. Covers tuition fee only, other fees remain payable.

title: Kanyashree Prakalpa
benefit_summary: Annual scholarship of Rs.1,000 for unmarried girls in classes 8-12 (K1), plus a one-time grant of Rs.25,000 at age 18-19 if still unmarried (K2, requires separate Form K2 application).
caveats: Income ceiling is Rs.1,20,000/year (not the Rs.2.5 lakh used for other WB schemes). Waived for orphans, 40%+ disabled girls, and juvenile justice home residents. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] K1 annual scholarship corrected from Rs.750/year to Rs.1,000/year (current rate since the 2018-19 Kanyashree financial year) -- confirmed via Wikipedia and three West Bengal district government sites. K2's Rs.25,000 one-time grant is unaffected.

title: Rupashree Prakalpa
benefit_summary: One-time financial assistance of Rs.25,000 to the bride's own bank account for her first marriage.
caveats: Bride must be 18+, unmarried, groom 21+; must be WB-born or resident 5+ years (or parents WB residents). Apply 3 months before to 1 year after the marriage date.

title: Widow Pension - Uttar Pradesh
benefit_summary: Monthly widow pension, recently raised from Rs.1,000 to Rs.1,500.

title: Widow Pension-West Bengal
benefit_summary: Monthly widow pension, currently Rs.1,000 (a rate increase to Rs.1,500-2,000 has been announced but not formally notified as of July 2026).
caveats: Family income limit is Rs.1,000/month (Rs.12,000/year) - this is the income ceiling, not the pension amount. Must be WB resident 10+ years; excludes professional beggars/mendicants. Now administered via the Jai Bangla portal.

title: Widow / Destitute Women Pension Scheme - Punjab
benefit_summary: Monthly pension of Rs.1,500 for widow, destitute, or unmarried women with no sustainable income.
caveats: Widow/destitute women must be under 58; unmarried women must be over 30.

title: Young Interns Program
benefit_summary: Internship stipend of Rs.30,000/month plus Rs.2,500/month mobility/connectivity support, for postgraduates or professional-degree holders (60%+ marks) placed in government departments.
caveats: Requires own laptop and internet connectivity.

title: Young Innovators Program
benefit_summary: Financial/institutional support up to Rs.5,00,000 for youth innovation projects in art, skills, crafts, literature, research, or science.
caveats: One-time benefit per innovation. Requires minimum 10th standard pass (relaxable).

title: Yuvasree Prakalpa
benefit_summary: Monthly unemployment assistance of Rs.1,500, plus job-search support via Employment Bank, skill training, and placement assistance.
caveats: Must be registered as a job-seeker with the Employment Bank, class 8 pass minimum, and not already receiving another self-employment scheme benefit. Only one family member eligible.

title: YSR Cheyutha
benefit_summary: Financial assistance of Rs.75,000 paid in four phases over four years for women aged 45-60 from BC/SC/ST/Minority communities.
caveats: Income ceiling Rs.10,000/month (rural) or Rs.12,000/month (urban) - urban figure used. Excludes families with government employees/pensioners, a four-wheeler (except taxis/tractors/autos), >300 units/month electricity, or income-tax payers. Excludes women already covered under YSR Pension Kanuka.

title: YSR Jala Kala
benefit_summary: Free borewell drilling (min. yield 1,000 GPH) plus recharge pit/water harvesting structure construction, for farmers without an existing or with a failed borewell.

title: Nethanna Bharosa (formerly YSR Nethanna Nestham)
benefit_summary: Rs.25,000/year cash assistance per eligible weaver family (~1.43 lakh families), plus 200 free electricity units/month (handloom) or 500 units/month (powerloom), 5% GST reimbursement, weavers' thrift fund, and new market-linkage initiatives -- since the August 2025 rollout of 'Nethanna Bharosa', succeeding the earlier YSR Nethanna Nestham (Rs.24,000/year).
caveats: One benefit per weaver family regardless of number of looms owned. Must be registered with the Handloom Association and present in the departmental database - beneficiaries need not apply separately. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Renamed/updated: as of National Handloom Day (7 August 2025), the AP government replaced YSR Nethanna Nestham (Rs.24,000/year) with Nethanna Bharosa (Rs.25,000/year plus added electricity/GST/thrift-fund benefits).

title: YSR Pension Kanuka
benefit_summary: Monthly pension (renamed 'NTR Bharosa'): Rs.2,250-3,000 for old-age/widow/weavers/toddy-tappers/fishermen/single women/cobblers/PLHIV categories (now increased to ~Rs.3,000), Rs.3,000+ for disabled persons, Rs.10,000 for CKDU/dialysis patients.
caveats: Common eligibility: income <=Rs.10,000/month (rural)/Rs.12,000/month (urban), land <3 acres wet/10 acres dry, no government employee/pensioner in family, no four-wheeler, <300 units/month electricity. Normally one pension per family (exceptions for 80%+ disability, dialysis, PLHIV).

title: YSR Rythu Bharosa
benefit_summary: Financial assistance of Rs.13,500/year (renamed 'Annadata Sukhibhava', now Rs.20,000/year) to landholder farmer families, paid in 3 installments; landless tenant farmers from SC/ST/BC/Minority communities also eligible.
caveats: Landholder benefit is regardless of holding size; landless-tenant benefit is restricted to SC/ST/BC/Minority categories and requires a minimum lease size.

title: Auto Driver Sevalo (formerly YSR Vahana Mitra / AP Vahana Mitra)
benefit_summary: Annual financial assistance (renamed 'Auto Driver Sevalo' via G.O. Ms. No. 33, ~13 Sept 2025) of Rs.15,000 (increased from Rs.10,000) for self-owned auto-rickshaw/taxi/maxi-cab driver-owners, for insurance/fitness/repair expenses.
caveats: One benefit per family. Excludes government employees/pensioners, GSTN holders, income-tax payers, families with >3 acres wet/10 acres dry land, >1000 sq.ft. municipal property, or >300 units/month electricity. [Audit fix 2026-07-23] Updated rename chain: the scheme was renamed again in 2025 to 'Auto Driver Sevalo' (not 'AP Vahana Mitra', which was itself an earlier rename) -- the Rs.15,000/year benefit amount is unchanged and correct.

title: Gruha Jyothi Scheme
benefit_summary: Up to 200 units/month free electricity for domestic households whose average FY2022-23 consumption was <=200 units.
caveats: Both APL and BPL households eligible.

title: Gruha Lakshmi Scheme
benefit_summary: Rs.2,000/month direct cash transfer to the female head of household (as per ration card).
caveats: Income-tax payers and government employees generally excluded.

title: Anna Bhagya Scheme
benefit_summary: 10kg free rice/person/month for BPL/AAY/Priority Household ration cardholders (5kg NFSA at Rs.1/kg + 5kg free state top-up).
caveats: Priority Household (PHH) cardholders also qualify, similar to BPL.

title: Yuva Nidhi Scheme
benefit_summary: Monthly unemployment allowance of Rs.3,000 (graduates) or Rs.1,500 (diploma holders), for up to 2 years.
caveats: Must be unemployed for 6+ months after completing graduation/diploma.

title: Shakti Scheme
benefit_summary: Free travel for all women on Karnataka government (non-luxury) buses.
caveats: No registration required.

title: Mahila Samridhi Yojana - Delhi
benefit_summary: Rs.2,500/month direct cash transfer to eligible women, plus Rs.500 LPG subsidy, free cylinder on Holi/Diwali, and Rs.21,000 + 6 nutrition kits for pregnant women.
caveats: Recently renamed "Delhi Lakshmi Yojana" in some sources (may still appear as "Mahila Samman Yojana" elsewhere) — same scheme. Requires 5 years Delhi voter registration/residency, BPL/EWS status, no income-tax payer in family, and no four-wheeler ownership. High query-volume expected.

title: Subhadra Yojana - Odisha
benefit_summary: Rs.10,000/year (Rs.5,000 x 2 installments) to women aged 21-60, totaling Rs.50,000 over the scheme's 5-year run (2024-25 to 2028-29).
caveats: Detailed eligibility criteria beyond age/gender not available in source data.

title: Indira Gandhi Pyari Behna Samman Nidhi Yojana - Himachal Pradesh
benefit_summary: Rs.1,500/month direct cash transfer to eligible women aged 18+.
caveats: Detailed eligibility criteria beyond age/gender not available in source data.

title: Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme -Tamil Nadu
benefit_summary: Rs.1,200/month cash pension for destitute BPL residents 60+ (raised from Rs.1,000 in Aug 2023), plus a free saree/dhoti at Pongal and Deepavali and free Anganwadi rice.
caveats: Once approved, no annual reapplication needed, though information may need periodic updating. A separate, higher disability-pension rate applies if the applicant has a qualifying disability instead (see igndpstn) — do not confuse the two.

title: Lakshmi Bai Samajik Suraksha Pension Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.1,100/month cash pension for widows (corrected from the outdated Rs.300 figure in the raw scraped data) via direct bank transfer.
caveats: CORRECTED per verification note: the scraped Benefits section says Rs.300/month, which is outdated — Rs.1,100/month is the current confirmed rate. Distinct from the separate Mukhyamantri Vridhjan Pension Yojana (old-age pension, not widow-specific, Rs.400-500/month) — do not confuse the two.

title: Mukhyamantri Kalyakani Pension Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.600/month cash pension for widows in Madhya Pradesh via direct bank transfer.
caveats: Must not be an income-tax payer or a government employee/officer, and the family must not already be receiving another Kalyani pension. Name must be registered on the Samagra portal. A proposed hike to Rs.1,500 has been reported but not confirmed as implemented — Rs.600 is the current confirmed rate.

title: Samagra Samajik Suraksha Vridh Ashram Mai Nivaasarat Ant-vasi Pension Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.600/month cash pension for destitute elderly (60+) residing in a Vridhashram (old-age home) in Madhya Pradesh.
caveats: Applicant must be residing in a Vridhashram and registered on the Samagra portal (Samagra e-KYC mandatory). A proposed hike to Rs.1,500 has been reported but not confirmed as implemented.

title: Mukhyamantri Kanya Abhibhawak Pension Scheme
benefit_summary: Rs.600/month cash pension to parent couples aged 60+ in Madhya Pradesh who have only daughters (no living sons).
caveats: Applies to couples where all children are daughters and those daughters are married; neither parent may be an income-tax payer. No explicit rupee income cap, but the income-tax-payer exclusion acts as a soft means test.

title: Delhi Pension Scheme To Women In Distress (Widow Pension)
benefit_summary: Rs.2,500/month cash assistance for widowed, divorced, separated, abandoned, deserted, or destitute women aged 18+ in Delhi, via ECS/PFMS bank transfer.
caveats: Also covers separated/abandoned/deserted/destitute women, not just widows/divorcees (our marital-status categories only capture the closest two). Requires 5 years Delhi residency, a single-operated Aadhaar-linked Delhi bank account, and must not already receive any other government pension/financial assistance.

title: Uttarakhand Widow Pension Scheme
benefit_summary: Rs.1,500/month cash pension for widows aged 18-60 in Uttarakhand.
caveats: Eligible if BPL category OR monthly income up to Rs.4,000 (~Rs.48,000/year). A son/grandson over 20 does not disqualify the applicant if that son/grandson is also BPL.

title: Disability Pension for the Construction Workers
benefit_summary: Rs.3,000/month disability pension plus a one-time Rs.1,00,000 ex-gratia payment for Delhi BOCW-registered construction workers permanently disabled by paralysis, leprosy, TB, accident, etc.
caveats: Requires registration with the Delhi Building & Other Construction Workers Welfare Board, with at least 90 days of board-registered service in a given year before the disability.

title: Disability Pension (A.B.O.C.W.W.B)
benefit_summary: Rs.2,000/month base plus Rs.100/month per completed year of registered service, for Assam BOCW-registered workers permanently disabled by paralysis, leprosy, TB, accident, etc, plus a one-time ex-gratia up to Rs.3,00,000 depending on disability percentage.
caveats: Requires active registration/membership with the Assam Building & Other Construction Workers Welfare Board.

title: Vidhva Vivah Uphar Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.51,000 one-time cash incentive for widows in Rajasthan upon remarriage.
caveats: Must already be entitled to a widow pension under the applicable rules, must not have remarried previously, and must have lived in Rajasthan for at least 3 years before the remarriage.

title: Mukhya Mantri Hamari Betiyan Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.15,000/year base (up to Rs.1,00,000/year with hostel/coaching bills) for Class 11-12; Rs.25,000/year base (up to Rs.2,00,000/year with hostel/coaching bills) for graduate/postgraduate study — for the meritorious girl students selected in Class 10.
caveats: Merit-based, not means-tested: awarded to the top 1-2 Class 10 scorers (Rajasthan Board, govt school, 75%+ marks) per district across three tracks — general, BPL-family, and orphan. Only a small number of scholarships are awarded per district each year, not a general entitlement. Only 1 girl child per family is eligible.

title: Old Age Assistance
benefit_summary: Rs.2,000/month (age 60-69) or Rs.2,500/month (70+) old-age assistance in Delhi, plus an extra Rs.500/month for SC/ST/Minority beneficiaries.
caveats: Requires 5 years Delhi residency and a single-operated Aadhaar-linked Delhi bank account.

title: State Disability Pension - Delhi
benefit_summary: Rs.2,500/month disability pension for persons with 40%+ disability, age 0-60, in Delhi.
caveats: Disability must be certified by a Government Hospital Medical Board. Requires 5 years Delhi residency.

title: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar State Award To SC/ST/OBC/Minorities Students
benefit_summary: Rs.25,000 one-time merit award for the SC/ST/OBC/Minority topper in each discipline of a professional/technical degree course.
caveats: Merit-based (topper only, one award per discipline), not means-tested — no family income limit. Must have passed 10th and 12th from Delhi, and produce a caste certificate. Also open to Minority-category students beyond SC/ST/OBC.

title: Financial Assistance For The Marriage Of Daughters Of Poor Widows And Orphan Girls
benefit_summary: Rs.30,000 one-time assistance per daughter (up to 2 daughters) for the marriage of daughters of poor widows, or for orphan girls themselves, in Delhi.
caveats: Also covers guardians/Homes/Institutions/foster parents applying on behalf of an orphan girl, not just widowed mothers (our marital-status field only captures the widow applicant case). The daughter/orphan girl being married must be 18+.

title: Delhi Arogya Kosh
benefit_summary: Up to Rs.5,00,000 financial assistance for treatment of any illness at a government hospital in Delhi.
caveats: Not health insurance — approved funds are paid directly to the treating government hospital, not to the patient. Requires 3 years continuous Delhi residency.

title: Delhi Arogya Nidhi
benefit_summary: Up to Rs.1,50,000 financial assistance for treatment of disease at a government hospital in Delhi, for National Food Security Card holders.
caveats: Requires a National Food Security Card (mapped here to AAY/BPL ration card types) and 3 years continuous Delhi residency. Treatment must be at a Delhi government hospital.

title: Higher Education And Skill Development Guarantee Scheme
benefit_summary: Collateral-free education loan up to Rs.10,00,000 for Delhi students pursuing a diploma/degree/skill course after Class 10 or 12, government-guaranteed against default.
caveats: This is a guaranteed bank LOAN, not a grant — it must be repaid, with a 1-year moratorium after course completion. Universal: open regardless of income or social background. Requires Class 10 and 12 completed in Delhi.

title: Accidental Death Assistance for the Construction Workers
benefit_summary: Rs.2,00,000 one-time payment to nominees/dependents when a Delhi BOCW-registered construction worker dies in a workplace accident.
caveats: Requires the deceased worker to have been registered with the Delhi Building & Other Construction Workers Welfare Board with at least 90 days of service in the relevant year. Paid to nominees/dependents, not the worker.

title: Funeral Assistance for the Construction Workers
benefit_summary: Rs.10,000 one-time funeral assistance to nominees/dependents on the death of a Delhi BOCW-registered construction worker.
caveats: Requires the deceased worker to have been a registered board member. Paid to nominees/dependents, not the worker.

title: Financial Assistance For Purchase Of Stationery To SC/ST/OBC/Minorities Students
benefit_summary: Rs.1,000/year (Class I-VIII) or Rs.2,000/year (Class IX-XII) stationery assistance for SC/ST/OBC/Minority students in Delhi.
caveats: Also open to Minority-category students, not just SC/ST/OBC (broader than our caste-category field captures). Requires a caste/minority certificate from the concerned Delhi district office.

title: Merit Cum Means Linked Financial Assistance Scheme
benefit_summary: 100% tuition-fee reimbursement for undergraduate students at Delhi public universities whose family holds a National Food Security Scheme card, or 50% reimbursement for other means-tested meritorious students.
caveats: Two-tier structure: full reimbursement is specifically for NFSA-cardholder families (mapped here to AAY/BPL ration types); other students get the 50% tier subject to income and academic performance criteria not otherwise captured here.

title: Bus Traveling Facility For Visually Impaired/Bus Concession
benefit_summary: Free DTC bus travel for persons with 40%+ visual impairment, plus a 50% fare concession for the escort/attendant of those with 100% blindness.
caveats: Requires a card from the Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM) before applying at the depot.

title: Education Assistance for the Construction Workers
benefit_summary: Monthly education assistance for children of Delhi BOCW-registered construction workers, tiered by class/course level: Rs.500 (Class 1-8) up to Rs.10,000/month (Engineering/Medical/MBA-level technical courses).
caveats: Requires board registration; assistance is for the worker's children (up to 2 nominated children), not the worker. Full tiers: Rs.500 (Class 1-8), Rs.700 (9-10), Rs.1,000 (11-12), Rs.3,000 (Graduation/LLB-3yr), Rs.4,000 (ITI/LLB-5yr), Rs.5,000 (Polytechnic Diploma), Rs.10,000 (Engineering/Medical/MBA). Distance-education students get 75% of the regular-study rate.

title: Ex-gratia Payment for the Construction Workers
benefit_summary: Rs.1,00,000 one-time ex-gratia payment for permanent disability of a Delhi BOCW-registered construction worker.
caveats: Requires board registration.

title: Financial Assistance for Miscarriage for the Construction Workers
benefit_summary: Rs.3,000 financial assistance for miscarriage, for registered women members (or wives of male members) of the Delhi BOCW board.
caveats: Requires board registration.

title: Financial Assistance for Marriage for the Construction Workers
benefit_summary: Marriage assistance for Delhi BOCW-registered construction workers: Rs.51,000 (female registered member or daughter of a member) or Rs.35,000 (male registered member or son of a member).
caveats: Requires board registration.

title: Grant for the Purchase of Work Related Tools for the Construction Workers
benefit_summary: Rs.5,000 grant for the purchase of work-related tools, once every 5 years, for Delhi BOCW-registered construction workers.
caveats: Requires board registration.

title: Jai Bhim Mukhyamantri Pratibha Vikas Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.2,500/month stipend for SC students in Delhi attending competitive-exam coaching classes, with the government covering 75% of the admissible coaching fee (student pays the remaining 25%).
caveats: Requires passing/studying Class 10 and 12 from a Delhi school.

title: Loan for the Purchase of Work Tool for the Construction Workers
benefit_summary: Loan up to Rs.20,000 for the purchase of work-related tools, for Delhi BOCW-registered construction workers, repayable in up to 60 installments.
caveats: This is a LOAN, not a grant — must be repaid.

title: Medical Assistance for the Construction Workers
benefit_summary: Rs.2,000 for the first 5 days of hospitalization plus Rs.200/day thereafter (max Rs.10,000 total), for Delhi BOCW-registered construction workers.
caveats: Requires board registration.

title: Mukhyamantri Vidyarthi Pratibha Yojna
benefit_summary: Rs.5,000/year (Class 9-10) or Rs.10,000/year (Class 11-12) merit scholarship for Delhi students.
caveats: Requires minimum 50% marks (Class 9-10) or 60% marks (Class 11-12). Family income must be within the EWS limit (Rs.8 lakh/year), subject to government-notified exclusions.

title: Natural Death Assistance for the Construction Workers
benefit_summary: Rs.1,00,000 to nominees/dependents on the natural death of a Delhi BOCW-registered construction worker.
caveats: Requires board registration. Paid to nominees/dependents, not the worker.

title: Pension Benefit for the Construction Workers
benefit_summary: Rs.3,000/month pension after age 60, plus Rs.300/year increase for every year of registered membership beyond 5 years, for Delhi BOCW workers.
caveats: Requires board registration.

title: Purchase/Construction of House for the Construction Workers
benefit_summary: Rs.3,00,000 (10 years left to age 60) or Rs.5,00,000 (15 years left to age 60) advance for house purchase/construction, for Delhi BOCW-registered workers.
caveats: Requires board registration and a minimum years-remaining-to-retirement threshold.

title: Yatra Pass in DTC non AC Buses for the Construction Workers
benefit_summary: A Rs.2,400/3-month non-AC DTC bus pass for Delhi BOCW-registered construction workers.
caveats: Requires board registration and at least 5 years of registered membership.

title: Maternity Assistance for the Construction Workers
benefit_summary: Rs.30,000 maternity assistance to registered women members (or wives of male members) of the Delhi BOCW board, for up to 2 children.
caveats: Requires board registration.

title: Old Age And Destitute Pension
benefit_summary: Tiered monthly pension in Puducherry: Rs.1,500 (destitute/deserted/unmarried women below 60), Rs.2,000 (age 60-79), Rs.3,000 (age 80+).
caveats: Covers old-age persons of either gender (55+), widows (18+), women deserted for 7+ consecutive years, unmarried women (40+), and transgender persons (21+) — eligibility age varies by category, our schema only captures a single min_age which cannot represent all five tracks. A Sept 2025 CM announcement referenced a possible Rs.3,500 rate for an expanded cohort, not yet confirmed as universal.

title: Specialized Treatment & Medical Assistance Scheme (PBAOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Up to Rs.2,00,000 medical assistance for specialized treatment (TB, lung disease, etc.) at hospitals tied up with Government General Hospitals in Puducherry/Karaikal/Mahe/Yanam, for registered construction workers.
caveats: Requires board registration, age 18-60.

title: Medical Assistance Scheme (PBAOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.500 for the first 5 days of hospitalization plus Rs.50/day thereafter, up to Rs.1,500/month, for Puducherry-registered construction workers.
caveats: Requires board registration, age 18-60.

title: Higher Educational Finance Assistance Scheme (PBAOCWWB)
benefit_summary: One-time or annual higher-education assistance for wards of Puducherry BOCW-registered construction workers, tiered by qualification: from Rs.2,000/year (UG/Diploma) up to Rs.1,50,000 one-time (MD Clinical Pharmacology), including Rs.1,00,000 (MBBS/BDS/MD/MS) and Rs.75,000 (M.Tech/M.E).
caveats: Applicant must be the ward (child) of a board-registered construction worker, not the worker themselves.

title: Cash Benefit Scheme Scheme (PBAOCWWB)
benefit_summary: One-time merit cash prize for wards of Puducherry BOCW-registered construction workers ranking 1st-3rd in HSC/equivalent: Rs.1,00,000/80,000/60,000 (state-level) or Rs.60,000/40,000/20,000 (region-level).
caveats: Merit-based (top 3 ranks only), not a general entitlement. Applicant must be the ward of a board-registered worker.

title: Skill Development Scheme (PBAOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Free skill development training for Puducherry BOCW-registered construction workers.
caveats: Requires board registration, age 18-60. In-kind training, not cash.

title: Relief under Natural Calamity / Pandemic Period (PBAOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.2,000 one-time relief via Direct Benefit Transfer for Puducherry BOCW-registered construction workers during a government-notified natural calamity or pandemic period.
caveats: Ad-hoc/event-dependent — only disbursed when a specific calamity/pandemic period is notified by the government, not a standing entitlement.

title: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar Memorial Award to Scheduled Caste Students
benefit_summary: Rs.15,000 one-time cash award for the SC topper (boy and girl) with 55%+ aggregate marks in the Higher Secondary exam, in each Puducherry region.
caveats: Merit-based (topper per region only), not a general entitlement. Requires 5+ years residency in Puducherry.

title: Grant Of Retention Scholarship to Scheduled Caste Girl Students
benefit_summary: Rs.1,000/year (Rs.100/month for 10 months) retention scholarship for SC girl students in Class I-V in Puducherry.
caveats: Requires 5+ years residency in Puducherry (or native status).

title: Mrityu Ki Dasha Me Antyeshti Evam Anugrah Sahayata Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.6,000 funeral assistance plus tiered ex-gratia (Rs.2,00,000 normal death, Rs.4,00,000 accidental death, Rs.2,00,000 permanent disability) for registered construction workers in Madhya Pradesh.
caveats: Worker must have been registered at least 6 months before death. Paid to spouse, sons, or unmarried dependent daughters, not the worker. Application must be submitted within 6 months of death.

title: Gaon Ki Beti
benefit_summary: Rs.5,000/year (Rs.500/month for 10 months) for rural girl students in Madhya Pradesh who scored 60%+ marks in Class 12.
caveats: Must be living in a rural area. A higher Rs.7,500/year tier for technical/professional courses has been reported but not confirmed as part of the base scheme.

title: Nihshaktajan Vivaah Protsaahan Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.2,00,000 marriage incentive if one spouse has 40%+ disability, or Rs.1,00,000 if both spouses are disabled, in Madhya Pradesh.
caveats: Male applicants must be 21+, female applicants 18+. Marriage must be solemnized by religious/social custom or a competent court. Paid after marriage, so eligibility is really about the marriage event rather than ongoing marital status.

title: Antim Sanskar Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.6,000 lump-sum funeral assistance for registered construction workers in Madhya Pradesh.
caveats: Cannot be combined with last-rites assistance from any other department.

title: 6 Varsh Se Adhik Aayu Ke Bahuviklang Aur Mansik Roop Se Aviksit Nisaktjan Ke Liye Sahayata Anudan Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.600/month cash benefit for severely multiple-disabled or mentally undeveloped persons above age 6 in Madhya Pradesh.
caveats: Name must be registered on the Samagra portal and verified on the Sparsh portal.

title: Divyang Shiksha Protsahan Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.600/month financial assistance for the education of disabled students aged 6-18 in Madhya Pradesh.
caveats: Name must be registered on the Samagra portal and verified on the Sparsh portal.

title: Shaikshanik Chatravriti Yojana
benefit_summary: Tiered scholarship amounts (varying by class/course, Class 5 through postgraduate/professional courses) for children of factory/institution workers covered under the MP Labour Welfare Fund Act 1982.
caveats: Only 2 children per family are eligible. Parent must work in an MP factory/institution under the Labour Welfare Fund Act — children of managerial-capacity officers/employees are excluded.

title: Usha Kiran Yojana
benefit_summary: Protection and support services against domestic violence for women of all ages and children under 18 in Madhya Pradesh.
caveats: In-kind protective/support service, not a fixed cash benefit.

title: Udita Yojana
benefit_summary: In-kind distribution of sanitary napkins plus nutrition/health education for adolescent girls and women aged 18-49, via Anganwadi centers in Madhya Pradesh.
caveats: In-kind service (napkins + education), not a cash benefit.

title: Vikramaditya Yojna
benefit_summary: Up to Rs.2,500/year financial assistance for General-category students in Madhya Pradesh who scored 60%+ in Class 12.
caveats: Income cap is Rs.1,20,000/year for higher education or Rs.54,000/year for graduation-level study (our schema only captures a single max_income; used the higher of the two here).

title: Mukhyamantri Aawasiye Bhu-Adhikaar Yojana
benefit_summary: Free residential plot (in-kind, not cash) for Madhya Pradesh households where more than one family shares a single house with no separate plot of their own.
caveats: Requires a PDS ration-card eligibility slip, and no family member may be an income-tax payer or government employee. Family must hold less than 5 acres of land.

title: Post Matric and Top Class Scholarship
benefit_summary: Rs.1,200/month subsistence allowance (hostellers) or Rs.550-650/month (non-hostel) plus mandatory-fee reimbursement, for disabled graduate/postgraduate students in Madhya Pradesh.
caveats: Income cap is Rs.2,50,000/year for the Post-Matric tier or Rs.6,00,000/year for the Top Class tier (used the higher figure here). Minor unresolved discrepancy on the exact non-hostel rate (Rs.550 per the central ministry vs Rs.650 as scraped).

title: Chief Minister's Comprehensive Health Insurance Scheme
benefit_summary: Up to Rs.5,00,000/year cashless family-floater health insurance at empanelled government and private hospitals in Tamil Nadu.
caveats: Applicant name must be present on the family (ration) card.

title: Chief Minister's Comprehensive Health Insurance Scheme - Tamil Nadu
benefit_summary: Up to Rs.5,00,000/year cashless family-floater health insurance (same CMCHIS coverage as the general scheme), for families with a differently-abled member in Tamil Nadu.
caveats: Likely the same underlying CMCHIS coverage as the general scheme (cmchis), just messaged for disability households — may not be a materially distinct benefit.

title: Assistance for Marriage
benefit_summary: Rs.2,000 marriage assistance for a differently-abled person (or for their child, if the child holds a disability identity card) in Tamil Nadu.
caveats: Applicant (or their child) must be at the legal marriage age.

title: Establishing Aavin Parlour for Differently Abled Persons
benefit_summary: Livelihood opportunity to operate an Aavin dairy-products parlour (milk, butter, curd, etc.), reserved for differently-abled persons in Tamil Nadu.
caveats: This is a business/livelihood opportunity (a parlour to run), not a cash grant.

title: E.V.R. Maniammaiyar Ninaivu Marriage Assistance Scheme for Daughter's of Poor Widows: Scheme-I
benefit_summary: Rs.25,000 marriage assistance plus a 1-sovereign (8g) 22-carat gold coin, paid to a widow for her daughter's (18+) marriage in Tamil Nadu.
caveats: Limited to one daughter per widow. A separate, higher-tier version (Scheme-II, Rs.50,000) exists for degree-holder brides.

title: E.V.R. Maniammaiyar Ninaivu Marriage Assistance Scheme for Daughter's of Poor Widows: Scheme-II
