benefit_summary: Rs.50,000 marriage assistance plus a 1-sovereign (8g) 22-carat gold coin, paid to a widow for her degree-holder daughter's (18+) marriage in Tamil Nadu.
caveats: Bride must be a degree holder (or other specified higher-education category). Can be paid directly to the bride if the widowed mother has since died.

title: Financial Assistance to Meet the Funeral Expenses of Differently Abled Person
benefit_summary: Rs.2,000 funeral expense assistance for the legal heir of a deceased differently-abled person in Tamil Nadu.
caveats: The deceased must have been a registered member of the Welfare Board for the Differently Abled. Paid to the legal heir, not the deceased.

title: Marriage Assistance
benefit_summary: Rs.10,000 marriage assistance for a Tamil Nadu Labour Welfare Fund-contributing employee, or their son/daughter, upon marriage.
caveats: Requires Labour Welfare Fund contribution and monthly basic pay + DA not exceeding Rs.25,000 (annualized here to Rs.3,00,000).

title: Migrants Employment Generation Programme
benefit_summary: 25% project-cost subsidy (up to Rs.2.5 lakh) for a self-employment project, for Tamil Nadu residents who returned to the state due to COVID-19 on or after 1 Jan 2020.
caveats: Age relaxation beyond 45 applies for women, minorities, BC/MBC/SC/ST, ex-servicemen, transgender persons, and differently-abled applicants.

title: Personal Accident Relief for Differently Abled Persons
benefit_summary: Tiered personal-accident relief for differently-abled persons in Tamil Nadu: Rs.1,00,000 for death, loss of both legs/hands, or sight in both eyes; lower tiers for partial loss (one hand, one leg, or one eye).
caveats: Triggered by a new accident causing death or disability, not pre-existing disability status alone.

title: Readers Allowance to Visually Impaired Persons
benefit_summary: Annual reader's allowance for visually impaired students in Tamil Nadu: Rs.3,000 (Class 9-10), Rs.5,000 (Degree), or Rs.6,000 (Postgraduate/Professional courses).
caveats: Must be enrolled in Class 9 or above at a recognized institution.

title: Sathiyavanimuthu Ammaiyar Ninaivu Free Supply of Sewing Machine Scheme
benefit_summary: Free sewing machine and accessories for destitute women, widows, deserted women, or differently-abled men/women in Tamil Nadu who know tailoring.
caveats: Applicant must already know tailoring. Also open to differently-abled men, not just the categories captured in our gender/marital-status fields.

title: Scheme of Personal Assistance Allowance to Differently Abled Persons with High Support Need
benefit_summary: Rs.1,000/month personal assistance allowance for differently-abled persons with high support needs in Tamil Nadu.
caveats: "High support need" is a specific severity classification beyond a general disability percentage, not otherwise captured in our schema.

title: Vishvakarma Durghatana Mrtyu par Antyeshti Evan Anugrah Raashi Bhugataan Yojana
benefit_summary: Tiered ex-gratia for registered Chhattisgarh construction workers: Rs.25,000 + Rs.5,000 funeral (normal death), Rs.1,00,000 + Rs.5,000 funeral (accidental death), Rs.75,000 (permanent disability).
caveats: Not payable if death was due to suicide or intoxicating-substance consumption. Registered under Section 12 of the BOCW Act.

title: Bhagini Prasuti Sahayata Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.10,000 maternity assistance (Rs.3,000/3,000/4,000 across pregnancy trimesters and post-birth) for registered women construction workers in Chhattisgarh.
caveats: Limited to the first 2 children. Registration as a construction worker required 1 year in advance. May also be known as "Minimata Mahatari Jatan Yojana" under a possible rebrand.

title: Asangathit Karmakar Ke Bachcho Hetu Chhatravriti Yojana
benefit_summary: Tiered annual scholarship for the first two children of registered unorganized workers in Chhattisgarh: Rs.500 (boys)/Rs.750 (girls) at Class 1-5, rising to Rs.4,000 (boys)/Rs.5,000 (girls) at postgraduate-professional/PhD level — girls receive a higher rate than boys at every tier.
caveats: Parent must be registered with the Social Security Board. Contract workers, domestic female workers, porters, and sanitation workers' children are NOT eligible for this specific scholarship (they have separate schemes).

title: BPL Scholarship for College Students
benefit_summary: Rs.300/month (undergraduate) or Rs.500/month (postgraduate) scholarship for BPL college students in Chhattisgarh government colleges, with a renewal lump-sum option (Rs.3,000 UG / Rs.5,000 PG).
caveats: Guardian must hold a BPL card. Must be studying at a Chhattisgarh government college under the Higher Education Department, and not already receiving a similar scholarship.

title: Durghatana Mein Chikitsa Sahaayata Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.20,000 or actual treatment cost (whichever is less) medical assistance for a registered construction worker in Chhattisgarh after an accident.
caveats: Requires 90 days of registered board service.

title: E-Rikshaw Sahayta Yojna
benefit_summary: Rs.30,000 grant (plus a Rs.10,000 worker contribution) toward an e-rickshaw, for registered auto/cycle-rickshaw drivers in Chhattisgarh.
caveats: Requires RTO registration and a valid driving/health certificate.

title: E-Thela Sahaayata Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.30,000 grant (plus a Rs.10,000 worker contribution) toward an e-cart (thela), for registered hand-cart workers in Chhattisgarh.
caveats: Requires RTO health certificate for commercial vehicle drivers.

title: Futkar Sabji, Phal-Phool Vikreta Hetu Taraju, Baat Evan Tokari Sahaayata Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.700 grant for scales, weights, and 2 baskets for a registered street vendor of vegetables/fruits/flowers in Chhattisgarh.
caveats: Must not have received a similar benefit from another scheme.

title: Kachara Binane Vaale Hetu Suraksha Upakaran Sahaayata Yojana
benefit_summary: Safety equipment (gloves, shoes, raincoat) or an equivalent cash amount for registered waste-pickers in Chhattisgarh.
caveats: Must not be receiving assistance from another parallel state scheme.

title: Mukhyamantri Asangathit Karmakar Cycle Sahayata Yojana
benefit_summary: A free bicycle for a registered female unorganized worker in Chhattisgarh.
caveats: Must not be receiving benefits under another parallel scheme for the same purpose.

title: Medhavi Chhatr/Chhatra Shiksha Protsahan Yojana
benefit_summary: Tiered annual merit incentive for children of registered Chhattisgarh factory workers: Rs.5,000-5,500 (Class 10/12) up to Rs.12,000-12,500 (vocational/professional courses); Rs.1,00,000 for the state top-10 merit rankers in Class 10/12 board exams; and full fee/hostel/food reimbursement plus Rs.2,000/year stationery for admission into Government ITI/IIT/Engineering/Medical/Law/Dental/Nursing courses.
caveats: Requires 75%+ marks and 90 days of registered factory-worker service by the parent.

title: Mahila Kamgar Kaushal Unnayan Evan Theka Shramik, Hamaal Tatha Ghareloo Mahila Kamgaar Parivar Sashaktikaran Yojana
benefit_summary: Free skill-development training (beautician, nutrition, cooking, tailoring, nursing, etc.) plus a training stipend and family-empowerment activities for women domestic/contract/porter workers in Chhattisgarh.
caveats: Must not be receiving a comparable benefit from another state scheme.

title: Mukhyamantri Raut, Charavaaha Evan Doodh Duhane Vaale Saayakal Sahaayata Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.3,000 (or CSIDC-fixed rate, whichever lower) for a bicycle, for registered cattle-herders/milkers in Chhattisgarh.
caveats: Must not be receiving benefits under another parallel scheme.

title: Readymade Kichan Sahaayata Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.30,000 grant (plus a Rs.10,000 worker contribution) toward a ready-made food cart/kitchen setup, for registered tea/snack/food vendors in Chhattisgarh.
caveats: Requires RTO health certificate for commercial vehicle drivers.

title: Saraswati Cycle Yojana
benefit_summary: A free bicycle for BPL or SC/ST Class 9 girl students in Chhattisgarh.
caveats: Only Class 9 girl students qualify. Eligible via BPL status OR SC/ST category (not necessarily both).

title: Goa Welfare / Pension Scheme For Seafarers
benefit_summary: Rs.2,500/month pension for retired Goan seamen (60+) or seamen invalidated from sea service on medical grounds, or widows of deceased seamen.
caveats: Capped at 3,000 total beneficiaries statewide — a first-come, capped scheme, not a universal entitlement. Reduced/disqualified if already receiving another named pension (Dayanand Social Security Scheme / Griha Aadhaar).

title: Disability Pension (GBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.300/month plus an ex-gratia up to Rs.10,000 (by disability percentage), for registered Goa construction workers.
caveats: Requires 90 days of registered board service in the year.

title: Funeral Assistance (GBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.5,000 funeral assistance for a registered Goa construction worker.
caveats: Deceased must have completed 90 days of registered board service.

title: Financial Assistance for Education (GBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: A board-determined education assistance amount for the children of registered Goa construction workers.
caveats: Applicant is the worker's ward (child), not the worker. Worker must have 90 days of registered board service.

title: Family Pension (GBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: 50% of the deceased pensioner's pension, or Rs.200/month (whichever higher), for the spouse of a deceased registered Goa construction-worker pensioner.
caveats: Applicant must be the surviving spouse of a deceased board-registered pensioner.

title: Pension Benefit (GBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.300/month pension plus Rs.10/year increase for every year of registered service beyond 5 years, for Goa construction workers.
caveats: Requires at least 1 year of registered "Building Worker" membership with the board's Fund.

title: Loan for the Purchase of Tools (GBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: A Rs.5,000 loan for tool purchase, for registered Goa construction workers.
caveats: This is a LOAN, not a grant — must be repaid. Requires 90 days of registered board service.

title: Financial Assistance to the Fish Vendors Registered with the Directorate of Fisheries to Purchase the Accessories Required for Fish Vending
benefit_summary: 50% subsidy (up to Rs.10,000, general category) or 60% (up to Rs.12,000, SC/ST/woman category) on a Rs.20,000 fish-vending accessories unit in Goa.
caveats: Must be a fish vendor registered with the Goa Department of Fisheries.

title: Financial Assistance for Purchase of Stake Net and its Accessories
benefit_summary: 50% subsidy (up to Rs.30,000, general) or 60% (up to Rs.36,000, SC/ST/woman) on a Rs.60,000 stake-net unit in Goa.
caveats: Must be a traditional fisherman by birth or profession, resident of Goa.

title: Financial Assistance for Purchase of Barrier Net and its Accessories
benefit_summary: 50% subsidy (up to Rs.30,000, general) or 60% (up to Rs.36,000, SC/ST/woman) on a Rs.60,000 barrier-net unit in Goa.
caveats: Must be a traditional fisherman by birth or profession, resident of Goa.

title: Financial Assistance to Purchase Outboard Motor of 2HP to 5 HP for Fitting to the Fishing Canoe
benefit_summary: 50% subsidy (up to Rs.30,000, general) or 60% (up to Rs.36,000, SC/ST/woman) on a Rs.60,000 outboard-motor unit in Goa.
caveats: Fishing canoe must be registered with the Goa Department of Captain of Ports.

title: Natural Calamity Relief to Fishermen of State
benefit_summary: Rs.5,00,000 for loss of life or total disability while fishing at sea/river in Goa; plus separate tiered relief for canoe/vessel/net loss or damage ranging from Rs.50,000 (nets) up to Rs.10,00,000 (6-8 cylinder fishing vessel), based on an authorized surveyor's assessment.
caveats: Requires contribution to the Fishermen Corpus Relief Fund and vessel registration with the Department of Fisheries.

title: Interest Subsidy on Loans for Agriculture and Allied Activities
benefit_summary: Loan up to Rs.5,00,000 with a 4% interest subsidy on short-term loans (differential subsidy on long-term loans) for farmers and inland-fisheries operators in Goa.
caveats: This is a LOAN interest subsidy, not a cash grant. Requires ownership/lease of a qualifying agriculture or fisheries operation with the necessary license.

title: Construction Injury Assistance - GBOCWWB (2026 expansion)
benefit_summary: Rs.25,000 one-time construction injury assistance for registered GBOCWWB workers, announced May 2026.
caveats: Very newly announced (May 1, 2026) with only one local news source available — no detailed eligibility criteria published yet beyond board registration.

title: Mukyamantri Samuhik Vivah Evam Anudan Yojna
benefit_summary: Rs.25,000 mass-marriage grant in Rajasthan: Rs.21,000 to the bride, Rs.4,000 to the marriage organizer, via IFMS.
caveats: Bride must be 18+, groom 21+, both unmarried, marriage registered per rules. Our min_age field reflects the bride's threshold (the lower of the two).

title: Devnarayan Gurukul Yojana
benefit_summary: Free admission to a prestigious private residential school (Class 6) for Class-5-passed students in Rajasthan from specific nomadic/backward communities (Banjara, Gadia-Lohar, Gujar, Raika, Gadaria, etc.), via entrance test.
caveats: Limited to specific named sub-communities (broader than a simple ST/OBC label), max 2 children per parent, parent must not be an income-tax payer, selection via competitive entrance test with limited seats.

title: Devnarayan Pre-Matric Scholarship Scheme
benefit_summary: Rs.50/month (boys) or Rs.100/month (girls) for Class 6-8; Rs.60/month (boys) or Rs.120/month (girls) for Class 9-10 — for specific OBC nomadic communities in Rajasthan.
caveats: Limited to specific named sub-communities (Banjara, Gadia-Lohar, Gujar, Raika, Gadariya, etc.), not all OBC. Must not already receive another central/state/public scholarship.

title: Devnarayan Post Matric Scholarship Scheme
benefit_summary: Reimbursement of maintenance allowance and course fees for post-matric students from specific OBC nomadic communities in Rajasthan.
caveats: Limited to specific named sub-communities (Banjara, Gadia-Lohar, Gujar, Raika, Gadariya, etc.), not all OBC.

title: Economic Help To Tribal Girls For Higher Education (Class 11 & 12)
benefit_summary: Rs.3,500 one-time (paid in July) for ST girl students in Class 11-12 at government schools in Rajasthan.
caveats: Parent/guardian/husband must not be an income-tax payer. NOT eligible if living in a government-run hostel (separate hostel benefits apply instead). Requires a Bhamashah card.

title: Economic Help To Tribal Girls For Higher Education (College Level)
benefit_summary: Rs.5,000/year (Rs.500/month for 10 months) for ST girl students in college-level general education in Rajasthan.
caveats: Parent/guardian/husband must not be an income-tax payer. NOT eligible if living in a government-run hostel. No gap allowed in continuous study after board exam. Requires a Bhamashah card.

title: Financial Help On Death Of Family Head
benefit_summary: Rs.10,000 financial assistance to the wife of a deceased family head, for the Sahariya tribe (a Scheduled Tribe community) in Rajasthan.
caveats: Limited specifically to the Sahariya tribe (Baran district), not all Scheduled Tribes broadly.

title: Gargi Puruskar Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.3,000/year cash award (paid on Basant Panchami) for girl students in Class 11-12 in Rajasthan who scored 75%+ in Class 10.
caveats: No income, occupation, or caste restriction — purely merit-based on the Class 10 score.

title: Indira Mahila Shakti Prashikshan Evam Kaushal Sanvardhan Yojna -RS-CIT
benefit_summary: Free basic computer training (MS Word/Excel/PowerPoint, email) for women and girls aged 16-40 in Rajasthan, via RKCL.
caveats: Priority given to widowed/divorced/abandoned women or violence survivors. Trainees must have passed Class 10 from a government school; Anganwadi workers applying must be graduates.

title: Indira Mahila Shakti Prashikshan Evam Koshal Sanvardhan Yojana (RS-CSEP)
benefit_summary: Free spoken English and personality development training for women and girls aged 16-45 in Rajasthan, via RKCL.
caveats: Requires Class 12 pass. Priority given to widowed/divorced/abandoned women or violence survivors.

title: Incentive To Saharia Students For B.Ed
benefit_summary: Rs.30,000/year (2 years total, Rs.26,000 fees/books + Rs.32,000 across both years for housing/food + Rs.2,000/year clothing) for Sahariya-tribe students in regular B.Ed training in Rajasthan.
caveats: Limited specifically to the Sahariya tribe (a Scheduled Tribe community in Baran district), not all STs. Parent/guardian must not be an income-tax payer. NOT eligible if living in a government-run hostel.

title: Incentive To Girls
benefit_summary: Rs.15,000/year (Class 11-12 agriculture stream) up to Rs.40,000/year (PhD, max 3 years) for girl students in agriculture-related education in Rajasthan.
caveats: Must not have failed the previous year or leave the course mid-session. Full tiers: Rs.15,000 (11th-12th agriculture), Rs.25,000 (agri graduate/4-5yr course), Rs.25,000 (M.Sc Agriculture), Rs.40,000 (PhD).

title: NEET/JEE Coaching For Tribal Students
benefit_summary: Reimbursement of coaching institute fees up to Rs.55,000, plus Rs.1,000/month for food/accommodation and a one-time Rs.5,000 for stationery, for tribal students in Rajasthan preparing for NEET/JEE.
caveats: Must have passed Class 12 in the science stream with first-class standing.

title: Nirman Shramik Avm Unke Aashrit Bacchon Dwara Bhartiya Rajasthan Prashasnik Seva Hetu Aayojit Pratibhabhik Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.1,00,000 (passing IAS preliminary exam) or Rs.50,000 (passing RAS preliminary exam) for registered construction workers or their dependent children in Rajasthan.
caveats: Applicant must not already be in government service. Only payable once per exam type, and only for Rajasthan-specific administrative exams (not other states).

title: Nirman Shramik Jeevan Bhavishya Suraksha Yojana
benefit_summary: Premium reimbursement for registered Rajasthan construction workers: 100% of the Rs.12/year PMSBY premium, 50% (Rs.165) of the Rs.330/year PMJJBY premium, and 50% of the Atal Pension Yojana contribution (for a Rs.1,000/month pension).
caveats: Requires a savings bank account and consent for automatic premium/contribution deduction.

title: Nirman Shramikon ke Liye Vyavsayik Rin Par Byaj ki Punarbharan Yojana
benefit_summary: Interest reimbursement on business loans up to Rs.5,00,000, for registered Rajasthan construction workers.
caveats: Loan must be used for the applicant's own business — not for a shop/plot/vehicle/household goods purchase. Only one spouse in a registered couple can use this at a time.

title: Nirman Shramik Antrashtriya Khel Pratiyogiyo Hetu Protsahan Yojana
benefit_summary: International sports incentive for registered Rajasthan construction workers (or their unmarried children): Rs.2,00,000 (participation) up to Rs.11,00,000 (gold medal).
caveats: Not applicable to online gaming/betting competitions. Voided if the medal is stripped for doping or other violations. Full tiers: Rs.2,00,000 (participation), Rs.5,00,000 (bronze), Rs.8,00,000 (silver), Rs.11,00,000 (gold).

title: Nirman Shramik Siksha Kaushal Vikas Yojana
benefit_summary: Tiered annual scholarship for children/wife of registered Rajasthan construction workers: Rs.8,000/year (Class 6-8) up to Rs.23,000-25,000/year (Postgraduate/Professional), with disabled students getting a higher rate. Separate merit cash awards up to Rs.35,000 for professional postgraduates.
caveats: Max 2 children (or 1 child + wife) eligible per worker/couple; no limit for merit cash-award recipients. Wife must be under 35 for scholarship eligibility. Parent must be board-registered, not the student themselves.

title: Widow B.Ed Scheme-Rajasthan
benefit_summary: Rs.17,880 fee reimbursement for widowed or abandoned women taking regular B.Ed training in Rajasthan.
caveats: Must not have already obtained a B.Ed degree. Requires 75%+ attendance. Must not be receiving another scholarship/equivalent scheme.

title: Mukhyamantri Samuhik Vivah Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.1,00,000/couple mass-marriage grant in Uttar Pradesh (corrected from an outdated Rs.51,000 figure): Rs.60,000 to the bride's bank account, remainder for household goods and ceremony expenses.
caveats: Open to all communities. Requires at least 10 couples participating in the same mass-marriage ceremony — not an individual application.

title: Gambhir Bimari Sahayata Yojana
benefit_summary: No-cap medical reimbursement for registered UP construction workers (and dependent parents, spouse, daughter, or son under 21) for serious illnesses (heart, kidney, liver, cancer, HIV/AIDS, etc.) not covered under Ayushman Bharat/PMJAY.
caveats: Cannot be combined with Ayushman Bharat/Chief Minister Jan-Arogya Yojana benefits for the same treatment.

title: Awasiya Vidyala Yojana
benefit_summary: Free residential education (accommodation, clothing, food included) for children (age 6-14) of registered construction workers in Uttar Pradesh.
caveats: Parent must be a registered construction worker.

title: Chetan Chauhan Labor Sports Promotion Scheme
benefit_summary: One-time sports incentive for children of Factories-Act-registered UP workers (or the worker herself, if a female player): Rs.25,000 (district level) up to Rs.1,00,000 (international level).
caveats: Worker's monthly salary (basic+DA) must not exceed Rs.15,000 (annualized here to Rs.3,00,000), with 6+ months continuous service. Limited to 2 children per worker. Only for selections on/after 23 March 2021.

title: Computer Training Scheme
benefit_summary: Reimbursement up to Rs.15,000 ("O" level, 1 month) or Rs.3,500 (CCC, 3 months) for computer training courses for unemployed UP youth.
caveats: Applicant must have passed Intermediate (10+2).

title: Financial Assistance to Former Sports Person of UP
benefit_summary: Monthly pension for former sportspersons in Uttar Pradesh facing hardship: Rs.2,000 (state-level) up to Rs.20,000 (Arjuna/Dronacharya/Khel Ratna/Padma awardees).
caveats: Applicant must be old, weak, or facing hardship with monthly income from all sources not exceeding Rs.10,000 (annualized here to Rs.1,20,000).

title: Fee Reimbursement Scheme
benefit_summary: Annual fee reimbursement for OBC students in Uttar Pradesh, tiered by course group: Rs.50,000 (Group 1: degree/professional courses) down to Rs.10,000 (Group 4: non-degree courses).
caveats: Selection is merit-based (cut-off percentage from the previous year, subject to budget availability), not a guaranteed entitlement for every eligible applicant.

title: Laxman Award / Rani Laxmi Bai Award Scheme
benefit_summary: Rs.3,11,000 cash prize plus citation, bronze statue, and scroll for elite UP sportspersons (Laxman Award for men, Rani Laxmi Bai Award for women) across 31 recognized sports.
caveats: Highly selective — requires 3 consecutive years on the state senior team plus National Games/Championship medals, and often international-competition participation. Not a general entitlement.

title: Laxman Award / Rani Laxmi Bai Award Scheme- Differently-abled and Posthumously
benefit_summary: Rs.3,11,000 cash prize plus citation, bronze statue, and scroll — the differently-abled/posthumous variant of the Laxman/Rani Laxmi Bai Award for elite UP sportspersons.
caveats: Highly selective, same rigorous sporting-achievement criteria as the general award. Not a general entitlement.

title: Kaushal Vikas Yojana
benefit_summary: Reimbursement of training-institute fees, textbooks, and stationery, plus a minimum-wage-equivalent stipend during training, for registered UP construction workers.
caveats: Age 18-35 applies to the worker undergoing training themselves; a dependent wife/unmarried daughter has no age limit, dependent son must be under 21. Must pass an assessment test after training. Only the registered worker (not dependents) gets the wage-equivalent stipend.

title: Marriage Grant Scheme
benefit_summary: Rs.20,000 marriage assistance for daughters of poor OBC families (excluding OBC-minorities) in Uttar Pradesh.
caveats: Income cap is Rs.56,460/year (urban) or Rs.46,080/year (rural) — used the higher urban figure here. Groom must be 21+. Limited to 2 daughters per family. Widows applying after husband's death get priority and don't need a caste certificate.

title: Marriage Incentive Reward Scheme
benefit_summary: Marriage incentive in Uttar Pradesh where at least one spouse has 40%+ disability: Rs.15,000 (disabled groom) / Rs.20,000 (disabled bride) / Rs.35,000 (both disabled).
caveats: Both must be UP residents (5+ years), ages 18-45 (bride) and 21-45 (groom), neither an income-tax payer or criminally convicted. Marriage must be registered. This is a post-marriage incentive — eligibility is about the marriage event, not ongoing status.

title: Nirmaan Kamgar Mrtyu Va Divyangta Sahayta Yojana
benefit_summary: Tiered death/disability benefits for registered UP construction workers: Rs.5,25,000 total (accidental death) / Rs.2,25,000 (natural death) / Rs.1,00,000 (death at workplace) / Rs.4,00,000 (100% permanent disability) / Rs.3,00,000 (50-99% disability) / Rs.2,00,000 (26-49% disability), each including a lump-sum funeral component and the remainder paid out over several years.
caveats: Paid to dependents (parents, spouse, daughter, or son under 21), not the deceased worker. Excludes deaths by suicide; deaths by murder, snakebite, lightning, childbirth, and natural calamities count as "normal" deaths for benefit purposes.

title: Raja Harishachandra Shramik Mratak Antyeshti Sahayata Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.10,000 funeral assistance for the family of a Factories-Act-registered worker in Uttar Pradesh who dies in service.
caveats: Worker's monthly salary (basic+DA) must not exceed Rs.15,000 (annualized here to Rs.1,80,000). Must apply within 1 year of death. Paid to spouse/dependent child, or parents if the worker was unmarried.

title: Panchyat Kalyan Kosh
benefit_summary: Welfare fund payout for elected Panchayat representatives in Uttar Pradesh, tiered by role: Rs.10 lakh (Pradhan/area or district Panchayat President) down to Rs.2 lakh (Gram Panchayat member).
caveats: Limited to elected Panchayat officials specifically — not a general citizen entitlement. No age bar.

title: Maternity Benefit Scheme (APB&OCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.1,000 maternity cash assistance for registered women construction workers in Arunachal Pradesh, payable for up to 2 adult daughters of the registered worker.
caveats: Membership must be active at time of application. Not entitled if the woman worker has remarried.

title: Baristha Bunakar Sahayata Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.2,000/month (weavers, assistants, handicraft artisans) or Rs.2,500/month (above 80), under the renamed Mukhyamantri Baristha Bunakar Sahayata Yojana in Odisha — corrected from an outdated Rs.500/700 figure.
caveats: Requires 20+ years in the weaving profession, or being the widow of a weaver of 10+ years. Must hold a valid weaver ID card and not receive another government pension. Only 1 family member can claim per household.

title: KALIA Scholarship
benefit_summary: Full tuition/fee reimbursement plus Rs.1,200/month (degree/PG/PhD) or Rs.1,000/month (diploma/ITI/polytechnic) hostel/mess allowance for children of KALIA-scheme-eligible farmers in Odisha, admitted to a government professional/technical course on merit.
caveats: Parent must be a verified KALIA beneficiary (cultivator or landless agricultural household support component). Only for government institutions, one professional course only, cannot combine with another scholarship.

title: Baristha Nagarika Tirtha Yatra Yojana
benefit_summary: Fully government-funded pilgrimage trip (transport, food, accommodation, travel insurance) for poor senior citizens aged 60-75 in Odisha, once in a lifetime.
caveats: Requires an Antyodaya/Annapurna/NFSA ration card, widow/old-age pension, or MGNREGS job card as proof of need. Must be medically fit to travel. Married couples can apply jointly even if one spouse is under 60. An attendant (18+) may accompany applicants over 70, paying 50% of travel cost.

title: Biju Patnaik Bravery Award
benefit_summary: Rs.1,00,000 cash award plus silver medal and scroll for an act of bravery performed in Odisha (or by an Odisha resident elsewhere), during the preceding calendar year.
caveats: Highly selective, discretionary award (not conferred every year if no suitable act is found), given once per lifetime. Not a general entitlement — depends on a qualifying act of bravery, which our schema cannot gate on.

title: "Reactivation Of Fisheries Cooperative Societies" Component of the "Mukhyamantri Maschyajibi Kalyan Yojana" Scheme
benefit_summary: A one-time Rs.2,00,000 revolving fund for an active, registered Primary Fisherman Cooperative Society in Odisha.
caveats: This is a grant to a fishing COOPERATIVE SOCIETY (a legal entity, 1+ year registered, meeting governance/audit requirements), not an individual fisherman — an individual applicant would need to be applying on behalf of/through such a society.

title: Revolving Funds For WSHGS Involved In Fisheries Activities- Mukhyamantri Maschyajibi Kalyan Yojana
benefit_summary: A one-time Rs.10,000 assistance per Women Self-Help Group (WSHG) engaged in fisheries activities (pisciculture, fish farming/marketing, etc.) in Odisha.
caveats: This is a grant to a WOMEN'S SELF-HELP GROUP (a collective entity), not to an individual applicant directly.

title: "Scholarship to Meritorious Student of Fishers Family" Component of the "Mukhyamantri Maschyajibi Kalyan Yojana"
benefit_summary: Rs.20,000 (80%+ marks), Rs.15,000 (70-80%), or Rs.10,000 (60-70%) scholarship for meritorious students from a fisherman family in Odisha, based on HSC exam results.
caveats: Cannot combine with another scholarship (ST&SC Development Dept, KALIA, etc.).

title: MMKY-Financial Assistance for New Boat, Engine, and Net
benefit_summary: Back-ended subsidy for a fishing boat/engine/net unit in Odisha (max Rs.10 lakh unit cost): 40% subsidy (up to Rs.4 lakh, general category) or 60% (up to Rs.6 lakh, women/SC/ST/PWD/transgender).
caveats: Limited to 1 unit per beneficiary. Boat procurement is mandatory; engine/net are optional. Family (not just individual) must not have received similar assistance in the last 3-5 years.

title: "Input Assistance to Farmers for Taking up Fish Farming in Farm Ponds" Component of the "Mukhyamantri Maschyajibi Kalyan Yojana" Scheme
benefit_summary: One-time input assistance (seed/feed/other inputs) for fish farming in an existing farm pond in Odisha: 40% subsidy (general) or 60% (SC/ST/women/transgender/PwD) of a unit cost that scales with pond size (Rs.4,000-16,000 depending on pond dimensions).
caveats: The farm pond must already exist (excavated under a prior government scheme like Watershed Development/MGNREGA), with minimum 5 ft depth and 5-month water retention. Limited to 0.5 acres per beneficiary; considered at the family level.

title: MMKY-New Tank Excavation Under Brackish Water Aquaculture
benefit_summary: Subsidy for new brackish-water pond excavation in Odisha (up to 2 hectares): 40% (general) or 60% (SC/ST/women/transgender/PwD) of a Rs.14 lakh/hectare model cost (capital + first-crop input).
caveats: Requires land free of encumbrances (owned or 7+ year lease, with documentary proof). Preference given to cluster-mode applicants. Considered at the family level.

title: Aapki Beti Hamari Beti
benefit_summary: Rs.21,000 one-time grant for a girl child in Haryana (1st daughter of SC/BPL families, or 2nd daughter of any family, born on/after 22 Jan 2015); Rs.5,000/year for 5 years for pre-2015 second daughters under the earlier Ladli scheme.
caveats: At least one parent must be a Haryana resident/domicile. Twin/multiple daughters each qualify separately. This is a child-benefit scheme — an adult FLOW user would be answering on behalf of/about their daughter, not themselves.

title: Assistance On Death Of The Unregistered Worker (HBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.2,50,000 to the legal heir/dependent of an UNREGISTERED construction worker who dies in a workplace accident in Haryana.
caveats: Unlike other HBOCWWB schemes, this specifically covers workers who were NOT registered with the board.

title: Bicycle Scheme (HBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.3,000 for bicycle purchase, for registered Haryana construction workers.
caveats: Requires 1+ year regular board membership. Usable once every 3 years.

title: Death Assistance For Registered Worker (HBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.2,00,000 to the nominee/legal heir on the natural death of a registered Haryana construction worker.
caveats: Requires active regular board membership.

title: Disability Assistance For Registered Worker (HBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Tiered lump-sum disability assistance for registered Haryana construction workers: Rs.1,50,000 (up to 50% disability), Rs.2,00,000 (51-75%), Rs.3,00,000 (76%+).
caveats: Must apply within 1 year of becoming disabled; disability % certified by a Government Medical Board.

title: Disability Pension For Registered Worker (HBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.3,000/month disability pension for registered Haryana construction workers with 70-100% permanent disability from an infectious disease or workplace accident.
caveats: Requires 3+ years regular membership. Cannot combine with another Haryana government disability pension. Requires annual life certificate + contribution deposit each November.

title: Financial Assistance To Disabled Children (HBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.2,000/month for a registered Haryana construction worker's dependent child with 50%+ physical/mental disability.
caveats: Requires 1+ year regular membership. Child must be unmarried, have no income of their own, and be listed on the family ration card. Annual life-certificate renewal required.

title: Financial Assistance For Education Of Children Of Registered Worker (HBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Tiered annual education assistance for children of registered Haryana construction workers: Rs.8,000 (Class 1-8) up to Rs.20,000 (Postgraduate), plus a one-time Class-10-merit incentive up to Rs.51,000 (90%+ marks) and up to Rs.1,20,000 hostel expenses.
caveats: Parent must have 1+ year regular board membership. Student must study in Haryana and not be self-employed/employed. Limited to 3 children per worker (3 daughters, or 2 sons).

title: Grant For Purchase Of Tools (HBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.8,000 grant for tool-kit purchase, for registered Haryana construction workers.
caveats: Requires 1+ year regular membership. Usable once every 3 years.

title: Rajiv Gandhi Family Insurance Scheme
benefit_summary: Tiered accident insurance for Haryana residents aged 18-60: Rs.1,00,000 (death/permanent total disability), Rs.50,000 (loss of 2 limbs/eyes or 1 limb+1 eye), Rs.25,000 (loss of 1 limb or 1 eye).
caveats: Requires being on the voter list or holding a ration card. Not available to government/semi-government employees. Still active under its original name as of this check (not renamed, unlike some similarly-named schemes in other states).

title: Financial Assistance on Death/Disablement of Beneficiary (CBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.50,000 ex-gratia to a widow on the death of a registered Chandigarh construction worker (any cause); Rs.25,000 (full disability) or Rs.15,000 (50% disability) to the worker themselves due to accident.
caveats: Requires the worker to not have already claimed similar assistance from another government body.

title: Financial Assistance for the Purchase of Sewing Machine (CBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.3,500 one-time assistance for the spouse of a registered Chandigarh construction worker to purchase a sewing machine.
caveats: Requires 6+ months of board membership and original purchase bills. Available once per lifetime; must apply within 1 year.

title: Financial Assistance to Physically/Mentally Disabled Children of Beneficiary (CBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.1,000/month for a registered Chandigarh construction worker's child with 40%+ disability, for as long as the child lives.
caveats: Requires 6+ months board membership. Limited to 2 children per worker.

title: Interest Free Loan (CBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Interest-free loan for a registered Chandigarh construction worker to buy a motorcycle/scooter (Rs.25,000), fridge/TV (Rs.15,000), cooler (Rs.7,500), fan (Rs.2,500), or bicycle (Rs.4,000), repaid via salary deduction over 10-20 installments.
caveats: This is a LOAN, not a grant. Requires 6+ months board membership, employer guarantee, and no default on a prior loan. One item at a time.

title: Kanyadaan Scheme (CBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.21,000 for a registered Chandigarh construction worker's daughter's marriage, or for the self-marriage of a female registered worker.
caveats: Requires 6+ months board membership, marriage registration certificate, and applying within 3 months of marriage. Limited to 2 daughters per worker.

title: Scholarship to the Ward of Beneficiary (CBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Tiered scholarship for children of registered Chandigarh construction workers: Rs.3,000-5,000 (Class 10/12, by marks) or Rs.7,500 one-time (Graduation, 60%+ marks).
caveats: Parent must have 6+ months board membership. No scholarship if the student has a subject compartment/fail. Limited to 2 children per worker. National/international sports medalists get the scholarship regardless of marks. Must apply within 3 months of the mark sheet issue date.

title: Widow Pension (CBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.1,000/month pension for widows of registered male Chandigarh construction workers.
caveats: Deceased husband must have been a board member for 6+ months. Not available if covered under EPF. Must apply within 1 year of death.

title: Beti Hai Anmol Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.21,000 at birth plus tiered annual education assistance (Rs.450-2,250 school, Rs.5,000/year college), for the first 2 daughters of BPL families in Himachal Pradesh, born on/after 5 July 2010.
caveats: Limited to 2 girls per BPL family. Girl must not marry before age 18. A NEWER scheme (Rs.25,000 at birth + parental life insurance) applies instead for girls born on/after 1 April 2026 — this record's terms apply to the pre-2026-April cohort.

title: Mukhya Mantri Bal Suposhan Yojana
benefit_summary: Nutrition/health monitoring and treatment services (anemia/hypertension detection, malnutrition treatment, protein-rich food) for children, pregnant/lactating women, and their families in Himachal Pradesh.
caveats: In-kind health service, not a fixed cash benefit. Targets pregnant/lactating women and young children specifically — doesn't map cleanly to a general adult FLOW profile.

title: Mukhya Mantri Grihini Suvidha Yojana
benefit_summary: Free LPG gas connection (1 domestic cylinder + 2 additional) for BPL families in Himachal Pradesh without an existing LPG connection.
caveats: Not available if the family (or any member) already has an LPG connection, including under PM Ujjwala Yojana.

title: Mukhya Mantri Gyandeep Yojna
benefit_summary: 4% per annum interest subsidy on education loans up to Rs.10 lakh, for Himachal Pradesh students pursuing professional/technical/higher education.
caveats: Cannot combine with another education-loan interest subsidy scheme. Subsidy covers the course period plus up to 1 year moratorium.

title: Mukhyamantri Krishi Utpadan Sanrakshan Yojana
benefit_summary: Subsidy for crop-protection infrastructure for Himachal Pradesh farmers: 80-85% for solar fencing, up to 80% for anti-hail net structures (max 5,000 sq.m), 70% for greenhouse poly-sheet renovation.
caveats: Solar fencing gets the higher 85% rate only if 3+ farmers jointly install it (80% for individual installation). Priority given to small/marginal farmers.

title: Mukhya Mantri Shahri Ajeevika Guarantee Yojna
benefit_summary: 120 days/year of guaranteed unskilled/sanitation work in Urban Local Bodies at minimum wage, for Himachal Pradesh urban residents; Rs.75/day unemployment allowance if not given work within 15 days of registration.
caveats: Urban areas only (within an Urban Local Body's jurisdiction). Reported budget cut from Rs.100 crore to Rs.5 crore in a recent year — actual availability may be far more limited than the formal 120-day entitlement suggests.

title: Mukhya Mantri Vidyarthi Kalyan Yojana
benefit_summary: Annual scholarship for IRDP-family students (Class 9 to University) in Himachal Pradesh: Rs.300-600 (Class 9-10) up to Rs.2,400 (college/university hostellers).
caveats: Limited to Integrated Rural Development Programme (IRDP) family students, and only in government/government-aided institutions in Himachal Pradesh.

title: The Andaman & Nicobar Islands Widow Pension Scheme
benefit_summary: Rs.2,500/month widow pension in Andaman & Nicobar Islands.
caveats: Requires permanent residency or 10+ years residing in A&N. Household income cap Rs.4,000/month (~Rs.48,000/year). Not payable if receiving another government grant, or after remarriage/becoming financially independent.

title: Disability Assistance (ANBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Up to 25% of the compensation due under the Employees Compensation Act 1923, for a registered A&N construction worker disabled in a workplace accident.
caveats: Requires a disability-percentage certificate from a competent medical authority.

title: Death Benefit (ANBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.1,00,000 (natural death) or Rs.2,00,000 (accidental death) to nominees/dependents of a registered A&N construction worker; Rs.50,000 for accidental death of an UNREGISTERED construction worker (certified by the local Tehsildar).
caveats: Paid to nominees/dependents, not the worker. Registration is not required for the reduced Rs.50,000 unregistered-worker tier.

title: Educational Assistance (ANBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Monthly education allowance for children of registered A&N construction workers: Rs.300 (Class 1-5) up to Rs.2,000 (Postgraduate); full cost of study covered for meritorious MBBS/BE/professional students on a case-by-case basis.
caveats: Parent must have active board membership. Assistance is for the worker's children, not the worker.

title: Funeral Assistance (ANBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.5,000 funeral assistance to nominees/dependents of a deceased registered A&N construction worker.
caveats: Requires active board membership at time of death.

title: Marriage Assistance (ANBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.20,000 marriage assistance for a registered A&N construction worker's own marriage, or for up to 2 dependent children's marriages.
caveats: Limited to 2 children per worker.

title: Pension Benefit (ANBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.1,000/month pension for A&N construction workers aged 55+.
caveats: Requires 5+ years of continuous construction work and 5+ years of regular welfare-fund contributions.

title: Scheme for Grant of Additional Scholarship to the Students Belonging to Scheduled Tribes of Andaman and Nicobar Islands for Pursuing Higher Studies
benefit_summary: Rs.1,000/month (10 months/year) additional scholarship for Scheduled Tribe students of Andaman & Nicobar Islands pursuing higher studies after passing 10+2.
caveats: Limited to the specific STs notified for A&N Islands under Article 342(1). Class 11/12 students are NOT eligible (only post-10+2 higher/professional study).

title: Financial Assistance To Ex-Convicts
benefit_summary: Rs.15,000 one-time self-employment assistance for BPL ex-convicts in Kerala.
caveats: Selected through the After Care Association via the District Probation Officer.

title: Sruthitharangam ( Cochlear Implantation Scheme )
benefit_summary: Free cochlear implantation surgery for hearing-impaired children in Kerala, normally aged 0-3 (exceptions up to age 5 case-by-case).
caveats: Administered by Kerala Social Security Mission; children selected by regional/state technical screening committees. This is a benefit for a young CHILD, not the adult FLOW respondent themselves.

title: Abhayakiranam Scheme-Financial Assistance To Destitute Widows
benefit_summary: Rs.1,000/month paid to a close relative who shelters/protects a destitute widow (50+) in Kerala.
caveats: Not payable if the widow already receives a service/family pension, or benefits from Aswasakiranam/Samashwasam schemes. Payment goes to the caregiving relative, not the widow directly.

title: Assistance to Traditional Pottery Makers
benefit_summary: Rs.25,000 for traditional pottery makers in Kerala to upgrade their occupation and purchase machinery.
caveats: Must belong to a State Backward Community and currently practice traditional pottery-making.

title: Barbershop Renovation Grant
benefit_summary: 50% of modernization project cost (up to Rs.25,000) for traditional barbers in rural Kerala to renovate their shop.
caveats: Must belong to Other Backward Communities, have 10+ years as a working barber, and operate in a rural area. Preference given to BPL/disabled/multi-daughter applicants; capped at 1,000 beneficiaries statewide via a competitive scoring process — not a guaranteed entitlement even if eligible.

title: Educational Assistance To Children Of Prisoners
benefit_summary: Rs.500/month (Class 1-5) up to Rs.1,500/month (Degree/Professional course) for children of imprisoned parents in Kerala.
caveats: Normally requires BPL status, but APL families can qualify if BOTH parents are imprisoned, verified by a District Probation Officer inquiry.

title: Entrepreneurship Development by SC & ST Women in Science Technology Engineering Mathematics
benefit_summary: Research/entrepreneurship fellowship for SC/ST women in STEM in Kerala: Rs.35,000/month + 10% HRA (M.Sc/M.Tech) or Rs.45,000/month + HRA (PhD), within a ~Rs.20 lakh institutional grant over 1 year.
caveats: Requires a PhD, M.Sc (Basic/Natural Science), or M.Tech qualification, plus a host institution and mentor. Extremely limited — only 3-5 grants awarded per year statewide. Most of the Rs.20 lakh grant is institutional overhead/capital/operational cost, not personal income.

title: Border Areas Scholarship
benefit_summary: Rs.5,400/month (general degree) or Rs.7,800/month (technical/medical/professional/paramedical), plus Rs.20,000/year hostel allowance and a Rs.5,000-10,000/year maintenance allowance, for SC/ST students from Meghalaya's Indo-Bangladesh border villages.
caveats: Only for students from notified border-area villages (both parents' income must derive from the border area). Not for PhD/M.Phil or government employees. Can be combined with other scholarships.

title: Death Benefit (MBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.2,00,000 (natural death) or Rs.3,00,000 (accidental death) to nominees/dependents of a registered Meghalaya construction worker; Rs.2,00,000/Rs.5,00,000 respectively if not covered under any insurance scheme.
caveats: Paid to nominees/dependents, not the worker. Can be claimed alongside other insurance schemes (PMJJBY/PMSBY).

title: Educational Assistance (Scheme for the Pre-Matric and Post-Matric Scholarship to Children of Construction Workers Registered with the MBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Monthly stipend for children of registered Meghalaya construction workers: Rs.400 (Class V-VII) up to Rs.800 (Degree), plus Rs.200/month extra for blind students and a one-time book/uniform grant (Rs.400-1,600 by level).
caveats: Parent must have active board membership. Limited to 2 children per worker. Not payable if the child already receives assistance from another source.

title: Free Studentship
benefit_summary: Rs.1,105-2,235 (varies by class/stream) fee waiver/assistance for SC/ST/OBC students in Meghalaya, Class 11 through degree level.
caveats: Cannot combine with the central Post-Matric Scholarship for SC/ST or other government scholarships. Not for government/non-government employees or students repeating a class more than once.

title: Marriage Benefit (MBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Rs.5,000 for a registered Meghalaya construction worker's own marriage, or for each adult child's marriage.
caveats: Requires 3+ years continuous board membership. Own-marriage benefit usable only once per worker.

title: Rehabilitation Treatment For The Disabled
benefit_summary: Free medical treatment (surgery, therapy), assistive devices (hearing aids, wheelchairs, prosthetics), rehabilitation services, and skills training for persons with 40%+ disability in Meghalaya.
caveats: In-kind service, not a fixed cash amount. Requires a disability certificate from a registered medical practitioner.

title: Scholarship To 2 Years Pre-Service Student Teachers Undergoing D.El.Ed Programme At DIETs And CTTC Sohra
benefit_summary: Rs.5,000/month for 2 years (10 months/year) for students undergoing the D.El.Ed teacher-training programme at DIETs/CTTC Sohra in Meghalaya.
caveats: Requires Class 12 pass with 50%+ marks (45% for SC/ST/OBC/PWD). Age 18-27 (up to 32 for SC/ST/OBC/PWD). Merit-based, competitive counseling process with limited block-wise seats — not a guaranteed entitlement even if eligible.

title: The Meghalaya Tribal Students' Book Grant (Post-Matric Education)
benefit_summary: Rs.500-1,500 one-time book grant (varies by course level) for Khasi-Jaintia or Garo tribal students in Meghalaya pursuing post-matric education.
caveats: Requires 60%+ aggregate marks in the preceding exam. Only for regular (non-technical/vocational) courses. Not for government employees. Switching courses forfeits further grants.

title: YSR EBC Nestham
benefit_summary: Rs.45,000 total (Rs.15,000/year for 3 years) for Economically Backward Class women aged 45-60 in Andhra Pradesh.
caveats: Income cap Rs.10,000/month (rural) or Rs.12,000/month (urban) — used the higher urban figure here. Land holding must be under 3 acres wet / 10 acres dry land. No family member may be a government employee/pensioner or income-tax payer, own a four-wheeler (except taxi/tractor/auto), or have >300 units/month electricity use or >750 sq ft built-up property.

title: Farmer Suicide Ex-Gratia
benefit_summary: Rs.7,00,000 to the family of a farmer/tenant farmer in Andhra Pradesh who dies by suicide for agrarian reasons (crop failure, debt, non-remunerative prices, etc.).
caveats: IMPORTANT: despite the formal Rs.7,00,000 entitlement, real-world news reporting describes many recognized eligible families NOT receiving payment, and the current government reportedly recognizing fewer beneficiary families than before — actual disbursal is unreliable in practice. "Farmer" includes tenant farmers and women farmers, not just titled landowners. Paid to a family member, not the deceased.

title: YSR Kapu Nestham
benefit_summary: Rs.15,000/year for Kapu community (Kapu, Balija, Telaga, Ontari) women aged 45-60 in Andhra Pradesh.
caveats: Same means-test structure as ysrebcn (income, land, electricity, property, vehicle, tax-payer exclusions) but for the Kapu community specifically, not general EBC. Income cap Rs.10,000/month (rural) or Rs.12,000/month (urban).

title: YSR Law Nestham
benefit_summary: Rs.5,000/month stipend for the first 3 years of legal practice, for junior advocates in Andhra Pradesh.
caveats: Requires a Law degree (2016+ graduate) and AP Bar Council enrollment. Only within the first 3 years of practice, age up to 35. One benefit per family (spouse + children).

title: Employee Health Scheme
benefit_summary: Up to Rs.2,00,000 cashless hospitalization per illness episode for Andhra Pradesh state government employees, pensioners, and their dependents, at empanelled hospitals via the Dr. YSR Aarogyasri Healthcare Trust.
caveats: Claims above Rs.2 lakh are settled separately by the Aarogyasri Trust CEO, not capped outright. Ward type (semi-private/private) depends on pay grade.

title: Dr. Ambedkar Awas Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.1,20,000 house-construction assistance (Rs.40k/60k/20k installments) for BPL Scheduled Caste families in Gujarat, plus a separate Rs.12,000 toilet grant if not otherwise eligible for one.
caveats: Must not already own a house/plot or have received another housing-scheme benefit. Construction must finish within 2 years of the first installment. Total construction cost capped at Rs.10 lakh (urban) or Rs.7 lakh (rural), though this cap doesn't apply to the Affordable Housing Scheme component.

title: Prosthetic Aid and Appliances for Person with Disabilities
benefit_summary: Assistive equipment up to Rs.20,000 for persons with 40%+ disability in Gujarat: artificial limbs, wheelchairs, hearing aids, Braille kits, or self-employment tools (sewing machines, repair-tool kits, etc.).
caveats: Employment-oriented tools not given to applicants under 16. Usable once every 5 years.

title: Sardar Patel Agriculture Research Award
benefit_summary: Rs.51,000 cash award plus shawl and certificate for the top farmer in each category annually in Gujarat (top 5 in each category also recognized with shawl/certificate); similar recognition for beekeeping, poultry, and fisheries achievements.
caveats: Merit-based/competitive award, not a general entitlement — requires being selected as a top performer.

title: Cash Award (A.B.O.C.W.W.B)
benefit_summary: One-time cash award for children of registered Assam construction workers scoring 55%+ in HSLC/AHM/HS exams: Rs.3,500 (55-65%) up to Rs.5,000 (75%+).
caveats: Parent must have active board membership. Limited to top 3 male and 3 female scorers per district.

title: General Pension (A.B.O.C.W.W.B)
benefit_summary: Rs.2,000/month plus Rs.100/year increase for every year of registered service, for Assam construction workers aged 60+.
caveats: Requires at least 1 year of registered board membership before turning 60.

title: Medical Assistance (A.B.O.C.W.W.B)
benefit_summary: Medical assistance for registered Assam construction workers: Rs.1,000/day (first 5 days hospitalized) + Rs.200/day thereafter (max Rs.20,000); Rs.25,000-1,50,000 by disability percentage; Rs.1,50,000 for critical diseases (cancer, heart attack, kidney failure, etc.).
caveats: The board's own site summarizes this as "up to Rs.1 lakh annually" — may represent an overall envelope around these more detailed tiers rather than a separate figure.

title: Maternity Benefit (A.B.O.C.W.W.B)
benefit_summary: Rs.20,000 maternity benefit for registered women construction workers in Assam, allowed twice per beneficiary.
caveats: Requires active board membership.

title: Chief Ministergi Artistesinggi Tengbang (CMAT) – Artiste's Pension
benefit_summary: Rs.4,000/month (National/State award-winning artistes, 150 slots) or Rs.2,500/month (other recognized artistes, 850 slots) for artistes aged 60+ in Manipur, plus up to Rs.2 lakh medical assistance under a companion scheme.
caveats: Must not be employed in any public/private undertaking. Recognized artiste status must be certified by a competent cultural authority. Capped at 1,000 total beneficiaries statewide — not a universal entitlement even if eligible.

title: Financial Assistance To Poor & Needy Widow Women
benefit_summary: Rs.2,000/year for BPL widows aged 18-40 in Manipur.
caveats: A separate "Chief Minister Widow Pension Scheme" (Rs.500/month) covers widows 40+ or HIV-positive widows 18+ — different scheme, not this one. Requires annual fresh/renewal application, subject to fund availability.

title: State Merit Scholarship Manipur
benefit_summary: Rs.6,000/year (top 300 Class X BSEM scorers, 2 years) or Rs.12,000/year (top 125 Science/125 Social Science/50 Commerce Class XII COHSEM scorers, 3 years) in Manipur.
caveats: Merit-based (top rankers only), not means-tested — limited slots, not a general entitlement. Cannot combine with another scholarship for the same course. Must maintain good conduct/attendance and not switch courses without approval.

title: Chief Minister's College Students Rehabilitation Scheme (CMCSRS)
benefit_summary: One-time rehabilitation grant (Rs.10,000: Rs.5,000 books + Rs.2,000 uniform + Rs.3,000 misc.) plus free college admission, transfer facility, and a free smartphone, for undergraduate students displaced by the Manipur conflict.
caveats: Only for students at Government/Government-Aided colleges in Manipur. Confirmed still active as of the 2025-26 academic session (May 2026 disbursement to 754 displaced students) — an ongoing crisis-response scheme tied to the state's conflict situation, not a permanent scheme.

title: AASRA Scheme
benefit_summary: Free PMSBY (accident, Rs.2 lakh) + PMJJBY (life, Rs.2 lakh) insurance for 5 years — premiums fully paid by the J&K UT government — for widows, destitute, and BPL/low-income breadwinners (income <Rs.75,000/year) in Jammu & Kashmir.
caveats: Applicant must have no other income source. Requires a zero-balance savings bank account.

title: Financial Assistance To The Child Victims Of Violence Under The National Foundation For Communal Harmony
benefit_summary: Rs.750-800/month (general education) + Rs.150/month (vocational training) until age 18 (extendable to 21), plus accident/disability cover up to Rs.25,000 and medical reimbursement, for orphaned/destitute BPL children of J&K whose breadwinner was killed/incapacitated in communal/ethnic/terrorist violence.
caveats: Figures may be stale (last confirmed circa 2018) — a possible newer Rs.1,250-1,750/month structure was flagged but not confirmed. Not payable if the child receives other regular assistance (one-time government payments excepted).

title: Financial Assistance To Gad-Hanjis
benefit_summary: Rs.200-500 for nylon-twine purchase (tiered by license fee paid), for licensed Gad-Hanji fishermen in Jammu & Kashmir.
caveats: Requires 3 consecutive years of Fisheries Department license. Income cap is unusually low (Rs.3,600/year) — likely a legacy/unrevised threshold. Cannot reapply within 2 years of last benefit.

title: Revised Education Scheme For Children Of Artisans/Weavers Of Handicrafts And Handloom Departments
benefit_summary: Rs.1,500/year (primary) up to Rs.3,000/year (Class 11-12), or actual course fee for technical/professional courses, for children of registered weavers/artisans in Jammu & Kashmir.
caveats: Parent must be registered with the Handicrafts/Handloom Department. Requires BPL/AAY/PHH card OR EWS certificate OR family income <=Rs.90,000/year. Cannot combine with other scholarship schemes (Pre-Matric, Post-Matric, PM Scholarship, etc.).

title: Differently Abled Pension Scheme
benefit_summary: Rs.1,500/month disability pension for persons with 40%+ disability in Tamil Nadu.
caveats: Not eligible if employed by government/government-affiliated bodies. If privately employed or self-employed, income cap is Rs.3,00,000/year.

title: Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme - Tamil Nadu
benefit_summary: Rs.1,500/month disability pension for persons with 80%+ disability (or severe/multiple disabilities) in Tamil Nadu.
caveats: Higher-severity companion scheme to the general Differently Abled Pension Scheme (daps) — likely overlaps in practice for 80%+ disabled applicants, who may qualify under either.

title: Old Age Pension Scheme under Chief Minister's Uzhavar Padhukappu Thittam
benefit_summary: Rs.1,000/month (age 60-79) or Rs.2,000/month (age 80+) for destitute farmers or landless agricultural laborers in Tamil Nadu.
caveats: Fixed assets must not exceed Rs.1,00,000. This is a farmer-specific old-age pension, distinct from and NOT the same rate as the general Tamil Nadu old-age pension (which is Rs.1,200/month) — do not confuse the two.

title: Financial Assistance For Aids And Appliances For Disabled Persons
benefit_summary: 100% cost coverage for disability aids/appliances up to Rs.15,000; up to Rs.15,000 more for costlier items (Rs.15,001-30,000 range), with a 50% co-pay tier if monthly income is Rs.22,501-30,000, for persons with 40%+ disability in Maharashtra.
caveats: The scraped Eligibility text itself still shows stale thresholds (Rs.1,500/2,000 monthly) matching the outdated benefit figures — both were corrected using divyangkalyan.maharashtra.gov.in's current published structure (Rs.22,500-30,000/month income bands). Usable once every 3 years (1 year for children under 12).

title: Nanaji Deshmukh Krishi Sanjivani Prakalp
benefit_summary: 75-80% subsidy on drip/sprinkler micro-irrigation (up to 100% for some components), plus support for protected cultivation, farm ponds, and climate-resilient seed production, for farmers in 5,142+ villages across 16 drought-prone Maharashtra districts.
caveats: Complex scheme with both individual and group/FPC-level components — farmer groups, self-help groups, and Farmer Producer Companies (100+ members) can access larger agribusiness components with loan-linkage requirements. Priority given to women, disabled persons, and landless laborers. Only available in the 16 specifically covered districts (Amravati, Akola, Washim, Buldhana, Yavatmal, Nanded, Hingoli, Parbhani, Jalna, Aurangabad, Osmanabad, Latur, Solapur, Satara, Beed, Nashik) — not statewide.

title: Mukhyamantri Sports Development Scheme - Unemployed Young Professional Sportsperson
benefit_summary: Rs.20,000/month fixed remuneration for unemployed experienced professional sportspersons aged 18-40 in Tripura.
caveats: Age relaxation of 5 years for SC/ST candidates. A sibling scheme for retired persons (not this one) pays Rs.30,000/month.

title: Tripura Pension Scheme For Providing Pension To The Retired Home Guard / Women Home Guard Volunteers
benefit_summary: Rs.2,500/month pension for retired Home Guard/Women Home Guard Volunteers in Tripura (corrected from an outdated Rs.750 figure).
caveats: Requires 20+ years of service, retirement via superannuation or medical invalidation only (not resignation/dismissal). Retirees are actively demanding a further hike to Rs.10,000, not yet granted.

title: Tripura Lynching/Mob Violence Victim Compensation Scheme
benefit_summary: Tiered compensation for victims of lynching/mob violence in Tripura: Rs.4,00,000 (death), Rs.2,00,000 (80%+ disability), Rs.1,00,000 (40-80% disability), Rs.95,000 (destroyed pucca house/shop) down to Rs.3,000-5,000 (partial damage) and Rs.4,000/hut.
caveats: Requires reporting to police/magistrate and cooperating with investigation/prosecution. Not payable if the victim's own wrongdoing/provocation caused the incident. Administered by District/State Legal Aid Committee, interim relief due within 30 days.

title: Nagaland State Merit Scholarship
benefit_summary: Merit scholarship (variable amount, ~Rs.14,500 average per recent cohort) for post-matric students in Nagaland scoring 70-80%+ marks, paid via DBT.
caveats: No fixed rupee figure is published — amount appears to vary by course/level rather than following a flat rate. Merit-based, subject to fund availability, not a guaranteed entitlement.

title: State Research Scholarship
benefit_summary: Research grant (variable amount, no fixed published figure) for Scheduled Tribe/indigenous Nagaland students pursuing M.Phil/PhD/D.Litt.
caveats: Cannot combine with another scholarship/fellowship. Not for government/semi-government employees. Usable a maximum of 3 times.

title: State Technical Scholarship for ST Student
benefit_summary: Annual book grant plus fee coverage (variable amount, no fixed published figure) for ST students in Nagaland pursuing Diploma/Degree/PG Engineering or Forestry courses.
caveats: Only for Engineering (AICTE-recognized) or Forestry courses — other courses not eligible. Not for government/semi-government employees. Disqualified if claiming more than one scholarship in the same year.

title: Bina Mulya Samajik Suraksha Yojana
benefit_summary: Free group insurance for unorganised workers in West Bengal: Rs.2 lakh (natural death), Rs.5 lakh (accidental death), Rs.5 lakh (permanent disability), Rs.2.5 lakh (partial disability); plus PF (worker Rs.25 + state Rs.30/month), Rs.20,000/year medical + Rs.60,000 surgery cover, and education assistance Class 11-postgraduate for children.
caveats: No income ceiling for construction or transport workers specifically. Entirely state-funded (Rs.500/year premium) — free for the worker. Covers 46 notified unorganised industries and 15 self-employed occupation categories.

title: Samajik Mukti
benefit_summary: Same benefit structure as Bina Mulya Samajik Suraksha Yojana (bmssy) — the 'Samajik Mukti Card' is the access card for these benefits: free group insurance, provident fund, and education assistance for unorganised West Bengal workers.
caveats: Likely the same underlying scheme as bmssy under a different name/branding, not a materially distinct benefit — avoid double-counting both in results for the same user. Income cap corrected to Rs.6,500/month (the originally scraped Rs.65,000/month was almost certainly a data-entry error).

title: Grant-In-Aid to Tripura and Mizoram for Rehabilitation of Bru Migrants
benefit_summary: Rs.4 lakh fixed deposit + Rs.5,000/month cash for 2 years + Rs.1.5 lakh house-construction assistance + a 30x40 sq ft land plot + 2 years free rations + free transport, for Bru (Reang) families resettling permanently in Tripura after fleeing ethnic violence in Mizoram (1997).
caveats: Specifically for Bru/Reang families from the 1997 Mizoram exodus who choose to settle in Tripura (not those repatriating back to Mizoram) — a narrow historical/ethnic-specific eligibility our schema can only approximate via the ST caste category. Most relief camps have closed since 2020-23; may only be relevant to remaining late-stage beneficiaries.

title: Post Matric Merit Scholarship
benefit_summary: Tuition fees, maintenance allowance, and book/stationery costs (variable amount, no fixed published figure) for meritorious post-matric students in Mizoram scoring 60%+ marks.
caveats: Cannot hold another scholarship of higher value simultaneously. Not for correspondence-course students, repeat-subject students at the same stage, or those switching between similar-level professional courses. Medical PG students only eligible if not permitted to practice during the course.

title: Incentive For The Devadasi Children's Marriage
benefit_summary: Rs.3,00,000 (groom) or Rs.5,00,000 (bride) marriage incentive for children of Devadasis in Karnataka, married on/after 1 April 2018.
caveats: Exclusively for the SC community. Must apply within 18 months of marriage. This is a post-marriage incentive — eligibility is about the marriage event, not ongoing status.

title: Madilu Kit
benefit_summary: Rs.4,000 cash assistance plus a free maternity kit (~19 daily-use items) for women delivering in a government hospital in Karnataka; Rs.1,000 instead of the kit for private-hospital deliveries.
caveats: This record's originally scraped content was a data mismatch (described an unrelated rural-entrepreneurship program) — this entry reflects the ACTUAL Madilu Kit maternity scheme, confirmed via multiple sources. Benefit is for a recent/upcoming childbirth, not a general entitlement.

title: Annath Pension Yojana (JBOCWWB)
benefit_summary: Family pension (at the deceased's pension rate) split evenly among all orphaned children under 18, when a pensioner registered with the Jharkhand Building and Other Construction Worker Welfare Board (JBOCWWB) dies. No fixed rupee figure — depends on the deceased's base pension (JBOCWWB's general contributory pension is Rs.1,000/month) and how many orphans share it.
caveats: Eligibility depends on a DECEASED PARENT's status (registered JBOCWWB pensioner), not the applicant's own occupation or worker-board registration — the applicant is the orphaned child. This is for orphaned children (under 18) of a deceased JBOCWWB pensioner specifically, not a general child-support scheme.

title: Prasuti Sahayata Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.21,000 for the birth of a daughter, Rs.20,000 for the birth of a son, for registered female construction workers in Rajasthan holding a beneficiary ID card under Section 13 of the Maternity Benefit Act; plus Rs.1,000 extra if not already receiving Janani Suraksha Yojana cash benefits.
caveats: Payable for a maximum of two deliveries only. Applicant must be at least 20 years old at the time of delivery and registered with the labour department as a construction worker.

title: Chief Minister Kanya Utthan Yojana
benefit_summary: Cascading cash/education benefits for girls in Bihar from birth through graduation: Rs.2,000 at birth + Rs.1,000 at age 1 (after Aadhaar registration) + Rs.2,000 for vaccination + Rs.3,700 total for uniforms (classes 1-12) + Rs.10,000 in class 10 + Rs.25,000 in class 12 + Rs.50,000 on graduating.
caveats: Limited to two girl children per family, born after the scheme notification. Early-life installments (birth/vaccination) are typically claimed by parents/guardians on the girl's behalf, not the girl herself — our schema models this against the female applicant, but a parent may need to apply for a young daughter.

title: Mukh Mantri Mawan Dheeyan Satkar Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.1,000/month direct cash transfer to women in Punjab (Rs.1,500/month for SC-category women), via Aadhaar-linked bank account. Confirmed live and paying out as of July 2026 (first installment released 1 July 2026, covering Jul-Sep as a lump advance).
caveats: Excludes current/retired government employees, PSU/statutory board staff, sitting or former MPs/MLAs, spouses of serving ministers/MPs/MLAs, and income-tax payers — our schema has no field for this exclusion, so it is not enforced automatically; check before assuming eligibility. Women already receiving widow/old-age/disability pension can still apply. Extremely new scheme (launched April 2026) — rollout terms could still change.

title: Indira Gandhi Shehri Credit Card Yojana
benefit_summary: Interest-free loan of up to Rs.50,000 (no collateral) for small traders, street vendors, and informal-sector workers in Rajasthan's urban areas — 3-month moratorium, 12-month repayment.
caveats: Individual monthly income must be Rs.15,000 or less and family monthly income Rs.50,000 or less (approximated here as a yearly cap of Rs.6,00,000 for the family — check the exact monthly figures locally). This was a Congress-era (Gehlot government) scheme; the current BJP (Bhajanlal Sharma) government has renamed several other "Indira Gandhi"-branded Rajasthan schemes (e.g. Indira Gandhi Shehri Rozgar Guarantee Yojana → Mukhyamantri Shehri Rozgar Guarantee Yojana) — this specific scheme was not found explicitly renamed or discontinued as of this check, but confirm it's still active under this name before relying on it.

title: Indira Gandhi National Vridhavastha Pension Yojana (Rajasthan)
benefit_summary: Rs.1,000/month old-age pension for BPL residents of Rajasthan aged 60 and above, under the centrally-sponsored National Social Assistance Programme (IGNOAPS) as implemented by Rajasthan.
caveats: Restricted to families below the poverty line per Government of India criteria.

title: Indira Gandhi National Vidhwa Pension Yojana (Rajasthan)
benefit_summary: Rs.1,000/month widow pension for BPL women aged 40-74, and Rs.1,500/month for those 75+, in Rajasthan (IGNWPS as implemented by Rajasthan).
caveats: Restricted to families below the poverty line per Government of India criteria.

title: Pedalandariki Illu
benefit_summary: Free house-site patta (1.5 cents in rural areas) issued in the woman beneficiary's name, plus government-sanctioned house construction assistance, for BPL households in Andhra Pradesh with no existing house/house-site anywhere in the state.
caveats: Household must not have benefited from any previous state housing scheme. Patta and construction sanction are issued to the woman of the household specifically, not any adult member.

title: Gharelu Hinsa Ki Pidita Ke Liye Sahayta Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.2,00,000 compensation for women/girls in Madhya Pradesh who suffer up to 40% disability due to domestic violence (by blood or marital relations); Rs.4,00,000 if disability exceeds 40%. Also includes transport to court for related legal hearings.
caveats: Requires the disability to have resulted FROM domestic violence specifically, not disability in general — our schema's disability_required flag cannot distinguish cause, so this may over-match women with an unrelated disability. Confirm the domestic-violence link applies before treating as eligible.

title: Dr. Ambedkar Centrally Sponsored Scheme of Post-Matric Scholarships for Economically Backward Class Students
benefit_summary: Maintenance allowance (Rs.335-750/month depending on hosteller/day-scholar status and course group) plus reimbursement of compulsory fees, for General-category (non-SC/ST/OBC) post-matric students in India whose family income is Rs.1,00,000/year or less.
caveats: Only two boys from the same family can receive this scholarship (no such limit for girls). Not for correspondence/aviation courses in most cases; repeating the same education stage in a different subject disqualifies.

title: Jal Hauj
benefit_summary: 60% cost subsidy (up to Rs.63,000-90,000 depending on lining specification) for farmers in Rajasthan to build an on-farm rainwater harvesting tank/pond (100 cubic metre / 1 lakh litre capacity).
caveats: Requires the applicant to own at least 0.3-0.5 hectare of cultivable land (sources vary slightly on the exact minimum) and to already have a water source/irrigation means.

title: Krishi Yantra
benefit_summary: Subsidy of 40-50% on farm equipment/machinery (seed drills, rotavators, disc ploughs, threshers, planters, tractor-mounted implements) for Rajasthan farmers, with the higher end reserved for SC/ST/small/marginal/women farmers.
caveats: Land (and, for tractor-operated implements, the tractor itself) must be registered in the applicant's own name. Cannot claim a repeat grant for the same implement type within a set period.

title: Zero Budget Natural Farming
benefit_summary: 50% subsidy on natural-farming inputs and equipment (drums, sprayers, filters, Trichoderma, mulch material, etc.) for Rajasthan farmers adopting zero-budget natural farming.
caveats: Applicant must own at least one acre of land (or be part of a family land-holding account) and have a demonstrated interest in natural farming.

title: Krshak Prashikshan Tatha Bhraman Karyakram
benefit_summary: Rs.1,000/day per farmer for in-state training (up to 7 days), Rs.1,500/day for out-of-state training or technology exposure visits, for Madhya Pradesh farmers of any category.
caveats: Covers travel/training-program costs, not a standalone cash grant — must actually participate in a scheduled training/exposure visit to claim it.

title: Riyaayati Dar Par Copies Ka Vitaran
benefit_summary: Subsidized school stationery for registered construction workers' children in Madhya Pradesh: Rs.10/copy (10 small copies) and Rs.14/register (10 registers).
caveats: Small, in-kind-value benefit — limited to a maximum of two children per worker. Worker must deposit the copy/register cost through the institute to the board.

title: Assistance Scheme For Reimbursement For Expenditure On Visa By Construction Workers For Employment Abroad
benefit_summary: Reimbursement of up to Rs.5,000 for visa/documentation expenses for registered Rajasthan construction workers who secure employment abroad through the Protector of Emigrants (POE) migration process.
caveats: Requires proper emigration clearance/permission from the POE office for the foreign employment — not for workers who migrate outside the official channel.

title: Akanksha Scheme
benefit_summary: Free coaching for Scheduled Tribe students in Madhya Pradesh (classes 11-12) preparing for JEE, NEET/AIIMS, and CLAT at reputed institutes in Bhopal, Indore, Jabalpur, and Gwalior.
caveats: Requires 60%+ marks in class 10, admission to class 10th-passed-into-11th-class standing, a digital caste certificate, and registration on the MPTAAS tribal-department portal. Merit-based selection via the coaching institute's own entrance exam, on top of meeting the income/eligibility bar.

title: National Scheme Of Incentive To Girls For Secondary Education
benefit_summary: Rs.3,000 fixed/term deposit (matures when the girl turns 18) for SC/ST girls who passed class 8 and enrolled in class 9 at a government/govt-aided/local-body school.
caveats: Girls from Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalayas qualify regardless of SC/ST status; otherwise restricted to SC/ST. No premature withdrawal allowed before age 18.

title: Pre Matric Scholarship For Students With Disabilities
benefit_summary: Rs.500-800/month maintenance allowance + Rs.1,000/year book grant + disability allowance (Rs.2,000-4,000/year depending on disability type) for class 9-10 students with 40%+ disability, family income up to Rs.2 lakh/year.
caveats: Not payable to a family's third child already receiving this scholarship. Cannot combine with another government scholarship.

title: Post Matric Scholarship for Students With Disabilities
benefit_summary: Maintenance allowance (Rs.750-1,600/month depending on course group and hosteller/day-scholar status) plus fee reimbursement for class 11 onward (including bachelor's/master's) students with 40%+ disability, family income up to Rs.2.5 lakh/year.
caveats: Not payable to a family's third child already receiving this scholarship. Cannot combine with another government scholarship.

title: Scheme For Adolescent Girls
benefit_summary: Take-home ration or hot cooked meal (Rs.9.50/day, 300 days/year) plus health check-ups, nutrition/health education, and life-skills education for out-of-school adolescent girls, via Anganwadi centres.
caveats: Specifically for girls aged 11-14 — our chatbot's age question only distinguishes "under 18" as one bucket, too coarse to enforce this narrower window, so age is left unconstrained here; verify the girl is actually 11-14 before treating this as a match. Delivered through Anganwadi centres, not a direct cash transfer.

title: SMILE - Comprehensive Rehabilitation For Welfare Of Transgender Persons (Scholarship)
benefit_summary: Rs.13,500/year pre-matric or post-matric scholarship for transgender students holding a Transgender Certificate from the National Portal for Transgender Persons.
caveats: Cannot be combined with any other central/state government pre-matric or post-matric scholarship for the same period. Our FLOW's gender options are female/male/other — this scheme is modeled against "other", which may not perfectly capture every transgender respondent depending on how they self-identify in the chatbot.

title: SMILE - Comprehensive Rehabilitation For Welfare Of Transgender Persons (Skill Development)
benefit_summary: Free skill-development training plus Rs.1,000/month stipend (non-residential training) for transgender persons with a valid Transgender Certificate/ID, plus post-training placement or self-employment support.
caveats: Requires 80%+ attendance in the training program to receive post-placement assistance. Same gender-mapping caveat as smile-scholarship applies.

title: Garima Greh Shelter Homes For Transgender Persons
benefit_summary: Free shelter, food, medical care, and recreational facilities at Garima Greh shelter homes for transgender persons aged 18-60, preferably below the poverty line.
caveats: Must not be engaged in sex work, begging, or any commercial/productive employment. Same gender-mapping caveat as smile-scholarship applies.

title: National Overseas Scholarship For Students With Disabilities
benefit_summary: Full funding for Master's/PhD study abroad for students with 40%+ disability: annual maintenance allowance (,400 or £9,900), contingency allowance, actual tuition fees, equipment allowance (Rs.1,500), and visa/travel costs.
caveats: Requires an unconditional admission offer to an accredited Master's/PhD program abroad already in hand. Age limit 35 as of the application month.

title: Griha Aadhar Scheme
benefit_summary: Rs.1,500/month direct bank transfer (by the 10th of each month) for married, widowed, or divorced homemaker women in Goa, where combined household income (with husband, if applicable) does not exceed Rs.3,00,000/year.
caveats: Requires 15 years of continuous Goa residency. A widow with a minor child already receiving Dayanand Social Security Scheme benefits may have different eligibility interplay — check locally if applicable.

title: Suraksha Laghu Evan Simant Vriddhajan Krishak Samman Pension Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.750/month pension for small/marginal farmers in Rajasthan below age 75, rising to Rs.1,000/month at 75+.
caveats: Minimum qualifying age differs by gender: 55 for women, 58 for men — our schema uses one min_age field, so this is set to the lower (55) bound; a male applicant just below 58 may be flagged as eligible when he is not yet, so this should be double-checked for men aged 55-57.

title: Deen Dayal Upadhyay Grameen Kaushalya Yojana
benefit_summary: Free residential skill training (food + accommodation + training covered) plus placement assistance for poor rural youth, targeting jobs paying Rs.10,000+/month; training partners must place at least 70% of trainees.
caveats: General age cap is 35; the 45 cap shown here only applies to women, PVTGs, persons with disabilities, transgender persons, and other specified vulnerable groups — a general-category man over 35 would not actually qualify even though our single max_age field allows it. Also qualifies via MGNREGA-worker or SHG/NRLM household membership even without a BPL/AAY card — not modeled here, so this may under-match some eligible rural youth.

title: Deendayal Upadhyay Bhoomihin Krishi Majdoor Kalyan Yojana
benefit_summary: Rs.10,000/year direct bank transfer (single annual installment) for landless agricultural labourer families in Chhattisgarh, including allied rural trades (shepherd, carpenter, blacksmith, cobbler, barber, washerman) and tribal priests (Baiga/Guniya/Manjhi).
caveats: Renamed from Rajiv Gandhi Gramin Bhoomihin Krishi Majdoor Nyay Yojana to Deendayal Upadhyay Bhoomihin Krishi Majdoor Kalyan Yojana under the current government (launched 20 January 2025), with the payout raised from Rs.6,000-7,000 to Rs.10,000/year. Not eligible if the family already receives another periodic government allowance/pension. Tribal priests (Baiga/Guniya/Manjhi) qualify even if they hold agricultural land — an exception our land_ownership_required=False flag cannot fully capture.
